# dsh-memory-recall

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

![language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-javascript-f7dc6f) ![style](https://img.shields.io/badge/style-vanilla-gray) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A5%2022-brightgreen) ![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-web%20profile-orange) ![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-offline_%C2%B7_100%25_local-brightgreen) ![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-passing-brightgreen)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that gives the model a memory, in the style of [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent): what it learns about you and your projects carries into every new chat, and it can look back through your earlier chats — **only after you allow it**.

**Everything stays on your machine.** Two small text files, dsh's own session index, no embeddings, no service, no telemetry.

![The Memory panel: the model's notes, with a budget bar and inline edit](assets/memory-panel.png)

It does six things:

- **A `memory` tool** — the model keeps two short files: a **user profile** (who you are, how you like to work) and its **own notes** (environment facts, conventions, lessons). Every chat gets both, as a context message you can see in the chat — at the start, again after a change or a compaction.
- **A 🧠 button in the message box** — lit when this chat has memory, dim when it has none, amber when the memory changed since; click it to see what this chat is running on.
- **A `session_search` tool** — the model reads your earlier chats to answer *"what did we decide last time?"*. dsh's own approval prompt asks you first, saying what it wants to look for.
- **A 🧠 Saved to memory note in the chat** — every save shows what changed and how full memory is, so nothing is remembered behind your back.
- **A sidebar 🧠 Memory panel** — everything kept, in two tabs, with edit, delete, add and search.
- **Chats and workspaces in the `@` menu** — grouped by workspace, under their real titles, so you can hand the model a chat or point its search at one workspace.

## Install

Requires a working dsh (0.1.5 or later) with a `web` profile.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-memory-recall
dsh --profile web
```

Or install from GitHub or a local folder instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:adithyanraj03/dsh-memory-recall
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-memory-recall
```

Then **restart dsh** (`dsh --profile web`) if it was already running, and **hard-refresh the browser** (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) — a plain refresh can serve a cached client bundle. **🧠 Memory** appears at the bottom of the sidebar.

### Turn on dsh's full-text search (recommended)

`session_search` uses dsh's own session index, which dsh ships **switched off**. Add this to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: session-query-sqlite
  config:
    path: '/absolute/path/to/.dsh/session-search.db'
    openAt: first-search
```

`first-search` opens the index only when something first searches; a file path keeps it across restarts. The index is derived from your session logs, so deleting the file only costs a rebuild. An override replaces the row's whole config — keep both keys.

Without it, `session_search` still works: it falls back to a literal scan of your 150 most recent chats — slower and unranked — and says so in its card.

## What you get

### Memory that carries over

Just talk. The model saves what will matter later — that you use PowerShell, that a server lives on another machine, that the docs build breaks on a trailing colon — and each save appears in the chat. Click it to see exactly what changed and how full that store is:

![Saves in the chat: an added note and an updated profile entry, each with its budget](assets/saved-chip.png)

![All five states of the note: saving, saved, updated, full — making room, and a write blocked by the safety scan](assets/chip-1.png)

You can also ask directly: *"remember that I prefer short answers"*, *"forget that I use npm"*.

Memory reaches the model as a context message — logged in the chat as 🧠 **Memory loaded** — before its first answer, and again after anything changes or the conversation is compacted, so a save made mid-chat is used in that same chat from the next step. The system prompt keeps only the short how-to, which never changes, so dsh's prompt cache holds.

### Looking back through earlier chats

Refer to an earlier conversation — *"what did we decide about the rollback?"*, *"do it like last time"* — and the model calls `session_search`. dsh's approval prompt takes over the message box with what it wants to read, e.g. *Search your earlier chats for "deploy rollback".*, with **Allow** and **Deny**. The chats it found appear in a card, each with its date, the matching lines and a link to open it:

![A recall card: three earlier chats found for "deploy rollback", with the matching lines](assets/recall-card.png)

It returns the chats' actual messages — nothing summarised, nothing invented — cut to about 9,000 characters so one search cannot flood the context. The asking chat and sub-agent sessions are never results.

### The Memory panel

**🧠 Memory**, at the bottom of the sidebar above ⏱️ Scheduled when both are installed, opens everything that is kept:

- **Notes** and **Profile** tabs, each with a ring and a bar showing how full it is.
- **Edit** or **delete** any entry in place (hover it), with an inline confirm for delete.
- **Add** an entry yourself, and **search** once a tab holds a few.
- **⚙ Display settings** — turn the 🧠 button in the message box and the chats and workspaces in `@` on or off, per browser.
- With the sidebar collapsed, it becomes a single icon, like Settings.

![The Profile tab in the light theme](assets/memory-panel-light.png)

Edits you make here are your own words, so they are not scanned (see [Safety](#safety)), but they still respect the budget. Hand edits to the files show in the panel at once and in open chats from their next step.

### Chats and workspaces in the @ menu

Type `@` in the message box. Below dsh's own files and folders, your chats are listed **grouped by workspace**, under the titles your sidebar shows:

- **Just `@`** — *This workspace* with its most recent chats, then *Workspaces* with every other one and how many chats it holds, then chats in no workspace.
- **`@` + text** — matching workspaces, then matching chats under their workspace's heading.
- **Tab, or the chevron, on a workspace** — all of its chats, with an *All workspaces* crumb back.

**Pick a chat** and dsh attaches a read-only snapshot of it to your message, exactly as its own `@` chat rows do — no search and no permission prompt, because you chose it. **Pick a workspace** and it reaches the model as `[workspace "Web Search" — /path/to/Web Search]`; `session_search` then searches only that workspace's chats (after asking, as always).

Every chat gets a readable name — its title, or the start of its first message if it never got one. Sub-agent sessions are left out, and nothing is capped at 50. These rows replace dsh's own flat `@` chat list while its file rows stay as they are; dsh offers no switch for that, so the plugin wraps its `@` source and restores it when unloaded.

## How asking works

- **Reading earlier chats asks first**, through dsh's own approval prompt.
- **One Allow covers that reply.** A search is usually followed by a closer read of the best hit; asking twice for one question is noise. The permission ends when the reply finishes, so the next question asks again.
- **Deny means nothing is read**, and the model is told not to ask again in that reply. If the prompt is withdrawn (you stopped the reply) or nobody can be asked, nothing is read either.
- **Saving to memory does not ask** — it is always shown in the chat and can be undone in the Memory panel. This matches Hermes Agent's default.

If dsh runs in `danger-full-access` mode its approval policy is `never`, which **rejects** every approval request without prompting — so recall is refused there. Set `askBeforeRecall: false` if you want recall without asking in that mode.

## What the model gets

Two parts, so dsh's prompt cache holds:

1. **The how-to** — a short, unchanging system-prompt note on how memory works. It is the only memory in the prompt prefix, so it never invalidates the cache.
2. **The memory itself** — a context message, logged in the chat as 🧠 **Memory loaded**, with the two stores rendered as Hermes renders them:

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════
USER PROFILE (who the user is) [14% — 189/1,375 chars]
══════════════════════════════════════════════
Works on Windows 11 in PowerShell; projects live under D:/code.
§
Prefers short answers with the command first, explanation after.
```

The budgets are small on purpose — **2,200 characters of notes and 1,375 of profile**, Hermes's defaults, together roughly 900 tokens — because they are paid in every chat. When a store is full, a save that would overflow it is refused whole, never cut; the model is shown the entries and consolidates in one batch that merges or drops stale entries and adds the new one, checked against the final size. Raise the budgets with `limits` (below) if you would rather pay more per chat.

Sub-agent sessions do not get the message; they are the model's own workers.

## Configuration

All optional, on this plugin's row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-memory-recall
  config:
    limits:
      memory: 4000
      user: 1375
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `~/.dsh/dsh-memory-recall` | Where `USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` live |
| `limits` | `{memory: 2200, user: 1375}` | Character budgets for the notes and the profile |
| `recall` | `true` | `false` drops `session_search` and keeps memory |
| `askBeforeRecall` | `true` | `false` reads earlier chats without asking |

An override replaces the row's whole config, so restate every key you set. Restart dsh after changing it.

## Safety

Memory is re-read into every future chat, so a poisoned entry would keep instructing the model until someone deleted it. Every write **the model** makes is scanned for prompt-injection and exfiltration phrasing — *ignore previous instructions*, *don't tell the user*, piping secrets to a URL, SSH keys, edits to dsh's own config, hidden Unicode — and refused with the reason. The patterns are Hermes Agent's.

Other guards:

- A change re-reads the file first, so a hand edit is never overwritten by a stale copy; writes are atomic and one at a time.
- Replace and remove need a piece of text unique to one entry; an ambiguous one is refused, not guessed.
- A batch is all-or-nothing.

## How it works

- **Host side** (`src/index.js`, `src/inject.js`): registers the `memory` and `session_search` tools, keeps a short how-to in each new top-level chat's system prompt on `agent/session-start`, and before every model step (`agent/pre-step`) appends the current memory to the step's messages as a logged context message when the chat does not already see it — at the start, after a change, and after a compaction. It serves the panel's routes under `/plugin-data/dsh-memory-recall/`. Recall goes through dsh's `sessionQuery` service and its `approval` service; nothing talks to the network.
- **Client side** (`lib/client.js`, plain JavaScript, no build step): the in-chat chip and recall card replace dsh's own rows for those two tools through the `tool.call.toolview` slot; the 🧠 **Memory loaded / reloaded / updated** row is a `conversation.chat.node` that shadows the plugin's own context message at priority −10 and delegates every other row; the 🧠 button mounts into `conversation.input.right`; the panel mounts into `sidebar.footer.action`; the `@` rows are an `inputTriggers` source.
- **Files**:

  ```
  ~/.dsh/dsh-memory-recall/USER.md     the user profile
  ~/.dsh/dsh-memory-recall/MEMORY.md   the model's notes
  ```

  Plain text, entries separated by a line holding only `§` — the same format as Hermes, readable and editable by hand.

## Requirements

- dsh 0.1.5 or later, with a `web` profile — from 0.2.1 also dsh 0.1.7+ and 0.2.x
- Node 22+
- No runtime dependencies — the client bundle requires only `react`

## Credits

The design — two bounded stores, a frozen per-chat snapshot, the batch-against-final-budget rule, `session_search`'s shapes, the §-delimited files and the threat patterns — comes from [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) by Nous Research (MIT). The brain icons are Lucide's (ISC) and Phosphor's (MIT).

## Licence

MIT — see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file, which also carries the notices for Hermes Agent, Lucide and Phosphor.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-schedule-later English | [中文](README.zh-CN.md) ![language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-javascript-f7dc6f) ![style](https://img.shields.io/badge/style-vanilla-gray) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A5%2018-brightgreen) ![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-web%20profile-orange) ![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-offline_%C2%B7_100%25_local-brightgreen) ![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-passing-brightgreen) A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that schedules a message into a dsh chat for later — picked by you from a date and time picker in the message box, or by the model with its own tools. **It runs on the host, not in the browser.** Schedule it, close the tab, go to sleep: the dsh process sends it on time as a **normal user bubble**, and the model replies to it exactly as if you had pressed Send. ![The scheduler in motion: the sky follows the chosen time and the countdown ticks](assets/main.gif) ![The sidebar panel with a live countdown](assets/scheduled.gif) It does five things: - **A ⏱️ Schedule button in the message box** — a day/night scheduler with a sky header that follows the chosen time, an analog clock, an AM/PM sun-and-moon pill and quick picks, on the same row as Send. - **Host-side delivery** — timing and message injection both run inside the dsh host process, so the browser is only a view; it works with the tab closed. - **A sidebar “⏱️ Scheduled” panel** — every pending message across all chats, grouped by chat, soonest first, tinted by the time it sends, where each message can be sent now, re-timed or cancelled. - **Three tools for the model** — `schedule_message`, `list_scheduled_messages`, `cancel_scheduled_message` — so the assistant can come back to a chat on its own. - **A `schedule-later` skill** — teaches the model when to schedule its own check-ins unprompted. ## Install Requires a working dsh with a `web` profile. ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-schedule-later dsh --profile web ``` Or install from GitHub or a local folder instead: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:adithyanraj03/dsh-schedule-later dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-schedule-later ``` Then **restart dsh** (`dsh --profile web`) if it was already running, and **hard-refresh the browser** (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) — a plain refresh can serve a cached client bundle. A **⏱️ Schedule** button appears in the message box row, and a **⏱️ Scheduled** entry appears at the bottom of the sidebar. ### Coming from `dsh-send-later`? This is the same plugin under its published name. **Do not run both** in one profile: they register the same three model tools and the same message-box button, so remove the old one first — its row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and its entry from the profile's `package.json`. Pending messages live in a folder named after the plugin, so to keep them, copy the queue across while dsh is stopped: ```sh mkdir -p ~/.dsh/dsh-schedule-later cp ~/.dsh/dsh-send-later/tasks.json ~/.dsh/dsh-schedule-later/tasks.json ``` ## What you get ### The scheduler Sits on the message box row, next to Send. Type as usual → click **⏱️ Schedule** → the scheduler opens (defaults to now + 5 minutes, any future time allowed) → **Confirm** turns the draft into a scheduled message and clears the box. **Nothing is sent immediately.** Multi-line text and Markdown source are kept exactly as typed. The header is a sky that follows the chosen time — dawn, day, dusk, night — with the sun or moon moving along its arc, and an analog clock sweeping to the hour, its face light by day and dark with stars by night. The time carries an **AM/PM pill with a sun or a moon**, so 9:00 PM is never mistaken for 9:00 AM. Quick picks: +5 min, +15 min, +1 hour, Tonight 9 PM, Tomorrow 9 AM, and a live “Sends in …” underneath. ![The scheduler by day](assets/scheduler-day.png) ![Night, with the click-to-pick hour list open](assets/scheduler-night-hour-list.png) It animates without being noisy: the stopwatch sweeps while you schedule and nudges on hover, the sidebar icon ticks slowly while anything is pending, and the hourglass turns over on every countdown. All of it stops when the OS asks for reduced motion. On phones and narrow windows (≤480px) the picker folds into a near-full-width popover, with touch targets at least 40px tall: ![The folded layout used on phones and narrow windows](assets/scheduler-compact.png) Cancel any pending message from the chip or the sidebar panel — both ask first. ### The sidebar panel An entry at the bottom of the sidebar, with a badge counting every pending message, opens a panel listing pending messages across **all chats**, soonest first, each row showing the message in monospace (clamped to two lines), the send time and a countdown. Messages are grouped under their chat — click the chat's name to open it. Click a message for its details: the full text, who scheduled it and when, and Send now, Change time and Cancel. Send now and Cancel ask for confirmation first. Cancel from here for any chat. Entries whose chat was deleted are greyed out but can still be cancelled. ![Pending messages across chats, tinted by the time they send](assets/scheduled-panel.png) Pending messages for the current chat also appear as a **one-line chip fused to the top of the message box** — the soonest message truncated, its time, a live countdown and a ✕ that cancels it after asking. With more than one pending, a “+N” badge counts the rest. Click the chip and the sidebar panel opens straight on that message, where the full text lives. ### The model tools Three tools let the assistant schedule messages into the chat it is working in — to come back to something later without you having to remember: | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `schedule_message` | Schedule a message into **this chat**, by `delay_minutes` or an ISO 8601 `at` (no offset = this machine's local time). | | `list_scheduled_messages` | List what is pending in this chat — yours and the assistant's — and the current local time. | | `cancel_scheduled_message` | Cancel a message **the assistant** scheduled. | Ask things like *“remind me at 6pm to push the release”* or *“check the CI run again in 20 minutes”*. When it fires, it arrives as a new turn and the model acts on it. Guard rails, because an assistant that can wake itself up could otherwise do so forever: - **This chat only.** It schedules into the chat it is running in, never another. - **Visibly marked.** Its messages arrive starting with `[Scheduled by the assistant]`, so nobody mistakes them for you typing live. - **At least 1 minute ahead, at most 30 days out, at most 10 pending per chat.** - **It cannot cancel yours.** It can list your scheduled messages but only cancel its own. - Everything it schedules shows up in the ⏱️ panel and the in-chat list, where you can cancel it. ### The skill The plugin ships a `schedule-later` skill (`SKILL.md`), registered with dsh's skills service, whose catalog entry the model sees every turn. It teaches when to come back unprompted — a build, deploy or job still running, a page or status that will change, something you said you would do later — how to write the message so its future self can act on it cold, and to tell you what it scheduled and when. Edit `SKILL.md` to change that behaviour; it is re-read on every catalog refresh. ## Requirements - A `web` dsh profile — `engines: dsh >= 0.1.0` - Node 18+ - No runtime dependencies — the client bundle requires only `react` ## Licence MIT — see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-tg-bridge

A Telegram bridge for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com): drive the agent from a
bot with text, voice and photos, without opening the desktop app.

Each forum topic is a separate project with its own session and its own working
directory. Replies arrive with progress, a "Stop" button and copyable code
blocks.

## Features

- **Text**: a regular task goes to the agent, the answer comes back in the same topic.
- **Voice**: local faster-whisper, the transcript is shown before the answer.
- **Photos**: the turn's own model reads them through `read_image`, text and UI
  included; no second model is needed (a vision overlay stays opt-in).
- **Project per topic**: `/cd my-app`, and all turns run from that directory.
- **Goal and checklist per topic**: `/goal`, `/task`; both survive restarts and are prepended to every turn.
- **Live progress**: one edited message per turn — steps, a timer and the cache hit rate, plus
  the model's reasoning in a collapsed block you can tap open. A long turn adds a second
  collapsed block with every tool call, so the whole run stays in the chat as one message.
- **No lost messages**: a journal with acknowledgement and replay.
- **Fail-fast**: when the quota runs out it switches to a free model right away.
- **`dsh-tg check`**: diagnostics in one command, no changes to the system.
- **Languages**: menus and service messages in `en`, `ru`, `zh`; `/lang` switches the topic language, a new user gets theirs from the Telegram `language_code` (anything outside ru/zh → `en`).
- **"Stop"/"Retry" buttons, tool confirmations**: right in the message, no commands to type.

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 20
- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer in the `0.2.x` line (`>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`)
- DeepSeek Harness installed (`~/.dsh/profiles/headless`)
- A Telegram bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)

The supported harness range is declared in `engines.dsh`; that field decides
compatibility on its own (DSH ignores `peerDependencies` when it is present).
The range includes an explicit prerelease branch, because a plain `<0.3.0`
silently excludes `0.2.2-*` builds. A future `0.3.0` needs an explicit bump:
the bridge relies on the `0.2.x` CLI flags and profile layout.

## Ecosystem

The Chinese DSH community maintains the largest plugin catalogs and the
in-app markets that read them; this bridge follows their packaging rules so it
can be listed next to them:

- [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) — bilingual (English /
  中文) plugin list and the `dsh-plugin-catalog` npm package
- [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — the Chinese-built
  in-app market with one-click install and themes
- [dsh-find-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/dsh-find-plugin) —
  finds a plugin from chat instead of browsing a catalog

## Languages

- Menus (`/` in chat): three sets, `ru` by default, plus `en` and `zh`.
- Topic language: `/lang en|ru|zh`; stored in `state.json` and survives a restart.
- A new user gets the language from the Telegram `language_code`; anything that is not `ru`/`zh` → `en`.
- Translated so far: menus, the start message, turn status, errors, `/cd`, `/new`, `/stop`, `/lang`,
  the reply to an unknown command. Long reports (`/status`, `/sessions`, `/model` and similar)
  are still in Russian, that is the next pass.

## Installation

One command: your bot token and your numeric id. Nothing to edit by hand.

**Any platform with Node.js ≥ 20**

```bash
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest setup
```

`init` writes the token, your id and the working directory; `setup` registers
autostart and starts the bridge.

**As a DSH plugin** (the package carries a `dsh.bundle`; the catalog entry is
pending review):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-tg-bridge
```

The plugin starts one bridge when DSH boots and stops it on shutdown; if a
bridge is already running (for example from the scheduled task), it leaves it
alone. Run `npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init ...` first so a config exists.

What `init` does:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| bot token | `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `refs.DSH_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`; other keys are left alone |
| your id and working directory | `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/config.json`; an existing file is not overwritten |
| `headless` profile | checked, with a hint on how to create it if missing |

`init` flags: `--cwd <path>` (default `~/Projects`), `--voice` (enable
voice transcription), `--dry-run` (show what would be written, change nothing).

Optional provider settings live in `config.json`:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `providerKeys` | extra env var names to pass to a turn, read from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; default `[]` |
| `pricesUrl` | public model page for `/prices`; default `""` uses models.dev only |
| `vision.patch` | opt-in overlay profile for photo turns; default `""` — the turn's own model reads images |
| `vision.enabled` | set `true` to run photo turns on `vision.patch` instead of the topic profile |
| `fallbackModels` | free-model fallbacks; default `[]` |

Get your id from [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot), the token from
[@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather).

### Bot settings in Telegram

Three things without which the bot will stay silent in a group or work only halfway:

1. **Privacy mode → Disable** (`/setprivacy` in BotFather). Otherwise the bot sees
   only commands, not regular text in a topic.
2. **Topics enabled** in the group settings (Edit → Topics). Without them all work
   goes to a single chat and per-topic sessions are not created.
3. **Pin Messages** permission for the bot. Only needed to pin the first
   message of a topic; without it the bridge keeps working but will not pin.

You do not need to set up the command menu by hand: `init` and `setup` install it
in Russian, English and Chinese at once. The menu is not refreshed by a plain
bridge restart, so after adding commands run `dsh-tg menu`. The full settings
table, permissions, checks and common errors are in
[docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md](docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md).

**Autostart** is installed by the setup: `launchd` on macOS, `systemd --user` on
Linux. On Windows `setup` registers the `DSH-TG-Bridge` task, which runs the
guarded supervisor (the same launcher on logon and every five minutes) so a
crashed bridge comes back without a second poller.

**Manual install** (if you want full control):

```bash
npm install -g dsh-tg-bridge
dsh-tg init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
dsh-tg check     # report only, changes nothing
dsh-tg setup     # stop the old bridge and start the new one
```

If the bridge is already installed, `setup` restarts it on the new code and reinstalls
the command menu.

## Troubleshooting

Error replies end with a code, which tells you what to fix:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA` | provider balance is empty: top up or stay on free models (`/prices`, `/model`) |
| `TG_CONFLICT` | a second process is polling the same bot: `/doctor`, then `/restart` |
| `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` | no provider key in the profile: add it in the DSH app |
| `NO_DSH_CLI` | DeepSeek Harness CLI not found: check the app installation |
| `NETWORK` | no network to the provider: retry, check VPN/DNS |
| `SANDBOX_DENY` | DSH denied access to a file or directory: check the project path and permissions |
| `UNKNOWN_MODEL` | the model from the config is unavailable: `/model` lists the working ones |
| `EMPTY_RESPONSE` | the model returned nothing: retry or switch model (`/model`) |
| `TURN_FAILED` | cause not recognized: `/doctor` and `/logs errors` |

## Checks

Send the bot:

| Command | Expected |
|---|---|
| `/doctor` | report: pid, Telegram, disk, directory, session |
| `/version` | bridge version, the latest on npm, bridge directory |
| `/update` | says whether a newer release exists (`/update confirm` installs it) |
| `/thoughts [file\|all\|off]` | the last turn's reasoning as a message; `file`/`all` send the full log as a Markdown document, `off` hides the block |
| `/help` | commands grouped by category |
| `/cd my-app` | topic bound to the project |
| `/prices` | model prices and the cost of the current one |

## Commands

```
Work:         /cd · /new · /stop · /send · /seed
Goals:        /goal · /task
Sessions:     /status · /sessions · /resume
Agents:       /agents · /agents <id> · /agents set model|depth|filter
Models:       /model · /model <id> · /prices
Tuning:       /effort · /permissions · /preset · /plan · /jobs · /remind
Profiles:     /profile · /profile <name> · /profile new <name> from <template>
Extensions:   /skills · /plugins · /soul
Diagnostics:  /doctor · /logs [errors|N|text]
Service:      /app · /restart · /help
Display:      /lang · /reasoning on|off
```

## How it works

```
Telegram → bridge.mjs → dsh --profile headless --json → reply
             │
             ├─ pending/ journal + ack  (messages are not lost)
             ├─ per-topic queue         (turns in topics run in parallel)
             ├─ progress + buttons      (you can see the work is going)
             └─ fail-fast on quota      (free models as a fallback)
```

The bridge is a single process with long polling. Each turn spawns a separate
CLI process that exits after the answer, so "no DSH process" between
turns is normal, not a failure.

### Steering during a turn

If you write in a topic while a turn is still running, the message does not queue
behind it: the bridge drops the task into `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/steer/`, the `dsh-steer-inbox`
plugin hands it to the live agent on its next step, and the agent immediately replies with a short
line in the chat: what it is doing now and where it put the addition. If the agent stays silent
for 90 seconds, the bridge writes one neutral line itself so there is no silence.

Attachments work the same way. A voice note is transcribed first and its transcript is echoed in
the chat, then the text is steered into the running turn; a photo or a file is downloaded to a
local path and that path is steered, exactly as an idle turn would hand it over.

What each kind of attachment becomes inside a running turn:

| Sent | Inside the turn |
|---|---|
| voice note, audio file, audio sent as a document | transcript, echoed as `🎤 …` before the steer |
| small text file (`.md`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.py`, `.log`, … up to 60 KB) | the content itself between `<file>` markers — no tool call needed |
| PDF, archive, binary, anything bigger | its local path under `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/inbox/` |
| video, video note, animation | its path; the agent can pull frames or sound out with ffmpeg |
| photo | its path plus one honest line; the turn reads it with `read_image`, and says so in one line if it cannot |

A caption does not turn the attachment into a text-only message: it is folded into the same
hand-over, so "why did this fail" plus a `.log` file arrives as one steer.

An album is one request, not ten. Telegram delivers it as one update per file, all sharing a
`media_group_id`; the bridge collects the group (1.2 s of quiet after the last item, at most
4 s) and hands it over once — one steer into a running turn, one turn when the topic is idle.

### When a turn hits the time ceiling

`turnTimeoutMs` (default 30 min, this install 75) is a ceiling, not a target: if a turn reaches
it, the bridge stops it with `⏱` instead of letting one runaway loop own the topic for hours.
Nothing is lost — the session and every file the turn produced stay in place — so the message
carries **⏵ Continue**, which asks the agent to check the state and go on from where it stopped.
That is deliberately not the same as **Retry**, which would redo the whole task from the start.

This needs the plugin from this repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add link:<path-to-repository>/plugin/steer-inbox
```

and a line in `~/.dsh/profiles/headless/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: steer-inbox
      name: 'dsh-steer-inbox'
```

The bridge checks the profile itself: if the line is missing, it does not write the task
(it would just expire) and behaves as before, queueing the message.

### Live thoughts and reasoning

Two things land in the same progress message, and neither sends a chat message of its own.

**The model's reasoning.** Every `thinking` block the CLI commits is folded into one
Telegram `<blockquote expandable>`: collapsed it is a single line, tapped it opens the whole
trail of the turn, and it stays there after the turn ends — the same way the desktop app shows
a reasoning section you can expand. The block is written once, in the final edit of the turn,
and never touched again: Telegram re-collapses an expanded block on every edit of its message,
which used to yank the chat away from a half-read paragraph. While the turn runs the message
only gets a counter (`🧠 Размышления · 4821`) and the last three steps, so the live edits stay
short. Escaped, and trimmed to its tail when a turn thinks longer than a message can hold; the
panel never exceeds one message. A cut block says `… · начало скрыто · /thoughts file`, which
sends the whole log as a document. If the API refuses the markup, the same content is retried
as plain text.

**The steps.** Three calls fit inline. A turn that makes more moves its complete step list into
a second collapsed block, added in that same final edit, so "what did it actually run" is one
tap away instead of a count.

**The agent's own notes.** The agent can add a short decision trail:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/tg-bridge/say.mjs --thought "checking why the watchdog fired twice"
```

The note is appended to `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/<chat>_<thread>.jsonl`; the progress
message shows the last two as `💭` lines. The command needs no ids: it falls back to the
newest turn's thought file, because tool shells do not inherit the bridge environment.
`--thought` never sends a Telegram message on its own.

`/reasoning` is the switch for the 💭 mechanism. It is on by default: every turn carries a
short instruction to leave one line at each decision point (task clear, cause found, risky
change, result checked). `/reasoning off` drops the instruction and the `💭` lines for that
topic — useful when the step list is all you want. The setting lives in `state.json` per topic,
so a chatty research topic and a terse deploy topic can differ.

The reasoning block itself is model output; `/thoughts` is what reads it back:

- `/thoughts` — the last turn as a message, in parts, deleted after a few minutes;
- `/thoughts file` — the **whole** last turn as `reasoning-<date>-file.md`, sent as a document
  (a five-hour turn is tens of thousands of characters, which no chat message can hold);
- `/thoughts all` — every turn of the session in one file (a long session is a couple of MB);
- `/thoughts off` / `on` — keep the block out of the turn panel (the panel then shows
  `🧠 Размышления · N · /thoughts file`) or bring it back.

The log is built from the session file on demand, so nothing is duplicated while a turn runs.
Files land in `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/` and older ones are pruned after a week.

### Profiles per topic

The desktop app lets you build several profiles for different kinds of work, each with its own
plugin set and model. The same switch works from a topic:

```
/profile                    current profile, available ones, hints
/profile research           run this topic's turns on another profile
/profile new research from web
                            create a profile from a shipped template and bind it
/profile default            back to the install default
```

A new profile is written by `dsh <name> --from-default-profile <template> --dump-config`, so
nothing boots and no plugin is loaded at creation time; dependencies are installed by the
profile's first turn. The binding is per topic: `/model` then edits that profile's model, and
`/plugins` manages that profile's rows.

### Goals and tasks

A topic carries its own goal and checklist, so the aim survives `/new`, a
restart and a different session:

```
/goal ship the release      set or replace the goal
/goal                       show the goal and the checklist
/task write the migration   add a task
/task done 2                tick it off
/task rm 2                  remove it
/goal done                  close the goal (all tasks done)
/goal clear                 delete the goal and its tasks
```

The bridge prepends the goal and the list to every turn, with the exact command
that updates it (`goal.mjs`). The agent ticks tasks as it finishes them, and the
next turn sees the new state. The bridge is the only writer of `state.json`: the
agent drops a job file into `goal-jobs/` and the bridge applies it, so there is
no lock race and no lost update.

## Security

- `config.json`, `state.json`, `pending/`, logs are in `.gitignore` and never
  end up in the repository.
- The token is stored in the DSH credentials store, not in code or config.
- The bridge only replies to ids in `allowedUserIds`.

## Documentation

- [docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md](docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md): BotFather settings, group and bot permissions
- [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md): what comes next
- [docs/UX-ANALYSIS.md](docs/UX-ANALYSIS.md): interactive UX review
- [docs/COST.md](docs/COST.md): what one turn costs and how to reduce it
- [docs/CHANGELOG.md](docs/CHANGELOG.md): change history
- [docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md): release readiness criteria

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-qq-bot —— 把 QQ 接到 DSH Agent

> **当前版本 0.11.x**：要求 **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 或更新的 0.2.x 版本**（工具走 `ctx.get('tools')` 注入契约；DSH 0.2.1 系列 rc.2 / rc.3 已实测适配）。
>
> **⚠️ 设置页入口变了**：不再是「设置 → QQ 机器人」，改为在**首页侧边栏打开 插件 → 已安装 → dsh-qq-bot**。
> 配置项与落点（profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`）都没变，**现有配置无需迁移**。
> 0.10 起**一套插件接五种协议**：OneBot 11（默认）/ OneBot 12 / Satori / Milky / QQ 官方机器人，见「三、协议与连接方式」。
> 本仓库就是维护主干 [arrow1031/dsh-qq-bot](https://github.com/arrow1031-dev/dsh-qq-bot)，**已解除封版**：
> 安装跟随 `main`、功能与修复走 PR。需要兼容 DSH 0.1.6 及更早的旧版本（0.6.x）请自行选择早期 tag 下载；
> 早期版本同时想用新功能，请自行处理。

**维护者** [@arrow1031](https://github.com/arrow1031) · **核心贡献者** [@nd002723](https://github.com/nd002723) · **许可** [MIT](LICENSE) · **AI 生成声明** [AI-DISCLOSURE.md](AI-DISCLOSURE.md) · **更新日志** [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

> **⚠️ 行为约定（0.6.8 起沿用，0.8.x 不变）：bot 不自动附带聊天上下文**
>
> 被 @ / 回复 bot 时，不再自动把群内「最近相关发言」硬塞进会话上下文（省 token、上下文更精简）。
> 需要结合群内近期消息/图片作答时，Agent 会**主动调 `qq_history` 工具**拉取（见 [qq_history 小节](#qq_history聊天记录ai-自取)）。
> 可感知影响：bot 对群内前文的「记忆力」取决于模型是否自觉调工具；若群成员觉得 bot 变迟钝，这是**预期行为**而非故障。

一个可以装进 DSH profile 的插件：QQ 消息进来 → 交给 DSH Agent → 回复发回 QQ。

复用现成生态，不自造协议：

```
QQ 客户端 / Koishi / QQ 开放平台
   │ 各家协议（OneBot 11/12、Satori、Milky、官方 API v2）
   ▼
lib/adapters/*.mjs（协议翻译层，零 npm 依赖，独立进程）
   │ stdin/stdout 换行分隔 JSON（契约见 lib/bridge/CONTRACT.md）
   ▼
lib/bridge/（中间表示：一套消息段 + 一套 message 帧）
   ▼
lib/index.js（Cordis 插件入口）
   ├ lib/config.js         Config schema / 默认值 / 深合并
   ├ lib/session.js        建会话、固定命名、访客工具闸
   ├ lib/tools.js          qqbot / qqconfig / qqgroup / qq_websearch / qq_webfetch / qq_imgsearch / qq_draw / qq_history
   ├ lib/admin.js          指令解析与三路权限
   ├ lib/owner-settings.js 拥有者设置通道（白名单 + 两步确认 + 限流 + 审计）
   ├ lib/workspace.js      QQ_msg 工作区根解析
   ├ lib/http.js           fetch + 代理隧道 + 公网地址校验
   ├ lib/websearch.js      多引擎搜索
   ├ lib/imgsearch.js      图床 + 反搜引擎
   ├ lib/imagegen.js       生图（qq_draw）
   └ lib/moli.js           dsh-moli 渲染抓取（可选）
   ▲ 设置面板读写（lib/client.js）  ← 插件面板「插件 → 已安装 → dsh-qq-bot」
   │ sessionController → agent.followup → whenIdle
   ▼
DSH Agent（默认模型 + preset 人格 + 工具）
```

## 一、已验证的东西（不是设计稿）

全部在本机实跑：

| 测试 | 命令 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OneBot 11 正向适配器 | `node test/test-adapter.mjs` | 19/19 |
| OneBot 11 反向适配器 | `node test/test-adapter-reverse.mjs` | 12/12 |
| OneBot 12 适配器 | `node test/test-adapter-onebot12.mjs` | 30/30 |
| Satori 适配器 | `node test/test-adapter-satori.mjs` | 70/70 |
| Milky 适配器 | `node test/test-adapter-milky.mjs` | 79/79 |
| QQ 官方适配器 | `node test/test-adapter-qq-official.mjs` | 87/87 |
| 打包后插件端到端（Host） | `node test/test-plugin.mjs` | 76/76 |
| 客户端设置页 | `node test/test-client.mjs` | 80/80 |
| 权限 · 群管理 · 访客工具闸 | `node test/test-admin.mjs` | 32/32 |
| HTTP / 代理层 | `node test/test-http.mjs` | 17/17 |
| 配置合并与还原 | `node test/test-config.mjs` | 11/11 |
| 多引擎搜索结果解析 | `node test/test-websearch.mjs` | 5/5 |
| 生图引擎 | `node test/test-imagegen.mjs` | 16/16 |
| 会话 id 回退 | `node test/test-session-id.mjs` | 5/5 |
| 运行时兼容自检 | `node test/test-compat.mjs` | 14/14 |
| 历史消息鉴权与定向 | `node test/test-history.mjs` | 23/23 |
| 主动发言 | `node test/test-proactive.mjs` | 49/49 |
| 拥有者设置通道 | `node test/test-owner-settings.mjs` | 58/58 |
| 一键全量 | `node test/run-all.mjs` | **18/18 套件 · 683 项** |
`test-plugin.mjs` 用假 ctx 加载真正的 `lib/index.js` + 真适配器 + 零依赖 OneBot 模拟器，跑通完整链路（无需 DSH / QQ / 网络）。

## 二、快速开始

### 1. 起一个 OneBot 11 实现（推荐 NapCat）

NapCat 官方 Docker 镜像（**支持 amd64 与 arm64**）：

```sh
docker run -d --name napcat --restart=always \
  -e NAPCAT_GID=$(id -g) -e NAPCAT_UID=$(id -u) \
  -p 3000:3000 -p 3001:3001 -p 6099:6099 \
  mlikiowa/napcat-docker:latest
```

- WebUI：`http://<主机IP>:6099/webui`，用手机 QQ 扫码登录；登录 token 默认在 `docker logs napcat` 里。
- 容器内配置目录 `/app/napcat/config`，QQ 数据目录 `/app/.config/QQ`（想固化登录就挂这两个卷）。
- 在 NapCat 的「网络配置」里确认 **OneBot 11**：
  - **HTTP 服务器** `3000` —— 用来发消息
  - **正向 WebSocket** `3001` —— 用来收事件
  - 若设了 `access_token`，记下来填进插件配置
- 端口默认就是 3000/3001，和本插件默认值一致，**不用改代码**。

### 2. 安装插件

本插件**不在 npm 上**，从本仓库或 Release 附件装（维护仓库：<https://github.com/arrow1031-dev/dsh-qq-bot>）。

**方式一：在 DSH 界面里装（推荐）**

在**首页侧边栏打开 插件 → 添加插件**，输入框里填写下面这行包名，确认后等它装完：

```
github:arrow1031-dev/dsh-qq-bot
```

装完**重启 DSH**（桌面版重启应用 / CLI 重启 `dsh web`），
再到 **插件 → 已安装 → dsh-qq-bot** 打开配置面板。

**方式二：命令行装**

```sh
# 跟随 main（已解除封版：升级即最新，不锁 tag）
# 升级已有安装：dsh plugin --profile web update
dsh plugin --profile web add github:arrow1031-dev/dsh-qq-bot

# 本地 tarball（自己改了代码之后）
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-qq-bot-<版本号>.tgz
```

`--profile` 换成你实际在用的 profile：**桌面版是 `--profile desktop`**，`dsh web` 部署一般是 `--profile web`。

`dsh plugin` 本质是 pnpm 的前置封装：装完包后，它会**自动把声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch` 的依赖加入 profile 的层栈**（本包的 package.json 已声明），并连同唯一的运行时依赖 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 一起装上。装完**重启 DSH（桌面版重启应用 / CLI 重启 `dsh web`）**生效。

> **版本要求**：0.11.x 要求 DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2；DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 已实测（见下文「DSH 0.2 兼容」）。

> **升级注意**：`dsh plugin add` 走 pnpm，按 tarball **完整性哈希**缓存——改了代码要打成**新版本号文件名**再装（0.8.0 → 0.8.1），沿用旧名会被判「已最新」跳过。
> `lib/client.js` 是浏览器侧代码，装完重启后还要**刷新浏览器页面**才加载新 bundle。

### 3. 在 QQ 里试

- **群聊**：默认要 **@机器人** 才有反应，`@` 会被去掉再交给 Agent。
  - **回复（引用）机器人的消息**也视同 @ 处理（`reply.botReply`，默认开启），带图照常走识图流程。
  - **需要结合群内近期消息/图片作答时，AI 会主动调 `qq_history` 工具自取**（不再自动硬塞上下文）——识别窗口锚定触发本条回复的那条消息往前 `scopeMessages` 条，最多 `imageLimit` 张图（默认 5/3，设置页可调）。
  - **回复别人 + 正文 @bot**：同样触发（引用回复），上下文同样交给 AI 自取。
  - **bot 被点名时（@ / 回复 bot / 命令前缀 / 管理指令）**：回复统一**引用你的消息**（QQ 引用回复）。
- **私聊**：默认直接回。
- 长回复按换行切成 ≤1200 字多条发送。
- 每个群/每个人是独立的 DSH 会话（id 形如 `qqbot-group-33333`），会落盘并出现在 Web UI 会话列表里，可以像普通会话一样打开继续聊。
- 新会话的**显示名固定为 `群聊_<群号>` / `私聊_<QQ号>`**（`session.fixedName`，默认开启），不再让 LLM 自动起标题；已建会话保持原名。

## 三、协议与连接方式

插件内核不感知协议。设置里选「协议」，适配器会自动切换并重启：

| protocol | 需要的协议端 | 传输 | 备注 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onebot11`（默认） | NapCat / go-cqhttp / Lagrange | 正向/反向 WS + HTTP | 与 0.9 的配置完全兼容 |
| `onebot12` | OneBot 12 实现端 | 正向/反向 WS + HTTP | @ 是 `mention`、回复是 `reply`、图片只有 `file_id` |
| `satori` | Koishi（Satori 服务端） | WS `/v1/events` + HTTP RPC | 消息体是类 XHTML 元素字符串，适配器内置 parser |
| `milky` | NapCat / Yogurt / Lagrange.Milky | `/event` WS + `/api` HTTP | 无 echo；消息 id 是 `message_seq` |
| `qq-official` | QQ 开放平台机器人 | Webhook 或 WS 网关 | AppID/AppSecret 鉴权；群/单聊用 openid |

想加新协议：读 [lib/bridge/CONTRACT.md](lib/bridge/CONTRACT.md)，写一个 stdin/stdout 适配器脚本，
再到 `lib/index.js` 的 `ADAPTER_FILES` 里登记一行。

### OneBot 11/12 的两种连接模式

| 场景 | 用哪个 | 配置 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 协议端和 DSH 在同一台机器/同一容器 | **正向 WS**（默认） | `mode: forward`，我们连 `ws://127.0.0.1:3001` |
| 协议端在别的容器/主机，或网络方向只允许它连出来 | **反向 WS** | `mode: reverse`，我们在 `0.0.0.0:6199` 监听，协议端填 `ws://<DSH主机IP>:6199/` |

反向 WS 的鉴权：请求头 `Authorization: Bearer <token>` 或 URL 上的 `?access_token=<token>` 都接受（后者是因为标准 WebSocket 客户端无法自定义请求头）。

### 其它协议的连接参数（插件设置页同名）

| 协议 | 参数 |
| --- | --- |
| `onebot12` | `protocols.onebot12.{mode,wsUrl,listen,httpUrl,accessToken}` |
| `satori` | `protocols.satori.{wsUrl,httpUrl,token,platform,selfId}` |
| `milky` | `protocols.milky.{wsUrl,httpUrl,accessToken}` |
| `qq-official` | `protocols.qqOfficial.{mode,appId,appSecret,botSecret,listen,path}`；`mode=webhook` 时端口只能 80/443/8080/8443 |

### 各协议的能力边界

- `qq-official`：官方 API **没有**踢人/禁言/改名片这些群管理动作，`qqgroup` 会明确回「不支持」；主动消息受平台配额与被动回复窗口约束。
- `onebot12`：图片段只有 `file_id`，要 URL 得再调 `get_file`；需要视觉识别的场景建议用 OneBot 11。
- `satori` / `milky`：协议层不定义限流，主动发言的节流仍由插件的 `proactive` 配置执行。
## 四、配置

### 方式一：在插件设置页里改（推荐）

> **入口**：在**首页侧边栏打开 插件 → 已安装 → dsh-qq-bot**。
> 这不是原来的「设置 → QQ 机器人」——设置页在 0.11.0 搬进了插件自己的面板。
> **本版要求 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 或更新的 0.2.x 版本。现有配置无需迁移。**

重启 DSH 后面板分四档，字段按功能归位：

| 标签 | 二级标签 | 放什么 |
|---|---|---|
| **连接** | — | 连接方式（OneBot 11 正向 / 反向、OneBot 12、Satori、Milky、QQ 官方）、WS/HTTP 地址、`access_token`、各协议参数 |
| **基本** | 准入与名单 | 群聊 / 私聊开关、@ 要求、白名单、命令前缀、拥有者与高级管理员、访客工具白名单 |
| **基本** | 发言与管理 | 回复策略（分片长度、慢回复提示、来源前缀、@ 回复、上下文头）、群管理指令与可管理群 |
| **能力** | 识图与绘图 | 图片视觉（开关 / provider / model / 最多张数 / 下载超时）、生图（接口地址 / key / 模型 / 重试与轮询） |
| **能力** | 搜索与抓取 | 联网搜索（代理 / 端点 / key）、图片反搜、`qq_webfetch` 与 moli 渲染 |
| **能力** | 对话与人格 | 人格（开关 / 名字 / 设定 / 自定义 preset id）、主动发言（判断用 provider / 模型下拉）、聊天记录读取 |
| **高级** | — | 会话（独立会话、固定命名、preset 与 owner/guest 分流 preset）、逐帧日志、重启退避 |

- 改完点「保存」；**连接方式那几项**（模式/地址/token）保存后会自动重启适配器，其它项下一条消息生效。
- 类型映射：布尔是勾选框；白名单是逗号分隔的文本框；连接方式是下拉框。
- **配置落点（本插件要求 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 起）**：插件把自己的 `Config` schema 交给 DSH 当设置表单，界面上的改动由 DSH
  写进 **profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`**（也就是下面「方式二」里那个文件）；0.1.6 时代的独立
  `settings.yaml` 文档已经不存在了。
- 设置命名空间就是**条目 id**（默认 `dsh-qq-bot`）；条目被改名时，客户端会回退匹配「以 qq-bot 结尾」的那个命名空间。
- 连接状态不在插件面板里显示，在对话里让 Agent 调用 `qqbot` 工具（`action=status`）看。
- `access_token` 是**只写**字段：已设置时页面显示「已设置；留空则保持不变」，只有输入新值才会覆盖。
  Host 侧把它声明成 schema 的 secret，值不会下发到浏览器，保存时也不会被空值清掉。

### 工作区（自动管理，无需配置）

Agent 会话的工作目录**不需要任何配置**：插件读取 DSH 官方默认 Workspace 的位置
（`<系统 Documents>/deepseek-harness`），在它的同级目录自动创建 `QQ_msg` 作为工作区根，
并注册为 DSH workspace——**Web UI 会话侧栏的「QQ 消息」分组**，新 QQ 会话自动归入该分组：

- Windows：`C:\Users\<用户名>\Documents\deepseek-harness\QQ_msg`
- Linux / macOS：`~/Documents/deepseek-harness/QQ_msg`（系统没有 Documents 目录时退到 `~/deepseek-harness/QQ_msg`）

带图消息的原图缓存放在 `QQ_msg/qq-images/<会话id>/`，**会话结算后自动删除该缓存**，
会话与工作区本身保留。旧的 `workspace` 配置项已废弃移除。

### 方式二：改 composition 行配置（当 base 层用）

**不要改包内的 `cordis.patch.yml`**（升级会覆盖）。写进你自己的
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` —— 它在所有 bundle 之后应用，按 id 定向覆盖：

```yaml
    onebot:

      enabled: true
      manageGroups: []            # 可管理的群；空 = 回退用 group.allow
      requireGroupAdmin: true     # 是否承认「本群管理员」这一路权限

      dryRun: false               # true = 只回复将执行什么
      allowConsole: false         # 允许 Web UI 会话直接调用管理工具
    session:

    proactive:                    # 主动发言（可选，默认关）
      enabled: false              # 打开且下面列了群号才生效
      groups: []                  # 生效群号；留空 = 不启用

      maxPerDay: 8                # 每天上限
      minGapMinutes: 15           # 两次发言最小间隔

      provider: ''                # 留空 = 跟随群会话模型（走 DSH 已配置的渠道，零密钥）

      enabled: false              # 打开后 AI 才能画图

      apiKeyEnv: IMAGE_API_KEY
      model: seedream-5.0-lite
      size: 1024x1024
      timeoutMs: 180000          # 单次请求超时
      maxAttempts: 4             # 失败重试次数（含首次；429/5xx/网络/空结果）
      retryIntervalMs: 5000
      poll: true                 # 供应商返回 task_id 时继续轮询
      pollIntervalMs: 5000
      maxPolls: 30
    persona:                      # 自定义人格：每个新会话第一轮附一次
      enabled: false
      name: ''
      text: ''
    agentPresetCustom: ''         # 自定义 preset id（如 qq）；非空时优先于 agentPreset
    imgSearch:                    # qq_imgsearch 图片反搜
      enabled: true               # 默认开；关闭后工具返回「已关闭」
      maxResults: 5               # 每次反搜最多返回结果数
      saucenaoKey: ''             # SauceNAO API key（saucenao.com 注册可得）；留空不启用
      weightedShuffle: false      # 有代理时按体量权重随机重排引擎顺序（避免固定引擎一直打头）
                                  # 请求全走上方 webSearch.proxy：无代理 = 直连引擎按可用性优先
                                  # （TraceMoe → IQDB）；有代理 = 放开全部可用引擎按用户体量优先
                                  # （Yandex → Tineye → Copyseeker → SauceNAO → IQDB → TraceMoe）
```

`agentPreset` 是换人格的正规做法：给 QQ 机器人做一个专属 preset，把 id 填进来。

### 图片视觉（vision）

收到图片时用视觉模型识别并并入 Agent 输入（原图缓存到 `<QQ_msg>/qq-images/<会话id>/`，会话结算后删除）。
`provider` / `model` 留空 = 会话模型；也可以给视觉单独指定 provider / model。

**官方视觉模型（DeepSeek API）**：`deepseek-flash` 接受图片与文本（OpenAI 兼容，base64 data URL 或图片 URL 均可，支持 JPEG / PNG / GIF / WebP）。
旧的 `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` 名字**已退役**，但请求仍被接受（由最新 Flash 服务）。见 [DeepSeek Vision 文档](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/vision/)。

其它 OpenAI 兼容通道：选一个在 DSH providers 里声明了 `input: [text, image]` 的模型即可；
注意 `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` 这类默认模型实测**不真正支持图片**（图不进上下文、会编造解释），换视觉模型时务必确认声明了图片输入。

## 五、权限与群管理

权限是**三路并行取并集**（不是"先命中先返回"）：

| 路径 | 谁 | 能做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 静态名单 `auth.owners` | 拥有者 | 全部权限 + **永久授权** + 可走独立的拥有者会话 |
| 静态名单 `auth.superAdmins` | 后台设定的高级管理员 | 群管理权限（**不能**永久授权） |
| 动态授权 | 被临时授权的人 | 仅被授予的那几项，**仅限本群**、带时限 |
| 本群身份 | 该群的 admin / owner | 群管理权限（可用 `admin.requireGroupAdmin` 关掉这一路） |

任一路给到某项权限即拥有它；来源会在 `/whoami`、`/perms` 里如实列出，便于排查"他为什么有权"。

权限项：`query`（查询）、`mute`（禁言）、`kick`（踢人）、`recall`（撤回）、`settings`（群名/名片/管理员/全员禁言）、`grant`（给本群成员授权），拥有者另有 `permanent`（永久授权）。

### 动态授权（群维度，不可跨群）

- 拥有者或**本群管理员**可以给本群成员临时授权：`/grant @某人 mute 30`（30 分钟）
- 只有**拥有者**能永久授权：`/grant @某人 kick forever`（非拥有者发这条会被拒）
- 群管理员单次最长 `auth.grantMaxTtlMinutes`（默认 1440 分钟）
- 授权键是「群号 + QQ 号」：**在 A 群授的权，在 B 群一律无效**
- `/revoke @某人 [权限]` 撤销、`/grants` 列出本群全部授权

### 非拥有者不使用 DSH 内部功能：执行级工具闸

用一个 `tools.guard` 硬闸，**只在建会话时注册一次**，判据是闭包里的可变标志位：

- 注册在 `agent.ctx` 上 → 只作用于该会话的 agent
- 每次工具执行时才求值 → 拥有者/访客交替说话**不需要增删限制**
- 用**白名单**（`auth.guestToolAllow`，默认 `qqbot,qqgroup,qq_websearch,qq_webfetch,qq_imgsearch,qq_history`）→ `run_code`（PTC 保留传输）这类"不在全局层"的特殊工具也会被自动挡住；访客联网统一走 `qq_websearch`（搜索）与 `qq_webfetch`（抓网页），DSH 自带的 `web_fetch` 已从默认白名单移除
- 被拦时返回拒绝原因，模型会把它转达给用户（最多多一次"被拒绝的调用"往返）

因此它同时满足：**0 额外 token**（不注入提示词、不改工具表、不记 `request/header`）、**单会话单历史**、**不改 DSH 本身**。

想放开就设 `auth.guestDshTools: true`（不建议）。

> 为什么不用"每条消息增删 `tools.restrict`"：`restrict` 是静态过滤器，想按说话人变就得反复增删，工具面抖动会让 agent loop 多记 `request/header`，反而更费 token、代码也更多。guard 是每次执行才求值的函数，配一个可变标志位就够。

### 会话分流（可选，**仅供人格分离**）

`auth.ownerPreset` / `auth.guestPreset` 都留空时，拥有者与非拥有者**共用一条会话**（默认，也是推荐）。填了 preset id 才分成两条：

- 拥有者走 `qqbot-group-<群号>`，挂 `ownerPreset`
- 非拥有者走 `...-guest`，挂 `guestPreset`

**这只是换人格，不是安全边界**——工具隔离由上面的 `guard` 负责。分流要付代价：同一个群会有两条历史，拥有者看不到访客说了什么。除非确实要给访客不同的说话风格，否则别开。

全局 `agentPreset`（设置页下拉：部署默认 / standard / ptc / minimal / cordis）决定**新会话**用什么 preset，已建会话不变；分流时某方 preset 留空会自动回落 `agentPreset`。

上下文头会带身份，例如 `[QQ群 33333 · 小明(22222) · 身份:访客｜本群管理员+动态授权[mute 至 ...]]`，让 Agent 自己决定怎么对待这个请求。

### 指令的严格性（防"聊天内容夹带指令样内容"被误执行）

1. 前缀必须位于**消息首位**（前面只允许空白）——`你好 /mute @x` 不会被当成指令
2. 动词必须完全匹配已知指令，未知动词照常交给模型
3. token 数量必须落在该指令声明的 `[min,max]` 内，**多余内容判为用法错误、不执行**
4. 权限不足直接拒绝，且不做任何动作

指令**不需要 @ 机器人**（刻意放在 `requireAt` 之前），但上述规则一条都不放宽。

### 指令表

| 指令 | 权限 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/help` | — | 列出全部指令 |
| `/whoami` | — | 看我在本群的身份与权限来源 |
| `/perms [@某人]` | query | 看某人在本群的权限来源（三路） |
| `/grants` | grant | 列出本群的动态授权 |
| `/grant @某人 权限[,权限] [分钟\|forever]` | grant | 临时授权（仅本群） |
| `/revoke @某人 [权限]` | grant | 撤销授权 |
| `/members` | query | 成员列表（最多列 30 条） |
| `/info` | query | 群信息 |
| `/mute @某人 [分钟=10]` | mute | 禁言（0 = 解禁） |
| `/unmute @某人` | mute | 解除禁言 |
| `/kick @某人` | kick | 移出本群 |
| `/recall [消息id]` | recall | 撤回；**回复某条消息再发 `/recall` 可省略 id** |
| `/banall on\|off` | settings | 全员禁言开关 |
| `/card @某人 新名片` | settings | 改群名片 |
| `/admin @某人 on\|off` | settings | 设/撤管理员 |
| `/rename 新群名` | settings | 改群名 |

### Agent 工具（与指令共用同一套鉴权）

`qqgroup` 的 `action`：只读 `group-list`/`group-info`/`member-list`/`member-info`，写操作 `mute`/`unmute`/`kick`/`whole-ban`/`set-card`/`set-admin`/`rename`/`recall`/`poke`。

工具的"说话人"取自**本会话最近一条消息**，所以群里普通成员没法靠一句话驱动管理动作——这一点是提示注入的主要防线。`group_id` 留空时默认用当前会话所在的群。

### 群事件

适配器会把完整事件字段透传上来（`operator_id` 谁操作的、`duration` 禁言时长、`target_id`、`card`，以及被引用消息的 `reply_to`）。当前版本只做透传与计数（`qqbot status` 里能看到），**自动治理尚未实现**。

### 建议的上线顺序

1. 在设置里填 `auth.owners`（至少填自己）
2. 打开 `admin.dryRun`，在群里发几条指令确认解析与回执
3. 关掉 dryRun，再按需加 `auth.superAdmins`
4. 非拥有者用 DSH 功能由**访客工具闸默认拦截**，无需额外配置；确实想放开再改 `auth.guestDshTools`

## 六、Agent 能用的工具

插件向 DSH 注册 8 个工具（访客只能看到 `auth.guestToolAllow` 里的那几个）。先看通用的 `qqbot`：

- `{action:'status'}` —— 连接状态、模式、适配器 pid/端口、各 QQ 会话的回合数、统计计数
- `{action:'send', message_type:'group'|'private', target_id:'123', text:'...', image?}` —— 主动发一条 QQ 消息；`image` 传本地图片绝对路径（**只允许 `<QQ_msg>/qq-images` 目录内**），插件转 base64 后与文本一起发出，用于「发自拍 / 自画像 / 刚生成的图」这类场景。
- `{action:'interrupt', conversation:'group-123'|'all'}` —— 中断正在跑的回合

### qq_websearch（联网搜索）

访客白名单内可直接调用：

- `{query, max_uses?}` —— 按关键词搜索，返回 `{ok, count, sources, text}`；后端走**多引擎组合搜索**（`multiEngine` 默认开）：Tavily（配 `TAVILY_API_KEY` 才启用，环境变量或 DSH 凭据 refs）→ DuckDuckGo（html→lite，串行 + 限流记忆）→ Yandex / Bing / Wikipedia 并发兜底、聚合去重（相关性闸门防无关链接）；关闭 `multiEngine` 则落回官方 DeepSeek web_search。抓取网页请用 `qq_webfetch`。

搜索请求都走 `webSearch.proxy`（非空时经 HTTP CONNECT 隧道 + TLS，含境内/境外分流；留空直连）。`webSearch` 配置段：代理 / 端点 / key 环境变量名（默认 `DEEPSEEK_BALANCE_API_KEY`，自动读 DSH 凭据服务）/ 每次最多触发次数 / 多引擎开关（默认开）。

### qq_webfetch（抓取网页）

访客白名单内可直接调用：

- `{url, max_chars?}` —— 抓取指定网页原文/渲染文本（http/https，仅公网），返回 `{ok, url, status|via, text}`；请求受 `webSearch.proxy` 管控（留空直连、非空走 HTTP CONNECT 隧道），抓取前校验目标为公网 IP，内网/回环/私有地址一律拒绝（防经代理扫内网）。
- 配置 `moli.enabled`（默认关）后改用 **Moli 无头浏览器渲染抓取**（可抓 SPA/JS 渲染页）；代理自动透传 `webSearch.proxy`（可被 `moli.proxy` 覆盖）；未检测到 moli 引擎时开关无效，工具返回 `moliUnavailable` 明确报错。

### qq_imgsearch（图片反搜）

访客白名单内可直接调用：

- `{url, max_results?}` 或 `{file, max_results?}` —— 给定**公网图片 URL** 或**本地图片文件路径**，返回 `{ok, count, sources, via, text}`；来源带 `url/title/snippet`。
- **本地文件流程**：先上传图床（`zixiaoyun/scdn/uguu` 三床按实测质量**加权随机**排优先度，依次试到第一个成功，一律走 `webSearch.proxy` 管控）拿公网 URL → 再反搜；**上传失败回退**：不经过图床、直接把文件发给 TraceMoe（文件直传搜图）。`file` 路径限 `qq-images` 目录内（访客不能读任意文件）。

引擎组合（全部请求走 `webSearch.proxy`，与 `qq_websearch` 同一套代理管控，本插件独立实现）：

- **无代理**（留空直连）：按**可用性优先** —— TraceMoe（动画截图识别，URL 模式 JSON，直连最快）→ IQDB（ACG 图库）→（有 key 时 SauceNAO）→ Soutubot
- **有代理**：**放开全部可用引擎按用户体量优先** —— Yandex（全球搜索引擎）→ Tineye（全球图片搜索）→ Copyseeker（聚合，结果最多）→（有 key 时 SauceNAO）→ Soutubot（搜图Bot酱，多库：pixiv/danbooru/gelbooru 等）→ IQDB → TraceMoe；聚合去重，cap 满即停，单引擎失败自动继续下一引擎。
- 开启 `imgSearch.weightedShuffle` 后，有代理时按**体量权重随机重排**（Yandex/Tineye/Copyseeker 权重 30/25/25，SauceNAO 15，Soutubot 8，IQDB/TraceMoe 5）：体量大引擎大概率先跑，但顺序每次不同，避免固定引擎一直打头。
- **Soutubot**（soutubot.moe，开源 imsearch）：API 只收文件 → 引擎先下载图片（二进制走代理）再上传 `/api/search` 拿 `result_id` → 查 `/api/results` 多库结果（pixiv 直链 / danbooru / gelbooru / zerochan 镜像 + 画师/角色标签）。
- **`kind=comic` 漫画模式**（`qq_imgsearch` 参数）：漫画/本子截图优先 **Soutubot → SauceNAO（有 key）→ IQDB → TraceMoe**（无代理同链），有代理时再 Yandex/Tineye/Copyseeker 兜底；`weightedShuffle` 开启时漫画权重 Soutubot 40 / SauceNAO 30 / IQDB 20 / TraceMoe 10 / 通用 5。**`kind=comic` + 本地文件（`file`）时不上图床**：Soutubot 直接传文件（soutubot API 只收文件），失败/无结果回退 TraceMoe 文件直传。

引擎实测（2026-10，PicImageSearch 图床 URL 全矩阵交叉验证）：直连可用 TraceMoe / IQDB / Soutubot；代理可用 Copyseeker（184 条）/ Yandex（15 条）/ Tineye（图床新图未收录时 0 条，收录后正常）；SauceNAO 需 `saucenaoKey`；其余（ascii2d / anime_trace / bing / google_lens / ehentai）不可用。`imgSearch` 配置段：`enabled`（默认开）/ `maxResults`（默认 5）/ `saucenaoKey` / `weightedShuffle`。

### qq_history（聊天记录，AI 自取）

访客白名单内可直接调用（群聊里被 @ 或需要结合群内近期消息/图片作答时，Agent 会主动调它）：

- `{group_id?, user_id?, count?, with_images?}` —— 拉取当前群最近消息，返回 `{ok, group_id, messages:[{time, user_id, nickname, text, images:[{url, description}]}]}`；`group_id` 默认当前群，`user_id` 可只筛某人的发言，`count` 默认 20、上限 50，`with_images` 默认开。
- **识别窗口锚定「最新提及」**：只对触发本条回复的那条消息（@ bot / 回复 bot / 命令前缀）**往前 `scopeMessages` 条**（默认 5）内的图片做识别，最多 `imageLimit` 张（默认 3，最近的优先）；更早的 @ 不锚定、其附近图片不因「也是被提及」而识别，避免重复拉取/重复识图。
- 窗口内图片用插件的视觉链路识别（下载 + `askVision`），返回 URL + 描述；识别失败只给 URL 不阻塞。配置见 `history` 段（`scopeMessages` / `imageLimit`）。

### qq_draw（生图，可直接发到 QQ）

在 插件 → 已安装 → dsh-qq-bot → 能力 → 识图与绘图 里填好接口后，AI 就能按描述画图：

- `{prompt, model?, size?, reference?, caption?, send?}` —— `prompt` 越具体越好；`reference` 可给公网 URL 或 `qq-images` 下的本地图（保持同一形象做「自拍」）；
  `send` 默认 true，直接把图画成 QQ 图片段发到当前会话，`caption` 是随图发的文字。
- 失败策略：`429 / 5xx / 网络错 / 空结果` 按 `retryIntervalMs` 重试到 `maxAttempts`；`4xx`（参数错、额度不足）直接报错、不重试。
- 异步供应商：响应里是 `task_id` 时按 `pollIntervalMs` 轮询（依次试 `.../images/generations/<id>`、`.../images/tasks/<id>`、`.../tasks/<id>`），最多 `maxPolls` 次；关掉 `poll` 就只尝试一次。
- 图片落盘：`<QQ_msg>/qq-images/gen/`；`qq_draw` 不在访客默认白名单（会花钱），要放开就自己加到 `auth.guestToolAllow`。
- 接口约定：OpenAI 兼容 `POST <baseUrl>/images/generations`，请求体 `{model, prompt, n:1, size?, image?}`，返回 `data[0].url` 或 `data[0].b64_json`（实测 `seedream-5.0-lite` 返回 url、约 40 秒）。

### 人格（人设）也在设置里换

两种做法，互不冲突：

- **自定义人格**：设置页「自定义人格」开关 + 名字 + 设定，开一次管所有新会话（第一轮末尾附一次身份设定，零额外 token）；已建会话不变，想立刻生效就删掉旧会话重开。
- **整档 preset**：`Agent preset` 下拉选内置 standard / ptc / minimal / cordis；自建 preset（例如 `qq`）填进「自定义 agent preset id」，非空时优先生效——这条路换的不只是人格，还有工具面。

### web_fetch（抓公网原文，仅拥有者）

DSH 自带的 `web_fetch` 工具仍然注册，但**已从访客默认白名单移除**——访客要抓原文请用 `qq_webfetch`（走 `webSearch.proxy` 代理、同样带公网 IP 过滤，`moli.enabled` 时可改用 Moli 渲染）。`web_fetch` 本身只允许公网 IP，内网/回环地址由 DSH 直接拒绝；拥有者不受访客白名单限制，照常可用。

### qqgroup（群管理）

见「五、权限与群管理」一节。工具路径的授权依据是「当前会话最近一条消息是否来自管理员白名单」。

### qqconfig（拥有者专用：在 QQ 里改设置）

0.10 起。让**拥有者本人在私聊里**直接改一部分插件设置，不用去翻 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`：

- `{action:'show'}` —— 列出可改项、当前值和配置修订号
- `{action:'propose', path:'group.allow', value:'[\"488136808\"]'}` —— **只校验不写盘**，返回改动预览与一次性 `token`
- `{action:'apply', token:'...'}` —— 凭 token 真正落盘
- `{action:'cancel', token:'...'}` —— 撤销预约

可改的是一组白名单字段：群/私聊开关与白名单、命令前缀、群管理开关、主动发言参数、图片识别、人设。
密钥、`onebot.*`、`auth.*`（拥有者名单）、模型名这类**改不了**——机器人无法借这条通道给自己扩权。

写盘要过三道：**只能是拥有者本人在私聊里**（身份取自当前会话发言人，不接受参数）→ `propose` 只生成 300 秒有效的一次性确认码 →
`apply` 时若配置已被别处改过就作废。落盘只走 DSH settings 服务（schema 校验 + 原子写 + 热重载），不手改 YAML；
另有每小时 6 次 / 每天 30 次的限流与 `QQ_msg/qqbot-config-audit.jsonl` 审计。完整威胁模型见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

总开关 `auth.ownerSettings`（默认开），关掉后全部动作拒绝。

## 七、排错

| 现象 | 检查 |
| --- | --- |
| 日志一直「OneBot 未连接」 | NapCat 的「正向 WebSocket」是否开在 `onebot.wsUrl`；reverse 模式下 NapCat 是否指向了 `ws://<DSH>:6199/`；防火墙；token 是否一致 |
| 能连上但收不到消息 | OneBot 版本要选 **v11**；不能只开 HTTP，必须开正向或反向 WS |
| 群里 @ 了也不回 | `group.enabled`；`group.allow` 白名单；`self_id` 与消息里的 `self_id` 是否一致（`logAdapterFrames: true` 能看到原始帧） |
| 回「（本轮没有产生文字回复：...）」 | 括号里是从会话日志读出的 `turn/end` 原因，据此定位（模型路由、额度、工具报错等） |
| 发送失败 | NapCat 的 HTTP 服务器（默认 3000）是否开着；`accessToken`；看日志里的「发送失败」 |
| 日志在哪 | 插件前缀 `[dsh-qq-bot]`，适配器前缀 `[dsh-qq-bot]/adapter`，都打到 DSH Host 的 stdout |

## 八、无 QQ 号自测


**先装依赖**（`Config` schema 需要 schemastery）：

```sh
npm install
```

装好之后裸克隆即可运行：需要 DSH 运行时才能成立的少数断言（动态工具注册、qqgroup 工具路径）
会自动跳过，而不是判失败；想看全，把 `DSH_PROFILE_MODULES` 指向一个装了 DSH 运行时的 profile 的
`node_modules`。
整套 **628 项**（18 个套件）：

```sh
npm test
```

或分开跑：

```sh
# 协议适配器回归（每家一个套件，全部用本地假协议端）
node test/test-adapter.mjs              # OneBot 11 正向（19 项）
node test/test-adapter-reverse.mjs      # OneBot 11 反向（12 项）
node test/test-adapter-onebot12.mjs     # OneBot 12（30 项）
node test/test-adapter-satori.mjs       # Satori（70 项）
node test/test-adapter-milky.mjs        # Milky（79 项）
node test/test-adapter-qq-official.mjs  # QQ 官方（87 项）

# 插件本体（假 ctx + 真适配器 + 假协议端）
node test/test-plugin.mjs     # Host 半边（76 项，含 Config 契约与热更新）
node test/test-client.mjs     # 客户端设置页（80 项）
node test/test-admin.mjs      # 权限·群管理·访客工具闸（32 项）
node test/test-http.mjs       # HTTP / 代理隧道（17 项）
node test/test-config.mjs     # 配置合并与还原（11 项）
node test/test-websearch.mjs  # 多引擎搜索结果解析（5 项）
node test/test-imagegen.mjs   # 生图引擎：重试 / 轮询 / 响应解析（16 项）
node test/test-session-id.mjs # 会话 id 回退（5 项）
node test/test-compat.mjs     # 运行时兼容自检（14 项）
```

也可以手动拿假 OneBot 试（端口正好是 NapCat 默认值）：

```sh
node test/mock-onebot.mjs --http-port 3000 --ws-port 3001
# 另开一个终端，伪造一条 @机器人的群消息
node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/__inject',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({message_type:'group',group_id:33333,user_id:22222,nickname:'小明',message:[{type:'at',data:{qq:'10000'}},{type:'text',data:{text:'你好'}}]})}).then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log)"
# 看机器人回了什么
node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/__sent').then(r=>r.json()).then(j=>console.log(JSON.stringify(j.messages,null,2)))"
```


## 九、关于 AstrBot

AstrBot 是 OneBot 的**消费方**（内置 aiocqhttp 反向 WS 服务端），和本插件角色重叠。
用 DSH 当大脑就别再接 AstrBot，否则同一条消息会被两个大脑各回一次。
对端只要是「OneBot 11 实现」（NapCat / OneDisc / Lagrange / LLOneBot 等）就行。

## 十、在手机容器里跑 NapCat 的注意事项

- NapCat 官方镜像有 **arm64** 版本，所以理论上能在 arm64 容器里跑；但容器里再跑 Docker 通常需要 privileged 权限，不一定允许。
- 备选：不用 Docker，直接在容器里跑 NapCat.Shell（需要对应的 Linux QQ + NapCat 版本）。
- 同容器时用 **forward 模式**连 `127.0.0.1:3001` 最省事；如果 NapCat 在别的容器，用 **reverse 模式**，让 NapCat 连到 `ws://<DSH主机IP>:6199/`。
- 端口 6099 是 NapCat 的 WebUI（扫码登录用），**不要暴露到公网**。

# dsh-git-graph-sidebar

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A Git browsing plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a branch chip in the composer, plus a **Repository graph** tab inside [dsh-better-sidebar](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-better-sidebar) that lists the Git repositories found up to three levels below the current workspace directory and draws the selected repository's commit graph as an SVG lane canvas.

![Repository graph tab, dark theme](assets/shot-dark.png)

## What it does

### Repository graph tab (better-sidebar)

The tab works from the session's working directory and treats that directory as a container: Git repositories up to three levels below it are reachable without registering each repository as a separate DSH workspace.

- **Multi-repository discovery** — the workspace root itself, plus repositories nested up to 3 levels below it. Each entry carries its current branch, short head, dirty-file count and conflict count.
- **A scan that costs what it should** — one `git for-each-ref` per repository returns the branch time, the upstream and the ahead/behind distance in one call; while the refs have not moved the whole answer comes from the last scan, and only the status probe (dirty files, conflicts) is repeated. A workspace full of repositories no longer gets slower with every extra one.
- **Repository tree** — the root, the intermediate directories and each repository, so the level relationship between them is visible rather than implied by a path.
- **SVG commit graph** — one row per commit, one colored lane per branch line, curved edges where a commit's parent sits on another lane, merge commits drawn as diamonds, ref badges and relative timestamps.
- **Zoom** — rows are two lines by default; `−` / `+` scale the rows and their text from a compact single line up to a roomy list.
- **Commit detail card** — the panel under the graph always shows the row you pinned: full hash, subject, author, absolute commit time, refs and parents. Click a row to pin it, click it again (or `×`) to clear.
- **Copy for the assistant** — *Copy commit info* puts a ready-to-paste block on the clipboard (repository path, hash, subject, author, time, refs, parents), so asking the model to "roll back to this commit" needs no retyping; *Copy SHA* copies the full hash alone.
- **Export an image** — *Export image* on the toolbar serialises the current view (filtered rows, lanes, ref chips, the highlight on the pinned row) into one standalone SVG: theme colours baked in, explicit size, downloaded as `git-graph-<repo>.svg`; environments without Blob/object URLs fall back to copying the markup.
- **Live updates, no flicker** — the tab subscribes to the host's Git change events and also polls quietly in the background, so a new commit or branch appears on its own. Every background refresh keeps the current rows on screen: an unchanged result is dropped without a re-render, and a failed poll never replaces real data with an error.
- **Refresh** — re-scans on demand. A manual refresh also keeps the panel content visible while it runs. The host caches a scan for 60 s (the refresh button bypasses it).
- **Reopens instantly** — closing and reopening the tab used to start from an empty panel. The tab now keeps the last painted list, selection and graph in memory, so a reopen draws that on its first frame and refreshes behind it.
- **Selected repository is obvious** — the active row in the repository tree is highlighted with a cyan tint and ring, so the repository whose graph is on screen is never ambiguous.
- **Git conventions** — a strip above the graph states which convention document the selected repository carries (`draft` / `settled` / missing), opens it in the editor, and offers six proven frameworks to bootstrap a brand-new repository.
- **One-click repository init** — a workspace directory that is not a repository yet gets an *Initialize Git repository* button. It asks once (target path and initial branch: `main` / `master` / `trunk` / `develop`), runs `git init -b <branch>` there, and then the conventions scaffold and framework picker open by themselves. It refuses when the directory already sits inside a repository, so it can never re-root an existing checkout.

- **The rules in force, at a glance** — the conventions strip lists the checkable rules the document itself states as small chips: `type: feat / fix / docs`, `subject ≤ 72`, `lowercase start`, `no trailing period`, `imperative`, plus `Chinese` / `English` / `Chinese + English` when the document names a subject language, and an amber *Strict* chip for a strict document. What you see is exactly what the agent is told. It does **not** tally commits that are already written: nothing in the panel can change them, so a count would be noise. A document with no checkable rule says so instead of guessing.
- **Upgrade preview** — on a repository that already carries a document, *Switch framework* no longer overwrites it: the tab first shows *What would change* — how many sections are added, rewritten or removed, with the titles — and nothing is written until *Write it* is pressed. *Cancel* leaves the file untouched.
- **Workspace document** — once the workspace holds more than one repository a *Workspace conventions* strip appears under the toolbar and writes `<workspace>/.dsh/GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` in one click; a repository without its own document inherits it and the injected block names the directory it came from.
- **Strict mode** — the picker used for a new document, a framework switch and the workspace document carries a *Strict* switch: it writes `strict: true`, and the injected block then tells the agent to rewrite an offending message before committing; the conventions strip shows a *Strict* badge. The list collapses as soon as a card is picked. A switch clicked on an existing document is stored right away, so the list always shows what the document says.
- **The workspace document reaches the prompt** — when the session sits in a container that is not a repository, the content of `<workspace>/.dsh/GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` (strict flag, subject language, machine-checkable rules and the body) goes into the injected block, followed by the index of the repositories below it.
- **Subject language** — the framework list carries one more row: Chinese, English or a mix. The choice lands in the document as `language: zh|en|mixed`, and the injected block repeats it as a single `Subject language: …` line; a Chinese subject under an English-only document is flagged, and the other way round, while a mixed document is judged by the other rules alone. A document without `language:` checks no language at all.
- **Chinese, English and mixed subjects** — compliance accepts all three: `新增` / `修复` / `文档` work as type aliases (so does a full-width colon), and the lowercase and imperative checks only run when the first word is Latin, so Chinese subjects are never flagged for case.

### Branch chip (composer)

The chip that ships with the upstream plugin is unchanged: on a blank conversation it lets you switch or create a branch, and it opens the interactive commit-graph dialog and the worktree manager. Branch operations run in the host process; the chip hides itself on active sessions.

## Requirements

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node (host runtime) | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| `dsh-better-sidebar` | needed **for the tab only** — without it the plugin still loads and the chip keeps working |

## Install

Grab the prebuilt bundle from the [latest release](https://github.com/Athosoo/dsh-git-graph-sidebar/releases/latest) — `dsh-git-graph-sidebar.tgz`, no build step needed — then install it as a plugin bundle:

- **Desktop app (the `desktop` profile is owned by the Electron app, so the CLI refuses it):** install the `.tgz` from the app's plugin page.
- **CLI-managed profile:**

  ```sh
  dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Athosoo/dsh-git-graph-sidebar
  # or from the downloaded tarball
  dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-git-graph-sidebar.tgz
  ```

**Restart DSH after installing.** The host half registers its `/git/*` HTTP routes at startup, so a page refresh alone is not enough for a first install, and an upgraded build is not picked up until the process restarts.

The tab needs [`dsh-better-sidebar`](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) installed; without it everything else — the branch chip, the graph dialog, worktrees — keeps working and only the sidebar tab is absent.

## Repository discovery rules

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scan depth | 3 levels below the working directory (a repository found at a level is not descended into) |
| Upper bound | 200 repositories per scan, then the result is flagged as truncated |
| Skipped directory names | `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `coverage`, `target`, `vendor` — plus every dot-directory |
| Repository marker | a `.git` entry (directory, file or symlink — so worktrees and submodules are both detected) |
| Per-entry status budget | 5 s; an entry whose `git status` did not return in time is still listed, without branch metadata |
| Cache | 60 s per base path, shared between concurrent requests; the tab's refresh button bypasses it |

## Git conventions

A commit graph shows what happened; a conventions document records what the team agreed to do next time. The tab can bootstrap that document for every repository it lists.

- **Bring your own document** — the plugin never invents house rules. It writes an empty scaffold with six sections marked `待定` / *to decide* and `status: draft`, so the team fills in the decisions instead of inheriting someone else's defaults.

- **Triggered by a new repository** — a repository that has no document and no commits yet (`unborn HEAD`) gets the empty scaffold automatically, and the framework picker opens right away. Repositories that already contain commits but no document are listed as missing it; one click writes the scaffold.

- **Six proven frameworks** — picking one writes its full template into the document and flips it to `status: settled`:

  | Framework | Best for |
  | --- | --- |
  | Conventional Commits | changelogs and semantic versions generated from commit messages |
  | GitHub Flow | small teams shipping from `main` with short-lived feature branches |
  | Git Flow | versioned releases promoted across several environments |
  | Trunk-based development | continuous delivery with very short-lived branches |
  | Conventional Branch | branch names that encode type and issue reference |
  | GitLab Flow | explicit environment branches between `main` and production |

- **Never overwrites** — an existing document is only replaced when the request carries `force`, which the UI does not offer for settled documents. The document is plain Markdown in the repository root, so it is reviewed and revised like any other source file.
- **The assistant actually reads it** — the host registers a `systemPrompt` section that is assembled before *every* model step, so the running agent is always told where the document is for the session's repository and gets its rules (up to 3 000 characters) inline. Nothing is injected for a workspace where no repository documents anything, and the text is cached per file mtime, so a step never re-reads an unchanged file.
- **The nearest document wins** — the section resolves the document in three steps: the repository the session directory is in, then the nearest enclosing repository (a monorepo container), then an index of the documented repositories below it. An inherited document is labelled `inherited Git conventions` and names the repository it came from, so an agent inside `packages/api` follows the container's rules until `packages/api` writes its own. The index walks up to three levels down, skipping dot directories and `node_modules`.

## Initializing a repository

A workspace does not have to start as a repository. When the root of the workspace is not one, the tab's toolbar offers **Initialize Git repository** (and a workspace with no repositories at all shows the same button in the empty panel).

- **Two steps, never one click** — the button opens a bar that names the target directory and the initial branch before anything is written.
- **Only `.git` is written** — `git init` creates the metadata directory; no file in the workspace is touched, and existing repositories below the workspace are unaffected.
- **It refuses to nest** — if the directory already sits inside a repository (including a parent outside the workspace), the host answers `already-repository` instead of creating a second root inside it.
- **It hands over to the conventions flow** — because the new repository has no commits yet, the empty conventions document is scaffolded and the framework picker opens immediately, so the first commit already follows an agreed rule set.

## HTTP routes

Registered by the host half under `/git`; all of them answer JSON (`{ok:true,value}` / `{ok:false,error}`), except `/git/events`, which is a server-sent event stream.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/git/repos` | multi-repository discovery for a path (`{path, refresh?}`) |
| `/git/status` | branch, head, dirty/untracked/conflict counts |
| `/git/branches` | branch list with the current one marked |
| `/git/graph` | commit list with parents and refs (`{path, limit?}`) |
| `/git/switch` | switch branch |
| `/git/create-branch` | create and switch |
| `/git/worktrees` | worktree list |
| `/git/worktree-add` | create a worktree |
| `/git/worktree-remove` | remove a worktree |
| `/git/conventions` | convention document state for a repository plus the framework catalog (`{path}`) |
| `/git/convention` | write the document (`{path, framework?, force?}`) |
| `/git/init` | initialize a repository in a directory that has none (`{path, branch?}`) |
| `/git/cleanup` | branch cleanup hints: merged/unmerged counts per local branch (`{path}`) |
| `/git/health` | repository health: detached HEAD, branches without upstream, stash, large untracked files, `.git` size (`{path}`) |
Note: since 1.6.1 `/git/cleanup` and `/git/health` stay as read-only HTTP routes only; the tab no longer has an entry point, and the toolbar dropped *Overview* and *Full-window view*.
| `/git/compliance` | Commit compliance: the last 20 commits checked against the document's rules, with reasons (read-only; the panel shows the rules in force, not these historical offenders) (`{path}`) |
| `/git/convention/preview` | upgrade preview: added/rewritten/removed section counts and titles, read-only (`{path}`, `framework`) |
| `/git/workspace-convention` | workspace document: `state`, `preview` or `write` `.dsh/GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` (`{path}`, `action`, `framework`, `force`) |
| `/git/events` | change notifications (polled by the UI) |

Every route resolves the requested path with `realpath` and rejects it unless it lands inside a registered workspace. Nested repository directories are accepted; anything outside a workspace gets `workspace-unknown`.

## Known limitations

- **The tab never changes an existing repository's Git state.** It writes the conventions document, and it can run `git init` for a directory that is not a repository yet — nothing else. No commits, no branch switching, no worktrees: those stay in the chip's dialog.
- **Do not install this alongside `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph`.** Both halves own the `/git` route prefix, and two registrations of the same prefix conflict. Install one or the other.
- **Repositories deeper than 3 levels are not listed**, and a repository inside a skipped directory name (`node_modules`, `dist`, …) is not listed either, by design.
- **The host half is a build output.** `lib/index.js` is edited directly (the added parts sit in marked `//#region` blocks); `lib/client.js` is generated by splicing `src/client/graph/SidebarTab.js` into it. See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md).

## Development

```sh
npm run build     # splice src/client/graph/SidebarTab.js into lib/client.js
npm run check     # node --check on both bundles
npm run validate  # every t("…") key exists in both locale dictionaries
npm run preview   # render the tab to preview/*.html without a running DSH
```

`npm run preview` writes standalone HTML files (dark and light theme) that show the tab with sample repositories and commits, so layout changes can be checked in a browser without installing anything.

## Attribution and license

Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

This is a fork of [`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph) 0.4.8 by linxin666, also Apache-2.0. The branch chip, the commit-graph dialog, the worktree manager and the host git service come from that project. Changes in this fork: renamed package, workspace gate widened from exact-path match to inside-a-workspace, added the `/git/repos` discovery route, added the better-sidebar tab (repository tree, SVG canvas, zoom, pinned commit card) and its locale keys.
