evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 24私助（24PA）：工作区与助理团队原型 这个可丢弃原型验证：**飞书统一向 Lead 交办，原生 Worker 办理，配置和 JSON 记忆通过 dsh 工作区会话维护，同一个助理会话也能交办事务，这是否符合你的工作方式？** 中文名 **24私助**，英文名 **24PA**；版本 `0.0.4-prototype.3`。本轮统一展示名称，不迁移技术 ID，也不覆盖已有工作区文件。历史截图、文档和会话可能保留旧称。这是实际 dsh bundle，包含 Host、原生侧栏面板「24私助工作区」、唯一的「24私助」preset，以及原生 continuable 子 Agent。它不计入正式版的功能 PR。 ## 1. 启动并选工作区 在仓库根目录运行： ```sh npm run prototype ``` 默认使用相邻已构建的 `deepseek-harness/apps/cli/lib/bin.js`，否则使用 PATH 中的 `dsh`。可通过 `PA24_DSH_CLI` 指定构建入口。脚本使用官方 CLI 初始化独立 Web profile、登记 bundle 后启动，不修改你的其他 profile。 默认 DSH_HOME 为仓库 `.prototype-runtime/home`；首次自动生成的工作区位于其中 `24pa-prototype/workspace`。首次选择自己目录： ```sh PA24_WORKSPACE=/srv/my-24pa npm run prototype ``` 这是 **dsh 所在服务器的目录**。已有 `AGENTS.md` 会保留，需要按生成模板添加唯一的 JSON 配置块。也可在 dsh 原生侧栏添加目录，再到“24私助工作区 → 工作区”绑定。切换前要先完成或停止运行中的事项；切换工作区会清空当前原型的内存业务视图，文件与原生会话保留。 打开终端输出的完整登录地址，点击 **24私助工作区**。管理台显示工作区路径、五类 Worker、事项、文档状态和只读记忆查询。点击“与24私助对话”，进入 dsh 原生会话。没有模型凭据时先在 dsh 模型设置中配置；不再用内置示例模型生成貌似真实的结果。 默认监听 `127.0.0.1:3210`，`PA24_PORT` 可改端口。占用时脚本会在安装前退出；先在原终端 Ctrl+C。找不到原终端时可用 `lsof -nP -iTCP:3210 -sTCP:LISTEN` 和 `ps -p -o pid,command` 确认确为自己的原型，再 `kill -TERM `。不同实例必须使用不同的 `PA24_DSH_HOME` 和工作区。 ## 2. 一个预设完成协调和维护 Agent 预设只需选择 **24私助**。它同时具备之前 Lead 的接单、委派、进度查询、继续/停止事项能力，以及配置、接入检查和 JSON 记忆维护能力。一般维护也在这个预设里完成，不必切到标准模式。 点击面板「与24私助对话」会打开或恢复本工作区的机器人会话。你也可以在同一工作区新建会话并选该预设。dsh 交办的 Worker 结果返回发起会话；飞书交办的结果返回机器人。两端共用配置、记忆与本次运行的事项视图，聊天历史仍按原生会话隔离。主动提醒按你的委托发到飞书。 管理面板按「事项总览、飞书接入、结构化记忆、手写审核、工作区、运行记录」组织。SVG 图标与彩色标签区分日程、待办、提醒、备忘和手写能力；状态同时提供文字和图标。总览计数取自本次运行的实际事项，记忆正文直接来自工作区 JSON，不注入演示记录。原始 JSON、长路径与内部诊断放在可展开的详情中。 界面跟随 dsh 的明暗主题，窄窗口下卡片自动换列，导航可横向滚动；键盘左右方向键及 Home/End 可切换页签。飞书配置与记忆维护继续通过对话进行。 Lead 是内部协调职责；飞书接入会话和 Worker 的原生链接在「运行记录 / 内部会话与诊断」及事项详情中。飞书入口、Worker 不获得本地配置和记忆写入权限。此前维护 preset 的历史文件保留，后续请使用新机器人入口，旧维护会话不再作为可继续的入口。如果原型拥有的入口会话被切到其他预设，重新打开时会保留旧历史并创建新的机器人入口，绑定关系随重启保存。 ## 3. AGENTS.md 是配置源 初始模板的 JSON 包含这些字段： | 字段 | 作用 | |---|---| | version / mode | 配置版本 1；demo 或 feishu | | larkProfile | 固定飞书 CLI profile，默认 default | | ownerOpenId | 唯一主人的飞书 open_id | | folderToken / tasklistId / calendarId | 体验文档目录、任务清单、本人日历；日历默认 primary | | timeZone | 默认 Asia/Shanghai | | appIdEnv / appSecretEnv | 应用凭据的环境变量名称，实际密钥不写入文件 | | maxWorkers | 同时处理数，1–8，默认 2 | | enabledWorkers | calendar、tasks、reminders、memo、handwriting 中启用哪些 | | workerModels | 可按 Worker 指定 dsh provider/model；未指定继承宿主模型 | 模式、身份与资源配置只在该文件中维护；旧 `PA24_MODE`、`PA24_LARK_PROFILE` 等环境设置不再读取。文件中的稳定规则也由 dsh 原生 agent-instructions 装载。 在同一个机器人会话可以说： > 查看这个工作区的 AGENTS.md，解释当前配置。 > > 把 maxWorkers 改为 3，检查配置并重载。 机器人使用原生文件工具与 `pa24_workspace`。也可以手工编辑文件，再点击管理台“重载 AGENTS.md”；运行中的业务未结束会拒绝重载。同一工作区重载保留本次业务记录，坏配置不替换当前有效配置。 ## 4. 查阅飞书接入 打开「飞书接入」，点击「检查接入状态」，或在机器人会话说 **“检查飞书接入，告诉我还缺什么”**。页面只读，不提供配置表单。 可查阅 CLI 实际路径和版本、固定 profile、CLI 用户与配置主人是否匹配、用户令牌校验、文档目录/任务清单/日历、环境凭据是否提供、配置来源与生效时间、最近一次检查结果、当前运行的机器人收发时间。 检查按需执行；页面刷新不会持续调用飞书。身份不匹配或未验证时不读资源。资源读取成功只代表可读，不能推断写入权限。文件改动未重载会明确标记；坏配置不替换生效版本。页面和工具只返回诊断字段，不返回 token 或密钥原值。 对话中提供非秘密配置，例如“把文档目录设为…，检查并重载”。机器人通过文件工具修改 AGENTS.md。**初次 CLI 安装、应用凭据注入和 OAuth 授权仍由你在服务器完成**；此版本没有代办登录流程。诊断不会发测试消息或写入飞书业务对象。 ## 5. 接入真实飞书 1. 服务器安装并授权 `lark-cli`，使用同一个机器人应用和固定 profile。可用 `lark-cli --profile default auth status --json` 核对用户 openId；插件会检查其与 ownerOpenId 一致。 2. 在飞书自建应用开启机器人和长连接，订阅 `im.message.receive_v1`、`card.action.trigger`。按 CLI 授权提示配置消息、图片资源、文档/图片、任务和日历权限。主人能访问指定目录、清单和机器人。 3. 将 `.env.example` 所示的应用凭据通过启动 shell 或服务管理器导出，插件不会自动读取 `.env`。使用自己已有的凭据管理方式即可。 4. 在工作区 AGENTS.md 填入 ownerOpenId、folderToken、tasklistId，mode 改为 feishu。不要把密钥原值写进 JSON。已运行进程无法获取之后新增的 shell 环境变量，首次配置凭据需要重启 dsh；已有环境中修改普通配置可重载。 5. 在 dsh 设置中配置 Lead 模型。手写 Worker 需要实际支持图片的路由；可在 workerModels.handwriting 中指定已配置的 provider 和 model。主模型是文字模型时必须单独配视觉模型。 6. 管理台看到长连接启动后，在手机给机器人发 `/24pa`，以真正收到回复为收发验证。 连接启动本身不等于飞书端到端验收。写入的任务和文档标题带 `[24PA原型]`，请使用专门的体验目录和清单。 ## 6. 从飞书体验 | 飞书输入 | 助理办理与当前范围 | |---|---| | “帮我记一个待办：周末整理书房” | Lead 委派 tasks，创建真实任务；可要求完成该原型创建的任务 | | “记一下：下周讨论新的合作方向” | memo Worker 写入指定目录的飞书备忘文档 | | “查一下明天日程，给我安排建议” | calendar 查询本人日历，缺少日期/时区先澄清 | | “明天 10 点到 11 点安排我写方案” | calendar 在时间明确后创建本人日程；原型不邀请他人、改期或删除日程 | | “30 秒后提醒我喝水” | reminders 创建单次提醒，计时到期后机器人主动发给本人 | | “看看正在办理的事”“继续整理那份笔记” | Lead 查询或继续原 Worker；多件事不需要 A–E 切换 | | “停止书房那项工作” | 停止后续处理；已创建的外部对象不会自动撤销 | | 飞书 App 拍一页纸质笔记并发送 | 保存收到的原图，Lead 交给 handwriting，实际视觉结果进入待审文档 | 手写输出要求忠实转写、摘要、疑点、候选行动和简单图示说明。看完飞书文档与原稿后，点击机器人发来的“本人审核通过”或“退回修改”。需要修订时回复原卡片，告诉 Lead 修改依据；修订生成新文档版本，旧卡不能批准新版本。 审核通过不会创建任务。需要执行时另发： ```text /执行 N-笔记编号 需要创建的任务内容 ``` 一份笔记在原型中每个版本只允许创建一次演示行动。多项选择和幂等批量执行是正式版范围。 原型只能识别单页 PNG/JPEG/WebP，最大 10 MiB；没有录音 Worker、多页合并或 PDF 处理。照片文字不构成新授权，手写 Worker 没有任何业务写入或批准工具。 ## 7. 查阅与维护 JSON 记忆 打开「结构化记忆」即自动读取已保存的内容，无需先查询。每条卡片展示主题、类别、确认状态、完整正文、来源和更新时间；展开「修订依据与 JSON」可查看具体字段。支持关键词筛选、查看全部、分页和刷新，超过 20 条可翻页继续查看。 当前没有保存记录时会显示明确的空状态；文件格式错误会显示读取失败，而不会伪装成没有记忆。切换工作区后重新读取对应文件。页面保持只读，通过机器人会话进行维护；会话修改后点「刷新记忆」即可看到更新。 点击“与24私助对话”，可以输入： > 记住我希望会议之间留 15 分钟，这是我明确的偏好。 > > 查看与项目 X 有关的记忆，给出来源。 > > 整理项目 X 的记忆，列出重复、冲突和过时条目，再按我的要求修改。 > > 删除刚才指定的过时偏好。 记忆位于 **工作区 `.24pa-prototype/memory.json`**。机器人先查询 revision，修改携带 expectedRevision、来源和本人指令依据；并发版本变化就拒绝覆盖。内容按 category、topic、content、source、confirmed/unverified 状态等字段保存。手工改文件后再次查询会读取新内容，无效 JSON 明确报错。 飞书接入会话与获准 Worker 可以检索，写入由 dsh 的机器人会话完成。没有自动归纳、定期整理或记忆后台定时器；业务提醒仍会自动到期发送。原型修订逐条提交，记录最后修改依据和原生工具日志，未实现完整修订历史/回滚。 ## 8. 安装到已有服务器 dsh 已核对本机 dsh `0.2.1-alpha.1`，Node 实测 `26.4.0`；包要求 `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`。使用兼容的常驻 Web profile，纯 headless 不满足该管理面板的依赖。 仓库方式： ```sh git clone --branch prototype/24pa-dsh git@github.com:benz-ai-x/dsh-24-PA.git cd dsh-24-PA PA24_WORKSPACE=/srv/my-24pa npm run prototype ``` 或先 `npm run prototype:pack`，上传 `artifacts/benz-ai-x-dsh-24pa-prototype-0.0.4-prototype.3.tgz`，使用独立 DSH_HOME 安装： ```sh export DSH_HOME=/srv/24pa-prototype-home export PA24_WORKSPACE=/srv/my-24pa dsh --profile pa24-prototype --from-default-profile web --dump-config >/dev/null dsh plugin --profile pa24-prototype add ./benz-ai-x-dsh-24pa-prototype-0.0.4-prototype.3.tgz --ignore-scripts dsh --profile pa24-prototype --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3210 --no-open ``` 已有该 Web profile 时省略初始化行。安装需要获取 SDK 依赖，不运行传递依赖安装脚本。文件无需额外构建。服务器通过已有 SSH 隧道或 dsh 的 HTTPS 代理访问，保留宿主认证。多个进程不要共用运行目录或工作区。 ## 9. 原型的持久化与验证边界 | 已实现的持久部分 | 本次运行的内存部分 | |---|---| | 工作区选择、AGENTS.md、JSON 记忆、收到的原稿文件、原生 dsh Session 日志 | 事项队列、提醒规则、图片运行索引、审核状态/卡片令牌、消息与事项路由 | 正式版业务使用 PostgreSQL Inbox/工作账本/审核/Outbox；这个原型没有连接 PostgreSQL，也不使用 SQLite。重启后旧卡失效，不能从旧文档标签推断当前正文已审核。配置重载与进程重启不同，前者在同工作区保留运行中的业务视图，后者没有业务恢复保证。 单次提醒使用 dsh-schedule 公开 after 规则与内存计时器，没有实现完整原生 Schedule 周期闭环。正式版智能计划必须挂到顶层 Lead，不能直接挂 child Session。晨报、全面同步、完整项目管理、多页识别与耐久恢复仍在正式规格中。 真实 Loader、原生会话/工具/子 Agent、文件写入和审核状态通过隔离验证；模型使用临时边界夹具，夹具不随包交付。真实模型判断质量、飞书平台收发/权限/回调/文档并发、中文手写识别效果和服务器运行尚需实际环境验收。具体证据见仓库 `docs/prototypes/24PA-原型验收记录.md`。 --- description: "Feishu-backed personal-assistant profile bundle for dsh: one 24私助 preset carrying the full standard tool base plus a SQLite-by-default ledger, seven business workers, task skills, voice digests, calendar-native reminders, handwriting review, and a staged access-setup wizard." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Install `@benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa` into a Profile to gain the「24私助」assistant preset and its host plugin: a Feishu plus local dual-entry coordinator delegating to seven business workers over a SQLite-by-default ledger (workspace `data/pa24.db`; optional PostgreSQL) for items, handwritten-note review, digests, and delivery receipts. Behavior ships as task skills — built-in plus workspace-customizable (`/.dsh/skills/`, hot-reloaded), each declaring a deterministic template track or a model-executed track — covering voice digests and calendar-native clock reminders that fire from the Feishu/WeCom app with the host offline. The preset carries the standard-mode tool base restricted per role, so the local session programs while the Feishu entry and workers keep business-only whitelists. Versions follow the dsh baseline (`.`) and support dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`–`0.2.1-alpha.5`, `0.2.1-rc.1`–`0.2.1-rc.2`. ## FAQ **What is 24私助 (24PA)?** — A Feishu personal-assistant plugin for dsh, shipped as a profile bundle: local dsh sessions and a Feishu bot coordinate seven business workers over a SQLite-by-default ledger — tasks, calendar, memos, digests, handwriting review, and a skill runner — while clock-type reminders ride native calendar events. **Which dsh runtimes are supported?** — dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`–`0.2.1-alpha.5`, `0.2.1-rc.1`–`0.2.1-rc.2`; versions are named `.` and npm dist-tags track baselines. **How do I install it?** — `dsh plugin --profile add @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa@`, then restart the profile (see [Installing the Bundle](#installing-the-bundle)). **Do reminders require the model to be online?** — No. Clock-type reminders are written as calendar events with native app alerts (Feishu or WeCom, per `calendarChannel`) — they fire with both the model and the 24私助 host offline; the ledger keeps a delegated backup row. Follow-up and conditional reminders run as agent-track skills. **Can I add or change routines without touching plugin code?** — Yes: periodic tasks, worker personas, access wizards, and workflows all ship as task skills. Drop a `.md` into the workspace `.dsh/skills/` directory (picked up hot) or rebind from the panel's plan cards; each skill declares a deterministic template track or a model-executed track with completion criteria, and can only tighten — never loosen — tool permissions. **How do I connect Feishu?** — Tell the local 24私助 session「帮我接通飞书」; the built-in wizard (`pa24_connection` `guide`, and `check` with `nextSteps`) walks app creation, authorization, resource ids, and health checks. The Feishu entry session can also run this read-only wizard and `wecom_guide`/`wecom_check` for channel diagnostics; configuration writes stay local-only (ADR-0001). ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package ### Installing the Bundle Pick the release matching your dsh runtime, then restart the Profile. The reconcile step activates the patch layer (one assistant preset row plus the host plugin row) for exactly this `dsh.bundle` declaration. ```sh # dsh 0.2.1-alpha.1 host (schedule service built in) dsh plugin --profile add @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa@0.2.1-alpha.1.6 # dsh 0.2.1-alpha.2 – 0.2.1-rc.2 hosts (peers span these baselines; rc.2 is the active release line) dsh plugin --profile add @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa@0.2.1-rc.3.1 # alpha.2 – alpha.5 hosts may also pin the alpha line (frozen at 0.2.1-alpha.5.1; preset content identical, only engines/peer range and docs differ) dsh plugin --profile add @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa@0.2.1-alpha.5.1 # dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 host — line frozen at 0.2.0-rc.2.3, no further releases (also add the two schedule companions for digests) dsh plugin --profile add @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa@0.2.0-rc.2.3 dsh plugin --profile add @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle dsh plugin --profile add /packages/schedule/schedule dsh plugin --profile remove @benz-ai-x/dsh-24pa ``` Removal withdraws the preset and host plugin on the next Profile start; PostgreSQL data, dsh sessions, and the workspace directory are untouched. Version naming follows `.`; npm dist-tags track baselines (`dsh-0.2.0-rc.2`, `dsh-0.2.1-alpha.1`, `dsh-0.2.1-alpha.2`, `dsh-0.2.1-alpha.5`, `dsh-0.2.1-rc.1`, `dsh-0.2.1-rc.2`). ### Configuration Secrets live only in the server environment; the workspace `AGENTS.md` holds one machine-checked JSON block with variable names, revalidated on reload — a bad block never replaces the effective configuration. | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `PA24_PG_DSN` | PostgreSQL connection string; the ledger uses an isolated `pa24` schema | | `PA24_WORKSPACE` | Absolute workspace directory bound on first start (or pick one in the panel / dsh settings) | | `PA24_FEISHU_APP_ID` / `PA24_FEISHU_APP_SECRET` | Feishu custom-app credentials (feishu mode) | `AGENTS.md` fields: `mode` (demo/feishu), `storage` (sqlite/postgres, default sqlite — the ledger is the workspace `data/pa24.db` file; SQLite uses the built-in `node:sqlite`, unflagged across this package's supported Node range; `postgres` requires `pgDsnEnv` and an external database), `larkProfile`, `ownerOpenId`, `folderToken`, `wikiNodeToken` (optional — memos and handwriting review docs land under this Feishu wiki node when set; empty falls back to folderToken), `tasklistId`, `calendarId`, `calendarChannel`/`todoChannel`/`notifyChannel` (feishu|wecom, default feishu — WeCom as the second operation channel for calendar/todo plus one-way reminder push, never inbound), `timeZone`, `appIdEnv`/`appSecretEnv`/`pgDsnEnv`, `maxWorkers`, `enabledWorkers`, `workerModels`, `extraBusinessSkills` (kebab-case allow list releasing workspace business skills to model-driven runs), `tts` (`engine` none/melo/volcengine, `voice`, `volcKeyEnv`, `meloDir` — voice digests via cloud Doubao TTS or local Melo), `extraLocalTools` (`subagent_codex`, `subagent_claude_code`, and QwenNote minutes tools via `mcp__qwennote__*` wildcard or precise names; entries naming unmounted tools are filtered out with a health note). For Feishu access setup, tell the local session「帮我接通飞书」or call `pa24_connection` with `action=guide`; the bundled `feishu-setup.md` is the single authority. ### Registered calendars (Manticore / M03) The Calendar card (`日程`) reads saved observations; **Verify calendars** explicitly reads the platforms. In Parameter configuration → Calendar & todo sources, register each personal, company or project calendar, choose its visible scope, creation default, project/company mapping and optional meeting duration. Registration does not grant platform permissions. Conversations query all enabled registered calendars; creation selects one explicit source, mapping or default. Missing or ambiguous targets require clarification. The `sources` object in the same AGENTS.md config block is authoritative. Without it, existing calendar/task-list fields yield stable migration candidates. Saving the source editor materializes those candidates; changing a legacy default through the form preserves the old source and adds the new default. An explicit empty registry stays empty. After a registry exists, change defaults there. Removing a source preserves remote objects and operation history. Pending operations retain their original identity and resource; an unknown result is never replayed as a new create. Feishu reads native instances plus paginated participant/group evidence. WeCom currently uses the authorized scope and a ±30-day window; a named calendar container, complete organizer evidence, invite and personal-reminder edit remain adapter gaps, reported explicitly. WeCom changes require the original confirmed creation receipt. Actual device notification delivery needs real-account verification. Todo sources can be registered/checked in M03; todo operations continue using the existing channel and task-list settings until M04. Schema 20 adds source registrations, access evidence, platform objects, per-source observations and memberships to both ledgers. Stop the host and keep a joint pre-upgrade backup of the ledger, workspace identity/config and native session history. Restore the whole backup with the matching code to roll back; do not drop migration records or run old and new hosts against the same ledger. See the initialization guide for recovery steps. ### Exposing the tool External CLI delegation rows ship enabled but stay dormant: `subagent_codex` and `subagent_claude_code` mount only after their provider bundles (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex` / `-claude-code`) are installed into the Profile, and the workspace must then opt in through `extraLocalTools`; entries naming tools that are not live are filtered before `tools.restrict()` runs and surface in maintenance health, so a missing provider or channel never breaks agent creation. QwenNote minutes tools pass the same gate from the host plane: add a `dsh-mcp-client` entry with `serverName: qwennote` (stdio + `mcp-remote` OAuth bridge, pinned version) to the Profile patch, complete the owner-browser authorization once, then opt in via `mcp__qwennote__*`. `ralph` is available to local sessions and follows its own tool contract: only on an explicit user request. ### What you get - The「24私助」preset: standard plugin set (platform shell, fs, search, jobs, skill, skill-filesystem, tool-skill, goal, plan-mode, compaction, delegation, ask-user, todo, web, present, ralph) plus `pa24-agent`; persona text merged into the assistant identity; `tool-schedule` deliberately excluded — clock-type reminders ride native calendar events, with the ledger as backup record. - Role-restricted tool surfaces: local sessions get the full standard base plus all `pa24_*` tools; the Feishu entry session and workers keep business-only whitelists (one preset never implies one permission set). - The host plugin: fixed Feishu access and local sessions, `pa24_delegate`/`pa24_jobs`/`pa24_notes`/`pa24_memory`/`pa24_maintenance`/`pa24_workspace`/`pa24_connection`/`pa24_work`, the SQLite-by-default ledger (optional PostgreSQL) with outbox delivery, the task-skill runtime (built-in plus workspace `.dsh/skills/`), calendar-native clock reminders, voice-capable digests, handwriting review cards, backup/health, the web panel (whose System category carries a parameter-configuration form: validate → rewrite the AGENTS.md config block → reload, with chat and the form sharing one config source; secrets are written via the Secrets group into a 0600 workspace store — write-only in the UI, env vars become optional overrides, and AGENTS.md/system prompts/backups never contain secret values), with workspace binding, switching, AGENTS.md reload, effective-config review, and health & budget living on the panel's System category under the Workspace & config card. WeCom access setup follows the bundled `wecom-setup.md` via `pa24_connection action=wecom_guide` / `wecom_check`. ### Failure and recovery Digests and meeting prep on a dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 host report「当前 Host 未提供原生 Schedule 服务」until the schedule companions above are installed; the registry `dsh-schedule@0.2.0-rc.1` is peer-incompatible and its row stays disabled. An uninstalled external CLI provider keeps its tool absent rather than erroring. A second active pa24 Host against the same `$DSH_HOME/24pa` refuses startup by lock. A fresh Profile ships an unresolved `allowBuilds` placeholder for `protobufjs` (a transitive dependency of the Feishu SDK), so the first install exits nonzero until you set it to `true` in the Profile `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; the package is fully added either way. A lark-cli timeout settles as result-unknown — verify the real Feishu object before retrying; nothing is blindly re-executed. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand This section explains how the assistant organizes work and where the observable behavior comes from; the consumer contract lives in [Use this package](#use-this-package). ### Design concept - **One preset, many permission sets.** Every session composes the same「24私助」preset; role whitelists applied at agent creation decide the visible tools, so inheriting the preset never inherits maintenance authority (ADR-0001). - **Calendars own clock-type reminders.** `tool-schedule` is excluded on purpose: clock-type reminders are written as calendar events with native alerts (per `calendarChannel`), firing even with 24私助 offline; the ledger keeps delegated backup rows for history and dedup (ADR-0001, revised 2026-10-18). - **Material never becomes authorization.** Notes, documents, subagent replies, and fetched web content are inputs; only the owner's explicit instruction authorizes an external write, and secrets are referenced by environment variable name only. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`cordis.patch.yml`](packages/24pa/cordis.patch.yml) | The Profile patch layer: preset row plus host plugin row | | [`src/index.ts`](packages/24pa/src/index.ts) | Plugin entry: config schema, runtime construction, panel | | [`src/tools.ts`](packages/24pa/src/tools.ts) | Tool registration, `STANDARD_CODING_TOOLS`, `ROLE_TOOLS` | | [`src/prompts.ts`](packages/24pa/src/prompts.ts) | Every built-in prompt with `PROMPTS_VERSION`, AGENTS.md template | | [`src/runtime.ts`](packages/24pa/src/runtime.ts) | Roles, delegation, ledger flows, reminders, digests, backup | | [`src/feishu.ts`](packages/24pa/src/feishu.ts) | SDK long-connection transport, access diagnostics, `setupNextSteps` | | [`feishu-setup.md`](packages/24pa/feishu-setup.md) | The bundled access-setup guide served by `pa24_connection guide` | ### Run flow On start the host plugin takes a single-writer lock on `$DSH_HOME/24pa`, opens the ledger (SQLite workspace file by default, or PostgreSQL), loads and validates the workspace `AGENTS.md`, and establishes the fixed Feishu access and local sessions through the SessionController. Inbound Feishu events durably enter an inbox before acknowledgment, the coordinator delegates to workers through the continuable child API, and each item records its origin, parent, and delivery target. Ticks drain the outbox with receipts, fire due non-delegated reminder occurrences, verify published note fingerprints, and wake digest plans through the native Schedule service; results return to the entry that originated the work. At agent creation the role whitelist restricts the inherited tool catalog, and an `AGENTS.md` reload replaces the workspace-rules prompt section without touching the effective configuration on failure.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when the package-level contract is not enough. They move from this bundle to the product it implements and the platform it plugs into. - [Agent guide](AGENTS.md) — task-specific reading paths and repository conventions. - [Product baseline](docs/agents/product.md) — how the approved Manticore targets relate to the v1 spec and delivery evidence. - [Product spec](docs/24PA-v1-SPEC.md) — v1 stories, scenarios, and test groups. - [Overall design](docs/24PA-整体设计方案.md) — flows, session topology, and confirmed trade-offs. - [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-workspace-session-boundaries.md) — the workspace/session permission boundary this preset enforces. - [Research records](docs/research/) — per-feature verified contracts, including the dual-baseline and access-wizard studies. - [Delivery plan](docs/planning/24PA-v1-PR交付计划.md) — feature groups and their dependencies. - [Delivery workflow](docs/agents/delivery.md) — branch reuse, dependency checks, acceptance evidence, and merge criteria. ----- ## Model Experience ### Assistant request #### What the model sees `pa24-agent` injects four ordered lead sections (identity and capability split, coordination, business domains, safety and reporting) plus the merged persona line; the workspace-rules section (order 910) carries `AGENTS.md` prose and stays empty until a workspace is bound. Workers receive four-part personas (职责/完成标准/边界/输出要求) instead. ##### Verbatim identity line (src/prompts.ts) ```markdown 统一提供助理协调、工作区维护和完整编程能力；按本会话实际可用的工具办理（身份与工作目录见系统提示开头）。 ``` #### Token effect Fixed per role after workspace bind; the workspace-rules section is conditional (empty until bound) and is replaced, not extended, on reload. #### KV Cache effect Stable repeated prefix within a session: an `AGENTS.md` reload replaces the rules section and invalidates reuse from that request on, while a `PROMPTS_VERSION` bump invalidates across deployments. Nothing else in this bundle rewrites the earlier prefix. ### Role-restricted tool catalog #### What the model sees Eight `pa24_*` schemas with fixed JSON parameters, plus the role restriction applied to the inherited catalog: the Feishu entry sees exactly its five business tools, workers exactly `pa24_work` and read-only `pa24_memory`, local sessions the full standard base plus all `pa24_*` tools. #### Token effect Fixed catalog per role for the session lifetime; `extraLocalTools` extends the local allow list only, and host-plane additions from other bundles (for example `schedule_*`) are outside this bundle's allow list. #### KV Cache effect Append-only: the catalog is constant across one session's requests, so conversation growth never rewrites the prefix; changing the workspace `extraLocalTools`, the preset composition, or upgrading the package invalidates reuse. Indirectly, through the preset rows this bundle composes, each inserted standard package owns its own tool descriptions and prompt contributions. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits define when this assistant needs special operational care. They are current package constraints, not a general Feishu comparison or a task backlog. - **Real-tenant operation is single-instance so far** — long-connection, identity, and renewal paths now run on one production Feishu tenant (WeCom channels and voice digests included); broader tenant and zone compatibility remains untested, and console permission scope names are keyword-based pending on-console verification. - **Handwriting recognition quality is unquantified** — multi-page transcription fidelity needs a 30–50 page real-sample evaluation before any accuracy claim; the visual route must be configured in `workerModels`. - **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 hosts ship no schedule service** — digests and meeting prep stay honestly unavailable until the schedule companions are installed, and the host-plane `schedule_*` tools those companions add cannot be hidden by preset restriction. - **External CLI delegation is dormant by default** — `subagent_codex`/`subagent_claude_code` mount only after their provider bundles are installed and `extraLocalTools` opts in; unconfigured tools stay absent rather than erroring. - **One writer per state directory** — a second active pa24 Host against the same `$DSH_HOME/24pa` refuses startup by lock; run one host per state directory. ### Dev Note
Working context for maintainers — click to expand This Dev Note is working context for maintainers: open questions and undecided directions. It is explicitly non-authoritative — shipped behavior and limits live in the sections above and in the package code. - **Multi-baseline verification** — regression runs select the runtime with `DSH_BIN` and append the rc.2 schedule companions with `PA24_E2E_EXTRA_PLUGINS`; the active release line is 0.2.1-rc.2 with the full suite at 258/258, while 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-alpha.1 remain covered by the dual-API fallback paths. - **Preset patch is generated** — `cordis.patch.yml` is produced by `scripts/sync-preset.mjs` from the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` standard preset pinned as a devDependency; never edit it by hand. On a new dsh baseline, bump the pin and run `npm run preset:sync`; `npm run preset:check` and unit tests fail when the checked-in copy drifts. - **Local harness adjacency** — dev type-checking links vendored peers from an adjacent `deepseek-harness` checkout through `scripts/link-peer.mjs`; registry installs never depend on that checkout.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-dotnet-runner

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web 插件：自动检测当前会话工作区里的 .NET 项目，在界面右下角提供「运行 / 重新运行 / 停止」三个按钮，并在「更多」面板里显示正在执行的 `dotnet` 命令和实时终端输出。

## 功能

- 以当前会话的工作目录作为工作区，递归查找 `*.csproj` / `*.fsproj` / `*.vbproj`（跳过 `.git`、`bin`、`obj`、`node_modules`、`.vs` 等目录）
- 工作区里没有 .NET 项目时，三个按钮整体隐藏；有项目才出现在右下角
- 「设备」下拉框像 IDE 一样探测本机可用目标：iOS 模拟器（`xcrun simctl`）、已连接的 iPhone / iPad 真机（`xcrun devicectl`，旧版 Xcode 回退 `xctrace`）、已连接的 Android 设备与 AVD（`adb` / `emulator`）、Mac Catalyst 本机；选中后带对应 RID / 设备参数编译运行
- iOS 真机部署需要项目已配置好签名与 Provisioning（自动签名或描述文件）
- 一个工作区有多个项目时，可在「更多」面板的下拉框里切换
- 普通项目：`dotnet build` 成功后执行 `dotnet run --no-build`
- MAUI 项目：`dotnet build` 成功后直接启动构建产物（macOS 上为 `*.app/Contents/MacOS/<AssemblyName>`），保持进程存活，因此「停止」可以真正结束 App
- 编译期间「运行」「停止」和项目下拉框禁用，绿色按钮显示转圈；「更多」始终可用
- 「更多」面板显示当前命令、工作区路径、项目选择和终端输出（约 900ms 刷新，自动滚动）
- 仅使用本地 HTTP 路由与 `ctx.fs` / `ctx.subprocess`，不引入任何第三方依赖

## 环境要求

- 已安装并登录的 DSH（Web GUI）
- .NET SDK（`dotnet` 在 PATH 中，或位于 `~/.dotnet/dotnet`、`/usr/local/share/dotnet/dotnet`、`/opt/homebrew/bin/dotnet` 等常见位置）
- MAUI 项目需要对应平台的工作负载

## 安装

从 npm 安装（推荐）：让 DSH 的 agent 执行 `plugin_manager` 的 `install_bundle`，目标为 `dsh-dotnet-runner`。

或从源码本地安装：

1. 克隆本仓库：

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/BigBearKing/dsh-dotnet-runner.git
   ```

2. 在 DSH 里把该目录作为本地 bundle 安装（`package.json` 已声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`），例如通过 Plugin Manager 的本地目录安装，或让 DSH 的 agent 执行 `plugin_manager` 的 `install_bundle`，目标为仓库的绝对路径。

3. 刷新 DSH 页面，右下角出现三个按钮。

## 可选配置

在 `cordis.patch.yml` 对应行的 `config` 中可覆盖：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dotnet-runner
      name: 'dsh-dotnet-runner'
      config:
        root: /path/to/workspace   # 覆盖工作区根目录
        dotnetPath: /usr/local/share/dotnet/dotnet  # 覆盖 dotnet 可执行文件
        scanDepth: 6               # 最大扫描深度
        maxProjects: 50            # 最多收集的项目数
```

## 结构

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Host 半：扫描项目、解析 csproj、编译/运行子进程、`/dotnet-runner` HTTP 路由 |
| `client.js` | Client 半：`shell.overlay` 浮动按钮、`conversation.composer.dock` 会话桥、状态轮询 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch |
| `locale/*.json` | 插件标题与描述 |
| `icon.svg` | 插件图标 |

## 说明

- 工作区来自当前会话的 `cwd`；取不到时依次回退到 `config.root`、第一个已注册工作区、DSH 的默认目录。
- macOS 上启动的 App 是插件的子进程，点「停止」会结束该进程；从 Finder 手动打开的实例不受管理。
- 插件的 HTTP 路由仅接受本机回环地址，并对 POST 请求校验 `Origin`。

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

--- description: "The dsh graph bundle: one CEO Agent over a refactory mode graph, for users running one committed mode end to end." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-graph ## Summary The `graph` profile layer drives one refactory mode graph end to end: it mounts the workflow spine with `executeCommands` on, replaces the base persona with the CEO wording, and adds a `run` subcommand that takes a mode and a task. You get one JSON report — the run's `best_score`, its session id, its work directory, and the CEO's final message — after the agent reaches quiescence. Install it into a profile with one `dsh plugin` command; the layer stacks over `dsh-base`, which supplies the model connection, the tool set, the session store, and the `shell` executor that deterministic nodes run in. The bundle holds no graph of its own: it loads `.graph.json` from `--graphs` at startup, so a mode is one file plus the Python ops its commands call. Choose it to run a committed mode; when the mode declares a `user` gate, the terminal answerer puts the gate to the person, so the same profile serves an unattended run and one with a person at the gate. Refactory's `python -m refactory_dsh.interactive /` is the entry point that prepares that run: it lowers the mode with its intent ledger folded in and starts this profile with the terminal attached. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package ### Install into a profile ```text dsh plugin --profile graph add /packages/bundle/graph dsh plugin --profile graph remove @deepseek-ai/dsh-graph ``` `graph` is not one of the shipped profile templates, so the profile must exist before a run: `dsh --profile graph` on a machine without one stops with `profile "graph" does not exist; create it with 'dsh plugin --profile graph add '`. The `add` form above links the package from a checkout, because `@deepseek-ai/dsh-graph` is not published to the npm registry. The command initializes the profile over `dsh-base` and installs the package; because the manifest declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, the reconcile step appends `@deepseek-ai/dsh-graph` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, after `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, and the layer activates on the next start. A dependency without that declaration installs as a plain package and never becomes a layer. `remove` drops the dependency and the layer together. ### Run a mode For normal use, run `uv run refactory ceo /` from the checkout. The Python bridge lowers the selected mode, supplies its graph directory and Python environment, and enables interactive chat unless `--headless` is given. The lower-level example below retains the legacy SRF defaults and requires its own graph files; it is not the new-user quickstart. See [the interface guide](../../../refactory/docs/interfaces.md). ```text dsh --profile graph run --mode gepa --task circle_packing --budget 20 ``` `--mode` and `--task` are required, and `run` is the default subcommand. `--budget` defaults to 10 and reaches the ops as `SRF_BUDGET`; `--knobs` takes a JSON object of `OptKnob` overrides; `--provider` and `--model` select the CEO's route. `--graphs` defaults to the checkout's `refactory/vendor/srf/graphs` (or `$SRF_GRAPHS`) and must hold `.graph.json`; `--python-bin` defaults to `.venv/bin` (or `$VENV_BIN`) and must hold the Python that has `srf` and `factory` installed. `--workdir` defaults to a fresh temporary directory. A missing graph fails at startup with the path it looked for and the `srf graphs` command that generates it. The run prints one JSON object with `mode`, `task`, `budget`, `best_score`, `session_id`, `workdir`, and `final` — the first 400 characters of the CEO's last message. `best_score` is 0 when no evaluated proposal was accepted. ### What you get - The `run` subcommand with its mode, task, budget, graph, Python, model, and knob options. - The CEO persona: `You are the CEO of an interactive refactory workflow, powered by the {{model}} model.`, with the working directory appended as the persona suffix. - The [workflow spine](../../workflow/workflow-spine/README.md) row: prefix `wf`, `executeCommands: true`, `maxIterations: 500`, a one-hour node-command timeout, and a `ceoDeny` list that leaves the CEO with the `wf_*` tools. The row is host-level, so its guard covers every top-level agent on the host, which on this profile is the CEO the runner boots: agent-node workers run in processes of their own. - The `subagent` and `subagent_fork` rows with the `ceo` preset's `toolFilter` allow-list, so a subagent started through either gets the file and web tools, `skill`, `todo_write` and `send_message`, and no `bash`. - The worker-thread code runtime, so a node's Python op runs without blocking the agent loop. - The item loader a `DataNode` iterates through: the spine runs `python -m refactory_dsh.items list|begin|end`, so a data-driven mode's items are selected by the same code on this profile as on the walker. - The runner, which drives the single CEO agent to quiescence and reports the run. - The terminal answerer, which puts a `user` gate to the person at the terminal and writes their verdict into the run's intent ledger. Without a terminal (a piped or captured stdin) it answers nothing, so a headless run refuses a person's gate rather than inventing a verdict. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The bundle is one patch document over `dsh-base` plus three runtime plugins. The patch restates the targeted rows' whole config — the persona templates, the tools mode and the two delegation rows — and inserts five rows: the worker-thread code runtime, the `graph-startup` provider, the workflow spine, the terminal answerer, and the `graph-runner` glue. `graph-startup` parses the command line, loads the mode's graph, resolves the work directory and the node-command environment, and publishes `graphStartup`; at boot, the startup plugin also discovers the `steerCommand` and `steerArgs` via a Python probe against the `refactory.steer` entry point (using `--python-bin`'s python). The probe defaults are: `$VENV_BIN`, else `$REFACTORY_DSH_HOME/.venv/bin`, else `/.venv/bin`. The spine row, the answerer, and the runner all inject that service, so one parse parameterizes them and the graph is inlined at boot. The YAML's `steerCommand` and `steerArgs` lines are `!!js` expressions that read from `graphStartup`; when the entry point is absent (core-only install), startup publishes `steerCommand: ''` and logs a warning, and `wf_steer` is not registered. The runner boots a single CEO agent, sends the driving prompt as a user message, waits for quiescence, flushes the session, reads `best_score` from the mode's state file in the work directory, and exits. Deterministic nodes run in-process through the `shell` executor that `dsh-base` mounts, and each routes its gate by the last non-empty stdout line. A `DataNode`'s subgraph is iterated once per item: the spine asks the loader how many items there are, materialises one before each pass and closes it after, and hands the pass's nodes over exactly as it hands over the rest of the graph. A `user` gate is not run: the spine resolves a pending, review-scoped decision through the ledger bridge, or asks the terminal/GUI answerer for a fresh answer. Interactive answers are recorded as used and never silently replayed on a later visit. `console steer --verdict` queues one answer for the current declared review inputs; changing those inputs expires it. Explicit `ceo --approve` and Python/authoring `verdicts` remain standing upfront authorization. Legacy unscoped ledger verdicts remain visible but require a new answer. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The layer: the persona, tools and delegation-row overrides, then the four inserted rows | | [`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts) | The `graph-startup` provider: command line, graph loading, work directory, command environment | | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | The `graph-runner` glue: one CEO agent, quiescence, session flush, and the JSON report |
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want the parts this layer composes rather than the run itself. - [Runtime architecture](../../../refactory/docs/architecture.md) — Refactory and the installed DSH core this layer patches. - [workflow-spine](../../workflow/workflow-spine/README.md) — the spine row and the `wf_*` tools the CEO drives. - [refactory glue](../../../refactory/README.md) — the Python modes, graphs, and ops a node command runs. - [Models and credentials](../../../refactory/docs/models.md) — provider configuration and nested execution. ----- ## Model Experience ### The CEO persona and the workflow tools #### What the model sees The layer replaces the base persona: the prefix reads `You are the CEO of an interactive refactory workflow, powered by the {{model}} model.` and the suffix states the working directory as `Your working directory is {{cwd}}.`. The inserted workflow-spine row registers the `wf_*` tools and their prompt section, and that section plus the `ceoDeny` list are what leave the CEO on the `wf_*` tools, delegation, read-only file tools, and the agent, job, goal, todo and plan-mode controls: no shell, no file writes, no web tools or `skill`, and no `workflow` or `ralph` to start a child outside the delegation rows' allow-list. A subagent started through `subagent` or `subagent_fork` sees only its row's allow-list. The code runtime and the two graph plugins register no model-facing text of their own. #### Token effect One persona prefix and suffix per request, plus the `wf_*` tool definitions and their prompt section; the graph's own node content reaches the model through the tool results the CEO reads, so a mode's prompt template costs tokens once, when that node is due. The `ceoDeny` guard removes the denied tools' definitions from the CEO's requests. #### KV Cache effect The persona, the tool definitions, and the prompt section are fixed for the life of a profile, so they sit in the cached request prefix. A node view that names the next node changes only the message suffix, and the graph is inlined at boot, so no message in a run rewrites the prefix. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits define the current headless run. They are current package constraints, not a mode-authoring backlog. - **The `graph` profile is not auto-initialized** — `dsh --profile graph` stops with a create hint until `dsh plugin --profile graph add` has created the profile, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-graph` is not in the npm registry, so `add` takes a path into a checkout. - **The graph is inlined at boot** — the spine reads `ctx.graphStartup.graph`, so editing `.graph.json` during a run changes nothing; restart the run to pick up an edit. - **Node commands run unconfined** — graph commands are trusted ops and run with full sandbox access. `ceoDeny` constrains the CEO's own tool list only. A subagent started through `subagent` or `subagent_fork` gets the delegation rows' allow-list, with no `bash`, but its `write` and `edit` are not yet confined to the run directory. - **PTC mode is outside the allow-list** — with `DSH_TOOLS_MODE` set to a PTC mode, every agent also gets `run_code`, which runs model-written code, is added after tool filters apply and cannot be named by one. - **`best_score` is read from the work directory** — the runner prefers the mode's known state file and otherwise takes the first JSON file with a numeric `best_score`, so a mode that records its score elsewhere reports 0. - **One workflow per process** — the default low-level run is one-shot. `--chat` keeps a conversation between turns; the public `refactory ceo` command enables it by default. - **Separate limits** — this profile supplies `maxIterations: 500` as a fallback; a gate can declare its own cap. `--budget` reaches operations as `SRF_BUDGET`, not as a global time/token limit. ### Dev Note
Working context for maintainers — click to expand None.
**Runtime invariant:** No runtime invariant companion is published because the layer carries a patch document and a one-shot runner whose only shared state is the `graphStartup` service; every inserted row's package owns that row's behavior and invariants. A terminal model failure is printed before the next chat prompt, including the provider's error code and message. You may send a follow-up to retry. Headless runs, or quitting after an unsuccessful turn, return a nonzero exit and `ok: false` with `error` in the final JSON. Success requires a completed latest turn and explicit workflow `done`; missing status is not completion. A later successful interactive retry can still complete normally. When reusing a run directory, the runner preserves its previous status as `.refactory/spine-status.previous-.json` before the first turn. Only status written by this invocation can certify its completion; old artifacts and status history remain available for inspection. # Refactory ![Refactory — agentic harnesses, built to improve](refactory/docs/assets/refactory-hero.svg) **Create a workflow. Run it interactively. Optimize the way it works.** Refactory turns agentic work into reusable **modes**: explicit graphs of coding agents, deterministic operations, checks and approval gates. Drive them from a terminal or browser, steer work as it runs, and search their prompts, graph structure and parameters with a configurable outer loop. [Get started](refactory/docs/getting-started.md) · [Terminal & GUI](refactory/docs/interfaces.md) · [Command reference](refactory/docs/cli.md) · [Write a mode](refactory/docs/tutorials/01-write-a-mode.md) The browser keeps Refactory’s original two-gear identity and blue theme. The Modes panel has separate Run and Optimize views, Package → Mode selection, contextual help and a large brief editor. A live workflow map and required questions stay attached to the watched run. [Panel guide](refactory/docs/tutorials/07-pick-and-watch-from-the-panel.md) · [Upstream compatibility](refactory/docs/upstream-compatibility.md) **Release status · 26 September 2026:** Profiles, live controls/recovery and DSH/Codex/Claude Code workers have completed bounded CLI and native GUI acceptance. Fast authoring is implemented, but successful completion through QA and bounded repair remains unverified. [Readiness and evidence ↓](#release-capabilities-and-validation) ## What you can build - **A reusable harness:** Create turns a brief into a package of modes. Bind a Task to work over a class of inputs, or choose a single-run harness. - **A better version:** Edit produces a new mode package with provenance and honest comparison status. - **An artifact:** Design builds software, files or reports against a brief and a check command. - **A measured improvement:** Optimize proposes allowed changes, validates them, evaluates candidates and audits the winner before adoption. ![Create and Edit produce reusable modes; Design produces artifacts; scored modes can be run, optimized and adopted](refactory/docs/assets/refactory-flow.svg) ## Why explicit graphs? The runtime tracks which node is due, executes operations, enforces gates and records the evidence. The conversational CEO delegates agent work and accepts your steering. Skills can help a worker, but **a skill document is not the graph executor**. The graph and knobs are inspectable data. The optimizer proposes typed changes to those data; the mode's scoring function and declared invariants remain outside that edit surface. A user-owned approval gate belongs to the user. ## Quickstart Requires Git, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) `^22.19` or `>=24`, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). The installer sets up the pinned dependencies, Python environment and DSH profile. ```bash git clone https://github.com/boston-harness-group/refactory-dsh.git cd refactory-dsh ./install.sh uv run refactory list ``` Start with a small **offline** search over a shipped example: ```bash uv run refactory optimize circle_packing/adaptive \ --optimizer random --preset knob_only --evaluator walker \ --epochs 2 --batch-size 4 --max-evaluations 8 --seed 5 \ --runs-root .factory/loop/first-search uv run refactory leaderboard --run .factory/loop/first-search uv run refactory best --run .factory/loop/first-search ``` This example needs no model key. It demonstrates candidate changes, scores and a recorded stopping condition. Use a new run directory for a separate search. Keep the winner as a new package: ```bash uv run refactory adopt --run .factory/loop/first-search --as first_tuned uv run refactory package smoke first_tuned/adaptive ``` The original package remains available. [Continue the walkthrough →](refactory/docs/getting-started.md) ## Updating After every pull, run the installer again and restart any running GUI: ```bash git pull ./install.sh ``` `./install.sh` is safe to repeat: it re-syncs the Python and Node dependencies, rebuilds every package and updates the DSH profiles only when they changed. A running `refactory ui` or `./refactory-dsh` keeps the build it started with, so restart it afterwards. If a run stops with `Workflow engine build is out of date … Run pnpm run build`, the source was updated without rebuilding. Run `./install.sh` (or `pnpm run build`) and restart. ## Choose your interface | Terminal | Browser | |---|---| | `refactory ceo` for conversation and approval gates | CEO chat for authoring and node-by-node interaction | | `refactory optimize` for explicit search configuration | Modes panel for saved profiles, knobs, search and resource limits | | `status`, `candidate`, `steer`, `adopt` for inspection and control | Run once, live graph/worker activity, questions and candidate comparison | ```bash uv run refactory ui --port 3081 ``` For all native web presets plus CEO and the Refactory Modes panel: ```bash ./refactory-dsh --additive --port 3081 ``` This creates and reuses `refactory-web`, declaring the web and Refactory bundles in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/refactory-web/package.json`. CEO is the default, and the existing `web` profile stays unchanged. Open the exact URL printed by the server, select the checkout as your workspace, then create a session. Open the right sidebar's **Modes** tab; no introductory chat message is required. Before model-backed work, save a provider key in **Settings → Models**. Nested workers and validation use the managed credential store; a checkout `.env` or exported key alone is insufficient for those scrubbed processes. `uv run refactory doctor` checks configuration, not authentication or quota. [Model setup →](refactory/docs/models.md) Try this in GUI chat: > Open counting_pack/fixed_step with target=20 and step=2. Drive it one node at a time and show me the recorded result. Or from the terminal: ```bash uv run refactory ceo counting_pack/fixed_step \ --knob target=20 --knob step=2 --intent "Count to twenty and explain the recorded result." ``` Chat supports Create, Edit and Design. The Modes panel's **Start** button launches optimization of a scored mode; **Run once** executes any enabled mode, including full and fast authoring modes. Attach a run to follow durable activity, worker receipts and pending questions. [Interface guide →](refactory/docs/interfaces.md) ## Create, edit or design | Goal | Example | |---|---| | Create a single-run harness | `uv run refactory ceo "Draft and check a project README from a supplied brief" --mode create --name readme_pack --single` | | Create a harness for a class of inputs | Use `--task module:TaskClass` instead of `--single`; see [Tasks and datasets](refactory/docs/datasets.md) | | Revise a mode | `uv run refactory ceo "Improve the search strategy" --mode edit --revise circle_packing/adaptive --name revised_pack` | | Build a checked artifact | `uv run refactory ceo "Build wordcount.py and a sample.txt; verify line, word and character counts" --mode design --name wordcount --check "python wordcount.py sample.txt"` | These commands call a model and can take substantial time. The current full authoring modes include research and reviews; you approve the strategy/design before implementation. Generated packages live in `.factory/packages/`. A Design run works on its own branch in a git worktree: of the repository you name with `--target`, or of a new project in `~/refactory-projects/`. Exact paths and validation outcomes are recorded in the run. For a small, focused task, choose `create_fast`, `edit_fast` or `design_fast`. Create plans a minimal reusable graph, then runs one coder and one QA agent sequentially; structural admission and canonical smoke remain required. Design uses the same three sequential roles for a small checked change, made where Design makes one: on the run's own branch, in a worktree of the repository or of a new project. Edit goes directly to one coder and one QA agent while preserving the source contract and optional score comparison. These graphs omit research and reviewer fan-out and allow one repair by default. All three fast paths completed their bounded CLI and native GUI checks, including real structural repairs and independent artifact checks; fast Design's worktree paths, so far, on the CLI only. Prior failures are retained. See [fast modes and shared budgets](refactory/docs/budgets-fast-modes.md). Canonical smoke/acceptance runs inside bounded repair **before** QA and Overwatch sign-off. Reviewers reuse its receipts and map the brief, accepted criteria/design and current intent ledger to actual evidence. Required behavior without evidence cannot pass; repairs and later instructions invalidate old sign-off. Full modes keep separate health, code and adversarial reviews plus Overwatch; fast modes keep one focused QA worker. [Evidence and graph details](refactory/docs/authoring-validation.md). For an intentional Edit tradeoff, `--knob allow_regression=true` skips **all original-mode execution and numerical comparison** while still validating the revised mode and preserving provenance. The default remains false. Skipped comparison is unmeasured, never a non-regression pass. Design produces the artifact itself. It does not need to produce a scored mode or enter the optimizer. [Authoring guide →](refactory/docs/tutorials/03-author-with-a-model.md) ## Optimize with a clear contract Choose an outer-loop strategy, a candidate proposer, an evaluator and permitted edits. Save a named [optimization profile](refactory/docs/optimization-profiles.md), preview its objective and validation contract, and launch the same settings from CLI or GUI. Each run retains its exact resolved snapshot. Candidate comparison includes lineage, changes, raw/adjusted scores, failures, trial variability, duration and available cost/usage. GUI chat can also launch a saved optimization profile, inspect its winner, adopt it and replay the adopted mode through Refactory tools. This path has [separate native chat acceptance](refactory/docs/release-validation-20260926.md#gui-chat-optimization-follow-up) alongside the CLI and panel checks. During a search you can add instructions, keep or reject candidate branches, pause/resume/stop at generation boundaries, and request adoption. A failed or unaudited candidate cannot be treated as a verified winner. A run may finish without finding an improvement. **Candidate limits, elapsed limits and token limits are separate controls.** Run-wide token/elapsed caps are optional and unset by default; fast work is bounded by its graph, repair policy and operation timeouts. [Choose a budget](refactory/docs/budget-strategy.md) using progress and measured usage rather than treating one token quota as a completion guarantee. Opt-in repeated trials and final holdout validation consume the shared run allocation; validation can have a reserved portion. Missing usage stays unavailable. Different models can change quality, cost and latency. [Optimization tutorial →](refactory/docs/tutorials/02-optimize-it.md) ## Models and coding workers DSH remains the default worker runtime, composed with Cordis. Its providers include DeepSeek, OpenAI and Anthropic. A DSH worker using an OpenAI model is still a DSH worker. Both evaluators carry the selected routing context; per-node overrides take precedence over per-role and run settings. Inspect actual execution receipts, not just the configured selection. [Routing and worker guide →](refactory/docs/models.md) Codex and Claude Code are explicit, optional worker backends through the installed DSH provider registry. They retain native authentication and product settings; unsupported capabilities fail before dispatch. External token-limited runs are refused because complete nested accounting is not established. Refactory still owns graph order, validation and gates. New workers default to **`skip`**, which bypasses native permission checks and, for DSH/Codex, their sandbox restrictions. Tools have the access available to your OS account. Choose `--permission-mode default` or **Native permission policy** in the GUI to retain the backend's checks. Existing saved runs and profiles preserve their policies. [Permission details](refactory/docs/models.md#model-provider-versus-coding-agent) ## Release capabilities and validation **All four release capabilities have completed bounded CLI and native GUI acceptance.** The checks cover the supported paths and sampled artifact contracts; they do not certify arbitrary generated projects or equal model performance. | Capability | CLI and native GUI acceptance | Guide / issue | |---|---|---| | Shared resource accounting and fast Create/Edit/Design graphs | **Complete:** all three fast modes, required validation, actual bounded repairs and explicit unresolved failure | [Fast modes and budgets](refactory/docs/budgets-fast-modes.md) · [#234](https://github.com/akashgit/refactory-dsh/issues/234) | | Live activity, questions, boundary controls and supported recovery | **Complete** | [Live control and recovery](refactory/docs/live-control.md) · [#235 closed](https://github.com/akashgit/refactory-dsh/issues/235) | | Versioned profiles, candidate comparison, exact adoption and replay | **Complete** | [Optimization profiles](refactory/docs/optimization-profiles.md) · [#236 closed](https://github.com/akashgit/refactory-dsh/issues/236) | | Routing and optional DSH/Codex/Claude Code workers | **Complete** | [Models and workers](refactory/docs/models.md) · [#237 closed](https://github.com/akashgit/refactory-dsh/issues/237) | The [release validation record](refactory/docs/release-validation-20260926.md) contains separate CLI/GUI evidence and resource limits. Codex and Claude Code passed native GUI artifact checks with the new `skip` default; registered stopped-owner recovery preserved completed work in both interfaces. External whole-tree token caps and in-flight worker-session resume remain unsupported. These bounded checks do not certify generated-artifact quality, equal backend performance or a clean full-repository test suite. ## The command line The full [command reference](refactory/docs/cli.md) covers authoring, packages, running, optimization, steering and adoption. Use `uv run refactory --help` for the installed command's options. ## Learn and contribute | Start here | Go deeper | |---|---| | [Getting started](refactory/docs/getting-started.md) | [Architecture](refactory/docs/architecture.md) | | [Concepts](refactory/docs/concepts.md) | [Python API](refactory/docs/api/index.md) | | [Tutorials](refactory/docs/tutorials/index.md) | [Tasks and datasets](refactory/docs/datasets.md) | | [Terminal and GUI](refactory/docs/interfaces.md) | [Verification](refactory/docs/verification.md) | | [Models and credentials](refactory/docs/models.md) | [Contributing](refactory/docs/contributing.md) | Refactory is under active development. Execution success, declared check results and the quality of generated content are separate evidence; inspect each when deciding whether an artifact meets your needs. ### Live help and project workers The CEO starts with a compact operating guide and can discover current mode and operation schemas through `refactory help`, then search/read complete shipped docs with `refactory docs`. Mode knobs, node roles, gates, examples and supported interface routes stay visible to the model. Builds check documentation coverage and reject stale generated references. See [discovery and extension checklist](refactory/docs/discovery.md). Put `refactory.workers.json` at the project root to select DSH, Codex or Claude Code workers, including a coder-only `node_routes.emit` override. CLI, native panel, CEO workflows and optimization resolve the same defaults; saved runs retain their routes. `refactory workers` explains effective settings and provenance. See [worker file examples and precedence](refactory/docs/worker-routing.md).
