# desk-panel（dsh 客户端插件）

DSH-ANYWORK 的「工作台用量」设置页：以 dsh 官方客户端插件机制注入（**不改 dsh 源码**）——
往 `settings.section` 槽位注册一个页面，数据来自门户的 `/portal/api/usage`。

## 挂载（每台实例）

```sh
DSH_HOME=<实例 home> node ~/deepseek-harness/apps/cli/lib/bin.js \
  plugin --profile web add file:<本目录绝对路径>
# 重启该实例后生效；`dsh plugin` 会自动把声明了 dsh.bundle 的包收进 profile 的 bundles 层
```

- 结构：`package.json`（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`）· `cordis.patch.yml`（插入 row）· `lib/index.js`（宿主空体）· `lib/client.js`（浏览器 bundle，闭包工厂格式）
- 仅依赖 `react`（平台种子模块，运行时由模块表提供），无构建步骤、无 npm 依赖。
- 直连实例端口时读不到账本（fetch /portal/api/usage 404）；从门户地址打开即可。

# DSH-ANYWORK

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md) | 📖 [User manual](docs/GUIDE.md)

**A self-hosted team workbench built around [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).**

Each member signs in with their own account and works in their own isolated workspace. The model API key stays on the server, and usage is metered per person — so a team can share one agent setup without sharing keys, files, or bills.

> **Status: building in public, early stage.** P0–P3 are done and verified on the LAN. P4 (delivery) is largely in place — `setup/backup/restore/logs` scripts, a one-page [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOY.md), and a green end-to-end [acceptance walk](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md); a from-scratch dry-run on a second machine is pending (the one-command Docker deploy completed a full from-scratch empty-volume run on this machine). The workbench UI is **bilingual (中文 / English)** — switch in Settings → General → Language. Roadmap and 22-task plan in [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md); verified findings in [`docs/BASELINE.md`](docs/BASELINE.md); daily progress in [`docs/devlog/`](docs/devlog/). 📖 **User manual** (Chinese): [`docs/GUIDE.md`](docs/GUIDE.md).

## Quick start (Docker · any Linux server)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bugbyc0922/DSH-ANYWORK.git && cd DSH-ANYWORK
cp .env.example .env    # set ANYWORK_HOST (your access address) and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
docker compose up -d --build
```

Open `http://<ANYWORK_HOST>/`. First build takes ~10-25 min (compiles the dsh engine); all data lives in a Docker volume and survives upgrades. Details in the [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOY.md).

## What this is

- **Engine**: the official [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`, MIT) — agent capabilities, tools, and the sandbox are reused as-is. This project does not modify dsh's source.
- **Shell (this repo)**: accounts and login, one isolated dsh instance and workspace per member, a model gateway that never exposes the real API key (per-person accounting and budget limits), and a portal to tie it together. Team modules inside the workbench: **task board with a submit → review/accept loop** (commit links + session refs for AI provenance), knowledge base, shared drive, notifications, announcements — and **session deletion with admin approval** (members request, admins approve).
- In one line: **dsh does the work; DSH-ANYWORK decides who gets to use it, where, and at what cost.**

## Documentation

- 📖 **[User manual](docs/GUIDE.md)** — every feature with its entry point, steps and notes (Chinese); includes a full feature index.
- [Deployment guide](docs/DEPLOY.md) · [Acceptance walk](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md) · [Known issues](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md)
- [Plan & tasks](docs/PLAN.md) · [Verified findings](docs/BASELINE.md) · [Daily devlog](docs/devlog/)

## Architecture (target)

```text
Member browser → Portal (login gate + reverse proxy)
                 ├─ /portal/*   portal pages (my usage / admin)
                 └─ all other paths → that member's dsh instance (HTTP + WS passthrough)
                        │
        dsh instance pool (one per member: own home / workspace / port)
                        │  DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL → gateway
                Model gateway (holds the real key, meters per person, enforces budgets)
                        │
                api.deepseek.com
```

## Roadmap

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Feasibility checks: multi-instance, launch flags, gateway interception, LAN access | 🟡 phone check pending |
| P1 | Model gateway + per-person metering | ✅ verified end-to-end |
| P2 | Accounts, login, portal | ✅ login, portal & instance proxy live |
| P3 | Per-member workspaces (instance management, autostart) | ✅ systemd units + autostart; isolation check green |
| P4 | Delivery: install, backup, acceptance | 🟡 scripts & docs done; acceptance walk green; Docker empty-volume run green; second physical machine pending |

Each task has a concrete acceptance check; the full list is in [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md).

## Development

Requirements: **Node 24+** — and nothing else. The service is dependency-free (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, built-in `fetch`), and TypeScript sources run directly via Node's type stripping.

```sh
# 1. Real upstream key (stays on the server)
mkdir -p ~/.desk
echo 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-…' > ~/.desk/keys.env
chmod 600 ~/.desk/keys.env

# 2. Portal + model gateway (one process; portal :8080, gateway :8100 on loopback)
node src/server.ts

# 3. CLI: users, passwords, budgets, instance ports, usage
node src/cli.ts user add alice             # prints her virtual key once
node src/cli.ts user passwd alice <password>   # portal login password
node src/cli.ts user budget alice 50       # monthly budget in CNY (or: off)
node src/cli.ts user agent alice 3301      # bind her dsh instance port
node src/cli.ts usage alice --month
```

Open the portal at `http://<machine>:8080` — each member signs in, sees their own usage, and lands in their own dsh instance. Admins manage members and channels inside the workbench (Settings → Members).

> Desktop app: for a standalone window, run `deploy/windows/dsh-workbench-app.bat` (Chrome/Edge app mode) or use the browser's "Install app / Create shortcut (open as window)". The shell loads the same web UI, so it stays in sync automatically.

The sidebar also carries WorkBuddy-style modules: **🧑‍💼 Assistants** (agent presets), **🧩 Skills & Connectors** (skill library reader + connector status), **⚡ Automation** (scheduled reminders, admin-managed).

Start a member's dsh instance with the helper (reads `~/.desk/agents/<user>.key`, adds `--trusted-host` for the portal authority automatically):

```sh
DESK_PORTAL_AUTHORITY=<portal host:port> scripts/start-agent.sh alice 3301 ~/desk-test/u1
```

### Autostart & management (systemd)

The whole stack runs as **systemd units** (portal + one unit per member instance; `Restart=always`), so it survives crashes and reboots:

```sh
sudo bash scripts/install-services.sh   # install + enable all units
sudo bash scripts/desk.sh status        # status | start | stop | restart [all|server|u1|u2|u3]
journalctl -u desk-server -n 50         # logs (same for each agent unit)
```

Windows side: a Startup shortcut boots WSL at logon, WSL idle auto-shutdown is disabled via `.wslconfig` (`vmIdleTimeout=-1`), and a one-time elevated task (`desk-net-refresh.ps1`) keeps the LAN port-proxy pointed at the current WSL IP.

### Workbench settings pages (dsh client plugin)

`plugin/desk-panel/` is a small **dsh client plugin** that adds a set of team pages to the dsh Settings dialog — **工作台用量** (my usage), **任务板** (team task board), **知识库** (knowledge base: search + note deposits), **公司盘** (shared drive), **成员管理** (members & channels — admin), **通知** (notification bridge + reminders — admin), **运维** (ops panel — admin) — plus a **📢 announcement board** pinned in the sidebar footer (announcements + member feedback, unread badge). Built on dsh's official client-plugin API (`settings.section` + `sidebar.footer.action` slots + `dsh plugin`) — **no dsh source changes, no build step, no npm dependencies**. Mount it per instance:

```sh
DSH_HOME=<instance home> node <dsh checkout>/apps/cli/lib/bin.js plugin --profile web add \
  file:<this repo>/plugin/desk-panel
```

Data comes from the portal's `/portal/api/usage` — open the workbench through the portal to see it. All surfaces (settings pages, sidebar panels, portal pages, the usage widget) follow the workbench language (中文 / English).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). This is a third-party project and is not affiliated with DeepSeek.

# dsh-agents-md — agents/*.md 子代理定义桥

把工作台的 `agents/*.md` 定义（Markdown + YAML frontmatter，正文 = persona）接入
dsh 的委派（subagent）体系：模型获得一个 `agent` 工具，按 `subagent_type` 把独立
任务交给定义好的子代理——**独立上下文、只返回最终结果**（跑在 dsh 引擎上）。

零依赖、零构建：纯 ESM JavaScript（只用 node 内置模块）。引擎助手
（`defineTool` / `settleRun`）在运行时从**正在运行的 dsh 安装**动态加载
（由 `process.argv[1]` 推导安装根，`config.dshRoot` 可覆盖），因此不需要把本包
装进 dsh 工作区、也不吃 npm 依赖解析。

## 定义文件

放在扫描目录下，任意文件名（建议 `<name>.md`）：

```markdown
---
name: code-reviewer
description: 代码审查：找 bug、性能问题并给修改建议
tools: [bash, read, grep]          # 可选：工具白名单（全局工具名）
disallowed-tools: [write]          # 可选：黑名单
model: deepseek-chat               # 可选：该子代理使用的模型
effort: high                       # 可选：推理强度（low|medium|high，适配器相关）
provider: spawn                    # 可选：spawn（默认）| fork（继承当前对话）
background: true                   # 可选：本类型默认后台运行
max-depth: 2                       # 可选：绝对委派深度上限（默认 3）
color: blue                        # 可选：面板配色
---

正文就是子代理的人设/系统提示词（写职责、口径、输出格式；知识放技能里）。
```

- `name`、`description` 必填；其余可选。
- 未知字段会给出 warning（防拼写错误）；有 error 的定义不可被委派（面板可见原因）。
- 别名：`maxDepth` / `disallowedTools` 也接受（对应 `max-depth` / `disallowed-tools`）。

## 扫描目录（优先级从高到低，同名先出现者生效）

1. `config.dirs`（显式配置，靠前者优先）
2. `$DSH_HOME/agents`（实例私有）
3. `~/desk-data/agents`（团队共享，容器内即 `/data/desk-data/agents`）

## 安装（每实例一次）

```sh
DSH_HOME=<实例> node <dsh>/apps/cli/lib/bin.js plugin --profile web add link:<本目录>
# 重启实例生效（host 组合插件）
```

容器版由 `deploy/docker/bootstrap.sh` 的 `install_plugin` 自动安装（`link:$repo/plugin/dsh-agents-md`）。

## 行为要点

- 定义目录内容变化（文件名/mtime/size 指纹）→ 下一次工具调用前自动重登记，工具描述里的目录随之刷新。
- 前台默认等结果；`background: true`（定义级）或调用参数 `run_in_background: true` → 走 jobs 后台任务（`job_output` 收取 / `job_kill` 停止）。
- per-def 的模型/推理强度/工具过滤/深度/persona 依赖 provider 能力；内置 spawn/fork 全支持，不支持时**响亮报错**而非静默忽略。
- 字段对应：`name`/`description` 同名同义；`tools` = 工具白名单；`model` = 模型；正文 = 系统提示词（此处为 persona）；`background` = 后台默认。

## 结算通知（可选）

子代理结束时，插件经通知桥 `POST <url>`（令牌文件认证）推送
「🔧 子代理「<label>」(<type>) 完成：…」。默认**只推后台任务**、目标路由按实例成员名推导
（`wechat-<成员名>`，容器即 `/data/desk-data/notify.token` + `http://127.0.0.1:8080/portal/api/notify`）。
可在 row config 覆盖或关闭：

```yaml
config:
  notify:
    events: all                    # background（默认）| all
    routes: [wechat-admin001]      # 覆盖默认目标（精确路由名）
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/portal/api/notify
    tokenFile: /data/desk-data/notify.token
  # notify: false                    # 完全关闭
```

## 调用方式（v0.3.0：自然语言）

对话里直接点名即可（助理按注入的系统提示精准路由）：

- 「让 code-reviewer 审一下 demo/app.py」
- 「交给 researcher 查一下…」
- 「@probe-lite 看下这个文件」
- 或显式：「用 agent 工具委派 code-reviewer，prompt：…」

`description` 参数已降为可选（缺省时自动从任务文本生成标签）。名字不在目录里或意图有歧义时，
助理会先追问一句——不会乱猜名字，也不会悄悄退回内置 `subagent` 工具。

```sh
node src/cli.ts user agent alice 3301      # bind her dsh instance port
node src/cli.ts usage alice --month
```

Open the portal at `http://<machine>:8080` — each member signs in, sees their own usage, and lands in their own dsh instance. Admins manage members and channels inside the workbench (Settings → Members).

> Desktop app: for a standalone window, run `deploy/windows/dsh-workbench-app.bat` (Chrome/Edge app mode) or use the browser's "Install app / Create shortcut (open as window)". The shell loads the same web UI, so it stays in sync automatically.

```sh

```

```sh

sudo bash scripts/desk.sh status        # status | start | stop | restart [all|server|u1|u2|u3]
journalctl -u desk-server -n 50         # logs (same for each agent unit)
```

Windows side: a Startup shortcut boots WSL at logon, WSL idle auto-shutdown is disabled via `.wslconfig` (`vmIdleTimeout=-1`), and a one-time elevated task (`desk-net-refresh.ps1`) keeps the LAN port-proxy pointed at the current WSL IP.

### Workbench settings pages (dsh client plugin)

`plugin/desk-panel/` is a small **dsh client plugin** that adds a set of team pages to the dsh Settings dialog — **工作台用量** (my usage), **任务板** (team task board), **知识库** (knowledge base: search + note deposits), **公司盘** (shared drive), **成员管理** (members & channels — admin), **通知** (notification bridge + reminders — admin), **运维** (ops panel — admin) — plus a **📢 announcement board** pinned in the sidebar footer (announcements + member feedback, unread badge).
```sh
DSH_HOME=<instance home> node <dsh checkout>/apps/cli/lib/bin.js plugin --profile web add \
  file:<this repo>/plugin/desk-panel
```

Data comes from the portal's `/portal/api/usage` — open the workbench through the portal to see it. All surfaces (settings pages, sidebar panels, portal pages, the usage widget) follow the workbench language (中文 / English).

**A self-hosted team workbench built around [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).**

Each member signs in with their own account and works in their own isolated workspace. The model API key stays on the server, and usage is metered per person — so a team can share one agent setup without sharing keys, files, or bills.

> **Status: building in public, early stage.** P0–P3 are done and verified on the LAN. P4 (delivery) is largely in place — `setup/backup/restore/logs` scripts, a one-page [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOY.md), and a green end-to-end [acceptance walk](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md); a from-scratch dry-run on a second machine is pending (the one-command Docker deploy completed a full from-scratch empty-volume run on this machine). The workbench UI is **bilingual (中文 / English)** — switch in Settings → General → Language. ## Quick start (Docker · any Linux server)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bugbyc0922/DSH-ANYWORK.git && cd DSH-ANYWORK
cp .env.example .env    # set ANYWORK_HOST (your access address) and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
docker compose up -d --build
```

## What this is

## Architecture (target)

```text
Member browser → Portal (login gate + reverse proxy)
                 ├─ /portal/*   portal pages (my usage / admin)
                 └─ all other paths → that member's dsh instance (HTTP + WS passthrough)
                        │

                        │  DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL → gateway
                Model gateway (holds the real key, meters per person, enforces budgets)
                        │
                api.deepseek.com
```

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Feasibility checks: multi-instance, launch flags, gateway interception, LAN access | 🟡 phone check pending |

# `third-party-backend` — the D-5 dogfood bundle A third-party backend bundle **as it would be published**: written against the frozen `tui.dsh/v1alpha1` `Backend` contribution family and nothing else — no `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency, no `src/` import, no host service. It is never published; `scripts/verify-backend-assembly.ts` installs it into a throwaway profile and drives the real assembly chain over it. What a bundle must get right, and where each piece lives here: | Piece | Why | File | |---|---|---| | `dsh.bundle.patch` | Only an installed package whose `package.json` declares it becomes a profile *layer* (`dsh.profile.bundles`), and that list is what the D-1 assembly reads | `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` | | package-root `dsh-plugin.json` | The declaration the host admits; it counts only beside the `package.json` that establishes the entry's package root (#1568) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | `contributes['x-dsh-tui']` with `kind: 'Backend'` | The writing surface: `apiVersion` + `kind` + contribution `id` + `name` + `spec` (`spec.id` is the backend id) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | handler export named `backend` | The registry's documented default (`backendExport` is in-tree only, so a declaration cannot name another export) | `backend.js` | | `spec.unloadExport` | Module-level/process-wide pools only; session-scoped resources belong to `session.dispose()` | `dsh-plugin.json` → `backend.js` | | `exports: { ".": "./backend.js" }` | Resolution goes through the entry the Loader's own resolver picks — an `exports` map that hides `./package.json` is fine on purpose | `package.json` | A bundle currently declares one backend: the fixed `backend` export must pass the handler assertion and carry the same id as `spec.id`. Multiple declarations are refused, as are manifests whose canonical projection rejects duplicate contribution identities. Entries awaiting authorization are not probed or loaded. The full field semantics are in [`notes/0009-backend-contribution.md`](../../../tui-profile/notes/0009-backend-contribution.md) and the seam write-up in [`docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md`](../../../tui-profile/docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md) (接缝十四). The published type face is exported from this package's entry (`BackendSpec`, `validateBackendSpec`, `backendAdmission`, …). This fixture stops at the picker: `detect()` says honestly that it ships no runtime, and `open()` refuses. Everything past the assembly chain — detection, sessions, catalogs, the install wizard — is a real backend's own work. `closeEchoPool()` is inert (there is no runtime to close) but counts its calls, and `echoPoolCloseCount()` exposes that count read-only. The regression reads it through the Loader's own module instance, so it observes that the host closes the declared pool exactly once, only for a backend it actually loaded.

# dsh-TUI > An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale > header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a > context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only > DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its > own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party > backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind. The prompt footer hides completed goals once the turn is idle; the Todo side panel retains their history. `Ctrl+Q` folds todos while working and hides/restores the idle goal/todo footer. Clicking its todo header also hides it while idle. Hiding changes only this display: a new goal/todo snapshot or session reveals it again, and `/goal clear` does not clear todos. Split diff cards give one-sided additions and deletions the full body width, without an empty opposite pane. Ordinary edits remain side by side, and mixed files choose their layout separately before folding or streaming reveal. Compaction status stays on one line in narrow panes: phase and cancellation hints yield first, then the label is shortened; elapsed time is shown only as a complete field. Image files referenced with `@path` use the same admission and resize/conversion policy as pasted images. Adjustment notices report the stored dimensions and format; required animation conversion is refused instead of dropping frames. Mention images and staged images still share count and stored-byte limits in source order. ## Highlights Panels without a verified Component identity are temporary: settings show their title and a distinct number for this run. Their toggles take effect immediately without being saved, and unrelated settings changes preserve that choice. Old `actN:panel` entries cannot be mapped safely: remove the placeholder and select the current panel again. Verified Components named `actN` keep their public runtime address; an explicit selection uses `component:actN:panel` in saved preferences to avoid claiming an old anonymous entry. The default reasoning-effort setting offers the current backend/model’s declared tiers, including custom IDs. Saved values absent from that catalog stay visible and stored; while loading or unavailable, only Auto is selectable. On DSH, Auto follows the saved `/effort` choice, then the configured effort, then the model default. Claude/Codex retain backend preferences for Auto at startup and for resumed sessions; explicitly choosing Auto resets the model default. Explicit settings changes affect the next request; unsupported preferences fall back with a notice and are never forced onto a route. Resuming a DSH session preserves its recorded reasoning effort (or its live selection when reattaching). The saved default seeds new sessions; explicit `/effort` and effort-default settings changes still apply to the current session’s next request. - **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task. - **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (API key / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`. - **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI. - **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, `bel`, or `windows`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. On local Windows, `auto` resolves to `windows`, the system's native notifications: a task-completion toast. The first toast registers that user's AppUserModelID under HKCU, the toast appears about 3 seconds after the task ends (the PowerShell cold start that buys the no-extra-install route), and for DSH sessions an enabled, active external DSH notification plugin in the running profile makes dsh-TUI yield to it (no toast, no bell); an installed but disabled plugin does not suppress notifications; if that AppUserModelID cannot be written, the notification falls back to the bell instead of going silent. SSH sessions keep the attached terminal's notification protocol in `auto` mode; explicit `windows` still selects the host's native transport. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes. - **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal. - **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals. - **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams. - **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals. - **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter. - **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. All eight built-in panels are enabled by default, and so are plugin panels registered later (`sidePanel.panels: '*'`; untick a row in `/settings` to switch to an explicit list). The header shows each inactive panel's symbol; hover to see its name. Narrow terminals and inline mode keep full-screen panels. In the `todo` panel a long goal wraps to the panel width with its phase on a separate row; when the content exceeds the viewport, focus the panel and scroll with `↑`/`↓` or the wheel (every todo is reachable too) (the compact goal row above the chat input stays a single truncated line with a hover tooltip). - **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Title, trajectory-strip and session-state animations update independently of the transcript and pause when idle or unfocused. Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details. - **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`. - **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor. `/btw` uses an overlay when its sidebar cannot render. Main-task questionnaires and the fullscreen draft editor take priority while preserving the side question and draft. - **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt. - **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires. - **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin. A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned. - **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more. - **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches. Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md). Plugin side panels stay enabled when unrelated settings change. Editing the enabled panel list still applies your explicit selection. Workspace side-panel counts match the session manager: the current conversation counts; empty logs, subagents, fork ancestors and archived sessions do not. Registered workspaces with no visible conversations remain at zero. Loading and read errors are shown separately; press `r` to refresh. When a DSH 0.2.1+ Agent moves its session to another directory (the `working_directory` tool or a Git worktree), the status line, Git branch, `@` completion, `!` commands, clicked paths, skill commands and loaded context follow it, including after `/resume`. The session stays registered under the project it started in. Relative paths in cards rendered before a move resolve against the session's current directory when clicked; absolute paths keep their target. Fullscreen mouse selection stays in the pane where the gesture starts, including chat, sidebar and either diff column. Diagonal, word and line selection copy that pane’s text; soft wraps join independently, source newlines remain, and divider drags only resize. ## Preview
## Featured & Listed Among the community plugins recommended by the **official lead of DeepSeek Harness**, dsh-TUI is the first. Featured by the **DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account**, listed in the [dshfind](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) plugin directory, and ranked **#7 on [GitHub Trending](https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168) daily** (TypeScript).

Featured by the official WeChat account

The `deepseek-official` API-key route needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. On DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+, the standard profile can instead use `/auth login deepseek-account` and select the separate account route through `/model`. Other supported accounts can sign in through `/provider` or `/auth` after startup. The primary compatibility target is DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`. This adapter supports its Shell API, V4 session messages, declarative presets, and profile-backed settings; older supported hosts retain their compatibility paths. See [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md). On DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later, `/settings` also selects DeepSeek Search / Fetch APIs and edits their endpoint and result limits, supporting custom Loader entry IDs and a masked API key input saved through DSH's credential store. It requires matching profile dependencies with `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 3.18.3 or newer; an incompatible schema stops TUI startup with repair guidance instead of showing an uneditable settings page. Older hosts keep their legacy settings scope. The `dsh-tui` section of `/settings` is saved in `~/.dsh-tui/settings.json`, shared by every kernel; the first launch imports it once from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (and an older host's `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`) (see [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md#tui-configuration)). ```sh # Install the CLI and this plugin globally (ships the dsh-tui command) npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui # Start (first run auto-initializes the profile; needs pnpm) dsh-tui # Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI. dst ``` Manual alternative: `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`. The repo's `sh install.sh` runs that step and checks the required commands. Afterwards `dsh-tui` and `dsh --profile dsh-tui` are equivalent. > **New-user note**: pnpm ≥11 blocks dependencies with install scripts by > default and reports `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. Updates skip foreign-platform > natives — the `@img/sharp-*` packages and the Claude SDK's per-platform > bundles — so only this machine's binaries are fetched. `/update` and > `dsh-tui update` write both settings automatically. An update never installs > the Claude SDK on its own: it enters a profile only when you pick that > backend in the kernel picker, which then installs the pinned SDK for the > running platform. No manual step needed. Details: > [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#pnpm-install-script-blocks-and-foreign-platform-natives). After startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never blocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade. It restarts automatically and resumes the current session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle, source builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former `dsh-cc-tui` package. ### CLI Automation: `dst -p "task"`, `dst run --json`, `dst session list --json`. The independent engine does not load the TUI or inherit its profile/preferences; it uses official DSH headless/services (validated on 0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3). `dst cli --help` lists its commands; `dst dsh ` forwards native DSH. See [Automation CLI](docs/cli.en.md) for protocol, limits, resume restrictions, and Node/Python/PowerShell integration examples. | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program | | `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · update the profile and align the launcher · pre-flight environment checks | | `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile | | `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install | Leading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch ` are forwarded unchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use `dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal prompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH directly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first `--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal prompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay and sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session. Safe mode: [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md). ### Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`) Bring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`: ```sh dsh-tui migrate # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing) dsh-tui migrate claude-code # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build) dsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run # preview what would land, write nothing ``` - **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable). - **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates. - **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up. In-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it. In-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow. CLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import. Full guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md). - More agents (pi, opencode, …) extend the adapter registry as adapters land; grok-build reads `GROK_HOME` when set. **VS Code**: use the integrated terminal or the `dsh-tui-vscode` extension. See [VS Code guide](docs/vscode.en.md). **Herdr**: run `dsh-tui` in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane; `idle` / `working` / `blocked` are reported through its local integration API. **Any terminal**: dsh-tui reports `idle` / `working` / `blocked` / `done` / `error` over the pty with [OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agentic inboxes that implement it can show what the session is doing; terminals that do not implement it ignore the sequence. Set `DSH_TUI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn it off. Bare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this launch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no last session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one that actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming a backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's source), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start, never another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume ` passes that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's "retry normal startup": it retries the kernel and session recorded in `last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold start — that retry is the last way back. ### Experimental: Claude backend dsh-TUI can also run its session on Claude: the same interface, driving the Claude Code CLI through the Claude Agent SDK. Your project's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, hooks, MCP servers and plugins load as the CLI loads them. ```sh # once, in the dsh-tui profile directory (the SDK is an optional dependency) cd ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-tui && pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.287 dsh-tui --backend claude # or pick Claude in /kernel; that choice is remembered ``` The easiest install: open the kernel picker (the launchpad "Kernel" entry or `/kernel`) and press Enter on the dim Claude row — the wizard locates the profile directory and installs the pinned SDK for you; the command above is its manual equivalent. The confirmation shows the exact package and version. Closing the wizard, including clicking outside it on the launchpad, cancels a pending installation. - **Sign-in**: a `/channel` relay profile, your dsh-auth `anthropic` sign-in (`/login`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or cloud-provider variables, or an existing `claude login`, in that order. A `claude` on `PATH` is used when present, then one in the native install directory under your home (`~/.local/bin`, or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows); every candidate has to launch and report a version, and the SDK's bundled binary is used only when none does. - **Works**: streaming, tool cards, approvals and questions, `/model`, `/effort`, Claude's permission modes (`/permission`, `Shift+Tab`), `/compact`, `/context`, `/mcp`, `/resume`, `/fork`, double-`Esc` rewind, subagents, background jobs, images, `/btw`, and the USD cost Claude reports. - **Not available**: DSH-only commands such as `/tree`, `/preset`, `/provider`, `/workspace`, `/agentview` and `/bg`. One process runs one backend; `/kernel` switches by restarting into a new session. - **Startup**: the screen appears before the session opens, with only a light profile composed (this package plus the profile's third-party plugins); see [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md#known-limitations). The DSH kernel starts from the same entry and loads DSH in the same process behind its first screen; `DSH_TUI_HOST_ENTRY=0` restores the old launch path for every kernel. Details and known limitations: [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md). ### Experimental: native Codex backend Run your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration, login, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads: ```sh npm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1 dsh-tui --backend codex dsh-tui --backend codex --resume ``` Protocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show drift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend. `codex resume ` can open the same thread after the other writer exits. This is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH. With native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the official background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed subscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes. Streaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and effort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP share the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex continues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and dismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying permission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex settings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers ChatGPT OAuth, a device code or an API key (the last writes to Codex’s own credential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed subscription tokens are only injected on first-party routes. dsh-TUI does not write `~/.codex/config.toml` or log out your native Codex account. A provider `env_key` from your own config (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) that the shell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref is stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so keep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed. When nothing can supply it, the session still starts and the reason is reported once as a start notice: Codex itself rejects every turn of that provider. For Claude and Codex, `/channel` tokens (`CHANNEL_*` refs) belong to the active `DSH_HOME` only. Disconnecting a channel cannot revive a token from the default home; reconnect it in the active home if needed. Provider `env_key` credentials retain the fallback described above. TPS includes hidden reasoning time and excludes tool execution time. Live text estimates are corrected when Codex reports output token usage. Decode spans of 500ms or less are excluded from TPS samples; token and cost totals still include all reported usage. Native browsing/archive, fork/conversation rewind (the first message requires Codex app-server 0.160.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-selection-actions A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI plugin: select any fragment of a conversation and turn it into a citation in the message you are about to send — or open it in a parallel chat. English | [Русский](#русский) ## What it does 1. **Selection toolbar.** Select text in the conversation and a small toolbar appears next to the selection: `Add to chat` and `Add in side chat`. 2. **Add to chat** stages the fragment in the current composer. The draft shows a compact `N conversation selections` strip with a remove control; hovering it slides out the staged citations. When you send, each fragment becomes a blockquote in the prompt — the model reads it as quoted context. 3. **Sent citations render as cards.** The transcript replaces the raw `> …` block with a card (quote glyph, excerpt, “Quote from the conversation”), so neither you nor the model sees a wall of markdown. 4. **Add in side chat** forks the current Session, opens the copy in the right Sidebar as a parallel chat and stages the same citation there, so follow-up questions do not pollute the main thread. ## Install The plugin is a bundle: the Host half is empty, everything lives in the Web client. Install it from this directory with the harness plugin manager (or `dsh plugin add `): ``` dsh plugin --profile add /path/to/dsh-selection-actions ``` Then reload the Web GUI page. It is a per-profile installation and survives restarts. ## How it works - `client.js` — the whole plugin (Web client half, `window.__ModuleLoader__` module): - `shell.overlay` — the floating toolbar next to a selection; - `conversation.input.dock` — the citation strip above the composer card; - `conversation.input.overlay` / host slots — not used; the strip lives in the dock seat because that seat renders reliably while the in-card overlay seat deactivated the entry; - `ctx.inputTriggers.registerSource` — a reference source whose `codec.serialize` turns a chip into the blockquote that reaches the model; - `ctx.uiConversation.userText.register` + `conversation.user.text.node` — the transcript card renderer. - `index.js` — empty Host half (`apply() {}`), so there is no Config and no Host-side settings. - `locale/en.json`, `locale/ru.json` — only `meta` (title and description for the plugins list). Button labels, counter forms and tooltips are registered by `client.js` itself for both languages. ## Known limitations - The citation strip is attached to the composer card from the dock seat (see above) and overlaps its top edge by a few pixels rather than being a child of the card. - The remove control clears this plugin’s citations only when the draft holds no foreign reference chips. - `Add in side chat` reuses the shipped `subagentchat` Sidebar tab, so the tab title falls back to the fork’s Session id when the Session has no projected title yet. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). ----- ## Русский Плагин для веб-GUI DeepSeek Harness: выделяешь фрагмент переписки и превращаешь его в цитату в отправляемом сообщении либо открываешь его в параллельном чате. - **Add to chat** — фрагмент попадает в композер текущего чата. Над полем появляется плашка `N conversation selections`: по наведению из неё выезжают добавленные цитаты, крестик убирает их. При отправке каждый фрагмент становится блокквотом в запросе — модель читает его как цитируемый контекст. - **Отправленная цитата рисуется карточкой** (кавычка, фрагмент, подпись «Цитата из переписки»), а не сырым `> …` текстом. - **Add in side chat** — форк текущей сессии открывается отдельной вкладкой в правой панели, туда же подставляется цитата; основная ветка не засоряется. Установка: `dsh plugin --profile <профиль> add /путь/к/dsh-selection-actions`, затем перезагрузить страницу. Host-половина пустая, настроек нет; вся логика в `client.js`.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-compound-memory

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-compound-memory.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-compound-memory)

English | [中文](#中文)

DeepSeek Harness bundle that launches the existing [compound-memory](https://pypi.org/project/compound-memory/) MCP server (`uvx --from compound-memory compound-memory-server`), mounts the bundled `skills/compound-memory` skill, and injects a short once-per-session usage reminder. It does not reimplement memory, it does not add a sixth MCP tool, and the server still has no LLM ([ADR-0001](https://github.com/chinwe/compound-memory)). This wrapper adds none. There are no install, lifecycle, or `postinstall` scripts.

`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` = `./cordis.patch.yml`. That file inserts three rows: the in-box [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/mcp/mcp-client/README.md) row (`mcp-compound-memory`), this package's own plugin (`compound-memory-rules` → `dsh-compound-memory` → `index.js`), and an in-box [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md) row (`compound-memory-skill`) whose only root is this package's `skills/`. Do not install that client yourself: DSH 0.2 already ships it, and a separately installed 0.1 client will not match ([discussion #8202](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8202)). This package declares no `@deepseek-ai/*` dependencies. The rules module does not import `@deepseek-ai/cordis` or the MCP client: Cordis calls `apply(ctx)`, and the [publish guide](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish) says to pin a peer only when the plugin must share that package's instance. `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` so current 0.2 prereleases match and 0.3 prereleases do not ([publish guide](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish), [market index](https://www.dsh-remote.com/notes/implemented/feature/2026-10-02-plugin-market-index-format)).

| MCP tool | Name inside DSH |
|---|---|
| `memory_search` | `mcp__compound-memory__memory_search` |
| `memory_get` | `mcp__compound-memory__memory_get` |
| `memory_write` | `mcp__compound-memory__memory_write` |
| `memory_link` | `mcp__compound-memory__memory_link` |
| `memory_feedback` | `mcp__compound-memory__memory_feedback` |

`memory_search` returns an object whose `hits` field is an array.

## Install

Requires the [`dsh`](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/) CLI and `uv` / `uvx` on the `PATH` of the process that starts `dsh`. The first `uvx` run needs network access to fetch `compound-memory` from PyPI. `uv` supplies the tool's Python; a system Python is not required.

Package version 0.1.6, published on npm as [`dsh-compound-memory`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-compound-memory):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-compound-memory
```

From GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:chinwe/dsh-compound-memory
```

From a checkout of this repository (the plugin root, not a subdirectory):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-compound-memory
```

Git install does not need `allowBuilds`: the package has no `prepare` script. Restart `dsh`. `dsh --profile web --dump-config` should show a `# == dsh-compound-memory` layer and the `mcp-compound-memory`, `compound-memory-rules`, and `compound-memory-skill` rows.

If the store does not exist yet:

```bash
uvx --from compound-memory compound-memory init
```

## Environment

Set these on the process that launches `dsh`. The patch reads them with `!!js` when config loads. Unset or blank uses the default. Nothing here is a secret. The stdio child starts from a scrubbed parent environment; configured `env` is merged on top.

| Variable | Default when unset or blank |
|---|---|
| `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` | `agent-dsh` |
| `COMPOUND_MEMORY_ROOT` | `$HOME/.agents/memory` (optional; the Python server expands a leading `$HOME` or `~`) |

`agent-dsh` is this host's stable id. Set `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` before starting `dsh` when this process should be a different host. A later patch layer replaces the whole `config`. To point `command` at an absolute `uvx`, restate the row in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (same fields: `serverName`, `transport`, `command`, `args`, `env`, `failOnStartupError`).

## Usage reminder

`compound-memory-rules` listens on `agent/pre-step` with `{ prepend: true }`. On the first eligible `enter` of a live agent (the decision is `enter` and the step signal is not aborted) it appends one user-role message. Later steps of that agent do not append it again. A new agent object whose session log already contains the reminder (resume, or this process restarted) does not get a second copy. The listener does not read the memory store and does not call a model (ADR-0001).

The message text is `RULES` in [`index.js`](index.js) (356 characters, under the 400-character Claude SessionStart budget). It states:

- `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` defaults to `agent-dsh` (overridable); pass that same id as `source` and `agent`
- `memory_search` before non-trivial work; `memory_feedback` after an adopted hit compounds the store
- in a repo, prefer project-scoped memories
- five MCP tools only, named `mcp__compound-memory__memory_*`; this package does not reimplement them

The source is `{ kind: 'plugin:dsh-compound-memory', form: 'instructions' }`, and the message has a fresh `id`. Session format v4 rejects the retired `{ kind: 'plugin', plugin }` wrapper and fails the whole turn ([discussion #8432](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8432)). `plugin:dsh-compound-memory` is the producer-owned kind the v3→v4 rewriter would derive for this package. A static `systemPrompt.section` was not required: pre-step accepts the message, and injecting once keeps it out of every later step.

### Disable the reminder

Stop only the reminder. In the profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`) or the home patch (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`), add:

```yaml
- id: compound-memory-rules
  disabled: true
```

A later layer addresses the row by id. `disabled: true` stops that loader entry. `mcp-compound-memory` is a different id and still launches `uvx`. `compound-memory-skill` is a different id and still mounts the bundled skill. `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-compound-memory` removes all three rows.

### Verify

`dsh --profile web --dump-config` shows `mcp-compound-memory`, `compound-memory-rules`, and `compound-memory-skill` under `# == dsh-compound-memory`.

Start a new session and send one message. The transcript should contain one user-role reminder whose `source.kind` is `plugin:dsh-compound-memory` and whose text starts with `compound-memory:`. A later step in that same session should not add another copy. `node --test` in this repository checks the listener without booting DSH.

## Skill

Usage for the five tools is [`skills/compound-memory/SKILL.md`](skills/compound-memory/SKILL.md). The injected reminder is the short hard rules. The skill is the long-form source. On a non-trivial task, call `memory_search` first. After a hit is actually used, call `memory_feedback` with `agent` set to `agent-dsh` (or whatever `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` is). Write only stable facts.

`compound-memory-skill` mounts that directory. The row names the in-box `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` provider, with `providerName: compound-memory` and `includeDefaultRoots: false`, so this provider does not scan project or user skill roots. `bundledSkillDir` is a `!!js` expression: join `skills` onto the directory of `createRequire(baseUrl).resolve('dsh-compound-memory/package.json')`. `baseUrl` is the DSH profile, so the path is the installed package and not the process cwd. `exports` includes `./package.json` because a map that only names `"."` makes that resolve throw `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. `exports["."]` is still `./index.js`.

After install or upgrade, restart `dsh`. `/compound-memory` loads the bundled skill. A manual copy or symlink is no longer required. One already on a skill root can stay. The registry keeps a single `compound-memory` name: within one layer the lower rank wins, and project or user roots (ranks 100–500) outrank this bundled root (rank 600) ([skills subsystem](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/skills.md)). The reminder does not load the skill, and the skill does not replace the reminder.

## 中文

这是 DeepSeek Harness 的 bundle，用 `uvx --from compound-memory compound-memory-server` 拉起 PyPI 上已有的 [compound-memory](https://pypi.org/project/compound-memory/) MCP server，挂载随包的 `skills/compound-memory` 技能，并在每个会话第一次进入模型步骤时注入一段短的使用提醒。不在 JS 里重写记忆，不增加第 6 个 MCP tool。server 内没有 LLM（[ADR-0001](https://github.com/chinwe/compound-memory)），这个 wrapper 也不加。没有 install、lifecycle 或 `postinstall` 脚本。

根上的 `package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch` = `./cordis.patch.yml`，插入三行：宿主自带的 [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/mcp/mcp-client/README.md)（`mcp-compound-memory`），本包自己的插件（`compound-memory-rules` → `dsh-compound-memory` → `index.js`），以及宿主自带的 [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md)（`compound-memory-skill`），它的唯一根是本包的 `skills/`。不要单独安装这个 client：DSH 0.2 已经带了匹配版本，另装 0.1 会对不上（[讨论 #8202](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8202)）。因此本包不声明任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖。规则模块不 import `@deepseek-ai/cordis`，也不 import MCP client：Cordis 调用 `apply(ctx)`；[发布指南](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish) 只要求在必须和宿主共享同一实例时才 pin peer。`engines.dsh` 为 `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`，当前 0.2 预发布能匹配，0.3 预发布不能（[发布指南](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish)、[市场索引格式](https://www.dsh-remote.com/notes/implemented/feature/2026-10-02-plugin-market-index-format)）。

DSH 里的工具名是 `mcp__compound-memory__memory_search`、`memory_get`、`memory_write`、`memory_link`、`memory_feedback`（前缀相同）。`memory_search` 的返回体含 `hits` 数组。

## 安装

需要 [`dsh`](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/) CLI，以及启动 `dsh` 的那个进程的 `PATH` 上有 `uv` / `uvx`。第一次 `uvx` 要从 PyPI 拉 `compound-memory`，需要网络。Python 由 `uv` 自己准备，不要求系统里先装 Python。

包版本 0.1.6，npm 包名为 [`dsh-compound-memory`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-compound-memory)：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-compound-memory
```

从 GitHub 安装：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:chinwe/dsh-compound-memory
```

用本仓库检出（插件根就是仓库根，不要指子目录）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-compound-memory
```

Git 安装不需要 `allowBuilds`：没有 `prepare` 脚本。装完重启 `dsh`。`dsh --profile web --dump-config` 应出现 `# == dsh-compound-memory` 层，以及 `mcp-compound-memory`、`compound-memory-rules`、`compound-memory-skill` 三行。

记忆库还不存在时先初始化：

```bash
uvx --from compound-memory compound-memory init
```

## 环境变量

写在启动 `dsh` 的环境里。patch 在加载配置时用 `!!js` 读取；未设置或空白才用默认值。这里没有密钥。stdio 子进程从清洗过的父环境启动，配置里的 `env` 再叠上去。

| 变量 | 未设置或空白时的默认值 |
|---|---|
| `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` | `agent-dsh` |
| `COMPOUND_MEMORY_ROOT` | `$HOME/.agents/memory`（可选；Python server 会展开开头的 `$HOME` 或 `~`） |

`agent-dsh` 是这个宿主的稳定 id。这个进程要当成别的宿主时，启动 `dsh` 之前设置 `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID`。后一层 patch 会整行替换 `config`。要把 `command` 改成 `uvx` 的绝对路径，就在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 里按 id 重写整行（字段仍是 `serverName`、`transport`、`command`、`args`、`env`、`failOnStartupError`）。

## 使用提醒

`compound-memory-rules` 以 `{ prepend: true }` 听 `agent/pre-step`。某个 agent 第一次合格的 `enter`（决定是 `enter`，且该步的 signal 未 abort）追加一条 user 消息。这个 agent 之后的步骤不再追加。新的 agent 对象如果会话日志里已经有这条提醒（resume，或进程重启后），不会再追加第二条。监听器不读记忆库，也不调用模型（ADR-0001）。

正文是 [`index.js`](index.js) 里的 `RULES`（356 字符，短于 Claude SessionStart 的 400 字符上限）。内容是：`COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID` 默认 `agent-dsh`（可覆盖），`source` 和 `agent` 传同一个 id；非琐碎工作前 `memory_search`；采纳命中后 `memory_feedback` 才让记忆库复利；在仓库里优先写项目作用域记忆；只有五个 MCP 工具，DSH 里的名字是 `mcp__compound-memory__memory_*`；本包不重写它们。

source 是 `{ kind: 'plugin:dsh-compound-memory', form: 'instructions' }`，并带新的 `id`。会话格式 v4 拒绝旧的 `{ kind: 'plugin', plugin }`，整轮会失败（[讨论 #8432](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8432)）。`plugin:dsh-compound-memory` 是 v3→v4 重写器会给这个包推导出的产方 kind。不需要改成静态 `systemPrompt.section`：pre-step 能写入这条消息，每会话一次也不会在后续步骤里重复。

### 只关闭提醒

MCP server 继续跑，只停提醒。在 profile 的 patch（`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`）或家目录 patch（`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`）里加：

```yaml
- id: compound-memory-rules
  disabled: true
```

后一层按 id 定位这一行。`disabled: true` 停掉这个 loader 条目。`mcp-compound-memory` 是另一个 id，仍会拉起 `uvx`。`compound-memory-skill` 也是另一个 id，仍会挂载随包技能。`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-compound-memory` 会三行一起去掉。

### 核对

`dsh --profile web --dump-config` 在 `# == dsh-compound-memory` 下应看到 `mcp-compound-memory`、`compound-memory-rules` 和 `compound-memory-skill`。

开一个新会话发一条消息。记录里应有一条 user 提醒，`source.kind` 为 `plugin:dsh-compound-memory`，正文以 `compound-memory:` 开头。同一会话的后续步骤不应再追加一条。本仓库的 `node --test` 不启动 DSH，只检查这个监听器。

## Skill

五个工具怎么用见 [`skills/compound-memory/SKILL.md`](skills/compound-memory/SKILL.md)。注入的是短硬规则；skill 是完整用法。非琐碎任务先 `memory_search`。实际采纳命中后，用 `agent` `agent-dsh`（或当前的 `COMPOUND_MEMORY_AGENT_ID`）调 `memory_feedback`。只写稳定事实。

`compound-memory-skill` 挂载这个目录。这一行是宿主自带的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`，`providerName` 为 `compound-memory`，`includeDefaultRoots: false`，因此这个 provider 不扫描项目或用户技能根。`bundledSkillDir` 是一段 `!!js`：对 `createRequire(baseUrl).resolve('dsh-compound-memory/package.json')` 所在目录再拼上 `skills`。`baseUrl` 是 DSH profile，所以路径指向已安装的包，而不是启动进程时的 cwd。`exports` 增加了 `./package.json`；如果映射里只有 `"."`，这次 resolve 会抛 `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`。`exports["."]` 仍是 `./index.js`。

安装或升级后重启 `dsh`，`/compound-memory` 就会加载随包技能。不再需要手动复制或软链。已经放在某个技能根上的副本可以留着。注册表里同名 `compound-memory` 只保留一份：同一层里 rank 更小的胜出，项目或用户根（rank 100–500）高于这个随包根（rank 600）（[skills 子系统](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/skills.md)）。提醒不会加载技能，技能也不代替提醒。

# aura-tools 0.6.1

一个包，两条路进 —— 读文件按意图取景、改文件按意图寻址，**逐字节保真**（前导 BOM 与每行行尾都不动），
改完还会**读回来验一遍**；区域在你读之后被别人动过时**结构化拒绝**，而不是静默覆盖。

## 一、一键安装（推荐：人双击，agent 一条命令）

交付包（zip）里除了本包，还有 `一键安装.cmd`（Windows 双击）、`一键安装.command`（macOS 双击）与 `install.mjs`：

```bash
node install.mjs --yes --json     # 人 / 脚本 / agent 都用这一条：非交互、幂等、结果机器可读
node install.mjs --dry-run        # 先看它要动哪些文件
node install.mjs --uninstall      # 撤销（只撤它自己加的东西）
```

它把包复制到 `~/.aura/pkg`、生成 `aura` / `aura-mcp`、把 MCP 服务器注册进检测到的 agent 配置
（Codex / Claude Code / Cursor，每个文件先备份成 `*.bak-aura-<时间戳>`），最后跑一次真自检。
只有手上**只有 .tgz、没有解压目录**时，才需要下面的手工路线。

## 二、手工路线（Codex / Claude Code / Cursor / 任何能跑命令的 agent）—— 不需要 DSH

拿到的是 .tgz 时（未发布到 npm）——先装一次，两个 bin 就上 PATH：

```bash
npm i -g ./aura-tools-0.6.1.tgz      # 或者项目内 npm i ./aura-tools-0.6.1.tgz（之后用 npx aura …）
```

然后接进你的 agent：

```bash
# Codex（子命令形状已实测：codex mcp add <NAME> -- <COMMAND>…）
codex mcp add aura -- aura mcp

# Claude Code（同形：claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args…]）
claude mcp add aura -- aura mcp
```

其它 MCP 客户端（Cursor / Zed / …）写进自己的配置，形状都一样：

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "aura": { "command": "aura", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

没做全局安装时：把 command 换成 npx、args 换成 ["aura", "mcp"]（项目内安装）。
**已发布到 npm** 时才有 npx -y aura-tools … 这种写法（本包当前按 tarball 分发）。

CLI 也可以直接调：

```bash
aura read  --file src/app.ts --mode map
aura edit  --file src/app.ts --hunks '[{"target":"main","replace":"…"}]'
aura --help
```

Windows / macOS / Linux 同一套命令（纯 Node，≥18，无原生依赖）。

**先读后改**：`aura read` 会给出一个 `version` 令牌；`aura edit` 会核对"这块区域在你读之后有没有被改过"。
观测缓存默认落在 `~/.aura/observations.json`，可用环境变量 `AURA_CACHE_DIR` 改（CI 里建议设成临时目录）。

## 三、DSH 用户（DeepSeek Harness）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./aura-tools-0.6.1.tgz
# 或：dsh plugin --profile web add aura-tools          （已发布到 npm）
# 或：dsh plugin --profile web add github:<user>/<repo>
```

装完重启 dsh。内置 `read` / `write` / `edit` / `read_image` **一个都没停用**：只加不减。

验证与回滚：

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep tool-aura     # 应看到两行
dsh plugin --profile web remove aura-tools
```

## 它带来什么

- `aura_read`（MCP 工具 / `aura read`）：`map` 符号目录、`digest` 接口、`full`、`around`、`lines`、
七种取景；65 种源码扩展名的符号表（由引擎语言表决定）；未索引扩展名自动退到整份内容。
- `aura_edit`（MCP 工具 / `aura edit`）：`target` / `lines` / `line_cue` / `anchor` 四层寻址，
  `expect` 断言、`dry_run` 预演、多 hunk 原子（任一失败则磁盘不变）、逐字节写回、
  区域级新鲜度闸门、落盘后整份回读校验。

## 已知边界

单 `\r`（老 Mac）行尾不支持（行号是跨层共享判据）；二进制文件两侧都拒绝；超大文件（>256 KiB）不进
观测缓存（此时回执带 `unverified_region`，闸门放行而不误拒）。

# Aura

[![aura-argus on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/aura-argus?label=aura-argus&color=2f81f7)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-argus)
[![aura-cardea on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/aura-cardea?label=aura-cardea&color=2f81f7)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-cardea)
[![aura-basetools on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/aura-basetools?label=aura-basetools&color=2f81f7)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-basetools)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f)](LICENSE)
[![node: >=20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-339933)](https://nodejs.org/)

[中文](README.zh.md)

Aura is a monorepo for independently installable tools. It is a distribution and maintenance boundary, not a shared runtime: each package has its own manifest, version, tests, and release cadence.

The shared constraints are deliberate:

- **Local-first.** No mandatory cloud account; data stays on the machine unless a tool explicitly retrieves a source.
- **Keyless where possible.** AuraArgus, AuraCardea, and AuraBasetools require no API key.
- **Agent-callable.** CLI, HTTP, MCP, and library surfaces are provided where they make sense.
- **MIT.** The code is readable, modifiable, and self-hostable.

---

## Projects

### AuraArgus — source-routed retrieval

AuraArgus routes a technical question to a registered official source, retrieves the page, extracts relevant passages, and returns an evidence bundle with URLs and scores. It also converts a URL into clean Markdown.

- 18 entities / 34 official sources currently registered.
- No API key, no per-call billing, zero runtime dependencies.
- Node.js ≥ 20; Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- CLI, HTTP, MCP stdio, and Node library surfaces.
- npm: [`aura-argus`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-argus)
- Source: [`aura-argus/`](aura-argus/README.md)

![Actual AuraArgus CLI output](docs/assets/aura-argus-output.svg)

*Actual output from v0.1.2, trimmed for display. The command and the retrieved passage are unmodified.*

```bash
npm i -g aura-argus
aura-argus search "SearXNG 对 429 的冷却时间是多少秒？" --json
aura-argus fetch https://docs.searxng.org/dev/search_api.html --max-chars 4000
```

MCP client configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aura-argus": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "aura-argus", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Scope.** AuraArgus is a registry-bound retrieval layer, not a general-purpose search engine. Unregistered entities return no evidence by default. Web fallback is opt-in and can be blocked by anti-bot pages. It does not log in, bypass CAPTCHAs, or generate an answer; the caller's model writes the answer from the returned passages.

### AuraCardea — DSH chat fold

AuraCardea is a web client plugin for DeepSeek Harness. It replaces the `conversation.chat.node` `turn-process` renderer and folds the intermediate rows of a turn — tool calls, reasoning, context injections, retries — into one row per kind. Category rows show success/failure counts and total duration; expanding a category reveals individual calls, parameters, output, exit codes, and image thumbnails.

- DSH 0.2.x web profile; Node.js ≥ 20.
- npm: [`aura-cardea`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-cardea)
- Source: [`aura-cardea/`](aura-cardea/README.md)
- Package shape: `dsh.bundle` with `cordis.patch.yml`, plus `dsh.client` for the browser half.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add aura-cardea
```

Then add the mount row to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: client-aura-cardea
      name: 'aura-cardea'
```

Restart `dsh web`. When the package is installed as a bundle through a configured plugin market, the bundle patch performs the mount automatically.

**Scope.** AuraCardea is DSH-specific. It does not add retrieval tools, alter model output, or provide a portable chat UI. It depends on DSH's chat DOM contracts, which can change between DSH versions; `tools/check-kinds.mjs` is included to detect new node kinds.

![AuraCardea in DSH: intermediate tool calls folded by kind](docs/assets/aura-cardea-ui.png)

*AuraCardea running in DSH 0.2.x from the published npm package. One turn's tool calls, reasoning, edits, and reads are folded by kind; each category row carries counts, failure markers, and duration.*

### AuraBasetools — byte-fidelity file tools for agents

AuraBasetools is a read / edit / write engine for coding agents that keeps bytes intact. Reads are intent-shaped — `map`, `digest`, `around`, `lines`, `search`, `changed`, plus a metadata-only `probe` — so a call returns the part that matters instead of the whole file. Edits address content (`old`), symbols (`target`), byte ranges (`handle`), or lines; stale regions are refused, and the file is read back to verify what landed.

- **Encodings:** UTF-8 (with or without BOM), UTF-16LE/BE, GB18030/GBK (including the 4-byte supplementary range), Shift_JIS, EUC-KR, Big5, Windows-1252. Writes go back in the file's own encoding and bytes outside the edit are preserved; ambiguous or non-reversible encodings are refused instead of guessed.
- **Structure:** 65 code extensions, plus documents and configs (`.md` with ATX and setext headings, `.json`/`.jsonc`/`.json5` key paths, `.yaml`, `.toml`).
- Zero runtime dependencies; Node.js ≥ 20; Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- CLI and MCP stdio; `aura-basetools-dsh` adds the DeepSeek Harness shell (`aura_basetools_*` tools).
- npm: [`aura-basetools`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-basetools), [`aura-basetools-dsh`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/aura-basetools-dsh)
- Source: [`aura-basetools/`](aura-basetools/README.md)

```bash
npx -y --package aura-basetools aura basetools mcp   # MCP server, zero install
npm i -g aura-basetools                              # CLI
dsh plugin --profile web add aura-basetools-dsh      # DSH plugin
```

**Scope.** AuraBasetools is a file layer, not a search engine or an agent: it does not decide what to edit, generate patches, or index a repository. On the DSH surface it sees host-decoded text only, so non-UTF-8 files are handled through the CLI or MCP. The strongest guarantee it makes is byte-level: if a file cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte, the write is refused.

---

## Verification

Last verified: **2026-10-22**. Network-dependent checks are not part of CI. The evaluation is a fixed internal regression set, not a public benchmark.

| Package | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| AuraArgus `0.1.2` | `npm test` | 51 / 51 |
| | `node eval/run.mjs` | 31 questions; 141 / 141 hard checks |
| | `node eval/verify.mjs` | 34 / 34 registered sources reachable |
| | Public npm install (`npm i -g aura-argus@0.1.2`) | 4 tools; `initialize` and `tools/list` verified; CLI `version` and `search` verified |
| AuraCardea `1.1.0` | `node tools/check-kinds.mjs` | 19 / 19 discovered kinds have a rule |
| | `npm pack` | 7 files; 23.7 kB packed |
| | Host import, client syntax, `npm install` | verified |
| | Public profile install (`dsh plugin ... aura-cardea@1.1.0`) | package resolves as `aura-cardea`; bundle metadata present |
| | DSH UI after restart | public bundle loaded; folded view verified (screenshot above) |
| | DSH MCP + web provider after restart | MCP `search` returned registry evidence; `web_search` returned the same official source |

**AuraBasetools `0.21.0`** (verified 2026-10-25): `node build/release-check.mjs` exited 0 (full suite; encoding 34, doc-map 45, probe 21 among the assertions), and `node build/post-publish-check.mjs --registry --version 0.21.0` passed 24 / 24 with the published files byte-identical to the local dist.

Two AuraArgus soft checks are intentionally disabled because web fallback is opt-in; they are reported separately from the hard suite and are not counted as passes.

The public packages were installed from the npm registry on 2026-10-22 and `dsh web` was restarted. The screenshot above is from that run. The DSH MCP `search` call returned registry evidence, and the DSH web provider returned the same official source. AuraCardea's UI is still manually inspected; no automated browser test is included.

Reproduction:

```bash
cd aura-argus
npm test
node eval/run.mjs
node eval/verify.mjs

cd ../aura-cardea
npm pack
node tools/check-kinds.mjs <dsh-node-modules>/@deepseek-ai
```

---

## How it compares

### AuraArgus: scope comparison, not a benchmark

| Dimension | AuraArgus | General search API | Keyless SERP | Documentation chatbot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coverage | Registered entities: 18 / 34 sources | Broad web | Broad web | A selected documentation corpus |
| Credentials | None | API key | None | Usually an account or key |
| Billing | None | Per request | None | Varies |
| Output | Passages with URL and score | Snippets with URL | Links and snippets | Generated prose |
| Strength | Traceable official-source evidence | Recall and freshness | No key | Fluent synthesis |
| Main limitation | Not a general web index | Cost, key management | Stability and anti-bot blocking | Provenance is indirect |

AuraArgus is not positioned as a replacement for general web search. It is appropriate when the question belongs to a registered entity and the caller needs citable passages from the official source. For open-web recall, a general search API remains the appropriate tool.

### AuraCardea: presentation layer, not a chat platform

| Dimension | AuraCardea | DSH default chat rendering |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | DSH 0.2.x web | DSH web |
| Intermediate rows | Folded by kind with counts, timings, and inline details | Shown as individual rows |
| Portability | DSH-only | DSH-only |
| Model behavior | Unchanged | Unchanged |
| Telemetry | None added | Not applicable |

AuraCardea does not claim to improve model quality. It changes the density and scanability of an existing turn, at the cost of coupling to DSH's chat DOM.

---

## Repository access

Installing a package does not require cloning this repository. For source inspection:

### Sparse checkout

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/Ck-epsilon/Aura.git
cd Aura
git sparse-checkout set aura-cardea
```

Replace `aura-cardea` with `aura-argus` or `aura-basetools` for another package.

### degit

```bash
npx degit Ck-epsilon/Aura/aura-cardea aura-cardea
```

### Package managers

```bash
npm i -g aura-argus
npm i aura-cardea
npm i -g aura-basetools
```

---

```text
Aura/
  README.md
  README.zh.md
  LICENSE
  docs/assets/
  aura-argus/          # retrieval: CLI / HTTP / MCP / Node library
  aura-cardea/         # DSH web client plugin
  aura-basetools/      # byte-fidelity read/edit: CLI / MCP / DSH plugin
```

Each package is independently publishable. Its manifest points back to this repository:

```json
"repository": {
  "type": "git",
  "url": "https://github.com/Ck-epsilon/Aura",
  "directory": "aura-cardea"
}
```

---

## Conventions

- **npm name:** `aura-<product>` (`aura-argus`, `aura-cardea`, `aura-basetools`).
- **Product name:** `AuraXxx` in prose and UI.
- **Versioning:** independent semver per package; recommended tags are `aura-cardea-v1.1.0`.
- **DSH packages:** declare both `dsh.bundle` and `dsh.client`; use `engines.dsh` for the supported DSH range.
- **No shared runtime:** packages do not depend on each other. A small amount of duplication is preferred to a premature shared abstraction.
- **No mandatory root workspace:** each package can be tested and released on its own.

Each package is versioned and released independently; see its README for the current version.
