evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Headless セッションのリソース解放 このプラグインは、rdsh専用のheadlessランタイムが作成したルートAgentのセッションのみを対象とし、破棄時またはプロファイル終了時におけるWebSocketの切断完了を待ちます。重複する終了通知に対して同一セッションを二重に解放することはせず、終了時には未完了の処理を待ち、元の失敗を`AggregateError.errors`に保持します。 対象となるのは、`@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.87.1`へ`rdsh`のheadlessランタイム作成手順で非同期終了APIを追加した構成です。公式pi-aiの`0.87.1`および`1.1.0`が公開している`cleanupSessionResources(): void`は、切断完了を返しません。この関数で代用することはせず、必要な`cleanupSessionResourcesAsync`が存在しない構成では、`RDSH_SESSION_CLEANUP_RUNTIME`によってプラグインの有効化を拒否します。同梱のheadlessパッチは、必須の`headless-runner`へ`rdshSessionCleanupReady`の依存関係を追加し、API検証と終了処理の登録が完了するまで実行を開始しません。パッチを適用せずにプラグインのみを導入した場合、プロファイル全体の起動拒否は保証されません。元の外部モジュール読み込みエラーは`cause`に保持します。 WebやDesktopなどのheadless以外の環境では、pi-aiを読み込む前に何も登録せずに終了します。正式Harness `0.2.1-alpha.3`のWebプロファイルにおける読み込みは、この非headless動作を確認するためのものであり、未変更のpi-ai `1.1.0`でheadlessの終了待機を確認した結果ではありません。既存のheadlessランタイム、インストール環境、外部ライブラリを、このプラグインから変更することはありません。 利用者向けのランタイム不足や終了失敗に関する文言は、`$DSH_HOME/rdsh.json`の`general.language`で`en`・`zh-CN`・`ja`を切り替えます。未指定または`auto`の場合は、`RDSH_LANG`、`LC_ALL`、`LC_MESSAGES`、`LANG`、Nodeのロケールの順に判定します。エラーコードと外部由来の元のエラー本文は変更しません。 ```sh node --test plugins/rdsh-session-cleanup/test/*.test.mjs ``` `RDSH_CANDIDATE`に新しい不変候補を指定した`node --test scripts/headless-runtime/test/actual-*.test.mjs`では、3言語での準備完了通知、所有セッションのみの切断待機、および必須API欠落時の起動拒否を確認します。正常に完了するCLIテストでは専用ループバックのWebSocket応答を使用し、有料APIへは接続しません。必須の依存関係を削除した独自の負対照テストは失敗し、同梱設定を省いたことによる有効化拒否だけを正常な起動防止と取り違えないようにしています。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rdsh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rdsh) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [日本語](README.ja.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## For AI agents Paste this before you ask an agent to work on this repository. ```text You are working on rdsh, a Rust launcher for dsh (DeepSeek Harness). - Native subcommands run in Rust. Every other argument is passed to upstream dsh unchanged. - A booted profile still runs Node.js, so conversations start and cost memory like upstream. Do not claim rdsh makes them faster or lighter. - Read AGENTS.md before editing. Do not touch credentials, published release assets or published tags. - Verify with: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo test. - Report only commands you actually ran, with their exit codes. ``` ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond process launch**: `rdsh --version` starts in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak RSS, versus ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh --version`. This is process launch only: a booted agent profile still runs upstream Node.js, so conversation startup and session memory match upstream. See [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. The design rationale behind this hybrid split is documented in [docs/PHILOSOPHY.md](docs/PHILOSOPHY.md). ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` Or install the crate from crates.io (needs Rust 1.85+): ```sh cargo install rdsh ``` `cargo install` builds from source and installs the same binary as the release archives. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users can also install the release [`.deb`/`.rpm`](#native-packages-deb--rpm) with `apt`/`dnf`. ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG or an Ollama API key for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Native Packages (`.deb` / `.rpm`) Linux x86_64 users on Debian/Ubuntu (and WSL) or Fedora/RHEL can install the same release binary with the OS package manager. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest) and install that file directly; no extra repository is configured. ```sh sudo apt install ./rdsh__amd64.deb # Debian, Ubuntu, WSL sudo dnf install ./rdsh--1.x86_64.rpm # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux ``` `` is the release tag without its leading `v` (`0.6.0` for `v0.6.0`). The package installs `/usr/bin/rdsh` together with the licence and README, so `rdsh --version` works right after installation: no Rust toolchain, no `install.sh`. Like `rdsh-linux-x64.tar.gz`, both packages carry the glibc build, so the musl archive and `install.sh` stay the fallback for older distributions. ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ### Package Managers (Homebrew / Scoop / winget) Advanced users on macOS and Windows can let a package manager own the installed `rdsh` binary. The manifests in [packaging/](packaging/README.md) pin the exact release archives and their SHA-256 values; [docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md](docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md) lists the install commands and the update procedure. **macOS (Homebrew)** — installs the Apple Silicon or Intel archive: ```sh brew install --formula ./packaging/homebrew/rdsh.rb ``` **Windows (Scoop)**: ```powershell scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/main/packaging/scoop/rdsh.json ``` **Windows (winget)** — winget 1.6 or newer reads the three manifests directly; submitting them to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` stays a manual step: ```powershell winget install --manifest .\packaging\winget ``` These channels track one release at a time, so a new tag is not served until `python3 scripts/update-packaging-manifests.py --version vX.Y.Z` refreshes them. ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh plugins status # essential plugins a profile is still missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # attach them after an upgrade rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Plugin provisioning (`rdsh plugins`) The essential plugin tier (the upstream tools absent from `dsh-base` plus the bundled rdsh plugins) only lived in `plugins/install.sh`, and nothing runs that script by itself: upgrading the binary leaves the profile manifest untouched, so an install can miss every essential package without any signal. The same catalog is compiled into the binary, so a release install can see and close the gap without the checkout: ```sh rdsh plugins status # read-only state per package, plus the fix rdsh plugins status --profile web --json # schema 1 for scripts and dashboards rdsh plugins install # attach what the profile is missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # web/desktop defaults also add the starter set rdsh plugins install --recommended=none # the essential tier only rdsh plugins install --no-bundled # no checkout: the upstream tools only rdsh plugins install --plugins-dir # or export RDSH_PLUGINS_DIR ``` Packages go through `dsh plugin --profile add ` (`RDSH_DSH_BIN` overrides the CLI), exactly as the checkout installer does. Bundled plugins are resolved from the checkout, and an absent checkout is reported instead of being skipped quietly. `rdsh doctor` prints the same gap for every initialized profile, and `--profile desktop` forwards to `rdsh desktop install`. See [plugins/recommended.md](plugins/recommended.md) for the tiers and the ids. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features and the privacy-sensitive switches (`discord`, `telemetry`) stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast, telemetry-free dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | SearXNG by default; `--provider ollama` uses `OLLAMA_API_KEY`; `--auto-start` starts the bundled local SearXNG compose service. See [Web search](docs/WEB-SEARCH.md). | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Command Code, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add commandcode --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # key from COMMANDCODE_API_KEY rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=` to keep the cache at a fixed location instead of the default, for example on hosts where `$HOME` is volatile. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Product language rdsh-owned CLI diagnostics and the native local page support English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese. Choose one run with `--language`, or persist it in `rdsh.json`; the default `auto` reads the first nonblank locale environment variable, falling back to English when it is absent or unsupported. ```sh rdsh --language ja settings show rdsh settings set general.language zh-CN ``` Precedence is `--language`, `RDSH_LANG`, `general.language`, then `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, and `LANG`. An explicitly invalid `general.language` stops the command without rewriting the settings file. Delegated `dsh` arguments, model output, JSON fields, files, and protocol identifiers are not translated. Interactive setup prompts and settings/policy validation use the selected language too. Authentication decisions and skipped-provider notes localize only the CLI presentation; their existing JSON strings remain unchanged, including malformed or oversized guard-input reasons. Native search continues to refuse unsupported non-Unix platforms before accessing the

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # rdsh-settings (test prototype) DSH設定サイドバーに rdsh セクションを追加するテスト用プラグインです。 デザインはDSHそのまま (settings.section スロットを使い、DSH変数で描画)。 ## 入る場所 - 設定モーダルの縦ナビに rdsh が追加されます - 順序は Models(10) / Built-in plugins(15) の次: order 20 - クリックすると、トークン予算、retriever/packer/verifier、goal、作業ファイル、未解決タスクを調整できます ## 画面の構成 設定画面は横並びのカードとして表示し、幅が足りないときは自動で縦に積みます。各カードは見出しをボタンにしていて、押すと本文だけを開閉します（見出しは常に残ります）。 幅640px以下では、rdsh設定の表示中は設定モーダルのナビゲーションを上に置き、カードと入力欄を1列に並べます。 実DSHでの保存・再読込と390px幅の[検証記録・実画面](../../docs/evidence/settings-mobile-anchor/README.md)を保存しています。 - 接続とプロバイダの共有（`search.dsh_search_provider` と `serve.port`） - モデル（`tokens.default_budget` と `compact.max_tokens`） - Discord Rich Presence（表示文・agent状態・プレビュー・保存） - 追加機能（context engine・作業記憶・長期記憶） - 詳細（全体設定・検索・セッション・ログ・サーバー・guard・bench・setup） 開閉状態はブラウザーの localStorage に `rdsh-settings-open:v1` というキーでカードごとに保存します。初回は「接続とプロバイダの共有」だけが開きます。折りたたんだカードの見出しには、現在のモデル予算・Discordの接続状態・context engineの状態などの要約を1行で表示するため、閉じたままでも要点を確認できます。見出しの右の「すべて開く / すべて閉じる」で5枚をまとめて切り替えられます。 見出しのボタンには `aria-expanded`、本文には `rdsh-group-` の id と `aria-controls` を付けています。色・境界線・角丸・文字はDSHのCSS変数（`--dsw-alias-*`）だけを使い、ライトテーマとダークテーマのどちらでもコントラストが崩れないようにしています。 ## 表示言語 「表示言語」で英語（`en`）・簡体字中国語（`zh-CN`）・日本語（`ja`）を選ぶと、設定画面とプレビューがその場で切り替わります。保存すると `general.language` に記録されます。`auto` はこの画面ではブラウザーの言語を使用します。読み込みエラーが発生した場合でも直前に選んだ表示言語を保持し、破損した設定で上書き保存することはありません。CLIや独立ダッシュボードにおける選択順は、[設定リファレンス](../../docs/RDSH-SETTINGS.md) を参照してください。 設定キー、プロファイル名、パス、goal などの入力本文、および明示的に指定した Discord 表示文は翻訳されません。Discord の既定表示文と稼働状態は、サーバー側で解決された言語に従います。`auto` では設定画面の言語と異なる場合があり、プレビューと反映確認には `/api/rdsh-discord` の `language` を使用します。空の `discord.details` は言語別の既定文を選択する指定であり、以前に保存された日本語を含む明示的な表示文はそのまま維持されます。 ## 保存先 - DSH_HOME/rdsh.json（単一の設定元。context・beta・全体設定のすべて） - 旧 DSH_HOME/rdsh-context.json は読み替え専用です。rdsh.json に context が ない場合（nullを含む）は画面に旧文脈を読み込み、全体保存で移行します。 contextを含まない部分保存では、未設定のcontextを新規作成しません。 旧ファイルを削除する前に、rdsh.jsonへの文脈の保存を確認してください。 - Rust側 `rdsh context build/search/status/explain` と同じファイルを読み書きします。 ## 試す APIにはDSHのGUIセッション認証とHost/Origin検証を適用します。 `connection.requestRejection` を提供するDSHが必要です（0.2.0-rc.2で検証済み）。 `webServer`と`connection`が揃った場合のみHTTPルートを登録します。 Discord連携はweb/headless/TUIの各プロファイルでも動作します。 サービスに認証APIがない場合、リクエストは503で拒否されます。 設定画面が扱わない既存キー（`extras.enable`など）は、保存時にも保持されます。 GETと保存応答は画面が扱う項目のみを返し、未対応項目はディスク上で保持されます。 設定保存のリクエスト上限は1MiBです。これには画面が返す項目の最大サイズを含みます。 Working Filesの空リストは明示的な指定として扱い、旧形式のファイル一覧には戻りません。 旧キー`context.files`は保存時に`working_files`へ移行します。 この読み込み動作を反映するには、Rustランチャーも更新してください。 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/rdsh-settings ``` 外すときは、プロファイルのプラグイン一覧から rdsh-settings を削除します。 テスト実装のため context engine は既定でOFF（beta.context_engine=false）です。 使用するときのみONにします。 ## Discord Rich Presence 設定 → rdsh → **Discordの作業状態**（英語では **Discord Rich Presence**）で変更します。既定ではONです。 新規設定時やDiscord設定が未指定の場合は、そのまま作業状態を表示します。 表示しない場合は「Discordに作業状態を表示する」をOFFにして保存します。 保存済みのOFF設定は維持されます。 Discordデスクトップアプリを起動し、Discord側でも活動の表示を有効にしてください。 共通のdshアプリ（Application ID: `1557873849280888903`）を同梱しているため、 利用者がDeveloper Portalでアプリを作成したりIDを入力したりする必要はありません。 このIDは公開識別子であり、Bot tokenやClient secretではありません。 独自のアプリを使う場合のみ「独自のDiscordアプリを使う」を開いてIDを変更します。 Application IDが未設定または空欄のときや、`rdsh settings unset discord.application_id` で リセットしたときは、共通のdshアプリに戻ります。 日本語の既定表示文は「dshで作業中」です。表示文、agentの状態や稼働数、経過時間を 個別に変更できます。DSHの `agent/status` イベントから「agent稼働中 (2)」や 「待機中」へと更新され、終了したagentは集計から除外されます。読み込み済みのagentも 現在の状態から集計されます。プロンプト、ファイル名、プロジェクトパスは送信しません。 表示文はDiscordの送信上限に合わせてUTF-8で128バイト以内に短縮されます。 設定画面には保存前の表示プレビュー、未保存の印、Discord専用の保存ボタンがあります。 Discordのみを保存しても、他の項目の編集中データは保持されます。 接続完了と表示への反映は分けて扱い、Discordから更新の応答が返ってから反映済みにします。 活動の共有をDiscord側で無効にしている場合、接続済みであっても他の人には表示されません。 「詳細設定」ではメンバー一覧に出す内容を表示文・agent状態・アプリ名から選択できます。 agentの表示をOFFにしている場合、一覧のagent状態は表示文に切り替わります。 共通アプリ名はDeveloper Portalで登録された `rdsh` です。画像は登録済みのアイコンを 既定で使い、「アプリの画像を表示する」でOFFにできます。プレビューには添付元のPNG `assets/rushDSH.png` を同梱し、認証済みの `/api/rdsh-discord/icon` から表示します。 Discord本体はDeveloper Portalに登録済みのアプリアイコンをCDNから取得します。 共通アプリの公開メタデータを最大1分間キャッシュし、App Iconの変更に自動追従します。 メタデータの取得に失敗しても、ローカルIPC連携は維持されます。 添付PNGはDeveloper PortalのGeneral Information → App Iconにも登録してください。 カスタム画像は Rich Presence → Art Assetsの画像キー（半角英小文字・数字・`_`・`-`）か公開画像URLを指定します。 リンクボタンは名前とhttp/https URLの両方を指定します。Discordの仕様上、 ボタンは他の人には見えますが、自身のプロフィールには表示されません。 画像やリンクを空欄にすると既定に戻ります。独自アプリで画像が空欄の場合は画像を送信しません。 送信は5秒以上の間隔を空け、連続したagent状態の変化は最新の状態にまとめられます。 OFFへの変更は待機中の更新を取り消し、表示を解除します。 Linux/macOSはローカルのUnix socket、Windowsは名前付きパイプを使用します。 WSLではローカルのDiscordが見つからなければ、Windows PowerShellを介して Windows側のDiscordに接続します。Discord未起動時は5秒間隔で再接続を試みます。 常駐サービスで`WSL_DISTRO_NAME`がない場合も、カーネル情報からWSLを判定します。 Windowsの実行ファイルがPATHにない環境では、存在確認済みの `/mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe`を使います。 設定をOFFにするかプラグインを外すと表示を解除します。 Discord Web版には対応していません。 設定は `$DSH_HOME/rdsh.json` の `discord` セクションで、Rust CLIと共有されます。 CLIからも変更でき、起動中のプラグインが5秒以内を目安に再読み込みします。 **Discord Rich Presence は既定で OFF** です（#585）。有効化するには `rdsh features on discord` または `discord.enabled: true` を指定します。 ```sh rdsh settings set discord.enabled true rdsh settings set discord.show_agent_status true rdsh settings set discord.show_elapsed true rdsh settings set discord.show_image true rdsh settings set discord.status_display state rdsh settings set discord.details 'dshで作業中' rdsh settings set discord.enabled false ``` 使うプロファイルにプラグインを追加してください。headless/TUIの場合も同じパッケージです。 ```sh dsh plugin --profile headless add ./plugins/rdsh-settings ``` 接続状態は設定画面に表示されます。認証済みGET `/api/rdsh-discord` でも `state`、`running_agents`、`started_at`（Unix秒）、`updated_at`（Unixミリ秒）、 `published_activity`（応答が返った最新の送信内容）を取得できます。 画面をスマートフォン幅で開くと、rdsh設定のナビゲーションが上部に配置されます。ホストの `data-shortcut-modal="settings"` を持つ設定モーダルに限定した調整です。 プロトコルは [Discord公式IPCの説明](https://github.com/discord/discord-rpc/blob/master/documentation/hard-mode.md) と [RPCのSET_ACTIVITY仕様](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rpc#set-activity)、 [Activityの表示フィールド](https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway-events#activity-object) に基づいています。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rdsh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rdsh) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [日本語](README.ja.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## For AI agents Paste this before you ask an agent to work on this repository. ```text You are working on rdsh, a Rust launcher for dsh (DeepSeek Harness). - Native subcommands run in Rust. Every other argument is passed to upstream dsh unchanged. - A booted profile still runs Node.js, so conversations start and cost memory like upstream. Do not claim rdsh makes them faster or lighter. - Read AGENTS.md before editing. Do not touch credentials, published release assets or published tags. - Verify with: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo test. - Report only commands you actually ran, with their exit codes. ``` ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond process launch**: `rdsh --version` starts in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak RSS, versus ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh --version`. This is process launch only: a booted agent profile still runs upstream Node.js, so conversation startup and session memory match upstream. See [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. The design rationale behind this hybrid split is documented in [docs/PHILOSOPHY.md](docs/PHILOSOPHY.md). ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` Or install the crate from crates.io (needs Rust 1.85+): ```sh cargo install rdsh ``` `cargo install` builds from source and installs the same binary as the release archives. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users can also install the release [`.deb`/`.rpm`](#native-packages-deb--rpm) with `apt`/`dnf`. ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG or an Ollama API key for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Native Packages (`.deb` / `.rpm`) Linux x86_64 users on Debian/Ubuntu (and WSL) or Fedora/RHEL can install the same release binary with the OS package manager. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest) and install that file directly; no extra repository is configured. ```sh sudo apt install ./rdsh__amd64.deb # Debian, Ubuntu, WSL sudo dnf install ./rdsh--1.x86_64.rpm # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux ``` `` is the release tag without its leading `v` (`0.6.0` for `v0.6.0`). The package installs `/usr/bin/rdsh` together with the licence and README, so `rdsh --version` works right after installation: no Rust toolchain, no `install.sh`. Like `rdsh-linux-x64.tar.gz`, both packages carry the glibc build, so the musl archive and `install.sh` stay the fallback for older distributions. ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ### Package Managers (Homebrew / Scoop / winget) Advanced users on macOS and Windows can let a package manager own the installed `rdsh` binary. The manifests in [packaging/](packaging/README.md) pin the exact release archives and their SHA-256 values; [docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md](docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md) lists the install commands and the update procedure. **macOS (Homebrew)** — installs the Apple Silicon or Intel archive: ```sh brew install --formula ./packaging/homebrew/rdsh.rb ``` **Windows (Scoop)**: ```powershell scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/main/packaging/scoop/rdsh.json ``` **Windows (winget)** — winget 1.6 or newer reads the three manifests directly; submitting them to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` stays a manual step: ```powershell winget install --manifest .\packaging\winget ``` These channels track one release at a time, so a new tag is not served until `python3 scripts/update-packaging-manifests.py --version vX.Y.Z` refreshes them. ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh plugins status # essential plugins a profile is still missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # attach them after an upgrade rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Plugin provisioning (`rdsh plugins`) The essential plugin tier (the upstream tools absent from `dsh-base` plus the bundled rdsh plugins) only lived in `plugins/install.sh`, and nothing runs that script by itself: upgrading the binary leaves the profile manifest untouched, so an install can miss every essential package without any signal. The same catalog is compiled into the binary, so a release install can see and close the gap without the checkout: ```sh rdsh plugins status # read-only state per package, plus the fix rdsh plugins status --profile web --json # schema 1 for scripts and dashboards rdsh plugins install # attach what the profile is missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # web/desktop defaults also add the starter set rdsh plugins install --recommended=none # the essential tier only rdsh plugins install --no-bundled # no checkout: the upstream tools only rdsh plugins install --plugins-dir # or export RDSH_PLUGINS_DIR ``` Packages go through `dsh plugin --profile add ` (`RDSH_DSH_BIN` overrides the CLI), exactly as the checkout installer does. Bundled plugins are resolved from the checkout, and an absent checkout is reported instead of being skipped quietly. `rdsh doctor` prints the same gap for every initialized profile, and `--profile desktop` forwards to `rdsh desktop install`. See [plugins/recommended.md](plugins/recommended.md) for the tiers and the ids. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features and the privacy-sensitive switches (`discord`, `telemetry`) stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast, telemetry-free dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | SearXNG by default; `--provider ollama` uses `OLLAMA_API_KEY`; `--auto-start` starts the bundled local SearXNG compose service. See [Web search](docs/WEB-SEARCH.md). | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Command Code, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add commandcode --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # key from COMMANDCODE_API_KEY rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact
