# dsh-nonead-universal-robots

**A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that lets you control Universal Robots (UR) collaborative arms directly from natural language, developed by Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd. based on the same logic as the company's own nUR MCP Server.** ([Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd.](https://www.nonead.com))

The plugin starts a persistent Python worker (which internally reuses the vendored `URBasic` library) and exposes robot control as **native DSH tools**: the tools talk to the robot through that worker, so after a single `connect` you can keep issuing commands to the same IP. Repository: <https://github.com/NoneadChina/dsh-nonead-universal-robots>

> ⚠️ **Safety notice**: this plugin drives a real robotic arm directly. Always keep the robot in sight, keep the emergency stop within reach, and keep the workspace clear of people and obstacles. Treat it with the same care as granting a model the `bash` tool. You (or the model) bear full responsibility for any motion command.

> 🛡️ **Motion approval gate**: the **53** commands that physically move the arm, run a program, take the arm out of program control, remove its rigidity, **overwrite/delete a program stored on the robot**, **drive a fieldbus device over Modbus**, **change the TCP / tool electrical configuration or switch digital/analog outputs**, or **push against a workpiece under force control** pause and wait for human confirmation before being sent to the robot:
>
> | Group | Tools |
> |---|---|
> | Motion | `ur_movej` `ur_movel` `ur_movep` `ur_movec` `ur_servoj` `ur_move_optimized` `ur_move_x` `ur_move_y` `ur_move_z` `ur_move_tool_x` `ur_move_tool_y` `ur_move_tool_z` `ur_move_force` |
> | Drawing | `ur_draw_circle` `ur_draw_square` `ur_draw_rectangle` `ur_draw_star` |
> | Programs & scripts | `ur_load_program` `ur_run_program` `ur_send_script` `ur_reset_error` |
> | Control mode / power / safety | `ur_set_freedrive` `ur_set_teach_mode` `ur_power_on` `ur_power_off` `ur_brake_release` `ur_unlock_protective_stop` `ur_shutdown` |
> | Force & velocity | `ur_force_mode` `ur_force_mode_settings` `ur_speedj` `ur_speedl` |
> | Tool & I/O configuration | `ur_set_tcp` `ur_set_tool_voltage` `ur_set_tool_output_mode` `ur_set_tool_communication` `ur_set_digital_out` `ur_set_analog_out` `ur_set_conveyor_tick` |
> | Program storage | `ur_upload_program` `ur_delete_program` |
> | Physical state changes | `ur_set_payload` `ur_set_payload_inertia` `ur_set_gravity` `ur_zero_ftsensor` `ur_motion_version` `ur_set_speed_scaling` `ur_set_conveyor_tracking` |
> | Modbus writes | `ur_modbus_add_signal` `ur_modbus_delete_signal` `ur_modbus_send_custom_command` `ur_modbus_set_output_register` `ur_modbus_set_output_signal` |
>
> Decelerations and exits (`ur_stopj`, `ur_stopl`, `ur_end_force_mode`) are deliberately **not** gated: they are how an operator (or the model, after a cancellation) makes the arm stop, and a confirmation prompt would only slow that down. Gating rules live in one place (`APPROVAL_OPS` in `lib/index.js`) and are asserted by `scripts/check-approval-gate.py` + `test/approval-gate.test.mjs`.
>
> In an interactive deployment (approval policy `ask`) a confirmation dialog appears in the UI. A call made without an approval service, without an agent, or answered with anything other than `allowed-once` **fails closed** — the command is rejected and never reaches the robot. The default lives in code (`config.requireApprovalForMotion ?? true`), so it cannot be turned off by a caller that skips schema parsing; set `requireApprovalForMotion: false` to disable the gate deliberately. `test/approval-gate.test.mjs` drives the real tool registry and proves all of the above, including that an extra `op` argument cannot re-route a call.

> 🧭 **Pre-flight safety gate**: a second layer that caps what a *single* command may ask for, independent of the approval gate. Limits: `safetyMaxStepM` (0.5 m — axis moves **and** drawing dimensions), `safetyMaxLinearSpeed` (0.5 m/s), `safetyMaxJointSpeed` (1.05 rad/s), `safetyMaxAccel` (2.0 m/s²), `safetyMaxDurationS` (60 s), `safetyMaxForceN` / `safetyMaxTorqueNm` (40 N / 10 N·m, force mode), plus an optional `safetyWorkspace` box (`"x:-1,1 y:-1,1 z:0,1.2"`) checked against explicit Cartesian targets — including the `center`/`origin` of the four `ur_draw_*` tools (and their `r` / `border` / `width` / `height` / `side` are capped by `safetyMaxStepM`). It runs **before** the approval prompt — an impossible request should not bother a human — and is **decoupled** from it: `requireApprovalForMotion: false` turns off the human confirmation only, never these physical caps; that requires `safetyGate: false`. A malformed `safetyWorkspace` **fails closed** (every motion op is refused) instead of being silently ignored. It is a guard against typos and unit mistakes, **not** a safety boundary (the controller's own safety configuration still is), and it deliberately does not cover `ur_send_script`, which is arbitrary URScript this gate does not parse.
>
> 📝 **Motion audit ledger**: every gated command appends one NDJSON line (`<DSH_HOME>/nonead-ur/audit.ndjson` by default; `auditLogPath` to move it, `auditLog: false` to disable, `auditLogAll: true` to also record unchecked reads) as `{ts, ip, op, tool_name, args, decision, reason}` with `decision ∈ {approved, denied, blocked, unchecked}` — so "what did the model actually do to the robot" is answerable after the fact. Writing to it never affects the robot path: an audit failure is reported, never thrown.

---

## Feature overview

**104** tools (`ur_*`) in total.

| Category | Tool(s) (`ur_*`) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | `ur_connect` / `ur_disconnect` | Connect / disconnect a UR robot by IP |
| Status | `ur_get_status` | One-shot read of TCP, joints, model, serial, version, safety mode, run/program state, voltage, current, temperatures, uptime, joint currents/voltages/speeds, TCP speed and wrench, speed scaling, plus `rtde_resync_bytes` (how many bytes the RTDE receiver had to drop to re-synchronise; `0` means a clean stream) |
| Pose | `ur_get_tcp_pose` / `ur_get_joint_pose` | Read current TCP pose / joint angles |
| Targets | `ur_get_target_values` / `ur_check_pose` | Read **where the controller is taking the arm**: target joint positions/velocities/accelerations and target TCP pose/speed, plus the matching actual values for comparison. Comes from the RTDE `target_*` fields, so it is free — and it is the only direct evidence for "command sent but not executed yet / being blended / held back by the safety limit". `ur_check_pose` answers the question worth asking *before* moving: is this TCP pose inside the controller's **safety limits**, and does **inverse kinematics** solve (is it reachable)? A read-only pre-check: the controller runs `is_within_safety_limits` + `get_inverse_kin` and the answers come back through output registers behind start/finish sentinels, so "the controller never ran it" is reported rather than guessed |
| Device info | `ur_get_robot_model` / `ur_get_serial_number` / `ur_get_uptime` / `ur_get_software_version` / `ur_get_safety_mode` / `ur_get_safety_status` / `ur_get_robot_mode` | Model (with a `remote_control` field) / serial / uptime / software version / safety mode / **safety and robot status bits** (which safety function fired, incl. violation / fault; the numeric limits themselves are not exposed by RTDE or the dashboard and must be read from PolyScope's Safety page) / run state |
| Programs | `ur_get_program_state` / `ur_load_program` / `ur_run_program` / `ur_stop_program` / `ur_pause_program` / `ur_list_programs` / `ur_upload_program` / `ur_download_program` / `ur_delete_program` | Program state, load, run, stop, pause, SSH listing, and **program file transfer over SFTP**. The three transfer tools each **verify what they did** instead of trusting that a transfer was requested: upload reads the remote size back, download reads the local size back, and delete confirms the file is really gone; a download never silently overwrites (an existing target is renamed to `<path>.bak` first, and a failed backup refuses the download). Their local paths are fenced to `programDir` — see "Local file access" below. `ur_list_programs` scans the real robot's `/programs` or the URSim `~/URSim_Linux-*/programs.*` layout (override with `programs_dir`); it reports `used_default_password` when no password was given and the `host_key_policy` in force, and an optional `known_hosts` file switches SSH to **strict `RejectPolicy` host-key verification** (a missing file is an error, never a silent fallback). Run/stop/pause check the controller's reply and report the run state |
| Operator messaging | `ur_popup` / `ur_close_popup` / `ur_add_log` | Talk to the person standing at the robot: show a **modal** popup on the teach pendant, close it, and write one line into the **controller's own log history**. None of them moves the arm, so none is behind the approval gate; the text is injection-checked (dashboard parses its commands line by line, so a newline would inject another command) and capped at 300 characters. Note that `ur_add_log` leaves a permanent trace on the controller — that is the point of it, so do not write secrets there |
| Modbus | `ur_modbus_add_signal` / `ur_modbus_delete_signal` / `ur_modbus_get_signal_status` / `ur_modbus_send_custom_command` / `ur_modbus_set_output_register` / `ur_modbus_set_output_signal` / `ur_modbus_set_runstate_dependent_choice` / `ur_modbus_set_signal_update_frequency` | Fieldbus I/O: add/delete the signals the controller supervises, read one back, set output registers and digital outputs, send a raw Modbus command, and tune a signal's run-state behaviour and refresh rate. ⚠️ The vendored `urScript.py`'s eight `modbus_*` methods are **stubs** (`raise NotImplementedError`), so these build the URScript themselves. ⚠️ Modbus writes get **no response** — all these tools can prove is that the URScript *ran on the controller* (start/finish sentinels), never that the PLC acted, so every reply carries `fieldbus_confirmed: false`; only `ur_modbus_get_signal_status` reads a value back (through an output register, behind its own sentinels). Signal names are whitelist-checked — they are interpolated into a URScript string literal, so a quote or a newline would inject script — and a read must declare `kind` because URScript is strongly typed (a digital signal returns a bool, a register an int, and one script cannot safely write both). The five write-side tools are behind the approval gate; the read and the two signal-configuration tools are not |
| Named poses | `ur_save_pose` / `ur_get_pose` / `ur_list_poses` / `ur_delete_pose` | A **local** table of named poses — one JSON file per pose, `<poseDir>/<name>.json`, default `<DSH_HOME>/nonead-ur/poses`: save the current pose (or explicit numbers), read one back, list them, delete one. The **name becomes a file name**, so it is whitelist-checked (Unicode letters/digits are fine, so Chinese names work; path separators, Windows-illegal characters, reserved device names and leading/trailing whitespace are refused), and the fence is applied after `realpath` — the same host-fences-it / worker-writes-it split as the program files. Writes are atomic (`tmp` + `os.replace`) and are then **read back and compared**; `VERIFY_FAILED` means do not trust the file. A read separates **"never saved" (`NOT_FOUND`) from "saved but corrupt" (`CORRUPT`)** — conflating them would send you off to re-save something that already exists. One corrupt entry never breaks a listing: it is reported per entry, with its file name in `broken`. ⚠️ There is deliberately **no "move to named pose"**: the numbers would be invisible to the safety gate and the approval gate until after the call, so the safe flow is two steps — `ur_get_pose(name)` then `ur_movel(pose, …)` — which puts the real numbers in front of both gates |
| Registers | `ur_get_int_register` / `ur_get_double_register` / `ur_get_bit_register` | Read Int / Double / Bool registers |
| Health | `ur_ping` | Check worker / Python / URBasic readiness without a robot |
| I/O | `ur_get_digital_in` / `ur_set_digital_out` / `ur_get_digital_in_bits` / `ur_get_digital_out_bits` / `ur_get_analog_in` / `ur_set_analog_out` / `ur_get_tool_analog_in` | Digital in/out (incl. bit-mask reads, and `which="tool"` for the tool-flange I/O) and standard analog in/out (**in engineering units**: URScript's `set_analog_out` takes a relative level [0,1], and `full_scale` may be set to 20 for a current-domain port). Reading a tool digital input is **sentinel-verified** — if the controller never reports the script finished, the tool refuses to give a number instead of reporting one it cannot vouch for |
| Tool config | `ur_set_tool_voltage` / `ur_set_tcp` / `ur_set_payload` / `ur_set_payload_inertia` / `ur_set_gravity` / `ur_zero_ftsensor` / `ur_set_tool_output_mode` / `ur_set_tool_communication` | Tool voltage (0/12/24 V), TCP, payload mass / centre of gravity, **mass + CoG + inertia matrix in one call** (`set_target_payload`, PolyScope 5.10+; unlike `set_payload` it does not reset the inertia matrix and leave the three parameters inconsistent), gravity direction (for non-horizontal mounting), force/torque sensor zeroing, **tool output mode** (normal / power dual-pin), **tool serial port** (TCI/RS-485 — ⚠️ enabling it disables the tool analog inputs). ⚠️ These are settings with **no read-back channel**: a successful reply says 「已下发（未校验）」 and carries `verified: false`, because all the plugin can prove is that the script reached the controller — UR accepts URScript only in remote-control mode and silently discards it otherwise |
| Control mode / power / safety | `ur_set_freedrive` / `ur_set_teach_mode` / `ur_power_on` / `ur_power_off` / `ur_brake_release` / `ur_unlock_protective_stop` / `ur_shutdown` | Freedrive / teach mode (move the arm by hand), power on / off / **brake release** (⚠️ the arm may fall under gravity), **protective-stop unlock only** (no power-on and no brake release — that is what distinguishes it from `ur_reset_error`), controller shutdown |
| Force control | `ur_force_mode` / `ur_end_force_mode` / `ur_force_mode_settings` / `ur_move_force` | **Force Mode**: the arm becomes compliant along/about the selected axes and keeps applying the requested force/torque. Arguments match the manual one by one — `task_frame` / `selection_vector` (1 = compliant) / `wrench` / `type` (1–3) / `limits` (compliant axes = max TCP speed, stiff axes = max deviation) / `damping` / `gain_scaling`. The script inserts the manual's recommended `sleep(0.02)` before entering force mode; exit with `ur_end_force_mode`. ⚠️ `damping`/`gain_scaling` cannot be read back from the controller, so the tool reports what it set instead of pretending to read the current value. **`ur_move_force`** is the assembly move built on top of it: one URScript program does `force_mode(...)` → `movel(...)` → `stopl(...)` → `end_force_mode()`, so the arm advances toward the target and stops at the workpiece. ⚠️ It is **not** the vendored `move_force_2stop`, which streams the wrench through RTDE **input** registers every 8 ms — this plugin deliberately has no send recipe, so those fields cannot be claimed here (claiming one makes the controller throw and kills the RTDE thread). Instead the whole motion runs on the controller, the start/finish sentinels prove it ran, and the actual TCP pose before/after is read back over read-only RTDE: "stopped short of the target" then means the controller could not advance further (which is what force assembly wants) — but it does **not** prove the force actually reached the workpiece, so the reply also carries `stopped_due_to_safety` and leaves the distinction between "held back by the force limit" and "stopped by safety" to you |
| Velocity control | `ur_speedj` / `ur_speedl` / `ur_stopj` / `ur_stopl` / `ur_wait_steady` | Joint/TCP **velocity commands** (`speedj` / `speedl`) and the matching decelerations (`stopj` / `stopl`). ⚠️ Velocity commands are **open-ended**: with `t=0` (the default) the function returns once the target speed is reached while the arm **keeps moving** — always finish with a `stop*` or `ur_wait_steady`. `ur_wait_steady` polls the RTDE speed fields rather than using URScript's `is_steady()` (which is documented to return false in force/teach mode) |
| Live telemetry | `ur_get_runtime_telemetry` / `ur_get_robot_voltage` / `ur_get_robot_current` / `ur_get_joint_temperatures` / `ur_get_speed_scaling` / `ur_get_tcp_force` / `ur_get_tool_telemetry` | Joint currents/voltages/speeds, TCP speed and wrench, tool accelerometer, speed scaling, robot voltage/current, joint temperatures, tool current/voltage, I/O current. **These fields are already in the 500 Hz RTDE stream**, so reading them is free and needs no reconfiguration. Single-value reads and the one-shot `ur_get_runtime_telemetry` summary coexist: poll a single value when that is all you need, use the summary for diagnosis |
| Conveyor | `ur_get_conveyor` / `ur_set_conveyor_tick` / `ur_set_conveyor_tracking` | Conveyor tick read / set, and starting or stopping **linear or circular tracking**. `ur_get_conveyor` self-verifies the script it depends on: the tick is only reported after the controller was observed finishing it. ⚠️ `ur_set_conveyor_tracking` is **not hardware-verified** — its signature and units follow the official manual, but tracking behaviour needs a real encoder-equipped conveyor to confirm; try it on URSim first |
| Motion | `ur_movej` / `ur_movel` / `ur_movep` / `ur_movec` / `ur_servoj` / `ur_move_optimized` / `ur_move_x` / `ur_move_y` / `ur_move_z` / `ur_move_tool_x` / `ur_move_tool_y` / `ur_move_tool_z` | Joint-space / linear / path / **circular** motion (`mode` 0 interpolates orientation, `mode` 1 keeps it fixed) / continuous servo / **OptiMove** (`optimovej`/`optimovel`: jerk-limited, smoother, less vibration — ⚠️ its `a`/`v` are **fractions of capability** in (0,1], not rad/s or m/s) / axis-aligned motion: the `_move_*` tools move along **base** axes and the `_move_tool_*` ones along the **current tool** axes (converted in the worker with a rotation matrix, so they do not depend on URScript `pose_trans`). Defaults are the manual's (`movej` 1.4 / 1.05, `movel` 1.2 / 0.25); with `t > 0` the duration takes precedence over `a`/`v` |
| Motion planning | `ur_motion_version` / `ur_set_speed_scaling` / `ur_get_freedrive_status` | Set the **Motion Version** (manual chapter 14) and the **jerk gain** (0.01–1.0, which only affects jerk-limited profiles: version-2 `movej`/`movel` and `optimovej`/`optimovel`). Version 2 clamps velocities/accelerations to the hardware limits while planning and **shrinks blend radii dynamically** instead of skipping the whole move with an "Overlapping Blends" warning. ⚠️ Newer robot models and PolyScope X support **only version 2**; CB3 has no such setting. ⚠️ Neither setting has a read-back channel. `ur_set_speed_scaling` sets the **speed slider** (`set_speed_slider`: 0 = stopped, 1 = full speed) — the most direct way to slow everything down before handing over a delicate motion. Unlike the other settings it **does** have a read-back channel (`target_speed_fraction`), so it reports `verified: true` only when the read-back matches, and `hardware_verified: false` because that mapping has never been confirmed on a real robot. `ur_get_freedrive_status` returns how close the current pose is to a **singularity** during freedrive (0 normal / 1 near / 2 too close — **not** an on/off flag), which is what tells an operator to pick another path |
| Drawing | `ur_draw_circle` / `ur_draw_square` / `ur_draw_rectangle` / `ur_draw_star` | Draw a circle / square / rectangle / pentagram. "Completed" is only reported after the script was actually observed running |
| Script / emergency | `ur_send_script` / `ur_reset_error` | Send URScript (**execution-verified**: sentinels are injected inside the function body / between top-level statements and read back, so "sent" never masquerades as "ran"; with several functions and no visible call site it refuses to verify and returns `verified: null`) / reset errors |

Every tool except `connect` takes an `ip` argument and requires that IP to be **connected first**.

---

## Read-only 3D digital twin

The plugin also ships a **read-only 3D digital twin** of the robot, rendered with three.js: the entry is a card in the **right sidebar's Start panel**, directly below the "Workspace files / New terminal / Browser" cards, and selecting it fills the right sidebar's content area with the live 3D view. The view subscribes to the host's **SSE stream** (`/twin/stream`, one frame every 100 ms) and stays in sync with the live robot's **joint poses, tool (TCP) coordinate frame and recent motion trajectory**. The twin is **strictly read-only — it never sends a command to the robot**: it only subscribes to the host's read-only routes and renders what it receives. A toolbar offers a reset-view control plus isometric / front / side / top presets, and the camera and base grid are framed from the model's bounding box, so a UR3 and a UR20 are both framed correctly. The numeric panel also shows the dashboard-side state (safety mode, robot mode, program state, speed scaling, joint temperatures, bus voltage/current), taken from the same route on a slower cadence.

The feed does not stall while the robot moves: telemetry is **pushed by the worker** at 20 Hz, and every twin frame reads that push cache first — **without touching the single-threaded command queue**, which is what a running motion confirmation loop occupies. On the wire a push is simply a JSON line without `id`, so an older host treats it as an unmatched response and nothing breaks. Only when the cache is stale (>300 ms) or missing does the twin fall back to an explicit read, and twin reads still use a dedicated **2.5 s budget with `killOnTimeout:false`** — a read-only visualisation read must never destroy the robot session (RTDE/Dashboard) just because it was busy. If a stall does happen, the stream emits `stale` events and the panel says "data stopped updating Ns · retrying" rather than leaving a silently frozen arm on screen. After a disconnect the stream reconnects indefinitely (exponential backoff capped at 30 s) and retries immediately when the window becomes visible again or the feed has been stalled too long. Set `DSH_UR_TWIN_PUSH=0` to turn the push channel off for comparison.

It follows the desktop app's colour theme: the panel's DOM half is coloured with the host's design tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`), so the toolbar, HUD and status line flip automatically with whatever theme is selected under Settings → Appearance (and with third-party themes) — **no JS needed**. The base grid lines and the fallback arm's material colour inside the WebGL canvas are repainted on a theme change by `src/client/theme.js`, which watches `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` (CSS cannot reach values inside WebGL). Theme detection only trusts that attribute and never falls back to the system preference.

Host-side routes (all fenced to loopback callers):

| Route | Description |
|---|---|
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/stream[?ip=<ip>]` | **SSE stream** (what the client uses by default): one full state frame every 100 ms, plus `stale` (this frame's read has not returned yet) and `frame-error` (this frame failed) events |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/state[?ip=<ip>][&detail=1]` | Live pose (joint angles / TCP / model). `detail=1` adds the dashboard-side state (safety mode, run state, speed scaling, joint temperatures/currents); the pose channel keeps polling independently and a failing detail query never takes it down |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/asset?model=<urXX>` | GLB mesh, with a content-hash `ETag` + `immutable` and `If-None-Match` → 304 support |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/models` | The model list actually present locally |

Failure responses carry a **machine-readable `code`** (`no_robot` / `robot_not_connected` / `ambiguous_robot` / `worker_unavailable` / `robot_error`) and echo the resolved `ip`, so the UI can say which of four very different failures happened. A read that is only **temporarily** unavailable (most often because the worker is busy executing a motion command) is not reported as `robot_error`: the host replays the last known reading with `stale:true` (for up to 30 s), so the twin keeps its picture and says the data is stale. A replayed frame never carries approval state — `pending_motion` is re-read live, so a finished approval cannot keep being drawn as a ghost target.

---

## Install into a DSH profile

> 📦 **Not published to npm (yet)**, so there is no version range to write into `dependencies`. Install from the plugin market / plugin page or from this repository (a local checkout or its GitHub URL).

### Option 1 — plugin market / plugin page (GUI)

The plugin is listed in the DSH plugin market as `dsh-nonead-universal-robots`. Open **Settings → Plugin market** (or the sidebar **Plugins** page), find it and install.

Two things to know:

- The market refuses to install **while an agent is running** ("installing changes plugin files, so a working agent can fail mid-turn"). Finish or cancel the running turn first.
- The market installs from the entry's GitHub URL, and pnpm fetches `github:` sources as a tarball from `codeload.github.com`. On a slow or filtered network that download can time out; the CLI route below avoids it entirely.

### Option 2 — CLI, from a local checkout (recommended for development)

```sh
# DSH Desktop ships a CLI wrapper per profile:
#   %APPDATA%\<app>\host-commands\<profile>\generations\<hash>\bin\dsh.cmd
dsh.cmd plugin add "file:D:/path/to/dsh-nonead-universal-robots"
# (the wrapper adds --profile <profile> itself; on other setups use `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <spec>`)
```

This is the same path the plugin page uses: it writes the dependency **and** the `dsh.profile.bundles` entry, and the plugin is hot-loaded into running sessions (no restart needed — the `ur_*` tools appear immediately).

⚠️ A `file:` install is a **copy**, not a symlink: **editing the checkout does not affect the installed plugin** — re-run the command after changing the source.

### Option 3 — as a bundle, by hand

1. Add the plugin to your target profile's `package.json`:

   ```jsonc
   // <DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/package.json
   {
     "dependencies": {
       "dsh-nonead-universal-robots": "file:D:/path/to/dsh-nonead-universal-robots"
       // or, once GitHub is reachable: "github:NoneadChina/dsh-nonead-universal-robots"
     },
     "dsh": {
       "profile": {
         "bundles": [               // add the plugin here (later order is fine)
           "...",
           "dsh-nonead-universal-robots"
         ]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. Install dependencies via `dsh plugin` (equivalent to running pnpm inside the profile directory):

   ```sh
   dsh plugin --profile <profile> install
   # or: cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>" && pnpm install
   ```

3. Restart DSH. The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin line into the config tree, and the tools appear in the model's tool list as `ur_*`.

---

## Python runtime

The plugin needs a usable Python with `numpy` and `paramiko` to start the worker:

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

> ⚠️ **Install those dependencies for the interpreter the worker actually uses.** `lib/worker.js`
> points `PYTHONPATH` at the plugin's `python/` directory, and CPython imports `sitecustomize.py`
> from there at startup if it exists — so a machine-local `sitecustomize.py` that pokes a user-level
> `site-packages` into `sys.path` "works" on one machine and fails everywhere else. Point `pythonBin`
> at an interpreter (or a venv) that has the dependencies.

`pythonBin` (default `python`), `commandTimeoutMs` (motion/script timeout, default `60000`) and `connectTimeoutMs` (first-connect timeout, default `30000`) are configurable in `cordis.patch.yml`. If `python` is not on PATH, use an absolute path, e.g. `"C:\\Python312\\python.exe"` or `"/usr/bin/python3"`. `ur_ping` / `npm run test:python` is the self-check for this chain.

---

## Health check / testing

Verify the plugin and Python runtime without touching a real robot:

```sh
npm run test:python   # python ur_worker.py --selfcheck: verify Python/numpy/paramiko/URBasic/RTDE config
npm test              # 56 items: all 42 test files + 9 gates + 5 offline probes, then a summary
npm run test:node     # Node side only: skip the test files *and* the gates that need Python
npm run check         # all static + cross-language gates without running the test files
npm run verify:host   # validate every tool schema through the host's real value-schema DSL, plus peer ranges
npm run verify:models # validate the structural contract of the 14 GLBs
```

`npm test` runs two kinds of thing, and both must pass:

- **42 test files** under `test/` (end-to-end protocol self-check, approval gate, twin routes, client state machine, FK, vendored-library regressions) — enumerated from `test/test-manifest.json`, which `check:manifest` keeps honest so a Python-using file can never be silently unlisted.
- **9 check gates** plus **5 offline probes**: `check-test-manifest` / `check-package-metadata` / `check-client-bundle` / `check-doc-tools` (Node) and `check-worker-ops` / `check-tool-params` / `check-rtde-recipe` / `check-approval-gate` / `check-new-ops` (Python), then the `scripts/probe-*.mjs` twin/SSE probes.
- The **host compatibility check** is also attempted (`check-host-compat --allow-missing-host`). It is an *environment* check, so it is reported on its own summary line and **excluded from the 56-item count**: a machine without DSH Desktop gets a loud `SKIP` with the reason, never a silent pass; a machine (or CI) that provides a host turns it into `PASS — 宿主真实 value-schema DSL 校验通过`.

**Skipped is not green.** A run with any skipped

# deep-learning

LearnHarness's learning loop, ported natively into the
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) as a
plugin: **measure, plan, teach, practice** — plus the persistent
knowledge graph, background research, and a practice mode.

Ported from [amosblomqvist/learnharness](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness)
(AGPL-3.0). This repository keeps that license and attributes the original
in [NOTICE](NOTICE). The teaching methodology — probe the learner's edge,
plan a dependency map, teach one reasoning step at a time, practice in
fresh surfaces — is carried verbatim in the prompt library under
[`prompts/`](prompts/); see the original's
[teaching methodology doc](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness/blob/main/docs/teaching-methodology.md)
for the theory behind it.

## How it works

1. **Measure.** The prober finds where your understanding ends on each
   strand the lesson depends on. Your answers, confidence, and
   think-out-loud notes tell it where to start.
2. **Plan.** The teacher authors a dependency map from that starting
   point to your goal (`plan_init`). The map lives beside the lesson and
   adapts when your understanding turns out different.
3. **Teach.** Each step builds on something you already hold. You
   predict, get the explanation, and check your understanding — checks
   with a wrong answer are repaired before anything is built on them.
4. **Practice.** Practice sessions pose problems that require the right
   knowledge to come to mind without being named first. Problems and
   hints adapt to your thinking.

**Think out loud.** Every question carries a thinking field — your
reasoning, uncertainties, and reactions in your own words. This is how
the teacher gets a detailed picture rather than a record of right and
wrong answers.

**The graph carries it forward.** What you are taught accumulates as
propositions and reasoning chains in a knowledge graph you can inspect
(plain files under `~/.dsh/deep-learning/graph/`). Future sessions read
the graph instead of starting from scratch; practice draws from it; the
Learning panel renders it. Import your own notes into the same graph.

## Install

Requirements: a DeepSeek Harness installation (`dsh`) with the `web`
profile, and one configured model route (any provider the harness
supports).

**From this repository (profile link):**

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web
pnpm add link:/path/to/deep-learning
# or, with the npm workflow:
npm install /path/to/deep-learning
```

Then add `"deep-learning"` to the `dsh.profile.bundles` list in
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` and restart:

```bash
dsh web
```

The Learning panel appears in the sidebar; the "Deep Learning" section
appears in Settings.

**From npm (once published):** `dsh plugin --profile web add deep-learning`.

## Usage

### Start a teaching session

Open the **Learning** panel → *new session* → pick **teach** → describe
what you want to understand → *start session*. The conversation begins
with the probe; answer in the question cards (options, a thinking field,
a confidence ladder). When the probe concludes you'll see your
assessment, then the plan map, then teaching begins.

Everything the model says or asks is inspectable and editable:

- **Prompts**: the fragment files under the package's `prompts/` directory
  are the system prompts. Copy any segment you want to change to
  `~/.dsh/deep-learning/prompts/<agent>/<file>.md` (same layout) and flip
  its switch in Settings → Deep Learning.
- **Data**: every learning record is a plain file under
  `~/.dsh/deep-learning/` — open them, back them up, grep them.

### Practice

Learning panel → *new session* → **practice** → describe what you want
to practice. Problems arrive one at a time; submit your working or your
answer; ask for a nudge when stuck; say "next problem" to move on.

### The graph

The Learning panel's **graph** view shows propositions (squares) and
arguments (junction dots) — drag to pan, scroll to zoom, click a node
for its statement. The **chains** view is the table of every reasoning
chain with its birth session. *import notes* pastes any text into the
graph through the same extraction pipeline the sessions use.

### Settings

Settings → **Deep Learning**:

| Setting | What it pins |
|---|---|
| model slots (strong / cheap / vision) | The default tiers conversation and background roles fall back to |
| role overrides (researcher, demo builder, visual maker, pdf reader, extractor, auditor) | A specific model for one role |
| quizzing mechanic | Multiple choice (probe/quiz) or free recall (recall/explain) |
| extraction chunk budget | Tokens per background extraction batch (floor 500) |
| prompt override switches | Which of your edited prompt segments go live |

## How model roles map to harness settings

The plugin never hardcodes a model. Every model call resolves through
the harness's own model configuration:

| Role | What it does | Where its model comes from |
|---|---|---|
| prober / teacher | The conversation (probe questions, planning, teaching) | **The session's model** — pick it with the harness's per-session model selector; nothing here overrides your choice |
| practice agent | Practice problem posing, hints, verdicts | The session's model (same rule) |
| researcher | Web research briefs (via the harness's web_search / web_fetch) | *researcher override* → else the **cheap** slot |
| demo builder | Interactive single-file HTML teaching instruments | *demoBuilder override* → else the cheap slot |
| visual maker | Precise SVG figures | *visualMaker override* → else the **vision** slot |
| pdf reader | Cited briefs over learner PDFs | *pdfReader override* → else the vision slot |
| extractor | Propositions + reasoning chains from your teaching (background) | *extractor override* → else the cheap slot |
| auditor | Identity verdicts merging new findings into the graph (background) | *auditor override* → else the cheap slot |

Unset pins degrade honestly: the Learning panel says what's missing, and
the feature that needs the role refuses with a clear message instead of
guessing.

The strong/cheap/vision slots exist so one settings edit can retune a
whole tier; per-role overrides win when set. Provider credentials, model
catalogs, streaming, retries, and cost metering all belong to the
harness (the Models page) — this plugin only names *which* model each
role uses.

## Development

```bash
npm install        # once (the harness peers symlink from the dsh install)
npm run build      # tsc (server) + esbuild (client bundle)
npm test           # deterministic suite: no network, no LLM, no filesystem writes outside temp dirs
npm run typecheck  # all three tsconfigs
```

Test layout mirrors the original's strata: pure core units (merger,
derivation, coverage, grading, plan parsing, phases, layout), pipeline
flows with scripted fake LLMs, and golden fixtures pinning the real
on-disk format (regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/regen-golden.ts`;
update fixtures in the same commit as any format change).

## License

[AGPL-3.0-only](LICENSE) — see [NOTICE](NOTICE) for the attribution to
amosblomqvist/learnharness and dependency license notes.

dsh-mnemon

English · 简体中文

Composable, view-based context for DeepSeek Harness.

Pluggable sources and strategies, with layered memory and self-evolving skills out of the box.

Install and start · Watch the demo · Documentation · Build a plugin

## Why dsh-mnemon An Agent that starts every session from scratch keeps asking what it was already told. Putting everything into one memory store is no better: it either floods each turn or misses what matters. dsh-mnemon gives DeepSeek Harness memory that is layered, visible and composable, and skills that improve with use. - **The right memory for each turn.** Preferences and working facts stay in context. Project documents and long-term evidence are searched only when a question needs them. - **You can see what a turn used.** Under each reply, the turn memory bar lists the documents and memories the turn read and wrote, and one click opens each in the Memory System. The Memory System shows everything that is stored and lets you edit it. - **Save to memory in one click.** When a conversation turns up a fact worth keeping, the brain mark under the reply hands it to a task Agent, which removes duplicates, distils it and writes it to the right Memory Space, or saves it where you choose: working memory, your profile or a Memory Space. The receipt says where it went. - **Skills that improve with use.** Skills keeps every DSH skill in one place. It can review your real conversations, draft a better `SKILL.md` and backtest it before you adopt it, and it installs more skills from skills.sh, GitHub and sites that publish Agent Skills. - **Compose it on the Plugins page.** Choose a main strategy and optional enhancements, and switch them without moving any data. Every component has its own page for its settings. - **Keep data where you want it.** Local by default with Mnemon Native, or one of eight third-party Providers. Storage can be global, per workspace, centralized or in a directory you choose, with ZIP backup. - **Extend it.** Sources and Strategies are ordinary DSH plugins built on public SDKs. An installed component gets the same pages and switches as the shipped ones. ## See it in action These recordings come from a real WebUI with the live DeepSeek model answering, on a seeded, fictional project, Lumen. Waits for the model play faster, marked in the lower right corner. **Save a new fact to memory.** A reply reports a new measurement. Select the brain mark under it, cut the candidate down to the sentence worth keeping and send it to the task Agent; the receipt names the Memory Space it went to and opens it in one click.

**See all memory in one place.** Status, runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces live in the Memory System. The graph links memories through the entities they mention, and Ask Agent answers with the memories it cites, by content.

**Compose memory on the Plugins page.** One main strategy, its memory sources and optional enhancements, each switch applying at once. Every component has its own page, and storage, backup and interface settings live here too.

Every step is explained in the [UI guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/ui-guide.md); all screens, recordings and the capture environment are in the [v0.5.32 gallery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/assets/webui-v0.5.32/README.md). ## Three kinds of memory | Memory | Keep here | How it reaches the Agent | |---|---|---| | **Runtime memory** | Preferences, working agreements, facts needed on the next turn | Injected every turn as compact USER.md and MEMORY.md | | **Project Documents** | Designs, investigations, procedures and handoffs | Searched first, then read when relevant | | **Memory Spaces** | Durable facts, decisions, entities and their relationships | Recalled on demand from the enabled Providers | The default **Layered strategy** keeps runtime memory resident and reads the other two on demand. The **General strategy** offers every available source within one budget and lets the model decide how to use each. A **memory space** is one named, Provider-backed scope for long-term evidence; the Chinese product term is 记忆空间. ## Skills that improve with use **Skills** is an experimental component for the `SKILL.md` skills DSH loads from your project and your home folder. Its page sits in the Memory System, or in the sidebar on its own. | A turn's review suggests an improvement | You adopt it after a backtest | |---|---| | [![The Turn skills line under a reply: release-notes, suggested 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/chat-skills.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#in-a-conversation) | [![A draft of release-notes with its backtest, Current 40 → Draft 93 +53, and the diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/skills-draft.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#evolution) | - **Manage.** Switch a skill off for the model or the `/` menu, use it in the conversation in one click, edit it, and go back to any earlier version. - **Evolve.** With self-evolution on, finished conversations are reviewed in the background for corrections, "from now on" instructions, failed tools and reusable procedures. A suggestion cites the steps it rests on; a task Agent drafts the new `SKILL.md`, which is backtested against the current version before you adopt it. Nothing changes without your **Adopt**. - **Test.** Each skill has its own cases, from reviews, from recorded conversations or written by hand, and a backtest scores any version on them. - **Install.** The market searches skills.sh's open index and reads any GitHub repository, any site publishing an Agent Skills discovery index, and curated catalogs; every install is previewed, with security reviews where they exist. - **In the conversation.** A line under each turn names the skills it used and what its review suggested, each one click from its page. Self-evolution stays off until you turn it on under **Plugins → dsh-mnemon → Skills**. The [Skills guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md) walks through every screen. ## Quick start DSH loads the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` automatically. Do not copy its `insert` block into your profile: duplicate Mnemon entries prevent Settings from saving. See [manual-installation recovery](docs/en/guides/installation.md#settings-cannot-save-after-manual-installation) if you already copied it. New to DSH? [Install and start](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/installation.md) walks from an empty machine to your first memory, with a screenshot for every step. The short version, with [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22.19 or later: ```sh npm install --global pnpm npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ```

1. In the page that opens, click **Plugins → Add plugin**, type `dsh-mnemon`, click **Install**, then **Enable now**. 2. Open **Memory System** in the sidebar. **Status** shows each memory component and Provider. 3. Tell a conversation something to remember. The turn memory bar under the reply lists what the turn read and wrote, and the brain mark saves a reply to memory. 4. For Memory Spaces, install the Mnemon CLI for Mnemon Native with `npm install --global @mnemon-dev/mnemon`, or enable another Provider on the Memory Spaces page. 5. Choose the main strategy and enhancements under **Plugins → dsh-mnemon**. dsh-mnemon supports DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (npm `latest` and `next`) and `0.2.0-rc.2`. The same package serves the desktop app's Plugins page, `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mnemon` on the command line, and Headless with `dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-mnemon`; older hosts keep the release [compatibility and upgrades](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/reference/compatibility.md) names for them. [Getting started](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/getting-started.md) continues from here, and [compatibility and upgrades](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/reference/compatibility.md) covers existing installations. ## How it works [![Source facts flow through a Strategy and Core validation into one View for the DSH Host](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/diagrams/en/composable-memory.png)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/architecture.md) - **Sources** own memory and its operations: Runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces, whose Providers are its children. - A **Strategy** decides how the available Sources take part in a turn: what stays resident, what can be searched, and which tools and budgets apply. Enhancements add to it through standard slots. - **Core** validates the result into one immutable **View** for the turn. The DSH Host pins it to that turn and controls tool access. The same public contracts serve the shipped plugins and external repositories. [Architecture](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/architecture.md) explains ownership, the turn lifecycle and the UI regions components contribute to. ## Official plugins The Starter pins a tested combination of independently versioned packages. One main strategy runs at a time; the enhancements are off until you turn them on. | Package | Role | Default | |---|---|---| | [dsh-mnemon-source-runtime](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-runtime/README.md) | Runtime memory: USER.md, MEMORY.md, revisions and local storage | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-documents](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-documents/README.md) | Project Documents: Markdown, search, revisions and archiving | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces/README.md) | Memory Spaces: durable evidence and their Providers | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-skills](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-skills/README.md) | Skills (experimental): DSH skills with versions, self-evolution from real conversations, tests and backtests, and a market of skills.sh, GitHub and Agent Skills sites | On (self-evolution off) | | dsh-mnemon

English · 简体中文

Composable, view-based context for DeepSeek Harness.

Pluggable sources and strategies, with layered memory and self-evolving skills out of the box.

Install and start · Watch the demo · Documentation · Build a plugin

## Why dsh-mnemon An Agent that starts every session from scratch keeps asking what it was already told. Putting everything into one memory store is no better: it either floods each turn or misses what matters. dsh-mnemon gives DeepSeek Harness memory that is layered, visible and composable, and skills that improve with use. - **The right memory for each turn.** Preferences and working facts stay in context. Project documents and long-term evidence are searched only when a question needs them. - **You can see what a turn used.** Under each reply, the turn memory bar lists the documents and memories the turn read and wrote, and one click opens each in the Memory System. The Memory System shows everything that is stored and lets you edit it. - **Save to memory in one click.** When a conversation turns up a fact worth keeping, the brain mark under the reply hands it to a task Agent, which removes duplicates, distils it and writes it to the right Memory Space, or saves it where you choose: working memory, your profile or a Memory Space. The receipt says where it went. - **Skills that improve with use.** Skills keeps every DSH skill in one place. It can review your real conversations, draft a better `SKILL.md` and backtest it before you adopt it, and it installs more skills from skills.sh, GitHub and sites that publish Agent Skills. - **Compose it on the Plugins page.** Choose a main strategy and optional enhancements, and switch them without moving any data. Every component has its own page for its settings. - **Keep data where you want it.** Local by default with Mnemon Native, or one of eight third-party Providers. Storage can be global, per workspace, centralized or in a directory you choose, with ZIP backup. - **Extend it.** Sources and Strategies are ordinary DSH plugins built on public SDKs. An installed component gets the same pages and switches as the shipped ones. ## See it in action These recordings come from a real WebUI with the live DeepSeek model answering, on a seeded, fictional project, Lumen. Waits for the model play faster, marked in the lower right corner. **Save a new fact to memory.** A reply reports a new measurement. Select the brain mark under it, cut the candidate down to the sentence worth keeping and send it to the task Agent; the receipt names the Memory Space it went to and opens it in one click.

**See all memory in one place.** Status, runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces live in the Memory System. The graph links memories through the entities they mention, and Ask Agent answers with the memories it cites, by content.

**Compose memory on the Plugins page.** One main strategy, its memory sources and optional enhancements, each switch applying at once. Every component has its own page, and storage, backup and interface settings live here too.

Every step is explained in the [UI guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/ui-guide.md); all screens, recordings and the capture environment are in the [v0.5.32 gallery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/assets/webui-v0.5.32/README.md). ## Three kinds of memory | Memory | Keep here | How it reaches the Agent | |---|---|---| | **Runtime memory** | Preferences, working agreements, facts needed on the next turn | Injected every turn as compact USER.md and MEMORY.md | | **Project Documents** | Designs, investigations, procedures and handoffs | Searched first, then read when relevant | | **Memory Spaces** | Durable facts, decisions, entities and their relationships | Recalled on demand from the enabled Providers | The default **Layered strategy** keeps runtime memory resident and reads the other two on demand. The **General strategy** offers every available source within one budget and lets the model decide how to use each. A **memory space** is one named, Provider-backed scope for long-term evidence; the Chinese product term is 记忆空间. ## Skills that improve with use **Skills** is an experimental component for the `SKILL.md` skills DSH loads from your project and your home folder. Its page sits in the Memory System, or in the sidebar on its own. | A turn's review suggests an improvement | You adopt it after a backtest | |---|---| | [![The Turn skills line under a reply: release-notes, suggested 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/chat-skills.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#in-a-conversation) | [![A draft of release-notes with its backtest, Current 40 → Draft 93 +53, and the diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/skills-draft.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#evolution) | - **Manage.** Switch a skill off for the model or the `/` menu, use it in the conversation in one click, edit it, and go back to any earlier version. - **Evolve.** With self-evolution on, finished conversations are reviewed in the background for corrections, "from now on" instructions, failed tools and reusable procedures. A suggestion cites the steps it rests on; a task Agent drafts the new `SKILL.md`, which is backtested against the current version before you adopt it. Nothing changes without your **Adopt**. - **Test.** Each skill has its own cases, from reviews, from recorded conversations or written by hand, and a backtest scores any version on them. - **Install.** The market searches skills.sh's open index and reads any GitHub repository, any site publishing an Agent Skills discovery index, and curated catalogs; every install is previewed, with security reviews where they exist. - **In the conversation.** A line under each turn names the skills it used and what its review suggested, each one click from its page. Self-evolution stays off until you turn it on under **Plugins → dsh-mnemon → Skills**. The [Skills guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md) walks through every screen. ## Quick start DSH loads the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` automatically. Do not copy its `insert` block into your profile: duplicate Mnemon entries prevent Settings from saving. For Memory Spaces, install the Mnemon CLI for Mnemon Native with `npm install --global @mnemon-dev/mnemon`, or enable another Provider on the Memory Spaces page. 5. Enhancements add to it through standard slots. - **Core** validates the result into one immutable **View** for the turn. The DSH Host pins it to that turn and controls tool access. The same public contracts serve the shipped plugins and external repositories. # dsh-mnemon-strategy-auto-capture Optional additive, **in-turn guidance** for any Mnemon main Strategy that accepts Core's standard `capture` slot, including the Layered and General strategies. The default targets ready `durable-evidence` Sources whose selected View exposes the Source-local `remember` Action. Custom Sources must configure the Action ids that actually mean recording: ```yaml - id: mnemon-strategy-auto-capture name: dsh-mnemon-strategy-auto-capture config: sourceKeys: - source:team-notes actionIds: - append ``` The plugin asks the current LLM to consider at most one qualified durable fact. It starts no background Agent or timer, executes no write during View composition, cannot expose an Action removed by the main Strategy or Host, and cannot bypass ActionOffer authorization. Model compliance and capture quality require task-level evaluation. ## Installation and verification The default Starter already installs this package as a disabled Entry. Use its switch on the `dsh-mnemon` page under **Plugins**; do not add a second copy of the same Entry. The configuration example above is for an explicitly composed custom Profile. Installing an npm package is not the same as activating a contribution. From a source checkout, run `pnpm verify` with declared public peers installed; use a packed peer for unreleased SDK work. [Plugin development and independent fixtures](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/extensions.md) · [中文指南](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/zh-CN/development/extensions.md)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-mnemon-strategy-light-context Optional additive projection cap for any Mnemon main Strategy that accepts Core's standard `projection` slot, including the Layered and General strategies. ```yaml - id: mnemon-strategy-light-context name: dsh-mnemon-strategy-light-context config: maxProjectionCharacters: 4096 ``` The cap is shared by all selected Sources and can only narrow the Host turn budget. It does not change read routes, actions, Source storage, or retrieval-result ceilings. Runtime projection has no automatic expansion route: choosing a very small cap may hide runtime memory, so benchmark a value appropriate for the workload. Uninstalling restores the original allocation. ## Installation and verification The default Starter already installs this package as a disabled Entry. Use its switch on the `dsh-mnemon` page under **Plugins**; do not add a second copy of the same Entry. The configuration example above is for an explicitly composed custom Profile. Installing an npm package is not the same as activating a contribution. From a source checkout, run `pnpm verify` with declared public peers installed; use a packed peer for unreleased SDK work. [Plugin development and independent fixtures](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/extensions.md) · [中文指南](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/zh-CN/development/extensions.md)

dsh-mnemon

English · 简体中文

Composable, view-based context for DeepSeek Harness.

Pluggable sources and strategies, with layered memory and self-evolving skills out of the box.

Install and start · Watch the demo · Documentation · Build a plugin

## Why dsh-mnemon An Agent that starts every session from scratch keeps asking what it was already told. Putting everything into one memory store is no better: it either floods each turn or misses what matters. dsh-mnemon gives DeepSeek Harness memory that is layered, visible and composable, and skills that improve with use. - **The right memory for each turn.** Preferences and working facts stay in context. Project documents and long-term evidence are searched only when a question needs them. - **You can see what a turn used.** Under each reply, the turn memory bar lists the documents and memories the turn read and wrote, and one click opens each in the Memory System. The Memory System shows everything that is stored and lets you edit it. - **Save to memory in one click.** When a conversation turns up a fact worth keeping, the brain mark under the reply hands it to a task Agent, which removes duplicates, distils it and writes it to the right Memory Space, or saves it where you choose: working memory, your profile or a Memory Space. The receipt says where it went. - **Skills that improve with use.** Skills keeps every DSH skill in one place. It can review your real conversations, draft a better `SKILL.md` and backtest it before you adopt it, and it installs more skills from skills.sh, GitHub and sites that publish Agent Skills. - **Compose it on the Plugins page.** Choose a main strategy and optional enhancements, and switch them without moving any data. Every component has its own page for its settings. - **Keep data where you want it.** Local by default with Mnemon Native, or one of eight third-party Providers. Storage can be global, per workspace, centralized or in a directory you choose, with ZIP backup. - **Extend it.** Sources and Strategies are ordinary DSH plugins built on public SDKs. An installed component gets the same pages and switches as the shipped ones. ## See it in action These recordings come from a real WebUI with the live DeepSeek model answering, on a seeded, fictional project, Lumen. Waits for the model play faster, marked in the lower right corner. **Save a new fact to memory.** A reply reports a new measurement. Select the brain mark under it, cut the candidate down to the sentence worth keeping and send it to the task Agent; the receipt names the Memory Space it went to and opens it in one click.

**See all memory in one place.** Status, runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces live in the Memory System. The graph links memories through the entities they mention, and Ask Agent answers with the memories it cites, by content.

**Compose memory on the Plugins page.** One main strategy, its memory sources and optional enhancements, each switch applying at once. Every component has its own page, and storage, backup and interface settings live here too.

Every step is explained in the [UI guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/ui-guide.md); all screens, recordings and the capture environment are in the [v0.5.32 gallery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/assets/webui-v0.5.32/README.md). ## Three kinds of memory | Memory | Keep here | How it reaches the Agent | |---|---|---| | **Runtime memory** | Preferences, working agreements, facts needed on the next turn | Injected every turn as compact USER.md and MEMORY.md | | **Project Documents** | Designs, investigations, procedures and handoffs | Searched first, then read when relevant | | **Memory Spaces** | Durable facts, decisions, entities and their relationships | Recalled on demand from the enabled Providers | The default **Layered strategy** keeps runtime memory resident and reads the other two on demand. The **General strategy** offers every available source within one budget and lets the model decide how to use each. A **memory space** is one named, Provider-backed scope for long-term evidence; the Chinese product term is 记忆空间. ## Skills that improve with use **Skills** is an experimental component for the `SKILL.md` skills DSH loads from your project and your home folder. Its page sits in the Memory System, or in the sidebar on its own. | A turn's review suggests an improvement | You adopt it after a backtest | |---|---| | [![The Turn skills line under a reply: release-notes, suggested 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/chat-skills.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#in-a-conversation) | [![A draft of release-notes with its backtest, Current 40 → Draft 93 +53, and the diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/skills-draft.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#evolution) | - **Manage.** Switch a skill off for the model or the `/` menu, use it in the conversation in one click, edit it, and go back to any earlier version. - **Evolve.** With self-evolution on, finished conversations are reviewed in the background for corrections, "from now on" instructions, failed tools and reusable procedures. A suggestion cites the steps it rests on; a task Agent drafts the new `SKILL.md`, which is backtested against the current version before you adopt it. Nothing changes without your **Adopt**. - **Test.** Each skill has its own cases, from reviews, from recorded conversations or written by hand, and a backtest scores any version on them. - **Install.** The market searches skills.sh's open index and reads any GitHub repository, any site publishing an Agent Skills discovery index, and curated catalogs; every install is previewed, with security reviews where they exist. - **In the conversation.** A line under each turn names the skills it used and what its review suggested, each one click from its page. The same public contracts serve the shipped plugins and external repositories. # dsh-mnemon-strategy-scoped Optional additive Source selection for any Mnemon main Strategy that accepts Core's standard `selection` slot, including the Layered and General strategies. Enable the plugin alongside the selected main Strategy. With no configuration it includes every ready Source whose role is `working-context`, `narrative`, or `durable-evidence`, in deterministic role/key order. Configure exact `sourceKeys` to express priority; configure `writableSourceKeys` to make the remaining selected Sources read-only in the View. ```yaml - id: mnemon-strategy-scoped name: dsh-mnemon-strategy-scoped config: sourceKeys: - source:global-runtime - source:project-runtime writableSourceKeys: - source:project-runtime ``` Keys name already installed Source instances; this plugin does not create or migrate storage. Uninstalling it removes only its selection contribution. If duplicate roles remain installed, the Layered strategy, unextended, reports the ambiguity rather than choosing by load order; the General strategy admits every instance. ## Installation and verification The default Starter already installs this package as a disabled Entry. Use its switch on the `dsh-mnemon` page under **Plugins**; do not add a second copy of the same Entry. The configuration example above is for an explicitly composed custom Profile. Installing an npm package is not the same as activating a contribution. From a source checkout, run `pnpm verify` with declared public peers installed; use a packed peer for unreleased SDK work. [Plugin development and independent fixtures](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/extensions.md) · [中文指南](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/zh-CN/development/extensions.md)

dsh-mnemon

English · 简体中文

Composable, view-based context for DeepSeek Harness.

Pluggable sources and strategies, with layered memory and self-evolving skills out of the box.

Install and start · Watch the demo · Documentation · Build a plugin

## Why dsh-mnemon An Agent that starts every session from scratch keeps asking what it was already told. Putting everything into one memory store is no better: it either floods each turn or misses what matters. dsh-mnemon gives DeepSeek Harness memory that is layered, visible and composable, and skills that improve with use. - **The right memory for each turn.** Preferences and working facts stay in context. Project documents and long-term evidence are searched only when a question needs them. - **You can see what a turn used.** Under each reply, the turn memory bar lists the documents and memories the turn read and wrote, and one click opens each in the Memory System. The Memory System shows everything that is stored and lets you edit it. - **Save to memory in one click.** When a conversation turns up a fact worth keeping, the brain mark under the reply hands it to a task Agent, which removes duplicates, distils it and writes it to the right Memory Space, or saves it where you choose: working memory, your profile or a Memory Space. The receipt says where it went. - **Skills that improve with use.** Skills keeps every DSH skill in one place. It can review your real conversations, draft a better `SKILL.md` and backtest it before you adopt it, and it installs more skills from skills.sh, GitHub and sites that publish Agent Skills. - **Compose it on the Plugins page.** Choose a main strategy and optional enhancements, and switch them without moving any data. Every component has its own page for its settings. - **Keep data where you want it.** Local by default with Mnemon Native, or one of eight third-party Providers. Storage can be global, per workspace, centralized or in a directory you choose, with ZIP backup. - **Extend it.** Sources and Strategies are ordinary DSH plugins built on public SDKs. An installed component gets the same pages and switches as the shipped ones. ## See it in action These recordings come from a real WebUI with the live DeepSeek model answering, on a seeded, fictional project, Lumen. Waits for the model play faster, marked in the lower right corner. **Save a new fact to memory.** A reply reports a new measurement. Select the brain mark under it, cut the candidate down to the sentence worth keeping and send it to the task Agent; the receipt names the Memory Space it went to and opens it in one click.

**See all memory in one place.** Status, runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces live in the Memory System. The graph links memories through the entities they mention, and Ask Agent answers with the memories it cites, by content.

**Compose memory on the Plugins page.** One main strategy, its memory sources and optional enhancements, each switch applying at once. Every component has its own page, and storage, backup and interface settings live here too.

Every step is explained in the [UI guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/ui-guide.md); all screens, recordings and the capture environment are in the [v0.5.32 gallery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/assets/webui-v0.5.32/README.md). ## Three kinds of memory | Memory | Keep here | How it reaches the Agent | |---|---|---| | **Runtime memory** | Preferences, working agreements, facts needed on the next turn | Injected every turn as compact USER.md and MEMORY.md | | **Project Documents** | Designs, investigations, procedures and handoffs | Searched first, then read when relevant | | **Memory Spaces** | Durable facts, decisions, entities and their relationships | Recalled on demand from the enabled Providers | The default **Layered strategy** keeps runtime memory resident and reads the other two on demand. The **General strategy** offers every available source within one budget and lets the model decide how to use each. A **memory space** is one named, Provider-backed scope for long-term evidence; the Chinese product term is 记忆空间. ## Skills that improve with use **Skills** is an experimental component for the `SKILL.md` skills DSH loads from your project and your home folder. # dsh-agent-activity

[![ci](https://github.com/oxygenforce/dsh-agent-activity/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/oxygenforce/dsh-agent-activity/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![DeepSeek Harness plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-4d6bfe.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that makes the agent's working process visible **while it is still working** — before the final answer lands.

The card docks right above the composer, in the same place as the todo panel, and answers three questions at a glance:

- **What has it already done?** Every tool call of the current turn, in order, with its target and how long it took (✓ / ✗ / spinner).
- **What is it doing now?** A phase label — *thinking*, *running a tool*, *writing the answer* — plus the current step number.
- **What is it about to do?** The tool calls the model has just announced but not yet run, followed by the next unfinished todo.

While the model streams a reply, the card also shows the leading edge of that reply, so you can tell the difference between "thinking", "stuck" and "writing".

It collapses to a single line and **stays there after the turn ends**, so the card doubles as the
entry point for "what did it just do?" — click it open, read the rows, click × to dismiss that turn
only. The card comes back by itself when the next turn starts, and reopening a past conversation
shows the last turn of that conversation (the projection keeps exactly one turn of history, which is
what the card needs).

## Why a plugin and not a skill

A skill can only add instructions to the model's context; it cannot render anything. This is a UI plugin: a Host half that folds the session event log into a small "activity" projection, and a Client half that renders it in the Harness Web UI.

## Install

The package is a DeepSeek Harness bundle. Install it from a directory or from a packed tarball with the Plugin Manager:

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=/path/to/dsh-agent-activity
```

`application: applied` means the Host half is live; the card appears above the composer in the Web UI. Replacing an already-installed version needs a Harness restart to pick up the new browser bundle.

There is nothing to configure. No data leaves the machine.

## What it renders

The card speaks in plain language instead of tool names: what happened, what is happening
now, and what is queued. It deliberately does **not** echo your message — the transcript right
above already shows it. The collapsed line is one stable row:

```
⠋ 正在做事   正在 改文件 · client.js                     已做 5 件事 · 12秒  ⌃
```

Click it and the panel opens as a floating overlay above the card (Escape, outside click or
a second click closes it) — opening it never changes the page layout:

```
我做了什么   改文件 3 · 跑测试 2 · 发版 1
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✓  改文件     …/lib/client.js                                        1.2s
   为了 先确认卡片头部现在渲染的是什么
✓  跑测试     npm test                                               3.0s
⠋  改文件     …/lib/activity.js                                       0.8s
   为了 把“为什么做这一步”接进每一行
接下来
○  跑测试     npm test
✎  正在写回答  “现在把计划行接进头部…”
```

Every row carries the reason the agent gave for that step — the sentence it wrote right before the
call, quoted back as 为了 …. When the agent said nothing (or the step is a long scripted chain),
the card falls back to the todo item it is currently working on, so a row is never just
"跑脚本 · x.py" with no purpose.

That is the whole point: **plain words**, then a recap of what the agent did for the task
(`改文件 3 · 跑测试 2 · 发版 1`), then the rows and what is queued. No API names — `npm test`
reads 跑测试, `"$NODE" --check lib/client.js` reads 检查语法 · client.js, `curl -o x.tgz …`
reads 下载文件 · x.tgz, `git push` reads 提交代码. A file path collapses to its last two
segments, a search shows its quoted term, and a command that cannot be classified shows
执行命令 next to the command itself — never a vague label with no information. Tool names
survive only in the hover tooltip. Wording follows the UI language (Chinese and English),
long rows wrap to two lines, and the answer preview keeps its line breaks.

If the agent also keeps a todo list, the panel shows it as a checklist under
「为了完成你的要求，我打算」 with ✓ done / ⠋ running / ○ pending — that is the plan in the
agent's own words, so it leads the panel whenever it exists.

## How it works

- **Host** (`lib/index.js`, `lib/activity.js`) registers the session projection `activity` with a single `apply(state, event)` fold over the durable event log: `turn/start`, `step/start`, `assistant/message`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `turn/end`. The fold is pure and synchronous, returns the same state reference for events it does not care about, and keeps a bounded log (32 tool calls) so long turns stay cheap.
- **Wire** (`wire.view`) hands the finished value to the Client. The Client never folds events itself — it reads `useProjection("activity")` and, for the plan row, the built-in `todos` projection.
- Because the projection is registered at boot and has no persisted rows yet, sessions restored from an older checkpoint simply re-fold their log through `init` + `apply`; no migration is needed.

The projection key is `activity`, and its state is plain JSON:

```ts
{
  v: 2,
  turn: number, step: number,
  phase: "idle" | "thinking" | "tool" | "writing" | "done" | "error" | "aborted",
  startedAt: number, updatedAt: number, endedAt: number | null,
  items: { id, name, target, kind, status: "running" | "ok" | "error", t0, t1 }[],
  plan:  { id, name, target, kind }[],
  draft: string,
  counts: { steps: number, tools: number, errors: number }
}
```

## Development

```bash
node scripts/check-manifest.mjs   # manifest, export map, patch row, icon, locales
node --test tests/activity.test.mjs
node --check lib/client.js && node --check lib/activity.js && node --check lib/index.js
```

`tests/activity.test.mjs` replays synthetic session events through the fold and asserts the item list, plan, phase transitions, error accounting and the projection's wire identity — no browser required.

## Layout

```
lib/index.js       Host entry: registers the session projection
lib/activity.js    Pure event fold + tool-call summarizer (no dependencies)
lib/client.js      Web UI card, dictionaries, styles
locale/*.json      meta.title / meta.description for the Plugin Manager
icon.svg           Original artwork shown in the plugin list
cordis.patch.yml   Bundle patch row
```

## License

MIT © oxygenforce
