# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core — host services

The runtime authority of the orchestrator: task engine and state machine,
scheduler, router, verifier, integration manager, evidence log, escalation
ledger, worker manager and recovery. It owns the SQLite state in `.sdlc/`.

**Never install this into a worker profile.** Mounting it there would start a
second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db` (errata E6 in the spec).
Worker profiles mount [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard)
and [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools)
only.

## Install

Installed as a bundle by the worker-free profiles (`sdlc-probe`) and as a module
dependency of [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core
```

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Node.js ≥ 22.13 (`node:sqlite`)

## License

MIT

# dsh-sdlc-flow — DSH SDLC Flow (DeepSeek Harness plugin suite)

> **Current release: 1.1.1.** Install from this checkout
> (`npm run install:local`), or the registry form
> (`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install`) — see
> [Install](#install). See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for scope and known
> limitations and [PROOF_REPORT.md](PROOF_REPORT.md) for measured evidence. No
> confirmatory developer-productivity claim is supported yet.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin suite that turns a requirement into a verified,
merged change: it plans a task DAG, dispatches role-preset workers into isolated
git worktrees, verifies against risk-appropriate gates, and integrates.

**Implemented from** [`universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md`](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md).

| Document | What it is |
|---|---|
| [universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md) | the normative specification |
| [SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md](SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md) | gate results, test pyramid, defects found |
| [SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md](SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md) | deviations D0–D7, fixes, what is not implemented |
| [EVAL_PROTOCOL.md](EVAL_PROTOCOL.md) | pre-registered A/B design proving the plugin beats plain DSH |
| [IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md](IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md) | honest audit: what was fixed, measured, or deliberately left |

## Tool startup troubleshooting

The source checkout contains unreleased tool-lifecycle repairs; reinstalling
`@latest` does not fetch these changes until a new release is published. Desktop
users can install the rebuilt `packages/sdlc-orchestrator` directory through
**Plugins → Add plugin** using its absolute path, then quit Harness completely
and reopen it. Do not edit the Desktop profile by hand. Once this build is
installed, later registry releases are checked on startup: stable builds install
automatically, prerelease builds report availability (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install`
opts in; `off` disables). Restart to load the new code.

### “The panel is newer than the SDLC host code”

Host plugin code is loaded once at process start; an in-place update replaces
files on disk but not the host code already running. The panel now probes the
routes and distinguishes three cases before telling you what to do:

- **status answers, flow does not** — an older host build is loaded; fully quit
  Harness and reopen. Closing the window can leave it running in the background:
  use **Quit** from the app/tray menu, or on Linux
  `pkill -f deepseek-harness` / `flatpak kill com.deepseek.harness`.
- **no SDLC route answers** — the host plugin is not registered or enabled in
  this profile; enable it in **Plugins**, or install it for that profile.
- **the probe cannot reach the host** — a transport/connection problem, not a
  version mismatch.

For the **Desktop app**, update through **Plugins → Add plugin** and restart.
`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install` manages the
`sdlc-web` / `sdlc-worker` / `sdlc-probe` CLI profiles; it cannot modify the
app-owned `desktop` profile. The panel shows the panel/host builds and a
**Copy diagnostics** action for support.

The panel also reads the **open session's workspace**, not the Harness process
directory, so the Desktop app shows the project you are actually working in.

For an offline runtime check (no model and no second web server):

```sh
node scripts/verify-tool-runtime.mjs /path/to/unpacked/dsh-runtime
```

It mounts all 26 role compositions and checks tool visibility, real pipeline
execution/rendering, invalid arguments, and worker denial of lead capabilities.
It also asserts that the shipped lead exposes one selectable preset (the Lead
Orchestrator), not the whole role roster. OS/delegation boundaries are stubbed:
this does not test running workers or the Desktop session-creation UI. An
optional second argument points to an unpacked plugin tarball.
A `never started` diagnostic means the loader did not create a plugin fiber;
look for the **earlier loader import error** in the application log. A missing
service instead reports `waiting for tools`. If the former persists after a
clean restart/install, include that earlier error and the installed version.

## Quick start

```sh
npm run build                     # artifacts (zero dependencies, offline; incl. UI bundle)
node scripts/validate-gates.mjs   # gate:P → gate:Q  (no model, no network)
npm run test:unit                 # L2 — pure modules + property tests
```

Every `test:*` script passes explicit globs rather than a directory: Node 24
resolves a bare directory positional as a *script* and fails with
`Cannot find module '<dir>'`, while globs work on every supported engine.

The deterministic control plane needs no model at all:

```sh
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs init        # .sdlc/, integration branch, detected gates
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs status
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs selftest --mock
```

## Flow visualizer (right sidebar)

While a session is open, the DSH right sidebar contains an **SDLC Flow** entry
(the guide's capsule, or auto-open on the first session that has an SDLC
project). It is a live, read-only view of the orchestrator, built around one
question: **what needs attention?** The old Status and Board tabs were duplicates
of data already in the flow snapshot, so the panel now has three primary
surfaces plus settings:

- **Flow** — a live **animated task map** (below) plus a “Needs attention” queue
  first (unresolved escalations, failed tasks, failing gates, orphaned worker
  runs, path conflicts), a progress ring and state distribution, live workers,
  and collapsible gates/routing/activity evidence. Click a task node to open its
  detail: role, risk, tier/model, attempts, resources, runs, gates, dependencies
  and the latest event, plus **Compare runs**.
- **Live map** — a deterministic SVG rendered in the browser from the flow
  snapshot (no model call, no generated diagram). Stages are horizontal bands, so
  parallel branches appear side by side; running nodes glow and stream packets
  along their dependency edges, completed paths stay lit, and blocked or failed
  paths turn red. Hover or select a node to trace its upstream and downstream
  path. The parallel meter shows active workers against the host-computed
  effective cap, and the progress card shows recorded tokens per completed task.
- **Tasks** — the board without columns: search, All/Active/Blocked/Done
  filters, tasks grouped by lifecycle state, and the same inline task detail.
- **Review** — task and run **selects** populated from the flow snapshot (no
  hand-typed IDs); defaults to the newest two runs, shows signed time/token/cost
  deltas, changed gates, and a collapsed trace path.
- **Settings** (gear) — a validated `.sdlc/config.yml` editor grouped by section.
  Only changed fields get a Save button; rejected writes never touch the file.

All surfaces share one `/api/sdlc.flow` snapshot and one config snapshot. Polling
is adaptive — 2.5 s while a task or worker is in flight, 8 s when quiet — and
each poll sends the newest event id as a cursor, so only new events cross the
wire and the client merges them into a bounded window. On a failed poll the last
snapshot is shown as *stale* rather than blanked. Opening the panel on a
workspace that has never been initialised **bootstraps it automatically** (see
[No init step — use the Harness model](#no-init-step--use-the-harness-model));
the guided state now appears only when auto-setup genuinely fails (no recognised
stack marker), with the real reason and a copyable `sdlc init` command that
prints the same diagnosis. A bare 404 is diagnosed as a host/client version
mismatch with restart and reinstall guidance (an in-place update does not
replace loaded host code). Missing cost/tokens/duration stay `—` with a reason,
never `0`. Set `autoOpen: false` in the UI row config to stop the automatic
open. DSH's right sidebar has **no surface without a session**, so the Start
screen cannot show it — start a session first.

## Install

### One command — always the latest published version

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
```

This resolves `latest` from the npm registry itself, pins the **exact** version
in the `sdlc-web` profile, records the matching pnpm release-age exemption,
creates the profile when missing, prunes packages left by older releases,
installs, re-selects the bundle (a failed uninstall can leave the package
installed but disabled), and verifies the installed `package.json`. Re-running
it upgrades an existing install instead of requiring an uninstall first.

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all          # lead + worker + probe
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --tag beta          # newest prerelease
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --version 1.1.1
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json      # no changes
```

It is idempotent. Prerequisites: `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13.

> **Restart after installing.** A running lead keeps the old module tree in
> memory even after the package on disk changes (deep-imported preset rows are
> not hot-replaced). Quit DeepSeek Harness completely and reopen it; otherwise a
> new session can still report the previous version's `agent-preset/invalid`.
> The installer prints this reminder.

### No-clone install — prebuilt release artifact

Download the release artifact and run its installer. Nothing is compiled on your
machine, and you do not need the source.

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/pwoodman/dsh-sdlc/releases/latest/download/dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
tar xzf dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz && cd dsh-sdlc-*/
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin tree to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-sdlc/<version>/` (so you can
delete the download), then creates the `sdlc-web`, `sdlc-worker` and `sdlc-probe`
profiles, installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It
is idempotent — re-run it any time.

Prerequisites: `dsh` **installed as a package** (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13. A wrapper that
merely answers `dsh --version` — an `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` shim, a shell
function, a hand-written script — is not enough: the platform gate reads the
installed package's own files, and the installer now refuses that setup with
this reason instead of failing later inside `gate:M0`.

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web          # the interactive lead (web GUI)
```

### Uninstall — one click in the plugin manager

The lead installs exactly **one** package (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`; its
members are folded inside it), so removing that single entry in the plugin
manager removes everything — no ghost entries, nothing "still required". From
the CLI it is the same one spec:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web remove @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow
```

A profile installed by a pre-fold release may still list the four members as
plain dependencies; re-run the installer (or this one command) to clear them:

```sh
pnpm remove --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui
```

On Windows, close a running lead first (`sdlc.db` and the bundle files are held
open while it runs). A profile directory itself (`~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web`) is
disposable and can always be deleted outright. The `@deepseek-ai/…` bundles you
see running (for example `dsh-agent-preset-registry`) are DeepSeek Harness's
own — they ship with the profile template and are not part of this plugin.

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop — what works today

The Desktop app owns its `desktop` profile and the `dsh` CLI refuses to manage
it, so the CLI/tarball paths above do not target it. Desktop users install
through the sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin** dialog (paste a package name, a
tarball URL, or an absolute path).

Two honest limits on a Desktop-only machine:

- the lead dispatches workers by spawning `dsh --profile sdlc-worker`, so it
  needs a `dsh` CLI on `PATH` for real task execution — without one, the lead,
  the tools, the presets and the web panel all work, but dispatch does not;
- package installs into `desktop` are the app's own operation, so a plugin that
  needs the worker/probe profiles is better tested against CLI profiles.

### Registry / Add-plugin wizard — one spec for the lead

Once the packages are published under an npm scope you own, the lead is a single
spec (the same shape `dsh-context` and `dsh-proactive` use: prebuilt `lib/` + its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no profile edits, no build
and no restart):

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create once
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

Or fill `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow` into the **Add plugin** wizard on the Plugins page.

> **Fresh release not installing?** pnpm 11 applies a 24-hour
> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a release published in
> the last day can resolve to the *previous* version. Prefer the installer
> above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you. For a
> manual install, pin it exactly
> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1`) and add **one list item per pattern** to
> the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1'
> ```
>
> A combined value such as `pkg@a || pkg@b` is not a valid pnpm pattern (it is
> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

#### Publishing under your own npm scope

The packages ship as `@patwoodman/*`. If your npm account does not own that scope,
`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

An npm **user scope** (`@your-username`) is free and exists automatically once
you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v1.1.1 && git push origin v1.1.1
```

The **Release** workflow verifies the tree, builds the tarball, publishes the
GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.
Create the token at <https://www.npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens> (an *Automation*
token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

### From a source checkout — one command

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

That single command generates the patches, builds the artifacts (zero
dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

Prerequisites: `dsh` installed as a package (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json
```

The lead also checks the registry on startup (at most once per 24 hours).
Stable builds install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease
builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).
The running process keeps the old code until it is restarted; the update reports
`restart-required`. A failed install is retried after a short backoff, the
installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

### Uninstall

Remove the package and its bundle selection from every managed profile:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

The GUI path is unchanged: the lead profile contains exactly one own-scope
package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: live flow map, tasks, review, validated config (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

Only the interactive lead can grant authority. A headless deployment is a guest
of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

## Web UI

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Flow | live animated task map, attention queue, parallel-worker meter, progress/spend, task detail |
| Tasks | search, All/Active/Blocked/Done filters, lifecycle grouping, inline task detail |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |
| Settings | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`,
`/api/sdlc.flow`) read the live DB and are scoped to the open session's
workspace; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI
uses. A project row belonging to another checkout is never rendered.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

### No init step — use the Harness model

Two rituals are gone: there is **no `sdlc init` step** and **no provider API
key**. DeepSeek Harness already resolves the signed-in provider/account (for
example `deepseek-account/deepseek-flash`) and its credential, and the
orchestrator now inherits both.

**Bootstrap on first touch.** The first panel request against a workspace root
materialises `.sdlc/` (tree, DB, gate detection, integration branch) and writes
a `config.yml` whose three tiers all name the model the current Harness session
resolves — the live `agentDefaultModel` selection, then on-disk profile
discovery, then DSH's own base default. `sdlc status` and
`sdlc config use-host-model` do the same from the CLI, so no command sequence
is required at all. The guarantees:

- **No key is ever implied.** A bootstrapped config names exactly one provider
  in its tiers and its price table — the fresh user is never asked for a
  second credential. `--no-host-model` (on `sdlc init`) opts out for
  deployments that route models some other way — read commands never write
  the spec defaults; exactly one of `--provider`/`--model` is a usage error,
  never a silent fallback.
- **Authored configs are never rewritten by a read.** Bootstrap only writes a
  config that does not exist yet. Changing the route later is an explicit
  action: **Settings → Harness model → Use this model for all tiers**, or
  `sdlc config use-host-model` (add `--provider`/`--model` to override, or
  `--dsh-home`/`--profile` outside the app). Both validate before writing,
  keep your own price rows without re-introducing legacy ones, and bootstrap
  an uninitialised workspace in one shot.
- **Half-projects heal themselves.** "Complete" means config.yml AND the
  database, and `ensureProject` is the single authority on it. An early
  `sdlc tasks` opens the DB before any config exists; a `git clean -fdx`
  removes the gitignored DB and keeps the config — the next touch repairs
  the missing half without touching the authored one.
- **No workspace is a dead end.** A workspace without a recognised stack
  marker (a plain folder, a Node project with only `package.json`, a
  `requirements.txt` Python project) still bootstraps — with
  `verification.detection: manual` and empty gates, the artifact the spec's
  own failure message prescribes. `sdlc config validate` visibly warns that
  verification passes vacuously until gates are authored, and the explicit
  `sdlc init` still refuses to guess. npm detection matches the spec's F.5
  table: `package-lock.json` is the npm marker — a bare `package.json` no
  longer produces `npm ci` commands that can never run.
- **Failure is actionable, never a mutation.** When auto-setup genuinely
  fails (an unwritable workspace, an unexpected error), the panel explains
  why with the host's real reason, the CLI prints a clean
  `BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` report, and nothing is guessed. A failed explicit init
  leaves the user's git repository untouched (no integration branch, no
  .gitignore); auto-setup never writes a `.gitignore` outside a git
  repository. A leftover tree cannot be poisoned: config writes and
  adoption require a complete project. The next request retries, so fixing
  the workspace recovers without a host restart.
- **"No project yet" is not a failure.** A set-up workspace with no project
  row shows an accurate empty state — "create a project with `/sdlc run`" —
  not a setup-failure card.

**Workers use the same route and the same credential store.** In-process
subagents already run on the parent route, so delegation needs no key of its
own. Process workers receive the adopted provider/model through the
`agent-default-model` tier overlay and `DSH_HOME`, so `deepseek-account`
resolves the same account token. No provider key is ever materialized into the
worker environment.

When DSH exposes no currency metadata, the adopted price entry is explicitly
`unknown`; cost renders as `—` instead of a guessed number. Configure prices in
Settings if you want cost estimates.

## Status

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 906 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness. The 1.1.1 packed tarballs install, boot the
probe, create a lead session and uninstall cleanly; the no-clone tarball also
installs end-to-end in a fresh `DSH_HOME` and passes M0. `doctor` passes with 0
errors and 0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard — worker-side enforcement

The policy half of the worker sandbox: a `tools/pre-execute` waterfall and the
`fs/*` write deciders. It denies writes outside the task contract's allowed
paths, protects the orchestrator's own files (`.sdlc/sdlc.db`, locks, the task
contract) and rejects forbidden command patterns (`git push --force*`,
`rm -rf /`, `git clean -fdx*`, `git reset --hard*`, …).

It has no host service and no database access. The guard is *policy*, not a
security boundary — the real controls are the sandbox root and the post-hoc
`git diff` check.

Installed into worker profiles beside
[`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools),
and into the boot probe for symmetry.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

## Configuration

The patch declares the defaults (`guardMode: deny`, `orchestratorPaths`,
`protectedOrchestratorPaths`, `guardForbiddenPatterns`). A profile-level
id-targeted override replaces the row's whole `config`.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Node.js ≥ 22.13

## License

MIT

# dsh-sdlc-flow — DSH SDLC Flow (DeepSeek Harness plugin suite)

> **Current release: 1.1.1.** Install from this checkout
> (`npm run install:local`), or the registry form
> (`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install`) — see
> [Install](#install). See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for scope and known
> limitations and [PROOF_REPORT.md](PROOF_REPORT.md) for measured evidence. No
> confirmatory developer-productivity claim is supported yet.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin suite that turns a requirement into a verified,
merged change: it plans a task DAG, dispatches role-preset workers into isolated
git worktrees, verifies against risk-appropriate gates, and integrates.

**Implemented from** [`universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md`](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md).

| Document | What it is |
|---|---|
| [universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md) | the normative specification |
| [SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md](SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md) | gate results, test pyramid, defects found |
| [SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md](SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md) | deviations D0–D7, fixes, what is not implemented |
| [EVAL_PROTOCOL.md](EVAL_PROTOCOL.md) | pre-registered A/B design proving the plugin beats plain DSH |
| [IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md](IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md) | honest audit: what was fixed, measured, or deliberately left |

## Tool startup troubleshooting

The source checkout contains unreleased tool-lifecycle repairs; reinstalling
`@latest` does not fetch these changes until a new release is published. Desktop
users can install the rebuilt `packages/sdlc-orchestrator` directory through
**Plugins → Add plugin** using its absolute path, then quit Harness completely
and reopen it. Do not edit the Desktop profile by hand. Once this build is
installed, later registry releases are checked on startup: stable builds install
automatically, prerelease builds report availability (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install`
opts in; `off` disables). Restart to load the new code.

### “The panel is newer than the SDLC host code”

Host plugin code is loaded once at process start; an in-place update replaces
files on disk but not the host code already running. The panel now probes the
routes and distinguishes three cases before telling you what to do:

- **status answers, flow does not** — an older host build is loaded; fully quit
  Harness and reopen. Closing the window can leave it running in the background:
  use **Quit** from the app/tray menu, or on Linux
  `pkill -f deepseek-harness` / `flatpak kill com.deepseek.harness`.
- **no SDLC route answers** — the host plugin is not registered or enabled in
  this profile; enable it in **Plugins**, or install it for that profile.
- **the probe cannot reach the host** — a transport/connection problem, not a
  version mismatch.

For the **Desktop app**, update through **Plugins → Add plugin** and restart.
`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install` manages the
`sdlc-web` / `sdlc-worker` / `sdlc-probe` CLI profiles; it cannot modify the
app-owned `desktop` profile. The panel shows the panel/host builds and a
**Copy diagnostics** action for support.

The panel also reads the **open session's workspace**, not the Harness process
directory, so the Desktop app shows the project you are actually working in.

For an offline runtime check (no model and no second web server):

```sh
node scripts/verify-tool-runtime.mjs /path/to/unpacked/dsh-runtime
```

It mounts all 26 role compositions and checks tool visibility, real pipeline
execution/rendering, invalid arguments, and worker denial of lead capabilities.
It also asserts that the shipped lead exposes one selectable preset (the Lead
Orchestrator), not the whole role roster. OS/delegation boundaries are stubbed:
this does not test running workers or the Desktop session-creation UI. An
optional second argument points to an unpacked plugin tarball.
A `never started` diagnostic means the loader did not create a plugin fiber;
look for the **earlier loader import error** in the application log. A missing
service instead reports `waiting for tools`. If the former persists after a
clean restart/install, include that earlier error and the installed version.

## Quick start

```sh
npm run build                     # artifacts (zero dependencies, offline; incl. UI bundle)
node scripts/validate-gates.mjs   # gate:P → gate:Q  (no model, no network)
npm run test:unit                 # L2 — pure modules + property tests
```

Every `test:*` script passes explicit globs rather than a directory: Node 24
resolves a bare directory positional as a *script* and fails with
`Cannot find module '<dir>'`, while globs work on every supported engine.

The deterministic control plane needs no model at all:

```sh
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs init        # .sdlc/, integration branch, detected gates
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs status
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs selftest --mock
```

## Flow visualizer (right sidebar)

While a session is open, the DSH right sidebar contains an **SDLC Flow** entry
(the guide's capsule, or auto-open on the first session that has an SDLC
project). It is a live, read-only view of the orchestrator, built around one
question: **what needs attention?** The old Status and Board tabs were duplicates
of data already in the flow snapshot, so the panel now has three primary
surfaces plus settings:

- **Flow** — a live **animated task map** (below) plus a “Needs attention” queue
  first (unresolved escalations, failed tasks, failing gates, orphaned worker
  runs, path conflicts), a progress ring and state distribution, live workers,
  and collapsible gates/routing/activity evidence. Click a task node to open its
  detail: role, risk, tier/model, attempts, resources, runs, gates, dependencies
  and the latest event, plus **Compare runs**.
- **Live map** — a deterministic SVG rendered in the browser from the flow
  snapshot (no model call, no generated diagram). Stages are horizontal bands, so
  parallel branches appear side by side; running nodes glow and stream packets
  along their dependency edges, completed paths stay lit, and blocked or failed
  paths turn red. Hover or select a node to trace its upstream and downstream
  path. The parallel meter shows active workers against the host-computed
  effective cap, and the progress card shows recorded tokens per completed task.
- **Tasks** — the board without columns: search, All/Active/Blocked/Done
  filters, tasks grouped by lifecycle state, and the same inline task detail.
- **Review** — task and run **selects** populated from the flow snapshot (no
  hand-typed IDs); defaults to the newest two runs, shows signed time/token/cost
  deltas, changed gates, and a collapsed trace path.
- **Settings** (gear) — a validated `.sdlc/config.yml` editor grouped by section.
  Only changed fields get a Save button; rejected writes never touch the file.

All surfaces share one `/api/sdlc.flow` snapshot and one config snapshot. Polling
is adaptive — 2.5 s while a task or worker is in flight, 8 s when quiet — and
each poll sends the newest event id as a cursor, so only new events cross the
wire and the client merges them into a bounded window. On a failed poll the last
snapshot is shown as *stale* rather than blanked. Opening the panel on a
workspace that has never been initialised **bootstraps it automatically** (see
[No init step — use the Harness model](#no-init-step--use-the-harness-model));
the guided state now appears only when auto-setup genuinely fails (no recognised
stack marker), with the real reason and a copyable `sdlc init` command that
prints the same diagnosis. A bare 404 is diagnosed as a host/client version
mismatch with restart and reinstall guidance (an in-place update does not
replace loaded host code). Missing cost/tokens/duration stay `—` with a reason,
never `0`. Set `autoOpen: false` in the UI row config to stop the automatic
open. DSH's right sidebar has **no surface without a session**, so the Start
screen cannot show it — start a session first.

## Install

### One command — always the latest published version

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
```

This resolves `latest` from the npm registry itself, pins the **exact** version
in the `sdlc-web` profile, records the matching pnpm release-age exemption,
creates the profile when missing, prunes packages left by older releases,
installs, re-selects the bundle (a failed uninstall can leave the package
installed but disabled), and verifies the installed `package.json`. Re-running
it upgrades an existing install instead of requiring an uninstall first.

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all          # lead + worker + probe
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --tag beta          # newest prerelease
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --version 1.1.1
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json      # no changes
```

It is idempotent. Prerequisites: `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13.

> **Restart after installing.** A running lead keeps the old module tree in
> memory even after the package on disk changes (deep-imported preset rows are
> not hot-replaced). Quit DeepSeek Harness completely and reopen it; otherwise a
> new session can still report the previous version's `agent-preset/invalid`.
> The installer prints this reminder.

### No-clone install — prebuilt release artifact

Download the release artifact and run its installer. Nothing is compiled on your
machine, and you do not need the source.

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/pwoodman/dsh-sdlc/releases/latest/download/dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
tar xzf dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz && cd dsh-sdlc-*/
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin tree to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-sdlc/<version>/` (so you can
delete the download), then creates the `sdlc-web`, `sdlc-worker` and `sdlc-probe`
profiles, installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It
is idempotent — re-run it any time.

Prerequisites: `dsh` **installed as a package** (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13. A wrapper that
merely answers `dsh --version` — an `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` shim, a shell
function, a hand-written script — is not enough: the platform gate reads the
installed package's own files, and the installer now refuses that setup with
this reason instead of failing later inside `gate:M0`.

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web          # the interactive lead (web GUI)
```

### Uninstall — one click in the plugin manager

The lead installs exactly **one** package (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`; its
members are folded inside it), so removing that single entry in the plugin
manager removes everything — no ghost entries, nothing "still required". From
the CLI it is the same one spec:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web remove @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow
```

A profile installed by a pre-fold release may still list the four members as
plain dependencies; re-run the installer (or this one command) to clear them:

```sh
pnpm remove --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui
```

On Windows, close a running lead first (`sdlc.db` and the bundle files are held
open while it runs). A profile directory itself (`~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web`) is
disposable and can always be deleted outright. The `@deepseek-ai/…` bundles you
see running (for example `dsh-agent-preset-registry`) are DeepSeek Harness's
own — they ship with the profile template and are not part of this plugin.

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop — what works today

The Desktop app owns its `desktop` profile and the `dsh` CLI refuses to manage
it, so the CLI/tarball paths above do not target it. Desktop users install
through the sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin** dialog (paste a package name, a
tarball URL, or an absolute path).

Two honest limits on a Desktop-only machine:

- the lead dispatches workers by spawning `dsh --profile sdlc-worker`, so it
  needs a `dsh` CLI on `PATH` for real task execution — without one, the lead,
  the tools, the presets and the web panel all work, but dispatch does not;
- package installs into `desktop` are the app's own operation, so a plugin that
  needs the worker/probe profiles is better tested against CLI profiles.

### Registry / Add-plugin wizard — one spec for the lead

Once the packages are published under an npm scope you own, the lead is a single
spec (the same shape `dsh-context` and `dsh-proactive` use: prebuilt `lib/` + its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no profile edits, no build
and no restart):

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create once
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

Or fill `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow` into the **Add plugin** wizard on the Plugins page.

> **Fresh release not installing?** pnpm 11 applies a 24-hour
> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a release published in
> the last day can resolve to the *previous* version. Prefer the installer
> above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you. For a
> manual install, pin it exactly
> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1`) and add **one list item per pattern** to
> the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1'
> ```
>
> A combined value such as `pkg@a || pkg@b` is not a valid pnpm pattern (it is
> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

#### Publishing under your own npm scope

The packages ship as `@patwoodman/*`. If your npm account does not own that scope,
`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

An npm **user scope** (`@your-username`) is free and exists automatically once
you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v1.1.1 && git push origin v1.1.1
```

The **Release** workflow verifies the tree, builds the tarball, publishes the
GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.
Create the token at <https://www.npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens> (an *Automation*
token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

### From a source checkout — one command

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

That single command generates the patches, builds the artifacts (zero
dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

Prerequisites: `dsh` installed as a package (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json
```

The lead also checks the registry on startup (at most once per 24 hours).
Stable builds install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease
builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).
The running process keeps the old code until it is restarted; the update reports
`restart-required`. A failed install is retried after a short backoff, the
installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

### Uninstall

Remove the package and its bundle selection from every managed profile:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

The GUI path is unchanged: the lead profile contains exactly one own-scope
package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: live flow map, tasks, review, validated config (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

Only the interactive lead can grant authority. A headless deployment is a guest
of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

## Web UI

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Flow | live animated task map, attention queue, parallel-worker meter, progress/spend, task detail |
| Tasks | search, All/Active/Blocked/Done filters, lifecycle grouping, inline task detail |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |
| Settings | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`,
`/api/sdlc.flow`) read the live DB and are scoped to the open session's
workspace; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI
uses. A project row belonging to another checkout is never rendered.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

### No init step — use the Harness model

Two rituals are gone: there is **no `sdlc init` step** and **no provider API
key**. DeepSeek Harness already resolves the signed-in provider/account (for
example `deepseek-account/deepseek-flash`) and its credential, and the
orchestrator now inherits both.

**Bootstrap on first touch.** The first panel request against a workspace root
materialises `.sdlc/` (tree, DB, gate detection, integration branch) and writes
a `config.yml` whose three tiers all name the model the current Harness session
resolves — the live `agentDefaultModel` selection, then on-disk profile
discovery, then DSH's own base default. `sdlc status` and
`sdlc config use-host-model` do the same from the CLI, so no command sequence
is required at all. The guarantees:

- **No key is ever implied.** A bootstrapped config names exactly one provider
  in its tiers and its price table — the fresh user is never asked for a
  second credential. `--no-host-model` (on `sdlc init`) opts out for
  deployments that route models some other way — read commands never write
  the spec defaults; exactly one of `--provider`/`--model` is a usage error,
  never a silent fallback.
- **Authored configs are never rewritten by a read.** Bootstrap only writes a
  config that does not exist yet. Changing the route later is an explicit
  action: **Settings → Harness model → Use this model for all tiers**, or
  `sdlc config use-host-model` (add `--provider`/`--model` to override, or
  `--dsh-home`/`--profile` outside the app). Both validate before writing,
  keep your own price rows without re-introducing legacy ones, and bootstrap
  an uninitialised workspace in one shot.
- **Half-projects heal themselves.** "Complete" means config.yml AND the
  database, and `ensureProject` is the single authority on it. An early
  `sdlc tasks` opens the DB before any config exists; a `git clean -fdx`
  removes the gitignored DB and keeps the config — the next touch repairs
  the missing half without touching the authored one.
- **No workspace is a dead end.** A workspace without a recognised stack
  marker (a plain folder, a Node project with only `package.json`, a
  `requirements.txt` Python project) still bootstraps — with
  `verification.detection: manual` and empty gates, the artifact the spec's
  own failure message prescribes. `sdlc config validate` visibly warns that
  verification passes vacuously until gates are authored, and the explicit
  `sdlc init` still refuses to guess. npm detection matches the spec's F.5
  table: `package-lock.json` is the npm marker — a bare `package.json` no
  longer produces `npm ci` commands that can never run.
- **Failure is actionable, never a mutation.** When auto-setup genuinely
  fails (an unwritable workspace, an unexpected error), the panel explains
  why with the host's real reason, the CLI prints a clean
  `BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` report, and nothing is guessed. A failed explicit init
  leaves the user's git repository untouched (no integration branch, no
  .gitignore); auto-setup never writes a `.gitignore` outside a git
  repository. A leftover tree cannot be poisoned: config writes and
  adoption require a complete project. The next request retries, so fixing
  the workspace recovers without a host restart.
- **"No project yet" is not a failure.** A set-up workspace with no project
  row shows an accurate empty state — "create a project with `/sdlc run`" —
  not a setup-failure card.

**Workers use the same route and the same credential store.** In-process
subagents already run on the parent route, so delegation needs no key of its
own. Process workers receive the adopted provider/model through the
`agent-default-model` tier overlay and `DSH_HOME`, so `deepseek-account`
resolves the same account token. No provider key is ever materialized into the
worker environment.

When DSH exposes no currency metadata, the adopted price entry is explicitly
`unknown`; cost renders as `—` instead of a guessed number. Configure prices in
Settings if you want cost estimates.

## Status

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 906 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness. The 1.1.1 packed tarballs install, boot the
probe, create a lead session and uninstall cleanly; the no-clone tarball also
installs end-to-end in a fresh `DSH_HOME` and passes M0. `doctor` passes with 0
errors and 0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-mock-llm — deterministic test provider

**Test-only, never published** (`"private": true`). Registers a deterministic
`ctx.llm` provider so every offline test and CI acceptance run is free,
networkless and reproducible.

Fault modes and injections are selected through the model string:

```
mock/<scenario>?fail=429:2                  # fail the first two calls
mock/<scenario>?inject=escape|falsefile|injection
```

Installed into the `sdlc-test` and `sdlc-probe` profiles only.

MIT

# dsh-sdlc-flow — DSH SDLC Flow (DeepSeek Harness plugin suite)

> **Current release: 1.1.1.** Install from this checkout
> (`npm run install:local`), or the registry form
> (`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install`) — see
> [Install](#install). See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for scope and known
> limitations and [PROOF_REPORT.md](PROOF_REPORT.md) for measured evidence. No
> confirmatory developer-productivity claim is supported yet.

and reopen it. Do not edit the Desktop profile by hand. Once this build is
installed, later registry releases are checked on startup: stable builds install
automatically, prerelease builds report availability (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install`
opts in; `off` disables). Restart to load the new code.

### “The panel is newer than the SDLC host code”

Host plugin code is loaded once at process start; an in-place update replaces
files on disk but not the host code already running. The panel now probes the
routes and distinguishes three cases before telling you what to do:

- **status answers, flow does not** — an older host build is loaded; fully quit
  Harness and reopen. Closing the window can leave it running in the background:
  use **Quit** from the app/tray menu, or on Linux
  `pkill -f deepseek-harness` / `flatpak kill com.deepseek.harness`.
- **no SDLC route answers** — the host plugin is not registered or enabled in
  this profile; enable it in **Plugins**, or install it for that profile.
- **the probe cannot reach the host** — a transport/connection problem, not a
  version mismatch.

For the **Desktop app**, update through **Plugins → Add plugin** and restart.
`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install` manages the
`sdlc-web` / `sdlc-worker` / `sdlc-probe` CLI profiles; it cannot modify the
app-owned `desktop` profile. The panel shows the panel/host builds and a
**Copy diagnostics** action for support.

The panel also reads the **open session's workspace**, not the Harness process
directory, so the Desktop app shows the project you are actually working in.

For an offline runtime check (no model and no second web server):

```sh
node scripts/verify-tool-runtime.mjs /path/to/unpacked/dsh-runtime
```

It mounts all 26 role compositions and checks tool visibility, real pipeline
execution/rendering, invalid arguments, and worker denial of lead capabilities.
It also asserts that the shipped lead exposes one selectable preset (the Lead
Orchestrator), not the whole role roster. OS/delegation boundaries are stubbed:
this does not test running workers or the Desktop session-creation UI. An
optional second argument points to an unpacked plugin tarball.
A `never started` diagnostic means the loader did not create a plugin fiber;
look for the **earlier loader import error** in the application log. A missing
service instead reports `waiting for tools`. If the former persists after a
clean restart/install, include that earlier error and the installed version.

## Quick start

```sh
npm run build                     # artifacts (zero dependencies, offline; incl. UI bundle)
node scripts/validate-gates.mjs   # gate:P → gate:Q  (no model, no network)
npm run test:unit                 # L2 — pure modules + property tests
```

Every `test:*` script passes explicit globs rather than a directory: Node 24
resolves a bare directory positional as a *script* and fails with
`Cannot find module '<dir>'`, while globs work on every supported engine.

The deterministic control plane needs no model at all:

```sh
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs init        # .sdlc/, integration branch, detected gates
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs status
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs selftest --mock
```

## Flow visualizer (right sidebar)

While a session is open, the DSH right sidebar contains an **SDLC Flow** entry
(the guide's capsule, or auto-open on the first session that has an SDLC
project). It is a live, read-only view of the orchestrator, built around one
question: **what needs attention?** The old Status and Board tabs were duplicates
of data already in the flow snapshot, so the panel now has three primary
surfaces plus settings:

- **Flow** — a live **animated task map** (below) plus a “Needs attention” queue
  first (unresolved escalations, failed tasks, failing gates, orphaned worker
  runs, path conflicts), a progress ring and state distribution, live workers,
  and collapsible gates/routing/activity evidence. Click a task node to open its
  detail: role, risk, tier/model, attempts, resources, runs, gates, dependencies
  and the latest event, plus **Compare runs**.
- **Live map** — a deterministic SVG rendered in the browser from the flow
  snapshot (no model call, no generated diagram). Stages are horizontal bands, so
  parallel branches appear side by side; running nodes glow and stream packets
  along their dependency edges, completed paths stay lit, and blocked or failed
  paths turn red. Hover or select a node to trace its upstream and downstream
  path. The parallel meter shows active workers against the host-computed
  effective cap, and the progress card shows recorded tokens per completed task.
- **Tasks** — the board without columns: search, All/Active/Blocked/Done
  filters, tasks grouped by lifecycle state, and the same inline task detail.
- **Review** — task and run **selects** populated from the flow snapshot (no
  hand-typed IDs); defaults to the newest two runs, shows signed time/token/cost
  deltas, changed gates, and a collapsed trace path.
- **Settings** (gear) — a validated `.sdlc/config.yml` editor grouped by section.
  Only changed fields get a Save button; rejected writes never touch the file.

All surfaces share one `/api/sdlc.flow` snapshot and one config snapshot. Polling
is adaptive — 2.5 s while a task or worker is in flight, 8 s when quiet — and
each poll sends the newest event id as a cursor, so only new events cross the
wire and the client merges them into a bounded window. On a failed poll the last
snapshot is shown as *stale* rather than blanked. Opening the panel on a
workspace that has never been initialised **bootstraps it automatically** (see
[No init step — use the Harness model](#no-init-step--use-the-harness-model));
the guided state now appears only when auto-setup genuinely fails (no recognised
stack marker), with the real reason and a copyable `sdlc init` command that
prints the same diagnosis. A bare 404 is diagnosed as a host/client version
mismatch with restart and reinstall guidance (an in-place update does not
replace loaded host code). Missing cost/tokens/duration stay `—` with a reason,
never `0`. Set `autoOpen: false` in the UI row config to stop the automatic
open. DSH's right sidebar has **no surface without a session**, so the Start
screen cannot show it — start a session first.

## Install

### One command — always the latest published version

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
```

This resolves `latest` from the npm registry itself, pins the **exact** version
in the `sdlc-web` profile, records the matching pnpm release-age exemption,
creates the profile when missing, prunes packages left by older releases,
installs, re-selects the bundle (a failed uninstall can leave the package
installed but disabled), and verifies the installed `package.json`. Re-running
it upgrades an existing install instead of requiring an uninstall first.

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all          # lead + worker + probe
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --tag beta          # newest prerelease
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --version 1.1.1
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json      # no changes
```

It is idempotent. Prerequisites: `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13.

> **Restart after installing.** A running lead keeps the old module tree in
> memory even after the package on disk changes (deep-imported preset rows are
> not hot-replaced). Quit DeepSeek Harness completely and reopen it; otherwise a
> new session can still report the previous version's `agent-preset/invalid`.
> The installer prints this reminder.

### No-clone install — prebuilt release artifact

Download the release artifact and run its installer. Nothing is compiled on your
machine, and you do not need the source.

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/pwoodman/dsh-sdlc/releases/latest/download/dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
tar xzf dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz && cd dsh-sdlc-*/
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin tree to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-sdlc/<version>/` (so you can
delete the download), then creates the `sdlc-web`, `sdlc-worker` and `sdlc-probe`
profiles, installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It
is idempotent — re-run it any time.

Prerequisites: `dsh` **installed as a package** (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13. A wrapper that
merely answers `dsh --version` — an `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` shim, a shell
function, a hand-written script — is not enough: the platform gate reads the
installed package's own files, and the installer now refuses that setup with
this reason instead of failing later inside `gate:M0`.

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web          # the interactive lead (web GUI)
```

### Uninstall — one click in the plugin manager

The lead installs exactly **one** package (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`; its
members are folded inside it), so removing that single entry in the plugin
manager removes everything — no ghost entries, nothing "still required". From
the CLI it is the same one spec:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web remove @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow
```

A profile installed by a pre-fold release may still list the four members as
plain dependencies; re-run the installer (or this one command) to clear them:

```sh
pnpm remove --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui
```

On Windows, close a running lead first (`sdlc.db` and the bundle files are held
open while it runs). A profile directory itself (`~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web`) is
disposable and can always be deleted outright. The `@deepseek-ai/…` bundles you
see running (for example `dsh-agent-preset-registry`) are DeepSeek Harness's
own — they ship with the profile template and are not part of this plugin.

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop — what works today

The Desktop app owns its `desktop` profile and the `dsh` CLI refuses to manage
it, so the CLI/tarball paths above do not target it. Desktop users install
through the sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin** dialog (paste a package name, a
tarball URL, or an absolute path).

Two honest limits on a Desktop-only machine:

- the lead dispatches workers by spawning `dsh --profile sdlc-worker`, so it
  needs a `dsh` CLI on `PATH` for real task execution — without one, the lead,
  the tools, the presets and the web panel all work, but dispatch does not;
- package installs into `desktop` are the app's own operation, so a plugin that
  needs the worker/probe profiles is better tested against CLI profiles.

### Registry / Add-plugin wizard — one spec for the lead

Once the packages are published under an npm scope you own, the lead is a single
spec (the same shape `dsh-context` and `dsh-proactive` use: prebuilt `lib/` + its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no profile edits, no build
and no restart):

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create once
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

Or fill `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow` into the **Add plugin** wizard on the Plugins page.

> **Fresh release not installing?** pnpm 11 applies a 24-hour
> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a release published in
> the last day can resolve to the *previous* version. Prefer the installer
> above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you. For a
> manual install, pin it exactly
> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1`) and add **one list item per pattern** to
> the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@1.1.1'
> ```
>
> A combined value such as `pkg@a || pkg@b` is not a valid pnpm pattern (it is
> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

#### Publishing under your own npm scope

The packages ship as `@patwoodman/*`. If your npm account does not own that scope,
`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

An npm **user scope** (`@your-username`) is free and exists automatically once
you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v1.1.1 && git push origin v1.1.1
```

The **Release** workflow verifies the tree, builds the tarball, publishes the
GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.
Create the token at <https://www.npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens> (an *Automation*
token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

### From a source checkout — one command

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

That single command generates the patches, builds the artifacts (zero
dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

Prerequisites: `dsh` installed as a package (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json
```

The lead also checks the registry on startup (at most once per 24 hours).
Stable builds install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease
builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).
The running process keeps the old code until it is restarted; the update reports
`restart-required`. A failed install is retried after a short backoff, the
installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

### Uninstall

Remove the package and its bundle selection from every managed profile:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

The GUI path is unchanged: the lead profile contains exactly one own-scope
package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: live flow map, tasks, review, validated config (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

Only the interactive lead can grant authority. A headless deployment is a guest
of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

## Web UI

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Flow | live animated task map, attention queue, parallel-worker meter, progress/spend, task detail |
| Tasks | search, All/Active/Blocked/Done filters, lifecycle grouping, inline task detail |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |
| Settings | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`,
`/api/sdlc.flow`) read the live DB and are scoped to the open session's
workspace; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI
uses. A project row belonging to another checkout is never rendered.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

### No init step — use the Harness model

Two rituals are gone: there is **no `sdlc init` step** and **no provider API
key**. DeepSeek Harness already resolves the signed-in provider/account (for
example `deepseek-account/deepseek-flash`) and its credential, and the
orchestrator now inherits both.

**Bootstrap on first touch.** The first panel request against a workspace root
materialises `.sdlc/` (tree, DB, gate detection, integration branch) and writes
a `config.yml` whose three tiers all name the model the current Harness session
resolves — the live `agentDefaultModel` selection, then on-disk profile
discovery, then DSH's own base default. `sdlc status` and
`sdlc config use-host-model` do the same from the CLI, so no command sequence
is required at all. The guarantees:

- **No key is ever implied.** A bootstrapped config names exactly one provider
  in its tiers and its price table — the fresh user is never asked for a
  second credential. `--no-host-model` (on `sdlc init`) opts out for
  deployments that route models some other way — read commands never write
  the spec defaults; exactly one of `--provider`/`--model` is a usage error,
  never a silent fallback.
- **Authored configs are never rewritten by a read.** Bootstrap only writes a
  config that does not exist yet. Changing the route later is an explicit
  action: **Settings → Harness model → Use this model for all tiers**, or
  `sdlc config use-host-model` (add `--provider`/`--model` to override, or
  `--dsh-home`/`--profile` outside the app). Both validate before writing,
  keep your own price rows without re-introducing legacy ones, and bootstrap
  an uninitialised workspace in one shot.
- **Half-projects heal themselves.** "Complete" means config.yml AND the
  database, and `ensureProject` is the single authority on it. An early
  `sdlc tasks` opens the DB before any config exists; a `git clean -fdx`
  removes the gitignored DB and keeps the config — the next touch repairs
  the missing half without touching the authored one.
- **No workspace is a dead end.** A workspace without a recognised stack
  marker (a plain folder, a Node project with only `package.json`, a
  `requirements.txt` Python project) still bootstraps — with
  `verification.detection: manual` and empty gates, the artifact the spec's
  own failure message prescribes. `sdlc config validate` visibly warns that
  verification passes vacuously until gates are authored, and the explicit
  `sdlc init` still refuses to guess. npm detection matches the spec's F.5
  table: `package-lock.json` is the npm marker — a bare `package.json` no
  longer produces `npm ci` commands that can never run.
- **Failure is actionable, never a mutation.** When auto-setup genuinely
  fails (an unwritable workspace, an unexpected error), the panel explains
  why with the host's real reason, the CLI prints a clean
  `BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` report, and nothing is guessed. A failed explicit init
  leaves the user's git repository untouched (no integration branch, no
  .gitignore); auto-setup never writes a `.gitignore` outside a git
  repository. A leftover tree cannot be poisoned: config writes and
  adoption require a complete project. The next request retries, so fixing
  the workspace recovers without a host restart.
- **"No project yet" is not a failure.** A set-up workspace with no project
  row shows an accurate empty state — "create a project with `/sdlc run`" —
  not a setup-failure card.

**Workers use the same route and the same credential store.** In-process
subagents already run on the parent route, so delegation needs no key of its
own. Process workers receive the adopted provider/model through the
`agent-default-model` tier overlay and `DSH_HOME`, so `deepseek-account`
resolves the same account token. No provider key is ever materialized into the
worker environment.

When DSH exposes no currency metadata, the adopted price entry is explicitly
`unknown`; cost renders as `—` instead of a guessed number. Configure prices in
Settings if you want cost estimates.

## Status

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 906 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness. The 1.1.1 packed tarballs install, boot the
probe, create a lead session and uninstall cleanly; the no-clone tarball also
installs end-to-end in a fresh `DSH_HOME` and passes M0. `doctor` passes with 0
errors and 0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow — the lead bundle

The **one** spec an interactive SDLC lead installs. Its patch layer is generated
as the union of its four members' rows (`scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs` in the
source repo), because the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a profile lists and
never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`.

Contains, in a single install:

| Member | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core) | the nine host services (tasks, scheduler, router, verifier, integration, evidence, escalation, worker-mgr, recovery) |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools) | the propose-only model tools and the `/sdlc` command surface |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets) | 26 role compositions; the lead publishes only the Lead Orchestrator as a selectable preset |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui) | the SDLC right-sidebar web UI and its host routes |

## Install

```sh
# create the profile from the shipped `web` template first
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config

# then the single spec
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow

dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

No build step and no profile edits: the package ships prebuilt `lib/` plus its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it automatically.

From a source checkout the members are unpublished, so the installer links them
as ordinary module dependencies instead (see `scripts/install-local.mjs` in the
source repo) — they must **not** be added as bundles there, or every row would
compose twice.

## Update, auto-update, uninstall

```sh
# upgrade in place (also prunes members left by older releases)
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all

# report only
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json

# remove the package and its bundle selection
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

On startup the lead checks the registry at most once per 24 hours. Stable builds
install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease builds only
report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in,
`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off` disables the check). The running process keeps the old
code until it is restarted; the result is reported as `restart-required`.
Failed installs retry after a short backoff, the version on disk is verified, and
a major release requires explicit consent. Link/file/git installs are never
replaced automatically.

The lead installs exactly one own-scope package, so the GUI **Remove** action
also uninstalls everything without ghost member entries.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` (declared as a `peerDependency`; DSH
  enforces this range at install and at load)
- Node.js ≥ 22.13 (`node:sqlite`)
