evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-model-picker-control

English | 中文

Model picker control for DSH — rename, regroup, sort, hide and badge every model in one place.

cross-provider partitions · rename models & groups · drag-to-reorder · hide a provider or a single model · suffix capsules · one-click restore

dsh plugin add dsh-model-picker-control

     

--- ## Why DSH ships a good model picker, but the display is fixed: providers come in a hard-coded order, model names are whatever the catalog says, and there is no way to put two models from different providers side by side. If you route some models through an account provider and others through a partner provider, the list you actually want never exists. This plugin gives you one settings page — sitting next to the built-in **Models** page — that owns the *display* of the picker, without patching a single third-party plugin. Hide the models you never touch, rename the rest into something you can recognise at a glance, drag the groups into the order you think in, and merge models from different providers into a partition such as **Free** or **Experimental**. ## Features | | | |---|---| | **Rename anything** | Model display names, provider group names, and a short suffix capsule per model. | | **Cross-provider partitions** | Create a partition and drop models into it from any provider — they render as one group. | | **Drag to reorder** | Reorder provider groups and partitions with a handle (or focus it and press ↑ ↓). | | **Hide, don't delete** | Hide a whole provider or a single model. Nothing is removed from the catalog. | | **In-group order** | Catalog order, or by model name. Per group or globally. | | **Suffix capsules** | A host-native pill after the name — blue, dark red or cyan — that sits beside the host's own `1017` tag. | | **Draft & save** | Every edit stays local until you press **Save**; leaving the page with changes asks first. | | **Restore** | One click clears the plugin's settings; the host default returns. | ## Screenshots Real setup, real host. This is the author's own picker: a cross-provider **Free** partition on top, a cross-provider **Fast** partition below it, a suffix capsule on nearly every name (`腾讯` `Tencent` `MiniMax` `Cmdc` `OpenAI` `Google` `Al`), providers he never touches hidden, and the host's own `1017` tag still next to the DeepSeek model.

**Settings → Groups & partitions** — drag the groups into your own order, rename or hide a provider, and create a partition that pulls models in from any provider:

**Settings → Models** — rename a model, type a suffix capsule and pick its tone, drop it into a partition, or hide it. Nothing is written until you press **Save**:

## Install ``` dsh plugin add dsh-model-picker-control ``` Then restart DSH. Open **Settings** — a new page, **Model picker** (模型选择器), appears next to the built-in **Models** page. Prefer a local build? ```bash git clone https://github.com/qzz19970504/dsh-model-picker-control.git cd dsh-model-picker-control npm install npm test npm pack # produces dsh-model-picker-control-.tgz dsh plugin add ./dsh-model-picker-control-.tgz ``` ## Quickstart 1. Open **Settings → Model picker**. 2. Under **Groups and partitions**, press **New partition** and name it, for example, `Free`. 3. In the **Models** table, pick `Free` in the partition dropdown of the models you want there — from any provider. 4. Drag the groups into the order you like, hide what you don't use, and give the important ones a suffix capsule such as `NEW` or `cheap`. 5. Press **Save**, then open the model picker in the composer. It matches immediately; no restart needed. ## Configuration Everything is stored under this plugin's own row in your profile config (`config.picker`), written through the host settings service: ```yaml - id: model-picker-control name: 'dsh-model-picker-control' config: picker: version: 1 enabled: true # false = restore the host display, keep the settings sectionOrder: [p:free, deepseek-official, workbuddy] providers: deepseek-account: { name: DeepSeek Account, hidden: false } models: deepseek-official/deepseek-pro: { name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Pro, suffix: { text: cheap, tone: red }, partition: p:free } workbuddy/step-5-preview: { suffix: { text: NEW, tone: cyan }, partition: p:free, hidden: false } partitions: - { id: p:free, name: Free } sort: { default: name, bySection: { workbuddy: catalog } } badges: { show1017: true } ``` | Key | Type | Notes | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | boolean | `false` restores the host's own picker but keeps your edits. | | `sectionOrder` | string[] | Section ids: a provider id, or `p:`. | | `providers[id].name` | string | Group heading. Empty = the catalog name. | | `providers[id].hidden` | boolean | Hide the whole provider. | | `models["provider/model"].name` | string | Display name. Empty = the catalog name. | | `models["provider/model"].suffix` | `{text, tone}` | `tone` is `blue`, `red` or `cyan`; up to 20 characters. | | `models["provider/model"].partition` | string | `p:` to move it into a partition. | | `models["provider/model"].hidden` | boolean | Hide this single model. | | `partitions[]` | `{id, name}` | A partition merges models from different providers. | | `sort.default` | `catalog` \| `name` | In-group order. | | `sort.bySection` | map | Per-section override. | | `badges.show1017` | boolean | Show or hide the host's `1017` tag next to a model. | ## How it works ``` composer ──► slot conversation.input.model (single, session scope) │ ├─ host @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-model-selection priority 0 └─ this dsh-model-picker-control priority -1 ← wins, host seat goes inactive │ │ ctx.modelDirectories.directoryFor(sessionId) ▼ catalog groups ──┐ your config ─────┴──► src/pipeline.js ──► sections (order, names, hidden, partitions) │ ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ picker menu + trigger /model popup rows │ │ └────────► directory.select() ◄───┘ ``` - The picker seat `conversation.input.model` is a single, session-scoped slot. The plugin registers it at priority `-1`, which shadows the host seat at priority `0`; disabling the plugin brings the host seat straight back. Selecting, reasoning effort, search, keyboard navigation, the pending state and the “not available in subagent sessions” behaviour are all ported from the host picker and use the host's own `model` translations. - The `/model` popup builds its rows through the same pipeline, so names, groups, order and hidden models match the picker. Row ids stay `provider/model`, so the host's own select handler is still what switches models. - The model list itself is never modified. The plugin reads `ctx.modelDirectories.directoryFor(sessionId)` and renders a section list derived from the catalog plus your config; choosing a model still goes through `directory.select()`. - Hiding only changes what is displayed. A saved selection that becomes invisible is left untouched — the trigger falls back to “Select model” and you can pick another one. - Writes are revision-checked by the settings service, rolled back on failure, and only ever touch this plugin's row — the rest of `cordis.patch.yml` is never rewritten. - The page is available in Chinese and English, following the GUI language. ## FAQ **Does this patch other plugins?** No. It only registers slots and wraps the host's `/model` contribution in memory, and restores it on dispose. **I hid the model I was using.** Your saved selection is kept; the trigger shows “Select model” and the picker offers whatever is still visible. **Where are the settings?** In your DSH profile config, under the plugin's row: `config.picker`. **Restore all defaults** clears them. **Can I keep the `1017` tag and add my own capsule?** Yes, they coexist — the tag and the capsule are separate slots. **Does it work in subagent sessions?** The picker behaves as the host does there: it is shown as unavailable, matching host behaviour. ## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # concatenates src/ into lib/client.js (no bundler required) npm test # pure pipeline tests (node:test) npm pack ``` The source is plain ESM + `h()` calls — `src/pipeline.js` is pure data transformation and is what the tests cover; `src/client/` holds the slot code. ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

# Academic Harness

[![verify](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
![DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1+](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-0.2.1%2B-5b7bd5)

**A research workbench for DeepSeek Harness** — literature and web discovery, verbatim paper memory, a writing oracle for LaTeX, systematic-review and hypothesis ledgers, 730 scientific skills, and local self-improvement, all inside the DSH web UI.

Academic Harness is a **DSH profile**: it installs as a plugin, adds a preset with a research persona and academic tools, and keeps the general-purpose tools available on every preset.

![Architecture overview](docs/assets/diagrams/architecture.svg)

## Why Academic Harness

| Principle | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| **Evidence, not citation-shaped guesses** | PaperMemory stores papers as content-addressed Markdown and anchors claims to exact quote spans. `quote_check` and `trace` verify a quotation before it becomes a citation; an empty `cite` means *do not invent one*. [Read more](docs/PAPERS.md#paper-memory) |
| **A writing oracle with a gate** | The vendored `ah_*` engine inventories every number, citation, unit, and claim in a LaTeX tree. A turn closes only when it introduced no open blocker or major. [Read more](docs/WRITING.md#academic-harness-engine) |
| **Auditable research ledgers** | Systematic reviews and hypothesis tournaments live in append-only logs under the workspace, so a resumed session sees the same protocol, screening decisions, and ratings. [Reviews](docs/RESEARCH.md#systematic-reviews) · [Tournaments](docs/RESEARCH.md#hypothesis-tournaments) |
| **Discovery across the real literature** | OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed/Europe PMC, arXiv, and Crossref through one `literature_search` entry point, plus Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, CORE, Elicit, and FutureHouse. [Read more](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **A lab notebook that survives context loss** | A JSONL notebook shared across the delegation tree, a schema-validated `scientific_result` card, and deletion-only reply folding at five levels. [Read more](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **Local-first by design** | Workspace search (zvec-grep), PaperMemory, TextFold, ledgers, and the RSI store stay on disk. No key is required to boot. [Read more](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs) |

## Install

Requires **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1 or later**.

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
```

Then either:

**A — from the DSH Web UI (recommended):** open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste `github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness`, click **Install**, and start a new chat.

**B — a dedicated CLI profile:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile academic-harness add github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness
dsh --profile academic-harness
```

Confirm the preset selector at the top of the message box reads **Academic Harness**. The academic tools are preset-only; a session left on Standard/PTC will fail with `tools[name] is not a function`.

Full instructions, migration from `researchcraft`, troubleshooting, and the "one DSH surface at a time" rule are in **[Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md)**.

## What is inside

![Capability map](docs/assets/diagrams/capability-map.svg)

| Surface | Highlights | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **Search and discovery** | `literature_search` router, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, Crossref, Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Jina, CORE, Elicit, FutureHouse | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **Papers and evidence** | `paper_download`, `paper_fold`, `pdf_to_markdown`, PaperMemory's 14 tools, `integrity_check`, Paper2Agent | [Papers](docs/PAPERS.md) |
| **Writing and citation** | `ah_*` writing oracle and gate, `citation`, `manuscript_citations`, LaTeX, `scientific-figure-making`, `diagram-design`, `image_generate`, `mermaid_render` (Pele) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) |
| **Reviews and hypotheses** | `review` PRISMA-style ledger, `coscientist` Glicko-2 tournament, published-results feedback, cross-session priors | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Clinical and policy records** | `clinicaltrials`, `openfda`, `dataset_search`, `journal_policy`, `funder_policy` | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Workspace and notebook** | zvec-grep semantic search, lab notebook, `scientific_result`, `fold_text`, `research_template`, `sci_inspect` | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **Compute and delegation** | `runpod_run`/`modal_run`/`vastai_run`, `subagent_pro`, `subagent_vision`, specialist briefs, `agent-browser` | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) |
| **Skills** | 730 bundled skills: 140 domain, 16 methodology, 503 expert profiles, 23 drug-discovery, plus writing, figures, agents, and compute | [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) |
| **Self-improvement** | Local RSI: capture, diagnose, admit, inject, compare against control, promote or quarantine | [RSI](docs/RSI.md) |
| **Configuration** | Settings → Academic Harness API keys; every credential is optional at install | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |

The complete tool list, with scope and links, is the **[tool index](docs/TOOLS.md)**. The [architecture guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains which tools are available on every preset and which are preset-only.

## How a request works

![Request lifecycle](docs/assets/diagrams/request-lifecycle.svg)

Discovery finds candidate papers, `paper_resolve` collapses their identifiers, and `integrity_check` reports retraction status. A downloaded PDF is stored as content-addressed Markdown in PaperMemory, and a quotation must pass `quote_check` or `trace` before the agent treats it as evidence. The notebook records the work; `scientific_result` records the final finding.

## Documentation

| Start here | Go deeper | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| [Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md) | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) | [Tool index](docs/TOOLS.md) |
| [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | [Papers and evidence](docs/PAPERS.md) | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |
| [Documentation home](docs/README.md) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) | [Changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md) |
| | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) | [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) |
| | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) | [Optional tools](docs/OPTIONAL-TOOLS.md) |
| | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) · [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) · [RSI](docs/RSI.md) | [Engine notes](docs/ACADEMIC-HARNESS-ENGINE.md) |

## Requirements and scope

- **DSH 0.2.1+.** The plugin's bundle patches the web-app layer, so the profile must include `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`; the standard `web` profile does.
- **A preset check matters.** The research persona, search connectors, PaperMemory, zvec-grep, paper tools, citation/review/tournament tools, and the `subagent_pro`/`subagent_vision` routes are scoped to the Academic Harness preset. Only the general-purpose tools (notebook, fold, images, LaTeX, PDF, Mermaid, compute, templates) are on every preset.
- **Keys are optional.** No credential is needed to install or start; each connector stays disabled until its key is present. Some runtimes install in the background on first use — see [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs).
- **One DSH surface at a time.** `dsh-web`, `dsh-tui`, `dsh-martty`, and `academic-harness` share `$DSH_HOME`, port `3080`, and the zvec-grep daemon. Stop the previous one before starting another; see [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#one-dsh-surface-at-a-time).
- **Renamed in v0.16.0** from `dsh-researchcraft` / ResearchCraft. Old env names are still honored; migration is in [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#renamed-in-v0160).

## Development

```sh
npm install       # once, for the Settings page build
npm run build     # after any client/ change
npm run docs:diagrams   # regenerate the SVG figures from docs/diagrams/*.mmd
```

Server-side code is plain ESM JS with no build step. Tests are plain Node scripts; see [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for the full suite and the `paper_fold` live test.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Scientific skills are vendored or adapted from several open-source catalogues; [NOTICE](NOTICE) records exactly what was copied, renamed, or adapted from each.

# billion-context

English | 中文

Context-compression plugin — billion-context is all you need.

small context windows (100K is enough) · 5× fewer tokens · month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) · high compression quality

npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local

                                           

--- > **Cache health at a glance:** a healthy session keeps a **95–97%** prefix-cache hit rate — compression itself costs ≤2%. Sustained lower? Check attribution with `/acp` or `/acp-cache` (see [FAQ](#faq)); usual causes, in order: upstream cache TTL expiry · model switch · a bili bug (please report) · other/unknown. ## Community QQ Group: 1056132097 (full) 1108730198 (open) --- ## 📄 Paper / Preprint - **[Model-Driven Incremental Hierarchical Compression: Training-Free Multi-Generational Context Management for Long-Lived Coding Agents](./paper/model-driven-incremental-hierarchical-compression-training-free-multi-generational-context-management-for-long-lived-coding-agents.md)** (English, v0.2) > 📝 **The paper itself is open-sourced under the MIT License as part of the codebase (`paper/`). It is a living document — anyone may edit it; improvements are welcome via pull request.** A production-scale longitudinal study: 4.5 months, three hosts, 174,327 model calls, 18.76B cumulative input tokens (~24.7B across all hosts), zero window violations on 204,800-token models, marathon sessions of 8,584–12,049 calls. --- `billion-context` sits between **any** agent and its model API, rewriting Anthropic/OpenAI streams with [acp-kernel](https://github.com/ranxianglei/acp-kernel) compression. The model decides **when** and **what** to compress into high-fidelity summaries — not a hard truncation limit. ## Why Long coding sessions blow up context. Each provider charges per token, and once you pass the context window the session degrades or dies. `billion-context` compresses consumed conversation into layered summaries so you can run a single session for days — billions of tokens through one context window. Unlike a host's built-in summarizer, compression here is **incremental, reversible, and prefix-cache friendly**: summaries are written in small ranges, can be decompressed on demand, and the cache prefix stays intact. ## How it works ``` Agent (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Aider ...) │ you point the agent's base URL at the proxy ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ billion-context│ 1. parse the request (Anthropic or OpenAI shape) │ proxy │ 2. run acp-kernel compression on the conversation │ │ 3. inject a `compress` tool + compression philosophy │ │ 4. forward to the real model API │ │ 5. rewrite the streaming response └─────────────────┘ │ ▼ real model API (Anthropic / OpenAI / compatible) ``` ### Context-management tools The proxy injects four context-management tools into the conversation; the model calls them itself as context grows, and the proxy executes `compress` server-side so folded ranges stay summarized in history until restored: - **`compress`** — fold a message range into a detailed summary. - **`decompress`** — restore a compressed range when exact details are needed again. - **`search_context`** — keyword search over compressed summaries and visible messages. - **`acp_status`** — context-usage overview plus which ranges are still compressible. ## Which do I need? Pick by your client: | Client | Use | |---|---| | **pi** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili pi` (launcher) or `bili plugin install pi` (native); standalone [`billion-context-pi`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi) remains usable — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#pi-pidev-coding-agent) | | **opencode** (1.x / 2.x) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili opencode` (launcher) or `bili plugin install opencode` (native); standalone [`opencode-acp`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/opencode-acp) remains usable on 1.x — full guide: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) | | **omp** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili omp` (built-in plugin) or `bili plugin install omp` (self-spawning native plugin, no launcher) | | **dsh** | `bili dsh` (launcher — full native plugin via `--patch`) or `bili plugin install dsh` ≡ `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` (one unified lane) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **kimi** | `bili plugin install kimi` (self-spawning native, Kimi Code ≥ 2.0.0) or `bili kimi` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **hermes** | `bili plugin install hermes` (self-spawning native, Python plugin #958) or `bili hermes` (cert-MITM) | | **zcode** (Z.ai / bigmodel coding plan) | `bili plugin install zcode` (self-spawning native, #1145) or cert-MITM via the GUI's Settings → Network or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **claude** | `bili claude` (launcher) or `bili plugin install claude` (native posture, #964 — managed settings block + session-owned proxy; see the notes below) | | **codex** | `bili codex` (launcher — the full zero-config posture) or `bili plugin install codex` (MCP-shell tools companion: **start bili first** — the shell never spawns a proxy and never routes codex's own traffic) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli) | | **jcode** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili jcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (compiled Rust binary, no plugin seam, [#962](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/962)) | | **gemini** (Gemini CLI) | `bili gemini` (launcher, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix — launcher-only (no in-loop tool seam, #1043) | | **iflow** (iFlow CLI) | `bili iflow` (launcher, `IFLOW_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix | | **qwen** (Qwen Code) | `bili qwen` (launcher, cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix | | **antigravity** (Antigravity CLI / agy, Google) | `bili antigravity` (launcher, `CLOUD_CODE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — Antigravity's real default upstream, #3129) or `/bili/` prefix — no plugin seam (closed Go language_server; its user-plugin surface is additive-only, #2115) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **mcode** (MiniMax Code) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili mcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (event hooks only, no model-request seam, [#1050](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1050)) | | **aider** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili aider` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (shell-command-only hooks, no tool-injection seam, [#1048](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1048)) | | **copilot** (GitHub Copilot CLI) | `bili copilot` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **amp** (Amp CLI) | `bili amp` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **crush** (Charm Crush) | `bili crush` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Go binary, no plugin seam; built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `base_url`s auto-discovered from crush.json (#2340) | | **zed** (Zed editor) | `bili zed` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Rust editor, no plugin seam; reqwest honors HTTPS_PROXY, CA via SSL_CERT_FILE (Linux env probing); built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `api_url`s auto-discovered from settings.json; loopback providers (ollama/lmstudio) stay direct via NO_PROXY (#2340) | | **goose** (Goose CLI) | `bili goose` (launcher) — rustls trusts no CA file, so no cert-MITM: openai/anthropic legs via `OPENAI_HOST`/`ANTHROPIC_HOST`, custom providers via a regenerated `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT` overlay (#1049) | | **everything else** (no context hook) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili ` (launcher, preferred) or `/bili/` prefix | **Native mode vs standalone extensions.** The host-native plugins (`bili plugin install …`) and the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) are **mutually exclusive** — both active means double compression. The installer makes the switch: it replaces the legacy entries (bare name, `npm:` alias, versioned, path form; array or object shape) and snapshots the original config to `.bili-bak` once; a **project-local** install is not touched — remove that one by hand. As a runtime safety net for manual installs, the native entries set `BILLION_CONTEXT_NATIVE=` synchronously at load so a standalone extension can stand down at action time. On the pi side the marker needs `billion-context-pi` **0.1.72+**, and the pi-native entry scans both pi settings files once its proxy is up and warns loudly when it spots a co-resident legacy entry the installer never saw — that warning is the only visible signal while an old `billion-context-pi` silently double-compresses. ## Install Linux / macOS — install with a user-level prefix (no `sudo`, no npm config changes, and `bili`'s self-update never hits permission errors): ```bash npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local ``` The `bili` command lands in `~/.local/bin` — already on PATH in most distros; if not, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. On nvm or Homebrew Node the default prefix is already user-owned — a plain `npm install -g billion-context` works as-is. On Windows the default prefix (`%APPDATA%\npm`) is also user-writable — plain `npm install -g billion-context`. This installs the `bili` command (`bili-proxy` is kept as an alias). Hitting `EACCES` with an old root-owned prefix? Reinstall with `--prefix=~/.local` (pass the flag again on any future npm reinstall of `bili`) — that is the permanent fix; avoid `sudo`. Prefer containers? A `Dockerfile` ships at the repository root — see [Running in Docker](#running-in-docker) below. ## Quickstart Three ways to use it — pick one: - **Native plugin (most native):** `bili plugin install ` — bili becomes a plugin inside the client; start the client as usual. - **Launcher (config-free):** one `bili ` command brings up the proxy and the client together — no real config file is ever touched. - **URL change (most universal):** prefix your client's baseURL with the proxy origin + `/bili/`. Mechanism details behind these three options (plugin lifecycle, runtime-info protocol, injection priority) live in [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Ports, briefly (#1660): `bili start` (manual) owns `8787`. Everything a lane spawns for you (native hooks, launcher lanes) lives in a separate self-managed zone starting at `18787` — collisions hop +1 and each lane remembers its drift, so zero-config installs never fight you for a port, and a deliberate `bili start` daemon is attached by default. Attach is lane-aware (#2905): a hook rides its own lane's instance first, NEVER another declared lane's — except lanes you list in `native.attachLanePriority` — and the 8787 user-zone daemon stays the LAST-resort fallback. An upgrade-restart that finds the previous build still draining on the lane's port waits for it to release (up to 5s) and rebinds the SAME port instead of drifting (#1723); only a genuinely occupied port hops +1 — and that hop is now logged loudly. ### Option 1 — Native plugin (`bili plugin install pi` / `omp` / `opencode` / `dsh` / `kimi` / `hermes` / `zcode`) The proxy lives inside the client: install once, then start the client exactly as you always do — no launcher command, no env vars, no fixed port, no URL edits. Supported today for **pi**, **omp**, **opencode** (1.x and 2.x), **dsh**, **kimi**, **hermes** and **zcode**: ```bash bili plugin install pi # registers a "billion-context" entry in pi's settings (npm form when bili itself was npm-installed) bili plugin install omp # registers an extensions entry in omp's config.yml (~/.omp/agent/config.yml) bili plugin install opencode # registers the plugin in opencode's real config + disables native auto-compaction bili plugin install dsh # runs 'dsh plugin --profile add billion-context' for every existing profile bili plugin install kimi # writes $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/billion-context/kimi.plugin.json (+ installed.json record); per-session routing block lands in config.toml on first start (Kimi Code >= 2.0.0) bili plugin install hermes # copies the Python plugin into ~/.hermes/plugins/billion-context/ (+ machine-owned bili.json sidecar) and enables it via `hermes plugins enable billion-context` bili plugin install zcode # writes hooks.enabled + a SessionStart hook + mcp.servers.bili into ~/.zcode/cli/config.json; per-session routing lands in the bigmodel provider store on first start bili plugin remove # undo (dsh removes through the same channel; config snapshots go to .bili-bak) ``` Where a client has its own plugin channel you can also install natively, skipping bili commands entirely: - **dsh:** `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` is the very command `bili plugin install dsh` drives per profile (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry — pasting a GitHub address installs source without `dist/` and the bundle never loads) — same end state either way (pnpm into the profile, bundled patch layer mounted by dsh itself); remove through the same channel. See the dsh section below. - **opencode:** add the bare npm name to your real config's plugin list — `"plugin": ["billion-context"]` (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry). The package publishes `exports["./server"]` → `dist/agent/opencode-native.js`, so opencode loads it through its own Npm.add machinery and the plugin self-spawns exactly like the bili-installed form. Do the two things the bili installer would have done for you too: set `"compaction": { "auto": false }` in the same config (otherwise OpenCode's native auto-compaction double-compresses) and keep a manual backup of the file first. - **claude:** this repository doubles as a Claude Code plugin marketplace — `/plugin marketplace add ranxianglei/billion-context`, then `/plugin install billion-context@billion-context`, then run `/billion-context:bili-setup` (it drives `bili plugin install claude` for you and tells you to restart). Same end state as the bili installer; the plugin ships no hooks or MCP entries of its own, so nothing double-registers. For pi / omp / kimi / claude there is no client-side channel — `bili plugin install ` writes their config entries for you (kimi's declarative `kimi.plugin.json` + registry record, claude's managed settings block, …). Notes: - Native mode is **mutually exclusive** with the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) — the installer swaps the entries and snapshots the original config (`.bili-bak`). - **pi:** native installs wire in built-in subagents by default (`acp_delegate` / `acp_delegate_wait` / `acp_delegate_cancel`) — how to disable them while keeping context compression: [Pi built-in subagents](#pi-built-in-subagents). - OpenCode legacy sessions, V1/V2 shapes and caveats: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode). - `kimi` reports runtime-info at bootstrap only (static headers can't carry per-request window/model values); subagent tool calls are routed by the proxy's outbound tool-use witness ring (#1685) — no model-visible conversation id. - `hermes`'s native plugin is Python: it points hermes' httpx stack at the proxy via env vars after a health check and stamps per-request headers through an `llm_request` middleware. - `codex` is the one client a plugin install cannot make self-sufficient: codex routes model traffic via env only (no config-file routing seam for the default ChatGPT-login provider — a managed `model_providers` block would force API-key auth and drop subscription login), and an MCP server cannot inject env into its parent. `bili plugin install codex` writes a single `[mcp_servers.bili]` block into `~/.codex/config.toml` (command = node, args = dist/mcp.js) exposing the four ACP tools; at session start the shell resolves a proxy — env `BILI_MCP_PROXY` > the live-instance record (any lane's proxy or a `bili start` daemon) > the 8787 user-zone default (#1660 removed the install-time origin bake, #403) — nothing reachable → `tools/list` fails with -32003. So: start bili first (`bili start` or any client's lane proxy), export HTTPS_PROXY yourself if you also want compression, or use `bili codex` for the zero-config full posture. Mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli). - `claude` has a native posture (#964): managed settings block + `SessionStart` hook + MCP shell; the hook rides the self-managed port zone (#1660) and re-pins the managed URL to the live origin each session, so port drift self-heals. Since #1821 the MCP shell also watches the proxy mid-session (30 s tick × 3 failures) and respawns a dead lane proxy itself, so model requests recover within ~90 s instead of a new session (same semantics as the zcode lane). Opt out with `BILI_NATIVE_CLAUDE=0` (passthrough). Mechanics: [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). **Known limitation (#2290):** the Claude Desktop app's Code tab (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-desktop`) sets its own `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on its embedded Claude Code, overriding the managed one — desktop sessions bypass the proxy entirely while the managed block's `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1` still applies, so they get neither bili compression nor native auto-compaction. The hook warns loudly at session start (and records it for `bili doctor`, which also flags machines where Claude Desktop is installed alongside the native lane); terminal sessions are unaffected. **Field-tested 2026-10-06 (#2290):** putting `HTTPS_PROXY` in the settings `env` block produced zero CONNECT traffic to a live MITM-enabled proxy on Claude Desktop 2.19675.1 / embedded CC 2.1.288 (Windows 11) — the variable reaches no network stack there, matching the CLI behavior of that era — note that newer builds (CC 2.1.301+) DO honour `HTTPS_PROXY` on the CLI, which is why `bili claude` routes via the `/bili/` base-URL rewrite — the launcher gives this lane no proxy and no CA at all, and a child that brings a proxy of its own gets the loopback hosts merged into `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` so that leg stays direct regardless of its proxy behavior (#3446). As of that version there is no usable routing seam on the desktop Code tab; the lane stays tracked in [#2290](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/2290) in case upstream changes behavior. Desktop-only users can restore native auto-compact with `bili plugin remove claude`. - `zcode` has a native posture (#1145): managed `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` block + per-session provider `baseURL` rewrite. Full mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md). - `jcode` and `aider` have no native mode (no plugin/MCP/tool-injection seam: #962, #1048) — use `bili jcode` / `bili aider`. - `copilot`, `amp` and `goose` are launcher-only (#1049); goose cannot be cert-MITMed (rustls trusts no CA file) and rides plain-HTTP base-URL redirects instead. ### Option 2 — Launcher (`bili pi` / `bili codex` / `bili claude` / `bili omp` / `bili opencode` / `bili hermes` / `bili dsh` / `bili codebuddy` / `bili qoder` / `bili trae` / `bili jcode` / `bili kimi` / `bili gemini` / `bili iflow` / `bili qwen` / `bili antigravity` / `bili mcode` / `bili aider` / `bili copilot` / `bili amp` / `bili goose`) The launcher wraps a client in one command: it starts a proxy on an independent port (a fresh instance is always spawned — a port is never reused), then points the client at it — **certificate-based MITM** where the client honors proxy/CA env vars, or an isolated **`/bili/` config rewrite** where it doesn't. No real config file is ever edited; the client's own config is READ to discover which HTTPS upstream hosts it talks to, and those hosts are whitelisted for MITM so the proxy can TLS-terminate exactly them and blind-tunnel everything else. ```bash bili pi # launch pi through the proxy — file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider, real ~/.pi untouched bili codex # launch codex through the proxy bili claude # launch claude through the proxy bili omp # pi-style, file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider + compaction cancel, real ~/.omp untouched bili opencode # OpenCode (1.x & 2.x): full guide in the [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) section below bili hermes # file-free (#535): hermes proxy env (HTTPS_PROXY + combined CA bundle via SSL_CERT_FILE) — https via CONNECT MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; real ~/.hermes untouched bili dsh # deepseek-harness: full native plugin injected via --patch (#941) — real dsh tools, session-bound /acp + /acp-cache (plugin mode); non-loopback upstreams ride proxy envs, loopback keeps the overlay DSH_HOME rewrite (#535); dsh auto-compaction off everywhere — host plane via the bundle patch, web-profile presets at load time (#1772/#2474/#3354) bili codebuddy # Tencent CodeBuddy Code CLI: CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite (OpenAI chat completions wire), budget aligned via CODEBUDDY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW; real ~/.codebuddy untouched bili qoder # qoder: model endpoint is hardcoded https (no /bili/ rewrite possible) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, default model hosts whitelisted (#653) bili trae # Trae CLI (ByteDance, closed Go binary, no base-URL override) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, model host from TRAE_CLI_API_HOST or the default enterprise gateway (#655) bili jcode # jcode (Rust agent harness) — env-only cert-MITM launch: HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, model host api.z.ai whitelisted, local loopback providers stay direct via NO_PROXY bili kimi # Kimi Code CLI (Moonshot): standard proxy envs except an unconditional loopback bypass — https via cert-MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; loopback endpoints inventoried with a manual /bili/ hint (#757) bili gemini # Gemini CLI (Google): GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite to generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Google native wire), real ~/.gemini untouched bili iflow # iFlow CLI: IFLOW_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite to apis.iflow.cn/v1 (OpenAI chat-completions wire), real ~/.iflow untouched bili qwen # Qwen Code (multi-protocol gemini-cli fork, no base-URL hook): cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, default DashScope/Qwen model hosts whitelisted, custom relays via --mitm-domain bili antigravity # Antigravity CLI (agy, Google): CLOUD_CODE_URL /bili/ rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — the real default upstream (bare cloudcode-pa 400s on /v1internal:*, #3129); undocumented language-server env override, v2.19.1 binary-verified; wire recognized as Google native by path (#2115) bili mcode # MiniMax Code CLI: same shape as kimi (proxy envs, unconditional loopback bypass, cert-MITM/absolute-form); session bound via X-Mavis-Session-Id (#1050) bili aider # Aider (Python pair programmer): cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; endpoint from OPENAI_API_BASE / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / --openai-api-base / .aider.conf.yml (#1048) bili copilot # Copilot CLI (GitHub, closed Go binary) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, api.githubcopilot.com + per-plan subdomains whitelisted (#1049) bili amp # Amp CLI (Sourcegraph, closed Go binary) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, ampcode.com whitelisted (#1049) bili goose # Goose (Block, Rust/reqwest): rustls release builds trust no CA file — openai/anthropic legs via OPENAI_HOST/ANTHROPIC_HOST, custom providers via a regenerated GOOSE_PATH_ROOT overlay (/bili/ rewrites, real config untouched) (#1049) bili pi --mitm-domain api.foo.com # add a domain to the MITM whitelist ``` ### Option 3 — URL change (`/bili/` prefix) Start the proxy: ```bash bili ``` Then just prefix your client's existing baseURL with `http://localhost:8787/bili/`. # dsh-plugin-reactive-resume Connect [Reactive Resume](https://rxresu.me) to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Read, create, and edit your resumes and job applications from a Harness session. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-reactive-resume ``` This package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the profile picks it up as a layer and mounts it automatically. Until you configure a key it mounts nothing and logs a warning, so installing it never leaves a profile unbootable. ## Configure Mint an API key at `https://rxresu.me/dashboard/settings/api-keys` and export it as `RXRESUME_API_KEY` — the bundle patch reads that variable. To set it explicitly, or to change any other option, patch the row by id from your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY ``` ### Options | Key | Default | Description | | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `apiKey` | `''` | API key from `/dashboard/settings/api-keys`. Empty mounts nothing. | | `url` | `https://rxresu.me` | Origin of your instance. Set this if you self-host. | | `serverName` | `resume` | Tool namespace. Tools reach the model as `mcp____`. | | `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-tool-call timeout. | Every tool Reactive Resume publishes is exposed. Narrowing that set is not currently possible from a plugin: Harness's `ctx.tools.restrict()` requires an agent-scoped context, which a plugin context is not. ### Self-hosted ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY url: http://localhost:3000 ``` ## What it does Bridges Reactive Resume's MCP server into `ctx.tools`, and contributes a system-prompt section covering the things models get wrong about resume editing: reading before patching, RFC 6902 path construction against the published schema, UUID-keyed section entries, and locked resumes. You could wire the bridge yourself with a raw `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. What you cannot do that way is contribute the prompt section — that is what this package adds. ## Harness compatibility The peer ranges list each supported DSH host line as an explicit `||` union: `^0.1.0-rc.6` (what this package already shipped against) plus `^0.2.0-rc.1` (which admits `0.2.0-rc.1` and `0.2.0-rc.2`). The union is purely additive — every version the old range admitted is still admitted. Every published DSH release is a prerelease, which makes the comparison mode matter: - The Harness host decides whether to mount a plugin with `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`. The upper bound is what rejected the old range there: `^0.1.0-rc.6` expands to `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`, and `0.2.0-rc.2` sorts above `0.2.0-0` because the numeric identifier `0` precedes `rc`. - npm's default mode — the one the plugin market's checker uses — additionally requires a comparator set to pin the same `major.minor.patch` tuple with a prerelease of its own. Under that mode the bare `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits only `0.1.0-rc.6` through `0.1.0-rc.8`. Measured against all 29 published host releases, that gap is wide: `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits 22 of them under the host's mode (every `0.1.x` line, including `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.7-rc.2`) but only 3 under npm's default mode. Widening the upper bound does not close it, because the default mode ignores the widened comparator: `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.3.0-0` still admits only those same 3, and `*` admits none at all. `^0.1.0-rc.6 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` admits 24 releases under the host's mode and 5 under the default one, so an explicit union member per host line is the only form both checkers agree on. Against `0.2.0-rc.2` this package needed no source change: `dsh-mcp-client@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps its `Config` union, its `apply(ctx, config)` signature, and the `mcp____` public tool name, while `dsh-system-prompt@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps `section({ name, order, text })`. What 0.2.0 adds to the bridge — MCP resource publishing and a server-instructions prompt section — is additive and scoped to `ctx.inject(["mcpResources"])` / `ctx.inject(["systemPrompt"])`, neither of which this package depends on. ## Development This package lives in the [Reactive Resume monorepo](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume) at `packages/dsh-plugin`, next to `packages/mcp` — the server it bridges. `src/tool-names.test.ts` checks every tool the prompt guide names against `@reactive-resume/mcp/tool-names`, so renaming a tool breaks this package in the same pull request. ```bash pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume test pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume build ``` ## License MIT > [!IMPORTANT] > Reactive Resume now lives at **[`reactive-resume/reactive-resume`](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume)** on GitHub. > GHCR images publish to `ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume`. > Docker Hub stays at `amruthpillai/reactive-resume`.

Reactive Resume

Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

Get Started · Learn More

Sponsored by

--- Create a free account, import an existing resume or start fresh, and see the finished page as you write. Download a PDF, Word, Markdown, or JSON file, or share your resume with a public link. You can also run the whole application on your own infrastructure. You own your data. The codebase is open source under the MIT license, with no tracking, no ads, and no paid tier. Optional AI features use a provider you connect; hosting and provider usage may have their own costs. ![Reactive Resume v6 editor with Write, Design, and Check modes and a live PDF preview](docs/images/getting-started/editor-overview.webp) ## Build a better resume, together [Join the Reactive Resume community on Discord](https://discord.gg/u9pAd3za9t) to exchange resume feedback, get help using or self-hosting the app, and share ideas with other users and contributors. - **Resume feedback:** post a redacted resume and one specific question, or help someone improve theirs. - **Help:** find troubleshooting discussions and ask questions in dedicated forum threads. - **Contribute:** discuss ideas, translations, and code with the people building Reactive Resume. Feedback comes from fellow community members. Remove contact details and other private information before posting. ## Features **Write, Design, and Check** - Redesigned editor with inline content editing and click-to-select on the page - Live PDF preview and browser downloads powered by Forme, rendered in a background worker - Rich text, custom sections, drag-and-drop ordering, and structured dates with consistent formatting - Autosave, local recovery of unsaved resume drafts, and up to 200 undo steps - Phone and tablet layouts, keyboard shortcuts, and a searchable command bar **Templates and Customization** - 18 templates, including the new Porygon and Smeargle, previewed with your own content - One-column, two-column, and ATS-safe template filters - Font presets, custom fonts, colors, spacing, A4 and Letter paper, and left or right sidebars - Fit overflowing content by adjusting density, margins, and text size - Custom Styles written as Semantic CSS, with an element picker on the page **Resume Checks** - Readability checks with findings pinned to the relevant lines - Job-posting keyword matching and a view of the text hiring software reads - Checks on the exported PDF, plus an optional AI writing review - A public [ATS checker](https://rxresu.me/ats-checker) that reads PDFs in your browser without an account **Documents and Cover Letters** - One searchable library for resumes and letters, with tags, sorting, and grid or list views - Standalone cover letters with their own editor, exports, and version history - Link a letter to a resume to keep its sender details and design in sync, or customize it independently - Automatic and named versions you can preview and restore - Trash with Undo and a 30-day recovery window **Job Applications** - List, Board, Insights, and Calendar views for tracking applications from Saved to Offer - Save jobs from a URL or pasted posting; optional keyword search through Firecrawl, Tavily, or Exa - Tailor a resume and draft a cover letter for a saved job - Track contacts, notes, follow-ups, application outcomes, and the documents you sent - Schedule interviews, export calendar events, and import or export applications as CSV **AI Assistant** - Assistant beside your resume or letter, with conversations tied to that document - Proposed edits show what changes and why; accept or reject each suggestion - Improve selected text, review writing, and draft letters from a resume and job posting - Connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, or other supported providers and compatible endpoints - Optional web search and page reading; self-hosters can configure shared AI and web-access providers **Import, Export, and Sharing** - Import Reactive Resume JSON, JSON Resume, LinkedIn data exports, PDF, and Word files - JSON, LinkedIn, and readable PDF imports work without AI; Word imports require a connected provider - Export resumes and letters as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, or JSON - Share resumes through public links with optional password protection and view/download statistics - REST API and MCP server for document management, imports, exports, checks, and application workflows **Privacy and Control** - Self-host with Docker, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or a 1-click deploy on Hostinger - No tracking or ads; export your account data or delete your account - Passkeys, two-factor authentication, and linked sign-in providers - Multiple interface languages, light/dark/system themes, and reduced-motion support ## Templates

For a deployment using published images, follow the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker). For source development, see the [development setup guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development). ## Tech Stack | Category | Technology | | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | Web app | React 19 SPA, TanStack Router, and Vite | | Server | Hono on Node.js 24 or Cloudflare Workers | | Language | TypeScript | | Monorepo | pnpm and Turborepo | | Database | PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM | | API | oRPC, OpenAPI REST, and MCP | | Auth | Better Auth | | Styling | Tailwind CSS | | UI Components | Base UI + shared UI package | | State Management | Zustand + TanStack Query | | PDF rendering | Forme, with PDF.js for the viewer | | Rich text | TipTap | | Localization | Lingui | ## Documentation The full documentation lives at [docs.rxresu.me](https://docs.rxresu.me): | Guide | Description | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | [Getting started](https://docs.rxresu.me/getting-started) | First-time setup and basic usage | | [What's new in v6](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/whats-new-in-v6) | Changes and where familiar features moved | | [Checking your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/checking-your-resume) | Readability, job match, and writing reviews | | [Using the assistant](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-assistant) | Ask for changes and review proposed edits | | [Writing a cover letter](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/writing-a-cover-letter) | Create a letter and link it to a resume | | [Tracking job applications](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/tracking-job-applications) | Saved jobs, stages, interviews, and insights | | [Exporting your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/exporting-your-resume) | PDF, Word, Markdown, and JSON downloads | | [API](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-api) and [MCP](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-mcp-server) | Connect scripts and external assistants | | [Self-hosting](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) | Deploy on your own infrastructure | | [Migrating from v5](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/upgrading-to-v6) | Migrations and integration changes | | [Development setup](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development) | Local development environment | | [Project architecture](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/architecture) | Codebase structure and package boundaries | ## Self-Hosting Reactive Resume runs the same application everywhere: PostgreSQL for data, plus storage for uploads. Pick the option that fits how much you want to manage. | Option | Best for | Guide | | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Hostinger](#hostinger) | A ready-made VPS with no setup | [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) | | [Vercel](#vercel) | Serverless, with managed database and storage | [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) | | [Cloudflare Workers](#cloudflare-workers) | Workers, R2 and your own PostgreSQL | [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) | | [Docker and Kubernetes](#docker-and-kubernetes) | Your own server, homelab or cluster | [Docker](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) · [Kubernetes](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) | > **PDF generation in v6** uses Forme in the browser and on the server. No Browserless, Chromium, or external print service is needed. Legacy `PRINTER_*` and `BROWSERLESS_*` environment variables can be removed. ### Hostinger The quickest way to get going is a 1-click deploy on Hostinger, starting at $6.49/month. Their VPS plans include a ready-made Reactive Resume template that provisions the Docker environment and brings the app up for you, with weekly backups and a Docker manager UI included — so you can skip the setup entirely. See the [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) for what the template sets up and what to configure afterwards, such as email, your own domain, and turning off sign-ups. ### Vercel [![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Freactive-resume%2Freactive-resume&project-name=reactive-resume&repository-name=reactive-resume&env=AUTH_SECRET%2CENCRYPTION_SECRET&envDescription=Generate+two+independent+secrets+with+openssl+rand+-hex+32.+Keep+these+values+across+deployments.&envLink=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.rxresu.me%2Fself-hosting%2Fvercel&stores=%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22upstash%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22upstash-kv%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22blob%22%2C%22access%22%3A%22private%22%7D%5D) Vercel provisions Neon PostgreSQL, private Blob storage, and Upstash Redis through its deployment wizard. Supply two persistent secrets and use the **Services** framework preset. Static assets run in the frontend service, and Hono serves the application routes and APIs from the backend service. See the [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) for setup, limits, and optional SMTP/OAuth configuration. ### Cloudflare Workers Cloudflare deployment requires **Workers Paid** and uses Static Assets, private R2 storage, SQLite Durable Objects, and PostgreSQL through Hyperdrive. Supply an existing PostgreSQL database and apply migrations before deployment. See the [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) for setup and runtime limits. ### Docker and Kubernetes The application needs: - **PostgreSQL** — Accounts, documents, applications, and assistant conversations - **Upload storage** — A persistent local directory or an S3-compatible bucket, such as SeaweedFS - **Redis** (optional) — Shared coordination across instances and resumable assistant replies - **SMTP** (optional) — Verification and password-reset emails Published releases are available from Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry (`latest` tracks the latest stable release): ```bash # Docker Hub docker pull amruthpillai/reactive-resume:latest # GitHub Container Registry docker pull ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume:latest ``` See the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) or [Kubernetes guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) for complete instructions. Running on a NAS? See the [Synology and UGREEN guides](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/nas). ### Configuration Every setting is listed in the [environment variables reference](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/environment-variables). Self-hosters can also configure [shared AI and job-search services](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/job-search-and-ai) and [single sign-on](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/sso). ### Upgrading from v5 Back up your database and uploads and stop all v5 instances before applying v6 migrations. Old visual style rules require a manual conversion; API and MCP integrations also have changes. Follow [Migrating from v5](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/upgrading-to-v6). ## Support Reactive Resume is and always will be free and open source. If it has helped you land a job or saved you time, please consider supporting continued development:

Other ways to support: - Star this repository - Report reproducible bugs and suggest actionable features - Help other users in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/discussions/categories/q-a) - Improve documentation - Help with translations ## Star History ## Contributing Every contribution helps, whether it is a typo fix or a new feature. 1. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-lan-relay

> **让不同机器上的 DeepSeek Harness Agent 直接对话。**
> 一个标准 DSH 插件：一台机器在 DSH 进程内当 hub，其余机器粘贴**加入码**即可加入；
> 消息离线补投、长轮询等回复、收到消息自动唤醒目标会话。
>
> MIT · DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2 · Windows / macOS / Linux

---

## 1. 特性

- **一个包、一次安装**：标准 DSH bundle（Host 半 + Web 半），在「插件 → 添加插件」里输入包名即可装好。
- **零外部依赖**：只用 Node 内置模块，不拉第三方包，不依赖 DSH 内部 API 的私有实现。
- **进程内 hub**：服务端不需要额外进程、不需要开机自启项；hub 跟着 DSH 启动和退出。
- **加入码配对**：服务端一键生成一行 `dshrelay1.…`，内含地址 + token；对端粘贴即可，不用抄 IP。
- **离线队列 + 长轮询**：消息落盘，接收方下次在线时补投；`lan_relay_wait` 最多等 50 秒。
- **自动唤醒**：消息到达后投递到指定会话并让 Agent 跑一轮；目标会话没打开也能冷启动。
- **全图形化配置**：设置 → 局域网中继：角色、端口、token、加入码、在线 peer、连接测试、防火墙放行。
- **原生 Agent 工具**：7 个 `lan_relay_*` 工具，装好即可调用，无需额外配置。
- **对话式配置**：不想点界面时，让 Agent 调 `lan_relay_configure` 就能切角色/加入。

---

## 2. 快速开始

前置：两台机器都装了 DSH（≥ 0.2.1-rc.2），在同一局域网、能互相 ping 通。
更详细的分步说明（含换 token / 换端口 / 换机器）见 [docs/TWO-MACHINE-SETUP.md](docs/TWO-MACHINE-SETUP.md)。

### 第一步：两台机器都安装插件

**图形界面**：侧边栏 → **插件** → **添加插件** → 输入 `dsh-lan-relay` → 安装。

**或命令行**：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-lan-relay
```

### 第二步：服务端机器

1. 打开 **设置 → 局域网中继**。
2. **运行角色** 选 **服务端** → **保存**。
3. 页面会显示：`Hub 状态：运行中`、端口 `8787`、**Token**、**加入码**（`dshrelay1.…`）、本机地址。
4. 防火墙开着的话，点 **一键放行防火墙** → 在 UAC 里点「是」。
5. 点加入码旁边的 **复制**，把这一行发给另一台机器。

### 第三步：客户端机器

1. **设置 → 局域网中继** → **运行角色** 选 **客户端**。
2. 把加入码粘贴到 **加入码** 输入框（会显示识别预览）。
3. **保存**。顶部显示 **客户端已连接**，`在线 peer` 里出现两台机器。

### 第四步：验证

在任意一台机器的会话里说：

> 用 lan_relay_peers 看下在线机器，然后给 pc1 发消息："ping from pc2"，并等 30 秒看回复。

对端 Agent 会自动被唤醒并回复。

---

## 3. 工作原理

```
             机器 A（服务端）                                机器 B（客户端）
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DSH 进程                                │    │ DSH 进程                                │
│  ┌─ Host 半 ─────────────────────────┐  │    │  ┌─ Host 半 ─────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ 内嵌 hub  0.0.0.0:8787             │  │    │  │ 中继客户端（HTTP 长轮询）          │  │
│  │ 中继客户端 127.0.0.1:8787          │◄─┼────┼──┤ 7 个 Agent 工具                    │  │
│  │ 7 个工具 + 自动唤醒                 │  │    │  │ 7 个工具 + 自动唤醒                 │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │    │  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  ┌─ Web 半 ──────────────────────────┐  │    │  ┌─ Web 半 ──────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ 设置 → 局域网中继                  │  │    │  │ 设置 → 局域网中继                  │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │    │  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘    └────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    └───────────── 明文 HTTP + x-relay-token（仅局域网）──────────────┘
```

- **Host 半**（`index.js`）：读配置 → 按角色启停内嵌 hub → 注册工具 → 后台长轮询并唤醒会话 → 给设置页提供同源管理 API。
- **Web 半**（`client.js`）：只渲染设置页；所有读写都走 Host 半的 `/lan-relay/api/*`（仅回环地址可访问）。
- **配置**：`~/.dsh/lan-relay/config.json`；**消息落盘**：`~/.dsh/lan-relay/hub/messages.jsonl`（最多 5000 条 / 8MB 轮转）。
- 协议：`/api/health`、`/api/peers`、`/api/inbox`、`/api/wait`、`/api/send`，全部要 `x-relay-token`（定长比较）。

---

## 4. 设置页：局域网中继

| 区块 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 顶部 | 运行状态徽标（服务端运行中 / 客户端已连接 / 未启用 / 异常）、刷新 |
| 运行角色 | **服务端**（本机起 hub）/ **客户端**（连别人的 hub）/ **关闭** |
| 服务端 | 端口、本机名称、Token（显示/复制/重新生成）、加入码（复制）、本机地址、Hub 状态/消息数/最新序号/数据目录、一键放行防火墙 |
| 客户端 | 加入码粘贴（自动解析）、或手填地址 + token、连接测试、在线 peer 列表、自动唤醒统计 |
| 底部 | 保存（只在点保存时写入）、每 3 秒自动刷新状态 |

所有改动都是**本地草稿**，只有点「保存」才生效；保存后 hub/轮询会按新配置立即重启，不需要重启 DSH。

---

## 5. Agent 工具

| 工具 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `lan_relay_send` | 给另一台机器发消息：`to`（peer 名或 `"*"`）、`text`、可选 `to_session`、`thread` |
| `lan_relay_inbox` | 拉取新消息（推进游标；`from_seq=0` 可重读历史） |
| `lan_relay_wait` | 长轮询等消息（≤50 秒；超时返回空数组，不报错） |
| `lan_relay_peers` | 谁在线（120 秒内有请求即在线）+ hub 是否可达 |
| `lan_relay_sessions` | 本机活跃会话列表（用于回复时指定对方 `to_session`） |
| `lan_relay_status` | 总览：角色、hub、连通性、peer、唤醒统计；排障先调它 |
| `lan_relay_configure` | 对话式配置：`role`、`join_code`、`relay_url`、`token`、`self`、`port`、`regenerate_token` |

---

## 6. 投递与自动唤醒规则

1. 消息带 `to_session` 且该会话在线 → 精确投递并唤醒。
2. 目标会话不在线 → `push.cold_session=prompt`（默认）用 `sessionController.prompt()` 自动 resume 并投递。
3. 没带 `to_session` → 投给 `push.default_session`，留空则投最近活跃会话。
4. `push.wake=false` → 只注入背景，不主动跑一轮。
5. 冷启动失败 → 记日志；只有 `push.offline_fallback=true` 才改投其它在线会话。
6. 插件与手动 `lan_relay_inbox` / `lan_relay_wait` 使用**独立游标**，不会互相抢消息。

> **成本提示**：一次投递 = 自动跑一轮模型调用。不需要自动唤醒时把 `push.enabled` 设为 `false`，改用工具手动拉取。

---

## 7. 加入码与安全

- 加入码 = `dshrelay1.` + base64url(`{u: 地址, t: token, n: 机器名}`)，**不加密**，等同明文 token。
- 服务端「重新生成 token」后旧加入码失效，需要把新加入码发给所有客户端。
- 明文 HTTP 只适合**可信局域网**；不要把 8787 暴露到公网。跨不可信网络请用 Tailscale / WireGuard 等隧道，再把地址填进加入码。
- 管理 API 只接受回环地址请求；消息正文会明文落盘，不要把密钥当消息发。

---

## 8. 防火墙与网络

- hub 监听 `0.0.0.0:8787`，端口可在设置页修改（改完重新生成加入码）。
- Windows 防火墙开启时，服务端需要放行入站 TCP 8787（一次即可）：
  - 设置页 **一键放行防火墙**（UAC 授权；规则限定 Private + 本地子网）；
  - 或管理员 PowerShell：
    ```powershell
    New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "DSH LAN Relay 8787" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8787 -Action Allow -Profile Private -RemoteAddress LocalSubnet
    ```
  - 精简版 Windows 没有 NetSecurity 模块时，脚本会自动退回 `netsh advfirewall firewall add rule ...`。
- 两台机器需在同一子网；跨网段把 `LocalSubnet` 换成对方网段。
- 多网卡时加入码默认用第一个局域网 IPv4；连不上就在「本机地址」里换一个，手动填到对端。

---

## 9. 配置参考

一般不用手改（设置页会写）。排查或脚本化时可编辑 `~/.dsh/lan-relay/config.json`：

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | 自动推断 | `server` / `client` / `off` |
| `self` | 主机名 | 本机 peer 名（小写字母/数字/`._-`，≤32） |
| `relay_url` | — | 客户端要连的 hub 地址；服务端自动写成 `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` |
| `token` | 服务端生成 | 两台机器必须一致 |
| `hub.host` / `hub.port` | `0.0.0.0` / `8787` | 服务端监听地址与端口 |
| `hub.data_dir` | `~/.dsh/lan-relay/hub` | 消息落盘目录 |
| `state_dir` | `~/.dsh/lan-relay/state` | 游标与调试日志 |
| `push.enabled` | `true` | 是否后台长轮询并自动唤醒 |
| `push.wake` | `true` | `false` = 只注入背景 |
| `push.default_session` | `""` | 没指定 `to_session` 的消息投给哪个会话 |
| `push.poll_timeout_seconds` | `25` | 每轮长轮询秒数 |
| `push.cold_session` | `prompt` | 目标会话未打开时自动 resume（`drop` = 放弃） |
| `push.offline_fallback` | `false` | 冷启动失败后是否改投其它会话 |
| `push.require_session` | `false` | `true` 时拒收没有 `to_session` 的消息 |

---

## 10. 故障排查

| 现象 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 设置页「未启用」 | 选「服务端」或「客户端」并保存 |
| 客户端连不上 hub | 服务端 DSH 是否在运行；加入码里的 IP 是否正确；防火墙是否放行；点「连接测试」看具体错误 |
| 服务端「端口已被占用」 | 8787 上已有 hub（同一台机器的另一个 DSH 实例）在跑；停掉它或换端口后重新生成加入码 |
| token 不匹配 | 两台机器 token 不一致；重新复制加入码，或在服务端重新生成 token |
| 消息到了不唤醒 | 目标会话是否存在/归档；检查 `push.wake`、`push.cold_session`；`lan_relay_status` 看 `stats` 与 `last_error`；日志在 `~/.dsh/lan-relay/state/plugin.log` |
| 收不到历史消息 | 同一条消息只投一次；`lan_relay_inbox(from_seq=0, mark_read=false)` 重读 |
| hub 数据被重建 | 客户端游标可能超前，会自动归零重拉（返回 `cursor_reset: true`） |
| 界面入口找不到 | 自定义侧边栏模式（如 DS Bot）可能替换了设置入口；直接让 Agent 用 `lan_relay_configure` 配置，或在经典模式下打开设置 |

---

## 11. 开发

```powershell
npm test   # 9 项 node:test：hub 内核 / 插件集成（含真实 hub + 唤醒投递）/ Web 半结构
```

| 路径 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host 半：角色开关、内嵌 hub、工具、自动唤醒、管理 API |
| `client.js` | Web 半：设置 → 局域网中继 |
| `lib/hub-server.mjs` | 可内嵌 hub 内核（`createHub()`，无进程副作用） |
| `lib/join-code.mjs` | 加入码编解码 |
| `lib/core.mjs` | 长轮询、按会话投递、冷启动唤醒 |
| `lib/relay-client.mjs` | HTTP 客户端 + 游标 |
| `lib/plugin-config.mjs` | 配置读写、角色推断、token 生成 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle patch（插入 `lan-relay` 行） |
| `locale/` · `icon.svg` | 插件卡片标题/描述与图标 |
| `test/` | 内核 / 插件集成 / Web 半结构测试 |

发布：

```powershell
npm publish --access public   # package.json 的 files 白名单已包含运行所需文件
```

> 修改 `scripts/*.ps1` 时要保留 UTF-8 BOM（PowerShell 5.1 会按 ANSI 读取无 BOM 文件，中文会解析出错）。

---

## 12. 限制

1. hub 在 DSH 进程内：服务端机器的 DSH 关闭后，其他机器发不出新消息（已入队的不丢）。需要 7×24 就让服务端 DSH 常驻。
2. 同一台机器同一端口只能有一个 hub；多个 DSH 实例都选服务端时，后来的会报端口占用（预期保护）。
3. 明文 HTTP + 明文 token，只适合可信局域网。
4. 冷启动唤醒会真的 resume 会话并跑一轮（消耗 token）；审批策略为 `ask` 且 GUI 没打开时，需要审批的操作会 fail-closed。
5. 消息正文上限 32000 字符；大文件请落盘后发路径，或走临时 HTTP + 校验和。

---

## License

MIT © ready-player-zero

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-inner-browser-use

**Lets an agent drive the built-in sidebar browser of DeepSeek Harness — the one already in the right panel, not a new window.**

The agent navigates, reads the page as numbered controls, clicks, types, and runs JavaScript. You watch it happen: a pointer moves to each target and ripples where it lands. Everything runs inside the `<webview>` the product already leases, with the same partition and the same cookies, so a page you signed into by hand is the page the agent works on.

> **On the name:** *inner* means the browser built into the Harness sidebar. This plugin opens no window of its own and never attaches to Chrome.

## What you get

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_navigate` | Opens a URL in this chat's built-in browser and returns the page. |
| `browser_view` | Returns the address, title, visible text, and every control as `#1 … #80`. |
| `browser_click` | Clicks one numbered control and returns the page it leads to. |
| `browser_type` | Types into one numbered field, optionally pressing Enter. |
| `browser_script` | Evaluates JavaScript and returns the last expression. |
| `browser_selection` | Returns the text currently selected in the page. |
| `browser_copy` | Copies the selection, or one control's text, to the clipboard. |
| `browser_screenshot` | Saves a PNG of the tab and returns its path. |
| `browser_download` | Saves a file the page offers into this chat's project folder. A file the page starts saving on its own lands there too, and the call that caused it reports the path. |
| `browser_upload` | Attaches a local file to a numbered file field. |

Every call is visible: the pointer travels to the control, a ring marks it, and the page scrolls the target into view first.

The first call opens the tab for you: the page half hears that a chat needs one and opens **内置浏览器** in the right sidebar. That tab is the product's own — same tab kind, same address bar, same partition — and this plugin adds nothing to the guide pane. A tab you opened by hand is the tab the agent drives.

## Where files land

The tab reports the folder its chat works in when it connects, and everything this plugin writes goes under one
folder of that working directory:

```
.dsh-inner-browser-use/
  .gitignore     keeps the folder out of your project's own version control
  screenshots/   PNGs from browser_screenshot
  downloads/     files the page offered to browser_download
```

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-inner-browser-use
```

Then in DeepSeek Harness: **Plugins → Install from folder**, and pick the clone. Or from a shell:

```bash
dsh plugin install /path/to/dsh-inner-browser-use
```

The plugin appears under **Plugins** as *内置浏览器*. It needs the Desktop app, because the sidebar browser is a Desktop capability.

## Use

1. Open the chat you want the agent to browse for.
2. Ask the agent for something on a page: *"打开 example.com，告诉我标题"*. The first call opens the built-in browser in the right panel; pressing **+ → 内置浏览器** yourself lands on the same tab.

The tab is per chat: each chat has its own in the same built-in browser. A call for a chat that never opened one opens it there.

## Drag data both ways

- **Page → chat:** `browser_script` returns strings and `browser_screenshot` saves a PNG, so the agent can read what the page shows and quote it — or hand you the image path — in the conversation.
- **Chat → page:** `browser_type` puts text into a field; `browser_script` can set values the page cannot be typed into.
- **Page → chat, by hand:** select text on the page and a **Drag to chat** handle appears in the tab's
  status row. Drag it into the conversation to carry that text with you. After the agent downloads something
  for this chat, the same handle carries that file, so a page's picture or PDF can be dropped into the chat
  as an attachment without leaving the app. The agent gets the same content through `browser_selection`,
  `browser_copy` and `browser_download`.

## What it will not do

- **It does not create a second browser.** No new window, no Chrome profile, no CDP mirror.
- **A sign-in outlives a restart only when the page can read its cookie.** The guest partition lives in memory; the cookies this page can see are kept per workspace in `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/cookies/` and written back when that workspace's pane opens again. A login held only in an `HttpOnly` cookie needs the password again.
- **Screenshots are viewport-sized.** A `<webview>` captures what is visible, not the whole scroll height; scroll first, then capture.
- **One partition per workspace.** Two chats in the same workspace share the browser's storage, exactly as two tabs of the built-in browser do.
- **No popups or permission prompts.** A link that wants a new window stays in the tab it is in. A file the page
  offers comes out through `browser_download`, which saves it into this chat's project folder and hands the path
  back to the conversation. A file the page starts saving by itself needs no call: it lands in the same folder,
  and the call that pressed the link reports where it went.
- **It opens the tab only when a call needs it.** A call for the chat you are reading may open the right
  panel; a call for any other chat gets a page out of sight instead, so the panel stays as you arranged it.
  At most three such pages are kept, and the oldest goes first.
- **A capture of a chat you are not looking at.** Reading, clicking and typing work on a tab that chat already
  had, because they drive the page itself; a tab is opened only for the chat on screen. Pixels come from a surface the app is drawing, and a view
  behind another tab of the same pane is not drawn: the capture tries to bring this chat's tab forward, and if the
  page still has no surface it says so in a couple of seconds instead of waiting. Read what you need from the page
  instead — `browser_script` returns the same content.

## Compatibility

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Harness | Desktop app, sidebar browser present |
| Tab kind | `browser` — the built-in browser's own kind |
| Host | Node 20+ |
| License | MIT |

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the wire and [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for version limits.

## Develop

```bash
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

The host half is plain ESM with no dependencies; the client half is a dynamic client module with no build step. Both are loaded by the app as-is.

- **The page comes back on its own.** The pane is rebuilt from time to time; when that leaves the view blank, the
  next tool call reopens the page that chat was last told to open, so a run is not interrupted by it.

## License

MIT © regrevia

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-lite-memory

**没有常驻的记忆正文：不写系统提示，不逐轮注入，命中才读。**
**No memory in the prompt: nothing injected per turn, read only on a hit.**

---

## 它是什么 / What it is

给 DeepSeek Harness 的轻量记忆：不写系统提示、不逐轮注入、不扫描文件。记忆只在两种时刻出现——你说「记一下」，或者它命中了一条查过的内容。

Lightweight memory for the DeepSeek Harness. Nothing in the system prompt, nothing injected per turn. Memory appears at exactly two moments: you ask it to remember, or a query matches something already stored.

## 触发方式 / Triggers

| 场景 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| **L0** 你明确要求「记住这个」 | 立即写盘，一条确认行 |
| **L1** 它发现有跨会话价值的经验 | 一行灰字 `memory · suggested "X" · sug_x` + 一个 `keep` 按钮；标题加一句话，看得懂才点，不点就永远不写，48 小时内不重复 |
| **L2** 常识、一次性参数、凭据的值 | 永不写入 |

这些行只属于产生它的那一轮：重进会话就没了，历史里只留正文。再记一次时插件自己判是更新还是新增：同层、同前置条件下，标题（或这条用过的旧标题）完全一致就更新原条目，换过说法而标题变了的旧标题记成别名以后也认得。像但不同名的不写：先在结果里回「相近：X」和它的 id，确认要更新就带那个 id 再存，确认是另一条才加 `resolution="distinct"`。更新时没给的字段保持原值，正文整段替换——旧正文原样留在 `versions` 里（每字都留，不截断）；前置条件不同的同一主题是两条。

写入时分两层：默认只在这个项目生效；用户说「以后所有项目都这样」才进全局层（上限 40 条），检索时一起查。同一主题在不同前提下用 `when` 区分，各存一条。

触发词：`记住`、`记一下`、`上次`、`规范`、`约定`、`路径`、`凭据怎么取`。

| Case | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **L0** you ask it to remember | written immediately, one confirmation line |
| **L1** it spots something worth keeping | one muted line `memory · suggested "X" · sug_x` with a single `keep` button — readable before you click, nothing written unless you click, at most once per two days |
| **L2** common sense, one-off parameters, credential values | never written |

Those lines belong to the turn that made them: reopening the session drops them, leaving only the prose in history. Saving again updates an entry only when the title (or one of its earlier titles) matches exactly under the same precondition. A merely similar title writes nothing first: the result reports the closest entry and its id, so the caller either updates that id or re-saves with `resolution="distinct"`. An update keeps every field it was not given and replaces the body wholesale; the previous body stays in `versions` verbatim. The same subject under different preconditions stays two entries.

Writes land in one of two layers: the current project by default, or the global layer (max 40 entries) when the user says the rule holds for every project. Both layers are searched together, and a `when` field separates the same subject under different preconditions.

## 点一下就存 / One click, no turn

`keep` 是同源直写：不产生消息、不动输入框、不打断当前回复。按钮变 `kept` 就结束了。行尾的 `✕` 按 id 撤销：改过的条目还原成上一版（显示 `restored`），刚建的条目移入归档（显示 `archived`）。

`keep` writes straight to disk from the page: no message, no extra model turn, the input box untouched. The button turns into `kept` and that is the whole interaction. The `✕` at the end of a line undoes by id: an edited entry goes back to its previous version (`restored`), a freshly created one moves to the archive (`archived`).

## 底部引用条 / Citation footer

这次会话真正读进来的记忆，会在输入框下面留一行 `记忆引用 N 条`：点开是标题，再点一条就地展开正文，再点收起。没读过记忆就不出现；换会话回来还在，一个会话最多留 20 条，30 天不用就清掉。

Memories actually read into this session leave one line under the composer — `记忆引用 N 条`. It expands to titles, a title expands to the raw body, and clicking again collapses it. Nothing read, nothing shown. It survives switching conversations; at most 20 rows per session, cleared after 30 days.

## 为什么轻 / Why it stays light

- **0 依赖**，存储层无定时器、无监听、无网络，只有同步单文件写；写入用一把有超时的锁，别的进程正在写就明确报「忙」，不抢别人的锁。
- 搜索最多 4 条、400 字；正文只在 `memory_read` 里出现，全文永不进上下文。
- 超限直接报错、原数据不动：单条正文 4096 字节、整库 512 KB、项目 200 条、全局 40 条、标题 60 字、摘要 60 字。90 天未用只留 `id + 标题`。超容量时最旧的转 `archive/`（正文与完整记录都留着，可人工取回），文件从不删除。
- 一个项目一个目录，项目之间互相看不见。

- **Zero dependencies.** The store has no timers, no listeners, no network — just synchronous single-file writes, guarded by a lock that gives up after 500 ms instead of stealing it.
- Search returns at most 4 hits and 400 characters. Full text only appears in `memory_read`.
- Over any limit the call fails and the old state stays: 4096 bytes per body, 512 KB per store, 200 entries per project, 40 in the global layer, 60 characters per title or summary. Unused for 90 days drops to `id + title`. When the store is full the oldest entries archive with body and full record kept, so an entry can be restored by hand. Files are never deleted.
- One directory per project, so projects never see each other's notes.

## 安装 / Install

Plugin Manager 里搜 `dsh-lite-memory` 直接装；或 `npm pack` 后用 Plugin Manager 安装生成的 `.tgz`。

Install from the DSH Plugin Manager (search `dsh-lite-memory`), or `npm pack` and install the resulting `.tgz` through it.

## 工具 / Tools

`memory_save` · `memory_suggest` · `memory_search` · `memory_read` · `memory_forget`

完整触发规则见 [TRIGGERS.md](TRIGGERS.md)。 / Full trigger rules: [TRIGGERS.md](TRIGGERS.md).

# dsh-unlag（解除卡顿）

**改完插件点一下就生效。界面卡了点一下就顺。正在跑的任务照常跑完。**

窗口右上角一个按钮，不重启进程、不刷新掉会话：插件代码原地换掉，老旧卡顿的界面重建一次。

## 两个日常场景

| 情况 | 按一下 |
| --- | --- |
| 改了界面类插件，手里还有任务在跑 | 插件当场换掉，任务继续跑完 |
| 界面越用越卡 | 直接恢复流畅，会话、队列、草稿都还在 |

以前两种都得关掉 App 再来。现在不用，也不用挑空闲时间——马上换，不等。

## 装

```sh
dsh plugin install dsh-unlag
```

安装后由 DSH 完成首次加载，之后的更新都走按钮。

## 用

点右上角那个按钮。设置里三行决定它做什么：

- **按下刷新时换掉插件代码**（默认开）
- **按下刷新时重建界面**（默认开）
- **改完文件自动刷新，不必按按钮**（默认关）

前两行都开＝先换代码再重建；只开一个＝另一项完全不动；都不开＝点击无反应。

## 刷新只有人能做

自动刷新默认关着，插件不改任何文件监视：保存了插件代码也不会自己生效，要有人按下按钮。

给 agent 的话：改完插件请用户点右上角按钮，不要建议重启 App，也不要自己请求刷新。

## 不会丢什么

- 正在跑的轮次、子代理、终端进程：都跑在宿主进程里，换代码不重启进程，所以不被打断，照常跑完。
- 界面重建会重新进入同一个地址：屏幕上正在显示的内容重新载入一次，会话记录还在。
- 排队消息、输入草稿、附件：重建前先提交焦点里的内容；有人没存完就拦下，不硬刷。
- 有未保存改动、开着弹窗、或下个页面要用的模块读不全：拦下并提示，提示里写明卡在哪一项，宁可不刷。
- 原来就起不来的插件不挡这一下：换代码照做，日志里点名哪个插件本来就没在跑。
- 三个开关读不到时不硬刷：提示稍后再试，日志记下是哪一步没读到，绝不谎称代码已是最新。
- 旧页面记着的启动清单分组变了（装过／卸过插件）：按插件逐个补齐再交给新页面，不会因为清单 404 把 App 带走。
- 从不自己重启或退出 App。

管不到（它会拦下并说明，不会硬来）：

- 改动替插件加原生能力、改服务声明或权限：这类改动不在一次点击的范围里。
- 独立进程和进程级的东西：宠物窗口自己的配置、DSH 自身升级、原生依赖变化。
- 万一新页面还是起不来：App 会进入错误恢复（退出，或请你停用第三方插件）。本插件不替你选，也不会自己重启或退出 App。

## 依据的官方约定

- 页面启动时，宿主把插件清单写成 `window.__DSH_BOOT__`；脚本地址形如 `/plugins/??<包>/client.js&rev=<修订>`，修订由文件的修改时间、变更时间、大小决定（`docs/subsystems/client-modules.md`）。
- 宿主对未知、被改过、过期的修订返回 404，不会拿别的字节顶上，也不会让单页应用的回退把 HTML 当脚本发出去（同上）。
- 插件代码重建、但入口没重启时，宿主用 `rebuilt()` 发布新修订，页面按新地址只换掉那一个插件（同上）。
- 页面只应用自己启动时那一版宿主的清单；宿主换了版本，页面要重新载入才能跟上（同上，Host release changes）。

本插件只做这些约定允许的事：换代码走宿主的插件重载入口，重建走一次页面载入。唯一的差异在下一节。

## 与官方约定的差异

官方的插件资源路由对未知修订返回 404。本插件对旧页面记着的旧修订返回当前内容：桌面版在窗口启动时固定了启动清单，页面按旧修订请求脚本是常态，返回 404 会让新页面起不来、App 直接退出。这是本插件的兼容措施，不是官方行为；不需要时可以整个关掉（设置里两行都关）。

同一原因下的第二种情况：启动清单里记着的插件在配置里已经被关掉或删掉了，官方路由对那一行只会 404。本插件改为返回一段空脚本占位，页面起来时不再加载这个插件，App 照常起来；日志会写明哪个插件被留下，`/dsh-unlag/verify` 的结论里也带 `leftOut` 字段。

## 排错

- 日志：`~/.dsh/unlag-reload.log`，换代码／跳过／被拦各一行，含原因。
- 状态：`GET /dsh-unlag/state` → `{"version":"<当前版本>","code":"<index.js 写入时间>","plugins":true,"page":true,"shim":{...}}`。`code` 用来分清「版本号没刷」和「旧代码真的还在跑」。
- 重建后的日志带起页面代次：`interface rebuilt; the page runs the plugins as served now (page <rev>)`，据此判断新文档加载的是新脚本还是旧脚本。

## 测试

```sh
npm test
```

对着正在运行的 App 走一遍真实判定（页面半、宿主半都是线上代码，用的是 App 现在渲染的启动清单；只回答「能不能刷」，绝不按按钮），并核对路由契约：读接口 200、写方法 405、不带页面头的按键路由 403：

```sh
npm run smoke
```

没有 App 在监听时打印 `skip` 并退出 0。
