# Power-Up

Small, opt-in upgrades for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).
The upgrades include a **right-click action menu in the Trajectory view**, an
optional **stop reason for background jobs**, and an in-place **plugin installer**.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @restregular/dsh-powerup
```

Then open a session, switch to **Trajectory**, and right-click a record row.

## What it does

Right-click a trajectory record:

- **Copy content** — copy the full text of the record.
- **Copy as quote** — produce a Markdown blockquote with the record kind.
- **Quote in composer** — insert that quote into the current input box.
- **Open record details** — open the host's record inspector.
- **Fork from here** — fork the session at that record (inclusive).
- **Copy session ID**.

Right-click empty space in the ledger:

- **Export trajectory JSON** — save the current trajectory snapshot.
- **Copy session ID**.
- **Open the Power-Up page** — the sidebar control panel.

The sidebar **Power-Up** page turns the menu on or off and lists the available
actions. The setting is stored in the browser. It also holds the defaults for
**one-click install** (auto-enable and auto-restart), which the plugin installer
uses.

### Stop a background job with a reason

The session header's background jobs panel keeps the host's list, live output,
and stop button. Clicking a running job's stop button opens a themed Power-Up
dialog instead of the host's two-press stop. The dialog is portaled to the
document body, so it renders above the jobs menu (which is itself a body portal)
and is not clipped by any slot's stacking context; its colors come only from
`--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so light and dark themes both work.

- The reason field is optional; an empty field keeps the host's default
  `cancelled by the user` reason. `Enter` confirms while `Esc` cancels.
- Confirming stops the job through the Host route, which records
  `cancelled by the user: <reason>`. The completion notice injected into the
  session and the shell tool's result therefore carry the reason.
- If the button cannot be resolved to a live job, the click is left alone and
  the host's original stop flow runs unchanged.

### Menu keys

`↑` / `↓` move, `Home` / `End` jump, `Enter` runs, `Esc` closes.

## Install a plugin

Open the built-in **Plugins** page. Every third-party card under **Installed
plugins** gains a small install icon in its action area. Clicking it opens the
install dialog:

1. The dialog reads the package's published versions from the Host's configured
   registries — the same list the **Add plugin** dialog offers, including the
   npmmirror fallback. Star any registry to make it Power-Up's default for
   later installs; otherwise the list starts from the Add dialog's remembered
   choice.
2. Type a version or pick one from the floating version list. The version in the
   input is authoritative: both install actions install exactly that version, so
   reinstalling or downgrading works. The installed version is tagged
   **Current**; the newest is tagged **latest**, and a version that is both uses
   one **Current · latest** tag.
3. **One-click install** installs the version in the input and skips both
   questions: by default the new copy is enabled and DSH restarts automatically.
   The Power-Up page can turn either default off. With auto-enable off, the new
   version is left disabled and nothing restarts. With auto-restart off (or when
   the current runtime cannot restart itself), the completion panel closes
   itself after a few seconds instead of staying on screen. Power-Up's own
   install keeps its background handoff and does not offer one-click.
4. Otherwise, confirming removes the installed copy, checks the spec the way
   **Add plugin** does, and installs the selected version without enabling it.
   Because the old copy is already gone at that point, a refused check or a
   failed install automatically re-installs the removed version with its
   previous enabled state; the dialog reports both the failure and the rollback
   result.
5. The dialog then asks whether to enable the new version.
6. After enabling, it asks whether to restart DSH. On the desktop app the
   `lib/restart-helper.cjs` helper relaunches the exact executable after the old
   Host exits; under `dsh web` the dialog explains that the terminal owns the
   process.
7. A management call that reports `restart-required` keeps a **Restart needed**
   tag on the card and adds the plugin to the count beside the **Installed
   plugins** heading. The heading bar is always present — with **No plugins need
   a restart** and the restart button when nothing is pending — and a **Restart
   DSH** button confirms and performs the same restart. The Host also audits
   profile bundle directories written after it started, so installs made through
   the built-in **Add plugin** / **Install** UI, or before this page loaded, are
   marked too.

Power-Up installs itself through the same dialog (the one-click action is hidden
for itself). Because removing the plugin unloads this panel, the Host answers
first and then hands `removeBundle` → `inspect` → `installBundle(enabled: true)`
to the built-in manager service, which keeps running after the Power-Up Host
fiber is unloaded. The panel closes; refresh the page when the install finishes.

## Design notes

- **Theme-safe by construction.** Every surface, border, text color, hover and
  switch state uses the host's `--dsw-alias-*` tokens. The switch follows the
  host convention (`--dsw-alias-border-l3` / `--dsw-alias-switch-thumb` off,
  `--dsw-alias-brand-primary` + `--dsw-alias-label-primary-foreground` on), so
  it stays readable in both light and dark themes. The only literal colors live
  inside the plugin's brand SVG artwork.
- **Two icons, two jobs.** `icon.svg` is the 256px brand tile shown by the
  Plugin Manager. The sidebar uses the same double-chevron mark as a 16-grid,
  `fill:none`, `stroke:currentColor` line drawing, but without the tile frame:
  the mark gets the full grid, so the chevrons and the amber baseline never
  collide with a border. The reference line artwork is
  `design/sidebar-icon.svg`; the runtime copy lives in `client.js`.
- **No imports from Harness Client packages.** The menu is plain React + CSS and
  observes the trajectory package's own `data-*` contracts. If those attributes
  change, row-specific actions degrade gracefully; session-level actions in the
  empty ledger area keep working.
- **The stop reason rides the host's own job registry.** The panel belongs to
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-jobs`, so Power-Up does not replace it: a capture
  listener recognizes its `button[data-kill-state]`, maps the button to the live
  row (DOM order plus the row's `title` label), and opens the reason dialog.
  The typed reason goes to `POST /dsh-powerup/api/job-kill`, which calls the
  registry's `kill(id, session, reason)` — the same admission the built-in
  Remote uses, with the reason settlement merges into the job's `detail` line.
- **The install entry uses the built-in page's contracts.** The Plugins page has
  no per-card slot, so the overlay injects one button into every
  `[data-plugin-group="bundles"] [data-plugin-package]` card and re-asserts it
  after React renders. Version listing is a plain registry `GET`; removal and
  installation use the same `remote.pluginManager` calls as **Add plugin**. The
  Host adds two loopback-only routes: `/dsh-powerup/api/restart` for the
  process restart, and `/dsh-powerup/api/self-update` for the self-install
  handoff.
- **Power-Up's own install outlives its unload.** The Host route sends its
  answer, then a timer starts `removeBundle` → `inspect` →
  `installBundle(enabled: true)` through the built-in manager service. Removing
  the bundle unloads Power-Up's own Host fiber, but the manager service and the
  pending promise stay in the Host process, so the reinstall finishes; failures
  are appended to `~/.dsh/powerup/self-update.log`. The Host captures the
  version it was loaded from before removal and re-installs that version if the
  check or install fails, so a failed self-install does not leave Power-Up
  missing.
- **One-click install is a client-side decision.** Both install actions use the
  version in the dialog input (so reinstall and downgrade are allowed) and both
  defaults live in the shared settings store (`dsh-powerup:settings:v1`), so the
  Power-Up page and an open dialog agree without a reload. A one-click run
  installs disabled — the same shape as **Add plugin** — then enables through
  `setBundleEnabled`, and posts the restart only when the defaults allow it. With
  auto-enable off the new copy stays disabled and nothing restarts. When no
  restart happens the completion panel closes on a timer; install, enable, and
  restart failures stay on screen with their reason instead.
- **The stop dialog is a body portal with host-dialog chrome.** `shell.overlay`
  is an absolute layer at `z-index: 20`, and the host jobs menu is a
  `document.body` portal at `z-index: 100`; a high z-index inside the overlay
  layer therefore still loses. The reason popover is rendered through
  `react-dom`'s `createPortal` into `document.body` and uses `z-index: 1400`.
  Its surface (`--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2`, `--dsw-radius-panel`,
  `--dsw-elevation-prominent`), 34px input, and buttons mirror the host dialog
  and menu primitives; the confirm button reuses the host's armed-stop
  treatment (red border, 12% red fill, red text) instead of inventing a solid
  danger style. Without `react-dom` it falls back to in-place rendering.
- **Restart status lives in this browser session.** A management result that
  says `restart-required` is written to `sessionStorage`; the card gets a
  **Restart needed** tag and the group heading gets a count plus a restart
  button. The Client also wraps the shared `remote.pluginManager` methods so an
  install started from the built-in Add plugin/Install dialogs is observed, and
  asks the Host audit route for profile bundles whose files are newer than the
  Host process. A real app restart clears the session, while a page refresh
  keeps the markers.
- **The dialog mirrors the host modal.** The backdrop is
  `--dsw-alias-bg-mask-1` with the shared mask blur, the surface is
  `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2` with `--dsw-radius-panel` and
  `--dsw-elevation-prominent`, and the primary button uses
  `--dsw-alias-button-primary-fill` / `-hover`, so the dialog follows both
  themes instead of inventing its own palette. The registry picker and version
  list are custom controls built from `--dsw-alias-*` tokens; both open as
  fixed-position popovers anchored to their triggers, so they never grow the
  dialog or get clipped by its scroll area.

## Development

```bash
node test/smoke.mjs
```

The smoke test loads the real Client module with React/browser doubles, applies
it to a fake slot context, and checks registrations, icons, helpers, theme
tokens, the stop-reason mapping and Host route, and the manifest.

# @romany-saad/dsh-cockpit

A durable task board for a DeepSeek Harness hub session: the session that coordinates builders across many pull requests. A board is a tree of steps, each linked to its work by free-form fields, and it is kept as one local JSON file that other processes can read.

**Status: in development.** The design is in [issue #1](https://github.com/romany-saad/dsh-plugins/issues/1). The plugin registers its four board tools; running drift, the routes and the web panel follow in later pull requests.

## What is here

- `index.js`: the host plugin. Registers `board_open`, `board_read`, `board_add` and `board_update` inside `ctx.inject(['tools'], …)`, with `defineTool` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`. Every agent in a profile that loads the plugin sees them; `tools.enabled: false` registers none.
- `lib/tools.js`: the tool bodies. Results are `{ ok: true, … }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }`, with the codes `not_bound`, `item_exists`, `item_unknown`, `invalid_input`, `board_unreadable` and `write_failed`.
  - `board_open({ key, parent? })` creates or opens a board and binds the session to it, in memory and in `sessions/<sessionId>.json`, so a resumed session finds its board without reopening it.
  - `board_read({ item?, status? })`: the tasks, the tree text, the flags, and the file's path and format version. The filters narrow the result only.
  - `board_add({ item?, what, status?, … })`: `item` defaults to the next integer, `status` to `next`. A field it does not know is refused (`invalid_input`); `extra` keeps anything else.
  - `board_update({ item, set? | remove? })`: `item` is one item or a list, changed in one write; one unknown item refuses the whole call. `null` in `set` clears a field. It returns `tasks` (after) and `previous` (before); a removal returns the removed tasks in `previous`, so `board_add` can put them back.
- `lib/config.js`: the config and its defaults, and `linkOptions(config, board)`, which turns the `links` patterns into the options of `refUrl` and `boardRows`.
- `lib/present.js`: one-line titles for the tool cards.
- `cordis.patch.yml`: the bundle patch (`dsh.bundle.patch`).
- `lib/task.js`: the task model. Statuses `next`, `now`, `waiting`, `done` and `dropped`; `done` and `dropped` are closed, so they block nothing. Fields: item, what, status, why, issue, pr, branch, worktree, provider, model, effort, nextAction, waitingOn, readyCommand, startWhen, parent, dependsOn, extra, updatedAt. Fields it does not know are kept.
- `lib/rows.js`: what each row says, derived and never stored: ready, blocked by, needs you (`waitingOn` is `owner`, in any case), progress (dropped counted apart from done), flags (`unknown_parent`, `unknown_dependency`, `parent_loop`, `duplicate_issue`, `duplicate_pr`), and links. Only full `http(s)` URLs link, unless the caller passes `links` URL patterns (`{ref}`, `{repo}`, `{number}`).
- `lib/tree.js`: the tree text, led by a Problems block. Bad data never moves a row.
- `lib/store.js`: `$DSH_HOME/data/dsh-cockpit/boards/<encodeURIComponent(key)>.json`, format `dsh-cockpit.board`, version 1, written by temp file, fsync, rename and directory fsync. A file it cannot read is never overwritten. `revision` counts changes to tasks or to the board's parent; a write that changes neither, such as a report-only drift result, does not bump it.
- `lib/drift.js`: the drift record. It keeps only the entries whose status differs from their task's, and `checked` counts every entry.
- `reader.js` (`@romany-saad/dsh-cockpit/reader`): `listBoards(dir?)`, `readBoard(keyOrFile, dir?)` and `boardTree(board)`, with no DSH imports. A miss names the folder it looked in and where `DSH_HOME` came from.
- `board.schema.json`: the file format as a JSON Schema, for a hub that writes the file without the plugin.

## Config

```yaml
- id: dsh-cockpit
  name: '@romany-saad/dsh-cockpit'
  config:
    tools: { enabled: true }      # false: register no tools
    route: { enabled: true }      # false: no routes, so no panel data (the routes come in a later step)
    drift: { command: '', cwd: '', mode: report }   # mode: report | apply (the runner comes in a later step)
    links: { issue: '', pr: '' }  # URL patterns with {ref}, {repo}, {number}; empty: only full URLs link
```

A profile patch with the same id replaces the whole config, so it restates the fields it keeps. For example, a profile on GitHub sets `links: { issue: 'https://github.com/{repo}/issues/{number}', pr: 'https://github.com/{repo}/pull/{number}' }`; `{repo}` comes from `owner/repo#12`, or for `#12` from the board's parent reference.

The peers are `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths`, which the profile's DSH provides.

## Test

```sh
pnpm test
```

## License

[MIT](../../LICENSE)

# dsh-plugins

Public plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), one package each under `packages/`, under the `@romany-saad` scope.

| Package | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`@romany-saad/dsh-cockpit`](packages/dsh-cockpit) | A durable task board for a hub session that coordinates builders: a tree of steps with free-form link fields (issue, PR, branch, worktree, model, effort), kept as one local JSON file per board that other processes can read | in development |

## Install

Nothing is on npm yet (#2). A profile installs a package from this repository, pinned to a commit or a tag:

```json
"@romany-saad/<package>": "github:romany-saad/dsh-plugins#<commit or tag>&path:packages/<package>"
```

## Develop

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test
```

To try a package from a checkout, install it by path into a scratch profile: `dsh plugin --profile scratch add ./packages/<package>`. A `link:` or path dependency is for local development only; profiles that others reproduce pin a commit or a tag.

## Layout

- `packages/<name>/`: one plugin, with its own `package.json`, `README.md`, `cordis.patch.yml` when it ships a patch layer, and tests.
- Each package declares the DSH packages it uses as `peerDependencies`, so it runs against the DSH the profile already has.

## Releases

Each release is a tag `<package>@<version>`, for example `dsh-cockpit@0.1.0`. Profiles pin the tag, or its commit if pnpm rejects the tag. Publishing to npm is parked (#2).

## Contributing

Pull requests are welcome. Every pull request gets one code review before the maintainer merges it.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# Harness Web Bridge

Use your logged-in web AI (DeepSeek, GLM / Z.ai, Kimi, Qwen, Doubao) as model providers inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/RSLN-creator/dsh-web-bridge). Web models emit tool calls, DSH
executes them under its native permission and approval system, and the results go back into the same
web session.

**No API keys** — it drives the site through your own browser login.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-webcode-bridge
```

> **Restart `dsh web` after installing.** Installing only swaps files on disk; the running process
> still has the old code loaded. This is the single most common "it does not work" report.

## Status & risks (read this first)

**Status**: this is a **work-in-progress project** — behavior and interfaces can change, and a site
redesign can break any site's channel at any time. **Forks and PRs are welcome** (see the repository
root's CONTRIBUTING.md for the commit-message shape and the local gates).

**Risks — evaluate for yourself before using**:

| Risk | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Site ToS / account restriction** | The plugin drives your **logged-in web sessions** with automation, which may violate a site's terms of service; accounts can be rate-limited or restricted — **one of the author's own DeepSeek web accounts has been restricted**. |
| **Tool mode = prompt injection** | With "local tool calling" enabled, the bridge injects tool-protocol teaching into the web conversation; that content is **visible to the site**. |
| **Page redesigns break things** | Every site is "the web page as a backend"; when a site ships a redesign its channel can break. |
| **Data locality** | Login state lives only in the plugin's **local** browser profile; no API keys, no telemetry, no cloud component. |

**Default mode**: tool calling is **off by default** — the bridge is then a pure web session: the
web model receives exactly your words, identical to the browser (no prompt injection, no call
replay). Enable it via **Settings → Web Bridge → Local tool calling** or the "local tools" pill
under the composer; enabling asks for a confirmation first. Tool calls always execute under DSH's
native permission system.

## What it does

- **Real sites in the DSH right sidebar** — not a screenshot, not a mock. The actual site is loaded
  through a same-origin mirror, so you can type, scroll and click in it. Login state persists.
- **Per-site protocol teaching** — each site is taught the tool-call shape it actually accepts
  (DeepSeek's native token format, GLM's fenced ```json code block, `<tool_call>` tags elsewhere),
  recomputed from the live tool list every turn.
- **Global and per-site settings** — model, instruction, send gap and prompt-delivery mode can each
  be set globally *and* overridden for one site, without disturbing the others.
- **Multi-account** — one site can hold several independent logins, each with its own browser profile
  and its own request pacing.
- **Observable** — every delivery, fallback and rate-limit event is projected into
  `GET /__webcode/status`.

## Requirements

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | 22.13 or newer |
| DeepSeek Harness | 0.1.0-rc.6 or newer |
| Browser | None to install — the plugin ships its own Chromium (Playwright). A system browser is used only as a fallback. |

## Install

### From the npm registry (recommended)

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-webcode-bridge
```

Pin a version with `dsh-webcode-bridge@<version>`.

### From a release tarball

Download `dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz` from
[Releases](https://github.com/RSLN-creator/dsh-web-bridge/releases), then:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add C:\path\to\dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz
```

### From source

```powershell
pnpm install            # do NOT add --frozen-lockfile, see ../../doc/ci-cd.md
pnpm pack              # produces dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz
```

Two local helper scripts exist for troubleshooting only: `scripts/verify-pack.mjs` compares the
packed tarball against the working tree file by file, and `scripts/install-profiles.mjs` removes the
old directory before unpacking (which avoids pnpm's "Already up to date" shortcut on a same-version
tarball). Both encode a bug that actually happened.

## Site status

**DeepSeek is the primary target and holds up over long sessions. GLM works, but it is unstable.**

| Site | Status |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek `deepseek:deepseek` | Primary. Validated over long multi-turn tool loops on a real browser session, with auto-continue, session-cursor persistence, and recovery from Harness history after a restart. |
| GLM `glm:glm-5.3` / `glm-5.3-flash` | Usable but unstable. The end-to-end tool loop passes on a real session: a random secret present only in the tool result is echoed back verbatim by the model, so the round-trip is genuinely live. |
| Kimi / Qwen / Doubao / Z.ai | Wired up, not validated over long runs. Availability depends on your login state. |
| Claude | Region-restricted; the site says so itself. |
| ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini | Not reachable from our network (502 plus an explanatory page). |

What "unstable" means for GLM, concretely:

- **Thinking cannot be turned off**, and it dominates the stream (1051 of 2472 replies were thinking-only).
- **The site intercepts tool-call tags in prose** through its own native tool layer, so GLM is taught only the fenced code-block shape, with fallback parsing from the thinking stream.
- **Deep-link navigation is stopped by an Aliyun slider captcha**, so probes go through the driver path instead.
- Two failure modes have been fixed and are worth knowing: a stream that died mid-thinking produced an empty reply, and call-fence tails leaked into the reply body as garbage.

Read it as: **DeepSeek is the one to run all day; GLM is a good second opinion.** When GLM fails,
retry — attributable failures surface as coded messages rather than silent degradation.

## Documentation

The full documentation lives in the repository:

| Document | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [README](../../README.md) | Project overview, install, configuration and troubleshooting. |
| [docs index](../../doc/README.md) | The authoritative entry point for repository documentation. |
| [progress ledger](../../doc/progress.md) | Where the project currently stands and what is next. |
| [long-term issues](../../doc/long-term-issues.md) | Known defects and why they are not fixed yet. |
| [permissions and boundaries](../../doc/permissions-and-boundaries.md) | Dependencies, permissions, external services and failure boundaries. |
| [settings copy](../../doc/settings-copy.md) | What every settings label means, and the full explanation behind it. |
| [CI/CD](../../doc/ci-cd.md) | Build, release and rollback. |
| [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) | Release history for this package. |

## License

**MIT** — full text in [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party notices are kept in
[permissions and boundaries](../../doc/permissions-and-boundaries.md) rather than in the license
body, so GitHub's license detection reports `MIT` instead of `NOASSERTION`.

SSE decoding protocol references the MIT project
[`three-water666/webcode`](https://github.com/three-water666/webcode).

# Harness Web Bridge

**English** · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Use your logged-in web AI — DeepSeek, GLM (Z.ai), Kimi, Qwen, Doubao — as model providers inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/RSLN-creator/dsh-web-bridge). Web models emit tool calls, DSH
executes them under its native permission and approval system, and the results go back into the same
web session.

**No API keys.** It drives the site through your own browser login.

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-webcode-bridge
```

---

## Status & risks (read this first)

**Status**: this is a **work-in-progress project** — behavior and interfaces can change, and a site
redesign can break any site's channel at any time (keeping selectors and protocol teaching aligned
with live pages is the daily work here). **Forks and PRs are welcome** — see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the commit-message shape and the local gates.

**Risks — evaluate for yourself before using**:

| Risk | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Site ToS / account restriction** | The plugin drives your **logged-in web sessions** with automation, which may violate a site's terms of service; accounts can be rate-limited or restricted — **one of the author's own DeepSeek web accounts has been restricted**. Pace your usage (the plugin ships send gaps and backoff, but guarantees nothing). |
| **Tool mode = prompt injection** | With "local tool calling" enabled, the bridge injects tool-protocol teaching into the web conversation; that content is **visible to the site**, and compared with plain browser use it widens the surface for being flagged as automation. |
| **Page redesigns break things** | Every site is "the web page as a backend"; when a site ships a redesign its channel can break. |
| **Data locality** | Login state lives only in the plugin's **local** browser profile; no API keys, no telemetry, no cloud component. |

**Default mode (important)**: tool calling is **off by default** — the bridge is then a pure web
session: the web model receives exactly your words, identical to the browser (no prompt injection,
no call replay). To let the web model call local tools, enable **Settings → Web Bridge → Local tool
calling** (the first card) or the "local tools" pill under the composer — enabling asks for a
confirmation first. Tool calls, once produced, always execute under DSH's native permission system.

## Why

Most "web model" integrations are fragile in the same three ways: they scrape HTML, they lose the
conversation when the page reloads, and they bypass the host's tool permissions. This plugin is
built the other way around:

| Concern | How it is handled |
| --- | --- |
| **Tool permissions** | The web model only *proposes* calls. DSH runs them with its own permission and approval system — the bridge cannot bypass it. |
| **Session continuity** | A per-session cursor keeps the web conversation alive across turns, across restarts, and after history rewrites. When the web session is lost the bridge replays the full first turn instead of silently starting over. |
| **Long prompts** | Over-threshold bodies are delivered as a file attachment, bypassing the composer's write-stall and truncation limits, with an automatic fallback to plain text if any step fails. |
| **Rate limits** | A configurable send gap (global **and per site**) plus automatic backoff-and-retry on the site's own rate-limit response. |

## Features

- **Tool calling is an explicit switch (off by default).** By default the bridge is a pure web
  session (zero injection, zero replay). When enabled, each site is taught the tool-call shape it
  actually accepts (DeepSeek's native token format, GLM's ```json code block, `<tool_call>` tags
  elsewhere); the protocol is recomputed from the live tool list every turn, so it never drifts.
- **Real site rendering in the DSH right sidebar.** Not a screenshot, not a mock — the actual site,
  loaded through a same-origin mirror so you can type, scroll and click in it. Login state persists.
- **Per-site and global settings.** Model, instruction, send gap and prompt-delivery mode can each
  be set globally *and* overridden for a single site — changing one site never disturbs the others.
- **Multi-account.** One site can hold several independent logins; each gets its own browser profile
  and its own request pacing.
- **Observable.** Every delivery, fallback and rate-limit event is projected into
  `GET /__webcode/status`, so "did it actually work" is answerable from the UI instead of from logs.

## Requirements

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | **22.13 or newer** |
| DeepSeek Harness | **0.1.0-rc.6 or newer** |
| Browser | None to install — the plugin ships its own Chromium (Playwright). A system browser is used only as a fallback. |

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-webcode-bridge
```

### From a release tarball

Download `dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz` from
[Releases](https://github.com/RSLN-creator/dsh-web-bridge/releases), then:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add C:\path\to\dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz
```

### From source

```powershell
cd package/dsh-webcode-bridge
pnpm install            # do NOT add --frozen-lockfile, see doc/ci-cd.md
pnpm pack              # produces dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz
```

> **Restart `dsh web` after installing.** Installing only swaps files on disk; the running process
> still has the old code loaded. This is the single most common "it does not work" report.

### Do not install by repository URL

The plugin lives in the `package/dsh-webcode-bridge` subdirectory of this repository; **the
repository root has no `package.json`**. Pointing `dsh plugin` at the repository therefore finds no
manifest, and the plugin ends up installed as a plain dependency with DSH warning:

```
dsh: warning: dsh-webcode-bridge declares no dsh.bundle — installed as a plain dependency, not a profile layer
```

and the plugin configuration UI shows *"Plain dependency (no dsh metadata declared), not a profile
layer plugin"* (已安装，未生效 / installed but not active). That warning means **the wrong directory
was installed**, not that this package is missing metadata — it does declare `dsh.bundle.patch`
(see `package/dsh-webcode-bridge/package.json`). Install one of these instead:

```powershell
# by package name
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-webcode-bridge

# or by the package subdirectory / a built tarball
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/RSLN-creator/dsh-web-bridge/tree/main/package/dsh-webcode-bridge
dsh plugin --profile web add C:\path\to\dsh-webcode-bridge-<version>.tgz
```

Nothing needs to be added to the repository root to fix this.

> **This plugin targets the `web` profile.** It declares `dsh.client.platform = "web"` and mounts its
> panel through the DSH web settings UI. Installing it into the `desktop` profile is not supported —
> use `--profile web` as shown above.

## Quick start

1. **Start** — `dsh web`, then open <http://127.0.0.1:3080>.
2. **Sign in to a site** — open the native *Settings → Web Bridge* panel and click **Log in** for the
   site you want. A real browser window opens; once you are signed in it closes and the session is
   reused headlessly from then on. Each site keeps its own login.
3. **Pick a model** — the model picker gains a **Harness Web Bridge** group listing every model from
   every signed-in site. Choose the default for new sessions in Settings.
4. **Use it** — the site appears in the DSH right sidebar (the official
   `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right` tabs; no third-party sidebar plugin involved). The
   default is a **pure web session** — the web model receives exactly your words, like the browser;
   to let it call local tools, enable **Settings → Web Bridge → Local tool calling** or the "local
   tools" pill under the composer (a confirmation dialog appears).

Tool calls produced by the web model run on your machine under DSH's normal permission prompts, and
the results are returned to the same web conversation.

## Configuration

All settings live in *Settings → Web Bridge* and can also be edited through the standalone settings
page. Settings are stored per profile.

### Global

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Local tool calling** | **The master switch (off by default)**: off = pure web session (zero injection); on = tool-protocol teaching is injected into the web conversation and the web model may propose local tool calls (still executed under DSH's permission system). Enabling requires a confirmation. |
| **Default model** | Which model a new session starts on. |
| **Global instruction** | A paragraph appended to the first message of every new web session (only injected while tool calling is enabled). |
| **Send gap** | Minimum wait between two sends to the same site. Default basis is *since last send* (protects against send-rate limiting); *since last reply finished* protects against talking too fast. |
| **Prompt delivery** | `Attachment` (default): over-threshold bodies are uploaded as a file. `Plain text`: always write into the composer (the pre-0.16 behaviour). |

### Per site

Each site gets its own tab where you can override, independently of the global value:

- **Account / login** — one row per login on that site, with add/switch.
- **Model** — which model this site should use.
- **Instruction** — an extra instruction that only applies to this site.
- **Send gap** — its own pacing; `Follow global` clears the override.
- **Prompt delivery** — `Follow global` / `Attachment` / `Plain text`.

The fallback chain is always **site override → global → built-in default**, and clearing an override
deletes the key rather than writing a third value — so "never configured" and "configured to follow
global" stay distinguishable in the settings file.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `WEBCODE_PROMPT_STORE_DIR` | Where the per-site prompt files are written. `off` disables writing them entirely. Default `~/.dsh/webcode`. |

## Site status

**DeepSeek is the primary target and holds up over long sessions. GLM works but is unstable.**

| Site | Status |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek `deepseek:deepseek` | **Primary.** Validated over long multi-turn tool loops on a real browser session, with auto-continue, cursor persistence and recovery from Harness history after a restart. |
| GLM `glm:glm-5.3` / `glm-5.3-flash` | **Usable but unstable.** The end-to-end loop passes on a real session — a random secret that exists only in the tool result is echoed back verbatim. |
| Kimi / Qwen / Doubao / Z.ai | **Wired up, not validated over long runs.** Availability depends on your login. Run the per-site check below to see where your machine stands. |
| Claude | Region-restricted; the site itself says so. |
| ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini | Not reachable from our network (502 plus an explanatory page). |

### Checking a site on your own machine

"Wired up" is not the same as "verified", so there is a per-site acceptance entry point that runs
the same minimum real loop against whichever site you have signed in. It ships in the **source
checkout**, not in the installed package (it is a development tool, like `test-mock/real-verify.mjs`),
so run it from a clone:

```powershell
cd package/dsh-webcode-bridge
node test-mock/site-verify.mjs --list          # every registered site
node test-mock/site-verify.mjs --site kimi     # one site
node test-mock/site-verify.mjs --site kimi --site qwen
```

It reads the login you already have and never signs in or solves a captcha for you. Each check gets
one of four verdicts, and only real pages plus real requests can produce `PASS`:

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PASS` | A real page and a real request support the conclusion. |
| `FAIL` | A real page reproduced a failure (with the readings attached). |
| `BLOCKED` | An external condition got in the way (not signed in, captcha, rate limit) — **not** a product verdict. |
| `UNVERIFIED` | This entry point does not cover that item, so nothing is claimed. |

It covers the minimum loop — login verdict, composer usable, real send, read-back, body in the
stream, tool call parsable, turn settles. It does **not** cover long-run stability, multi-turn tool
convergence, restart recovery, vision upload, or thinking-effort read-back; those need their own
probes. A `--site kimi` run on a fresh empty profile currently reports a login-verdict inconsistency
(the panel can show "signed in" for a site that is not), recorded as long-term issue #53.

What "unstable" means for GLM, concretely:

- **Thinking cannot be turned off**, and it dominates the stream (1051 of 2472 replies were thinking-only).
- **The site intercepts tool-call tags in prose** through its own native tool layer, so GLM is taught
  only the ```json code-block shape, with fallback parsing from the thinking stream.
- **Deep-link navigation is stopped by an Aliyun slider captcha**, so probes go through the driver path.
- Two failure modes have been fixed: a stream that died mid-thinking produced an empty reply, and
  call-fence tails leaked into the reply body as garbage.

Read it as: **DeepSeek is the one to run all day; GLM is a good second opinion.** When GLM fails,
retry — attributable failures surface as coded messages rather than silent degradation.

## How it works

A few design notes worth knowing before you read the source.

### Right sidebar, one origin per site

Each site is served from `http://<siteId>.localhost:8931/`, so the pathname the site sees matches its
real site and SPA routers and root-relative assets work unchanged. The exception is **DeepSeek, which
is always mounted at the relay root** — it validates the hostname, and a subdomain gives a blank
`Unknown hostname` page. `*.localhost` resolves to loopback, so the exposure surface is unchanged.

Sites often load scripts and styles from a *different* origin with `crossorigin`, and that origin's
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` may be an illegal wildcard (`https://*.deepseek.com`), which browsers
refuse outright. `lib/mirror.js` therefore rewrites those URLs to same-origin `/__static/<host>/…`,
strips `integrity` and `crossorigin`, rewrites the runtime `fetch`/`XHR` calls that target those
origins, and installs an idempotent runtime hook to catch lazily-built chunk URLs.

**Order matters:** rewrite the site HTML first, *then* inject the bootstrap. Reversed, the constants
inside the bootstrap get rewritten too and the runtime comparison never matches. `test/mirror.test.mjs`
locks this in.

### Prompt delivery

Bodies over the threshold go up as an attached `.md` file instead of being typed into the composer,
which sidesteps two measured failure modes: `PROMPT_WRITE_STALLED` (the composer stops growing while
being written) and `PROMPT_TRUNCATED` (the site accepts only half). **Any** failure on that path
falls back to plain text — delivery is an implementation detail, "the message gets sent" is the
contract.

Two sites (DeepSeek, Kimi) have their own lower thresholds because their composers were measured to
truncate earlier than the global default. Sites where upload is confirmed to *not be read* are
downgraded at runtime and remembered.

### Token accounting

Token estimates use three measured densities (0.19.3 onward) — CJK **0.75**, prose ASCII **0.30**,
other ASCII (digits, punctuation, source) **0.70** — plus a 10% margin. The rule is that the estimate
**never understates**; the single source of truth is `TOKEN_DENSITY` in `lib/metrics.js`. Speed
figures are measured from the site's own SSE stream and are kept separate from the estimate.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing appears after installing | **Restart `dsh web`.** Then check that the plugin is listed for the `web` profile. |
| A site shows "not logged in" but you are logged in | The bridge uses its **own** browser profile. Sign in through *Settings → Web Bridge → Log in*, not in your daily browser. |
| Right sidebar is blank for one site | That site's page failed to load. The panel shows a per-site explanation with a retry button rather than raw JSON. |
| "Import login state from this machine" fails | Expected on Edge 128+: cookies are app-bound encrypted (`v20`), so copying a profile cannot decrypt them. Use **Log in** instead. |
| Long prompt was typed instead of attached | Check the **Prompt delivery** setting for that site — a per-site override may be set to `Plain text`. |

`GET /__webcode/status` exposes the live readouts (last delivery, transport mode, session slot,
rate-limit retries, fresh-conversation reasons) — that is the first place to look when the UI is
ambiguous.

## Development

```powershell
cd package/dsh-webcode-bridge
pnpm test              # regression, parsing and Harness adapter contracts
pnpm lint:comments     # comment discipline gate
pnpm ci:local          # full local CI
```

Useful single-file runs:

```powershell
node test/glm-session-replay.test.mjs        # replay a real GLM session shape offline
node test-mock/real-mirror-matrix.mjs        # right-sidebar acceptance matrix, 10 sites
node test-mock/run-real-longrun.mjs          # long real-browser tool loop
node scripts/verify-pack.mjs                 # tarball vs working tree, byte for byte
```

## Documentation

| Document | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [docs index](doc/README.md) | The authoritative entry point for repository documentation. |
| [progress ledger](doc/progress.md) | Where the project currently stands and what is next. |
| [long-term issues](doc/long-term-issues.md) | Known defects and why they are not fixed yet. |
| [permissions and boundaries](doc/permissions-and-boundaries.md) | Dependencies, permissions, external services and failure boundaries. |
| [settings copy](doc/settings-copy.md) | What every settings label means, and the full explanation behind it. |
| [CI/CD](doc/ci-cd.md) | Build, release and rollback. |

## License

[permissions and boundaries](doc/permissions-and-boundaries.md) rather than in the license body, so
GitHub's license detection reports `MIT` instead of `NOASSERTION`.

[`three-water666/webcode`](https://github.com/three-water666/webcode).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-auto-paste

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-auto-paste?color=3b6cf6)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-auto-paste)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--alpha.5%20%7C%200.2.1--rc.1-6b6cf6)](https://github.com/sakuraqqq/dsh-auto-paste)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/sakuraqqq/dsh-auto-paste?style=social)](https://github.com/sakuraqqq/dsh-auto-paste/stargazers)

**往输入框里粘 8000 字日志，最后只剩一张卡片。**

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件：粘贴超过 500 字（默认阈值，可配置）时，原文自动保存到当前工作区的 `pastes/<时间戳>.txt`，输入框里只插入一张卡片；发送后消息里也是同一张卡片，模型收到的是一行文件引用，按需再读。聊天框和上下文都不会被长文占满。

![demo](docs/demo.gif)

## 安装

```sh
npm i dsh-auto-paste
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-auto-paste
```

装完刷新页面即可，不需要改配置。桌面版（DeepSeek Harness 桌面应用）需在它自己的 profile 上单独装一次，见下文 [安装与激活](#install--安装与激活)。

## 适用

日志与堆栈、代码与 diff、论文、会议记录、聊天导出——凡是「很长、但不想让它占满聊天框」的文本。

## 兼容性

| DSH 版本 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| 0.2.1-alpha.5 | ✅ 实测可用 |
| 0.2.1-rc.1 | ✅ 实测可用 |
| 0.2.1-rc.2 | 未验证 |

## 如果它帮你省了时间

点一个 **Star** ⭐ —— 这是对作者最直接的鼓励，也能让更多人看到它。遇到问题欢迎开 issue。

## Release / 发布状态

- **npm**：[npm 页面](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-auto-paste) —— 官方源 `registry.npmjs.org`。发版策略：新版本先发到 `dist-tag: next` 观察，再人工转为 `latest`。**当前 `0.3.1`**（`latest` 与 `next` 一致）。
- **源仓库**：`https://github.com/sakuraqqq/dsh-auto-paste`（tag 与版本号一一对应）。
- **许可**：MIT（见下）。
- **同步提示**：npm 发布后国内镜像（npmmirror）同步有几秒到几分钟延迟，以官方 registry 为准。

## License / 许可

MIT License — Copyright (c) 2026 misakamaster。
本插件以 MIT 许可开源：可自由使用、修改、再分发（含商用），需保留版权声明与许可文本。详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。
**反馈**（bug/建议）欢迎提交：QQ 群测试反馈或直接联系作者。

## What it does / 功能

1. **Web 客户端粘贴钩子（主路径）** — `dsh.client.platform: web`。在输入框粘贴超过阈值（默认 500 字符）的文本时：
   - 客户端拦截粘贴事件，通过现有 connection RPC（`/api` → Typert gateway）调用宿主 `pasteStore/savePaste`；
   - 宿主把文本写入当前会话工作区的 `pastes/<时间戳>.txt`；
   - 输入框里插入 **dsh 原生原子引用卡片**（与 dsh 自己的附件同一套节点）：
     - 只显示**文件名 + 字符数**（`📄 20260815-103000.txt · 1234 字符`），不显示路径；
     - **一键删除**：Backspace / Delete 一次把整张删掉——它是 Lexical 装饰节点（`contenteditable="false"`），不存在被逐字删的中间态；
     - **点击即在右侧栏打开全文**（官方侧栏对 `.txt` 走纯文本预览，**只读**；要能编辑需装 dsh-better-sidebar，见下）；
     - 发送后消息里是**同一张可点卡片**。模型侧**不塞正文**：卡片序列化出来就是 `@"pastes/20260815-103000.txt"` 这个引用，`dsh-file-reference` 明确该语法**不增加请求 token**，模型据此自己去读那个文件。
   - **降级（自动，无提示）**：拿不到上面那套输入框接口时——老 dsh 线、输入框正忙（提交中）、或光标在你打字期间被改动——退回**文本引用** ` @"pastes/20260815-103000.txt" (1234 字符)`：发送后同样渲染成可点卡片，只是输入框里是纯文本、要手工删。两条路径给模型的文本完全一致。
   - 其中 **N 是 UTF-16 code units**（即 JS 的字符串长度：emoji/代理对算 2，CJK 算 1），与 UTF-8 字节数不是一回事——这个口径是**冻结**的，已发消息里的引用数字不会被改写。卡片上的数字走**卡片自己的显示字段**，**不进引用本身**（引用必须是裸的 `@"路径"`，否则点击时会把数字当成路径的一部分而打不开）。
   - 保存失败时会尝试把原始文本插回输入框，并**如实说明是否插回成功**：插回去了就说已按原样粘贴；没插回去会明说「没能自动插回、内容仍在剪贴板，请手动 Ctrl+V 重试」，不做未经验证的承诺。
   - 超过 **1 MiB** 的文本会被服务端拒绝（大小上限，防资源耗尽）：报错并回退为普通粘贴，不落盘。
2. **save_paste 工具（纪律兜底）** — 宿主同时注册 `save_paste` 工具，模型在用户贴大段文字时可主动调用，把文本持久化为 `pastes/<时间戳>.txt` 并在回复中引用路径。工具输出只含 `path` / `bytes` / `chars`（**不含本机绝对路径**，RPC 结果同样收窄：绝对路径含用户名与目录结构，仅宿主内部使用）。建议在项目 `AGENTS.md` 加一行纪律：

   ```markdown
   ## dsh-auto-paste 纪律
   用户粘贴大段文字（约 500 字符以上）时：若输入框钩子未拦截，主动调用 save_paste 工具
   把文本存入 pastes/<时间戳>.txt，并在回复中引用该工作区相对路径，不要复述原文。
   ```

### 可选集成：dsh-better-sidebar（在侧栏编辑粘贴文件）

本插件**不调用** better-sidebar 的 API，只探测它在不在（`ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'])`，仅用于下面那行提示与设置页状态）。**点粘贴卡片的动作由 dsh 内核路由**：内核把卡片地址交给右侧栏，装了 better-sidebar 时它认领该地址、用它的编辑器打开 `pastes/*.txt`（可编辑）；没装则落到 dsh 自带的**只读**纯文本预览。

因此：

- **没装时**：第一次粘贴出卡片后会**就地说明一次**（一行提示，可关闭，关掉后不再出现）；万一错过了，设置页 General 分区的「侧栏集成」一行会一直写着，装上后自动消失。
- ⚠️ **版本要求：`dsh-better-sidebar` ≥ 0.28.0**。更早的版本里，侧栏编辑器保存时会用**工作区相对路径**，而它的写接口只接受绝对路径 ⇒ 保存报 400（`is not an absolute path`，host 侧校验在 `lib/index.js` 的 `if (!isAbsolute(path)) throw …`）。那是上游 [omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar#646](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar/issues/646)（**本插件无关**，已于 2026-10-04 修复）。
  - **0.28.0 实测可正常保存**（2026-10-17，桌面版）。
  - 若暂时无法升级，两条替代路径：从 **better-sidebar 自己的文件树 / 路径输入框**打开同一文件再保存（那条路会传绝对路径）；或继续用 `pastes/` 下的文件本身（内容已在磁盘上，编辑只是便利）。

> **与 dsh 自带文件面板的区别**：自带面板能**浏览**工作区文件（包括 `pastes/`），但只读、改不了；装了 better-sidebar 才有编辑入口。两者的差别只在"能不能改"，不在"能不能看"。

## Install / 安装与激活

**方式一：从 npm 安装（推荐）**

```sh
npm i dsh-auto-paste                          # 最新版（dist-tag: latest）；--save-exact 可锁版
npm i dsh-auto-paste@0.3.1                    # 或指定版本（换成你要的版本号）
# 在插件父目录执行，以包名注册到目标 profile：
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-auto-paste
dsh --profile web            # 重启 web profile，观察: [dsh-auto-paste] host ready ...
# 刷新浏览器页面后，控制台可见: [dsh-auto-paste] client paste listener attached — threshold 500 chars until the host's config arrives
#                              随后: [dsh-auto-paste] config from host: minChars=500 (deployment), maxBytes=1048576
```

**方式二：本地目录安装（开发/调试）**

```sh
# 在插件父目录（本仓库根）执行；相对路径锚定调用目录：
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-auto-paste
dsh --profile web
```

改动插件后：`pnpm install && pnpm run build`（tsc → dist/），然后重启 `dsh --profile web` 并刷新页面。

**官方桌面版（DeepSeek Harness 桌面应用）**：同样支持，但要在**桌面版自己的 profile 上单独装一次**（它不复用 web profile 的装配）——桌面版自带 CLI，在应用安装目录下执行：

```sh
set "DSH_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.dsh"          # 换成桌面版实际使用的 home（隔离启动器会改它）
resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add dsh-auto-paste
```

桌面版是独立 dsh 线（如 `0.2.0-rc.2`）。若它的运行时版本超出本插件声明的 peer 范围，dsh 会**拒绝加载该 bundle**（表现为插件完全无输出、设置里也没有本插件的阈值项），需要**精确版本豁免**——用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop allow-version dsh-auto-paste@<版本> --dsh-version <运行时版本> --accept-risk`，它会在 profile 目录写一个 `compatibility.json`；`--dsh-version` 必须填它报错时给出的那个值。豁免是**精确配对**的，插件升级或 dsh 升级都不会继承。

`minChars` 有两个入口：**Settings → General 的「大段粘贴阈值」**（保存即生效、不用重启；旁边的「恢复默认」清掉这次覆盖），以及 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 row config（**部署默认值**，改完只需重启 dsh、不用重新构建）。用户设置优先，没设置时用部署默认值。

覆盖值存在哪里随 dsh 线而变，保存后都立即生效：**dsh 0.1.5 线**存进 dsh 自己的设置文档；**dsh 0.1.7 起** dsh 改成"从插件自己的 Config 投影"，覆盖值写回 profile patch（同一个 `cordis.patch.yml`）—— 所以本插件把 `minChars` 声明为 schemastery 的 volatile 字段：没有它，dsh 不会为该插件生成表单，写入也会被拒。当前 dsh 无法在界面保存时（没有 settings 服务、或该线不支持 volatile），设置行会说明原因并禁用保存。

host 始终是唯一权威：客户端半身拿不到 row config（dsh 的 `dsh.client` 只认 platform/inject/external/immediately，启动图里不带 config），它在启动时、以及每次保存设置后，都用 `pasteStore/getConfig` RPC 取生效值；取不到时用 500 兜底并在控制台标出来源。`maxBytes` 只有 row config 一个入口（属部署口径）。

## Verification without an API key / 无 key 验证

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep dsh-auto-paste   # 配置层含本行
dsh plugin --profile headless add ./dsh-auto-paste
dsh --profile headless "run a probe"                    # host 半身加载；模型调用会 MISSING_CREDENTIAL
```

## Manifest checklist / 清单自查

- [x] `dsh.bundle.patch` → `./cordis.patch.yml`（dsh 加载插件的硬性要求，缺失只会被当作普通依赖安装）
- [x] `dsh.client.platform: web` + `exports["./client"]` → `dist/client.js`
- [x] `exports["./typert"]` → `dist/typert.host.js`（typert-loader 自动注册 remote 调用）
- [x] 代码无外发数据：插件不发起任何网络请求，只写工作区 `pastes/` 下的本地文件
- [x] DSH peer 范围**两段并列**（`^0.1.5-rc.1 || ^0.2.0-rc.2`）——**别改回单段**：dsh 在挂载前用 semver 逐个校验 `@deepseek-ai/dsh`/`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer（带 `includePrerelease`），任一不满足就**整包拒绝加载**。单段 `^0.1.x` 会拒掉 0.2 线（官方桌面版在跑 0.2.0-rc.2）；写成区间（`>=0.1.5-rc.1 <0.3.0`）又会把**没测过的** 0.2.1+ 一并放行。并列两段 = 只放行实测过的线

## Dependencies pinned / 依赖锁定

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`: `^0.1.5-rc.1 || ^0.2.0-rc.2`（peerDependency — 两段并列，见上）
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol`: `^0.1.5-rc.1 || ^0.2.0-rc.2`（peerDependency — 同上；RPC schema 那一层）
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis`: `^4.0.1` (peerDependency — host provides it; runtime import of `Service` resolves through the profile's node_modules).
- `zod`: `^4.4.3` (Typert host schema instances, same line as in-box host remotes).

## Pitfalls / 坑（从真实 spike 提炼，防呆）

1. Node version: DSH requires Node ^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0. Older Node (e.g. v22.17) only warns EBADENGINE but may hit runtime issues — upgrade if you can.
   - Node 版本：DSH 要求 ^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0。旧版本（如 v22.17）只告警 EBADENGINE，不阻断，但建议升级。
2. npm dist-tag trap (the big one): `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` `latest` is a STALE 0.0.1-rc.1; the real line is under the `next` tag (0.1.0-rc.x). This scaffold pins the next-tag version for you — never `npm i @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` over it.
   - npm dist-tag 坑（最大）：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 的 latest 是过期的 0.0.1-rc.1，正确版本在 next tag。本脚手架已锁 next 版本，勿再手动 npm i 覆盖。
3. Version-line alignment: keep every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` package on the same `0.1.0-rc.x` line so pnpm does not install two module copies.
   - 版本线对齐：所有 @deepseek-ai/dsh-* 包统一用同一 0.1.0-rc.x 线，避免 pnpm 装两份模块。
4. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency: import only `type { Context }` where possible (erased at compile). At runtime the host hands you `ctx` — the `Service` base class import resolves through the profile's node_modules.
   - @deepseek-ai/cordis 是 peerDep：尽量只 import type（编译期擦除），运行时 ctx 由宿主传入。
5. Pure ESM: package.json must set `"type": "module"`; build with `module: esnext` + `moduleResolution: bundler` to keep bare specifiers.
   - 纯 ESM：package.json 必须 "type": "module"；tsc 用 module:esnext + moduleResolution:bundler 保留 bare specifier。
6. `dsh plugin add <dir>` anchors relative paths to the INVOKING directory — run it from the parent directory, not from inside the plugin.
   - dsh plugin add <dir> 的相对路径锚定调用目录——要在插件的父目录执行。
7. A DSH peer mismatch is a SILENT total failure on the desktop build: dsh evaluates every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer before mounting a bundle, and a rejected bundle is skipped without a word — no host log, no client bundle request, no settings row. If the plugin "does nothing at all" on a newer dsh line (the desktop app runs its own line, e.g. `0.2.0-rc.2`), read `package.json` peer ranges FIRST, then grant the exact-version exemption (see Install).
   - DSH peer 不匹配在桌面版上是**完全静默**的失败：dsh 在挂载 bundle 前逐个校验 peer，被拒的 bundle 被直接跳过——host 无日志、client bundle 不被请求、设置里也没有本插件的行。若插件在某条更新的 dsh 线（桌面版自带一条，如 `0.2.0-rc.2`）上"毫无反应"，**先看 `package.json` 的 peer 范围**，再考虑精确版本豁免（见安装节）。
8. In the bundle `cordis.patch.yml`, `name` is a package name (resolved via node_modules / `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules`), not a relative path.
   - bundle 的 cordis.patch.yml 里 name 用包名（走 node_modules 解析），不要用相对路径。
9. Registrations are effects: `ctx.tools.register()` / `ctx.on()` auto-dispose on unload. Wrap your OWN resources (timers/connections) in `ctx.effect(() => { acquire; return cleanup })`.
   - 注册是 effect：ctx.tools.register()/ctx.on() 卸载自动清理；自己的资源（timer/连接）要包 ctx.effect(() => {…; return cleanup})。
10. Load order = service dependencies, never file order: `export const inject = ['tools']` makes the plugin wait until `ctx.tools` is ready.
   - 加载顺序靠服务依赖（inject），不靠文件顺序。
11. Full end-to-end (model actually calls your tool) needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; without it `--verify` proves load/list/event, and the model call fails with MISSING_CREDENTIAL.
    - 端到端（模型真正调工具）需 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY；无 key 时 --verify 只能证明加载/列出/事件，模型调用会 MISSING_CREDENTIAL。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-qq-group

> 当前版本：**v1.26.2**（QQ空间配图/@/远程读取、红包、主动 @主人、七角色语音）

独立的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) QQ 群聊插件：有人设、有记忆、会判断该不该接话，支持主动/被动搭话、语音、唱歌、表情包、日记、QQ空间说说和视觉看图。

A standalone QQ group-chat plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): persona, memory, value-based reply decisions, proactive/passive chat, voice, singing, stickers, diary, QQ Zone posts and optional vision.

> 本项目从 [dsh-whale-girl](https://github.com/SenuMirai/dsh-whale-girl) 的 QQ 模块拆分而来，数据、模型、人设与桌宠完全独立。
> This project was split out of the QQ module in [dsh-whale-girl](https://github.com/SenuMirai/dsh-whale-girl); its data, model, persona and lifecycle are fully independent from the desktop pet.

---

## 中文

### 功能与特点

| 能力 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **OneBot 11 / NapCat** | 通过 WebSocket 连接 NapCatQQ，支持自动重连、启动检查、自动拉起 |
| **人设与模型** | 多张人设卡；可按群绑定，一张卡可绑多个群，未绑定跟随全局；模型 provider/model、推理档位、备用模型可按群单独选 |
| **主动搭话** | 独立页：搭话模式按当前群/私聊单独生效（私聊禁用并注明），冷场阈值、概率/峰谷命中线、近远时机、冷却、每日上限、安静时段、试运行、主动语音概率 |
| **红包识别** | 识别红包卡片并用模型发一句感谢；当前 NapCat 没有领取接口，只能识别/感谢，不能保证抢到 |
| **主动 @主人** | 接话或主动开口时按概率 @ 主人，向她吐槽、分享群里趣事、抱怨群友或告状；仅群聊生效，私聊禁用；概率、冷却、每日上限可调 |
| **价值评分 v3** | 不是每条都回：@/叫名字/引用直接回；普通闲聊按关键词、成员、上下文、熟识度、好感度、夜间等算 0~100 分 |
| **冷场逻辑** | 任何人类消息都会重置接话去抖和主动开口倒计时；群里一直有人说话时她不插话 |
| **直接对话队列** | 她正在生成时收到的 @/引用会排队，不会丢；主动开口会给 @ 让位 |
| **群友画像** | 每群每人独立熟识度/好感度；主人数值全局统一且可编辑，不被互动或衰减改动 |
| **群聊开关** | 设置页顶部逐群开关；关闭后完全不接该群消息、不主动开口、不写互动 |
| **日记** | 每条回复记录上下文、评分理由、内心吐槽；thought 放在 JSON 第一项；支持筛选、导出、删除单条/按人删除；列表可滚动加载全部，不再只看最近几十条 |
| **表情包** | 自动收藏、AI 打标签、按语境/关键词选图；自拍图已并入常用库，用“尾巴/自拍”标签即可被明确请求选中 |
| **语音 / 唱歌** | 只保留 Edge TTS 与 GPT-SoVITS；GPT-SoVITS 已接 v2ProPlus 七角色（三月七、银狼、藿藿、白露、虎克、青雀、克拉拉）与 7 种情绪参考音；支持试听、按群概率；RVC 已移除 |
| **七情绪** | 开心 / 生气 / 吃惊 / 中立 / 难过 / 厌恶 / 恐惧；按回复文字自动选参考音，也可手动指定 style |
| **QQ空间** | 手动/草稿/自动；配图 0~9（固定/区间/模型决定，可选表情包仓库）；文本 @ 名单/模型/概率；本地记录按日期筛选、排序、滚动；群聊可读自己最近说说；远程读取他人空间/评论默认关闭并标风险 |
| **视觉看图** | 可看当前/引用图片，也支持转发聊天记录里的图片；嵌套转发最多展开两层；本地路径与文件头识别 |
| **回复引用** | 目标消息被后续消息隔开时自动带 QQ 引用，可开关；文件/合并转发/语音不引用，失败自动改发纯文字 |
| **省 token** | 自适应上下文（自包含短句少读、指代/追问读全量）、contextTurns、记忆注入条数、情绪/敌意判断开关 |
| **永久记忆** | 双层：全局主人记忆 + 各会话独立记忆；全局私密不进群；自动记录名单；容量满只封存；手动增删/提升/多选 AI 合并 |
| **夜间免打扰** | 支持跨午夜；夜间不再主动开口，普通接话按命中扣分（0~100，默认 20） |
| **心情** | 每群独立心情；会随互动升降、随时间回落，被辱骂/恶意攻击会下降 |
| **用量统计** | 按群、按用途、按模型统计 token；图片调用与估算调用单独标记；月历、余额估算、单价校准 |
| **稳定性** | 事件/定时器/异步回复全部兜异常；模型只回 reasoning 时自动提取/重试/备用模型 |

### 部署要求

- **DeepSeek Harness** 桌面版或可加载插件的主机
- **Node.js 22.12+**、**pnpm 9+**
- **NapCatQQ** + **QQ NT**（Windows 推荐；Linux 可用 NapCat Docker，需自行确认 QQ 登录）
- 一个 QQ 小号作为机器人，已加入目标群
- 可选：视觉模型（识图）、edge-tts（语音，联网）、ffmpeg（部分音频转换）

### 部署步骤

#### 1. 安装并登录 NapCat

1. 安装 QQ NT 与 NapCatQQ；
2. 用机器人 QQ 登录；
3. 在 NapCat 中启用 **OneBot 11**，添加 **WebSocket 服务器**：
   - 地址：`ws://127.0.0.1:3001`（默认）
   - access token：自己生成一个强随机串
4. 确认 NapCat 控制台显示 OneBot WebSocket 已启动。

#### 2. 安装本插件

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SenuMirai/dsh-qq-group.git
cd dsh-qq-group
pnpm install
pnpm run build
```

把目录 link 进 DSH profile（或使用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <绝对路径>`）：

```jsonc
// <DSH_HOME>/profiles/desktop/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-qq-group": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-qq-group"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        // ... 其它插件
        "dsh-qq-group"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**重启 DSH**。设置页出现「QQ 群聊」即加载成功。

#### 3. 配置连接

DSH 设置 →「QQ 群聊」→「连接」：

| 项 | 示例 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket 地址 | `ws://127.0.0.1:3001` | NapCat 的 OneBot WS |
| Access Token | `<YOUR_TOKEN>` | 与 NapCat 一致，不要提交到仓库 |
| 机器人自称 | `小鲸鱼` | 群里被叫到的名字，可逗号分隔多个 |
| 主人 QQ | `<YOUR_QQ>` | 用于好感初始值与主人识别，可留空 |
| 自动连接 | 开 | DSH 启动后自动连 |
| 自动拉起 NapCat | 按需 | 需要填写启动脚本绝对路径 |

#### 4. 启动

设置页点「启动」，或在群里 @ 机器人测试。首次建议先点「体检」与「模型检查」。

### 配置参数推荐

以下是**起步值**，按群氛围调整：

| 参数 | 推荐 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 搭话模式 | 主动 | 被动只回 @/叫名字；主动才会插话和冷场开口 |
| 评分阈值 | 55~65 | 越高越挑；太低会频繁接话 |
| 接话概率 | 0.15~0.35 | 分数达标后的二次掷骰 |
| 冷却 | 20~45 秒 | 两句之间的最小间隔；直接对话会跳过 |
| 普通 10 分钟上限 | 6~10 | 防刷屏；按群活跃度调 |
| 直接回复上限 | 20~40 | @/引用/接着聊单独计数 |
| 去抖 | 6 秒 | 等一波人说完；任何新消息都会重置 |
| 夜间免打扰 | 23:00–08:00，扣 20 | 想更安静就调大，0 = 不扣 |
| 看图策略 | 自定义：@ + 问看法 | 最省 token；需要“所有图”再选 all |
| 语音概率 | 0.1~0.3 | 太高会刷屏，且增加 TTS 延迟 |
| 表情包概率 | 0.15~0.3 | 配合自动收藏使用 |
| 备用模型 | 选一个同 provider 的可用模型 | 主模型空回复/限流时兜底 |

模型建议：

- 日常文字：`deepseek-v4.1-flash` 或你额度充足的模型；
- 需要识图：选支持 `text + image` 的模型（如 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`step-5-preview`、MiniMax 多模态型号）；
- 推理档位：群聊建议 `low`；太高会增加延迟和 token；
- 换模型后历史用量按 provider/model 分开统计，余额是全局钱包。

### 设置页结构

- **人设 / 模型**：人设、搭话模式、模型、推理档位、备用模型、用量与积分；
- **连接**：OneBot、token、自称、主人、自动拉起、Cookie 清理提示；
- **聊天频率（按群）**：阈值、关键词/成员概率、冷却、上限、连发、语音/唱歌/表情包概率、看图策略；
- **白名单 / 黑名单**：一行一个 QQ；白名单抬评分下限，黑名单压上限；
- **夜间**：时段与命中扣分；
- **语音**：Edge / GPT-SoVITS、音色、情绪、语速、试听、网关检查；
- **QQ空间**：启用、模式、可见范围、频率、草稿生成与发布；
- **表情包**：自动收藏、数量/MB 上限、看图策略；
- **日记**：筛选、导出、删除、滚动加载全部。

所有页签的「保存全部」固定在顶部，不需要滚到底部。

### 数据与隐私

| 路径 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/qq.json` | 连接、群策略、语音/唱歌 |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/settings.json` | 人设、模型、名单、夜间、看图 |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/qq-memory.json` | 每群短期记忆（上限 200 条/群） |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/permanent-memory.json` | 永久记忆（不摘要、不淡忘，按会话分开） |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/profiles.json` | 每群每人画像 |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/diary.json` | 日记（上限 1000 条） |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/qzone.json` | QQ空间发布记录（tid、正文、时间、可见范围） |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/stickers/` | 本地表情包 |

仓库**不包含**任何聊天记忆、日记、QQ 号、token、Cookie 或用户路径；这些只存在于本机运行时。`.gitignore` 已排除数据文件。

### 接话逻辑（简版）

1. @ / 叫名字 / 引用她 → **100% 直接回**；
2. 其它消息在 6 秒去抖后算 0~100 分：
   - 基础 30；关键词/指定成员概率；刚跟她聊过 +30；带“你” +15；
   - 熟识度、好感度、@ 别人、被冷落、夜间扣分、单条消息；
   - 白名单抬下限、黑名单压上限；
3. 分数 ≥ 阈值 → 按 `分数/100` 掷骰 → LLM 闸门（读最近上下文判断是不是在跟她说）；
4. 她说完后同一人接着说：高概率候选，但仍过闸门；
5. 任何人类消息都重置冷场计时与主动开口倒计时。

### 视觉看图

「表情包」→「看图策略」：

- 关闭 / 自定义（多选）/ 所有图片；
- 自定义可同时勾选：`@/叫名字/引用`、`强相关上下文`、`文字里问她看法`；
- 只有真正回复且命中条件才下载并计费；纯图片、无文字、没 @ 她的消息不触发。

### 主动 @主人

接话或主动搭话时，偶尔会专门 @ 主人，而不是只对群里说话。

- 开关在「主动搭话」页签最前面；勾选后展开详细设置。
- **仅群聊生效**：私聊会话里选项禁用，并标注原因。
- 可调参数：命中概率、最小间隔（分钟）、每日上限（0 = 不限次数）。
- 冷场主动开口、普通接话时都可能触发，不会每条回复都 @。
- 这次会强制用文字发，避免语音抢占 @；正文不写 @，由系统自动带。
- 提示词会要求她讲具体的事：吐槽、分享刚发生的趣事、抱怨群友、告状、撒娇。

### 红包识别与感谢

识别 `json`/`xml` 红包卡片或 `redbag` 消息段，标记为 `[红包]`。开启后用模型生成一句 20 字以内的感谢，并 @ 发红包的人。

**当前不能真正领取红包**：NapCat 的 OneBot action 列表没有领取接口，插件不会用 DOM 自动化伪装，也不会声称“抢到了”。

详见 [docs/RED-PACKET.md](./docs/RED-PACKET.md)。

### QQ空间增强

- **配图**：0~9 张；固定张数、区间随机、或模型决定；来源可选表情包仓库。
- **文本 @**：NapCat 没有真正的空间 @ 参数，只能正文写「@昵称」，不保证通知；支持名单随机/模型决定/概率。
- **本地说说记录**：按日期筛选、最新/最早排序、滚动加载全部。
- **群聊读自己的空间**：消息提到空间/说说/动态时，注入最近 5 条本地记录。
- **远程读取**：通过 Qzone cookie 读取自己/指定 QQ 的说说和评论，默认关闭，需接受风险；只建议手动低频。
- **回复评论**：目前只读，写入评论留到下一阶段。

完整参数与风险说明见 [docs/QZONE.md](./docs/QZONE.md)。

### 语音模型安装

GPT-SoVITS 模型不随仓库分发，需要本地放置：

```text
GPT_SoVITS/GPT_weights_v2ProPlus/<角色>-e10.ckpt
GPT_SoVITS/SoVITS_weights_v2ProPlus/<角色>_e10_s<步数>.pth
GPT-SoVITS/ref/voices.json
GPT-SoVITS/ref/*.wav
```

完整步骤见 [docs/VOICE-MODELS.md](./docs/VOICE-MODELS.md)。

### 已知边界

- NapCat/QQ 的登录与风控由 QQ 侧决定，插件不绕过；
- 语音/唱歌依赖 edge-tts 网络与本地音频工具；
- 视觉识别受所选模型能力限制，不支持图片的模型会退回文字；
- 群聊内容会发给所选模型 provider，请自行评估隐私；
- 请遵守 QQ 与群规，不要用于骚扰、刷屏或未授权自动化。

## English

### Features

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| **OneBot 11 / NapCat** | WebSocket connection to NapCatQQ; reconnect, startup checks, optional auto-launch |
| **Persona & model** | Multiple persona cards; bind per group (one card can serve many groups), otherwise follow global; provider/model, reasoning effort and fallback can be per group |
| **Proactive chat** | Dedicated tab: chat mode, idle threshold, peak/off-peak hit lines, timing factors, cooldown, daily cap, quiet hours, trial mode, proactive voice chance |
| **Proactive @owner** | Occasionally @ the owner during proactive chat to complain, share group gossip or report on members; group chats only, disabled in private; chance, cooldown and daily cap are configurable |
| **Value scoring v3** | Not a reply to everything: @/name/quote always reply; ambient chat is scored 0–100 from keywords, members, context, familiarity, affinity and night penalty |
| **Cold-start logic** | Any human message resets both the reply debounce and proactive countdown; she stays quiet while the group is active |
| **Direct-message queue** | @/quote messages received while generating are queued, never dropped; proactive messages yield to direct ones |
| **Member profiles** | Per-group, per-user familiarity 0–100 and affinity -100–+100, updated by speech, mentions, replies, continuity and hostility |
| **Diary** | Every reply records context, score reasons and inner thought; `thought` is the first JSON field; filter, export, delete one/person |
| **Stickers** | Auto-collect group images, AI rename/tag, context-aware sending; count and disk caps |
| **Voice / singing** | Edge TTS and GPT-SoVITS only; GPT-SoVITS ships 7 v2ProPlus characters (March 7th, Silver Wolf, Huohuo, Bailu, Hook, Qingque, Clara) with 7 emotion references; preview and per-group probability; RVC removed |
| **QQ Zone** | New tab: manual / draft / auto modes; visibility defaults to private; daily cap, minimum interval, auto chance; draft from today’s diary; strips links and QQ/group numbers before publishing; local history with delete |
| **Vision** | Optionally pass real QQ images to a vision model: @ / strong context / opinion questions; local paths and magic-byte detection supported |
| **Reply quoting** | Auto-quote when the target is separated by newer messages; toggleable; files/forwards/voice are skipped and failed quotes retry as plain text |
| **Token saving** | Adaptive context (fewer turns for self-contained messages, full context for references), contextTurns, memory injection count, mood/hostility toggles |
| **Night DND** | Cross-midnight window; configurable score penalty (0–100, default 20) |
| **Usage stats** | Token usage by group, purpose and model; image/estimated calls marked; calendar, balance estimate, rate calibration |
| **Stability** | Guards around events/timers/async replies; extracts JSON from reasoning, retries, optional fallback model |

### Requirements

- **DeepSeek Harness** desktop or a host that can load plugins
- **Node.js 22.12+**, **pnpm 9+**
- **NapCatQQ** + **QQ NT** (Windows recommended; NapCat Docker on Linux is possible, confirm QQ login yourself)
- A spare QQ account for the bot, already in the target group
- Optional: a vision model, edge-tts (network), ffmpeg for some audio conversions

### Deployment

#### 1. Install and log in to NapCat

1. Install QQ NT and NapCatQQ.
2. Log in with the bot account.
3. Enable **OneBot 11** and add a **WebSocket server**:
   - URL: `ws://127.0.0.1:3001` (default)
   - Access token: generate a strong random string.
4. Confirm that NapCat reports the OneBot WebSocket as running.

#### 2. Install this plugin

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SenuMirai/dsh-qq-group.git
cd dsh-qq-group
pnpm install
pnpm run build
```

Link the directory into your DSH profile (or run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <absolute-path>`):

```jsonc
// <DSH_HOME>/profiles/desktop/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-qq-group": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-qq-group"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        // ... other plugins
        "dsh-qq-group"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Restart DSH.** The "QQ Group" settings page appearing means the plugin loaded.

#### 3. Configure the connection

DSH Settings → "QQ Group" → "Connection":

| Field | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket URL | `ws://127.0.0.1:3001` | NapCat OneBot WS |
| Access token | `<YOUR_TOKEN>` | Must match NapCat; never commit it |
| Bot display name | `LittleWhale` | Names she answers to; comma-separated aliases allowed |
| Owner QQ | `<YOUR_QQ>` | Owner detection and initial affinity; may be empty |
| Auto-connect | on | Connect when DSH starts |
| Auto-launch NapCat | optional | Requires an absolute launcher path |

#### 4. Start

Click "Start" in settings, or @ the bot in a group. For first use, run "Health check" and "Model check".

### Recommended settings

Starting points; tune to your group:

| Setting | Recommendation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chat mode | proactive | Passive only answers @/name; proactive also joins and starts cold chat |
| Score threshold | 55–65 | Higher is pickier; too low is noisy |
| Reply chance | 0.15–0.35 | Second roll after the score passes |
| Cooldown | 20–45 s | Minimum gap; direct conversations bypass it |
| Normal 10-min cap | 6–10 | Anti-spam; tune to group activity |
| Direct 10-min cap | 20–40 | Separate counter for @/quote/continuation |
| Debounce | 6 s | Wait for the group to settle; any new message resets it |
| Night DND | 23:00–08:00, penalty 20 | Increase for quieter nights; 0 disables the penalty |
| Vision policy | custom: @ + opinion questions | Cheapest useful default; choose all only if needed |
| Voice chance | 0.1–0.3 | Too high adds latency and spam |
| Sticker chance | 0.15–0.3 | Pair with auto-collect |
| Fallback model | A working model on the same provider | Covers empty replies/rate limits |

Model tips:

- Text: `deepseek-v4.1-flash` or another model with sufficient quota.
- Vision: choose a model with `text + image` input (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `step-5-preview`, multimodal MiniMax models).
- Reasoning: `low` is usually best for chat; higher effort adds latency and tokens.
- Usage history is kept per provider/model; the balance is a global wallet estimate.

### Settings layout

- **Persona / Model**: persona, mode, model, reasoning effort, fallback, usage/credits.
- **Connection**: OneBot URL, token, bot name, owner, auto-launch.
- **Chat frequency (per group)**: threshold, keyword/member chances, cooldown, caps, burst, voice/sing/sticker chances, vision policy.
- **Allow / block lists**: one QQ per line; allow-list raises the score floor, block-list lowers the ceiling.
- **Night**: window and penalty.
- **Voice**: voice, rate, pitch, volume, presets, preview.
- **Stickers**: auto-collect, count/MB caps, vision policy.
- **Diary**: filter, export, delete.

### Data and privacy

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/qq.json` | Connection, group policy, voice/singing |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/settings.json` | Persona, model, lists, night, vision |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/qq-memory.json` | Per-group memory (200 turns/group) |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/profiles.json` | Per-group member profiles |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/diary.json` | Diary (1000 entries) |
| `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq-group/stickers/` | Local stickers |

The repository contains **no** chat memory, diary, QQ numbers, tokens, cookies or user paths; those exist only in the local runtime. `.gitignore` excludes data files.

### Reply logic (short version)

1. @ / name / quote → **always reply directly**.
2. Other messages are scored 0–100 after a 6-second debounce:
   - base 30; keyword/member chances; +30 for the same person continuing; +15 for "you";
   - familiarity, affinity, @ someone else, being ignored, night penalty, single-message penalty;
   - allow-list floor, block-list ceiling.
3. Score ≥ threshold → roll `score/100` → LLM gate (recent context decides whether it is addressed to her).
4. Same person continuing after her reply: high-probability candidate, still gated.
5. Any human message resets the cold-start timer and proactive countdown.

### Vision

Stickers tab → "Vision policy":

- off / custom (multi-select) / all images.
- Custom modes can be combined: `@/name/quote`, `strong context`, `opinion question`.
- Images are downloaded and billed only when she actually replies and a condition matches; image-only messages without @ do not trigger.

### Credits

Design ideas were informed by:

- [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet): plugin/desktop-pet engineering; the QQ module later split into this project.
- [zaofan-make/dsh-qqbot](https://github.com/zaofan-make/dsh-qqbot): value scoring, persona, member profiles, context compression.
- [Jiangsubei/dsh-napcat-bridge](https://github.com/Jiangsubei/dsh-napcat-bridge): proactive chat, night DND, aliases, memory design.
- [NapNeko/NapCatQQ](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ): OneBot implementation for QQ NT.
- [OneBot 11](https://github.com/botuniverse/onebot-11): protocol standard.
- [rany2/edge-tts](https://github.com/rany2/edge-tts): free, GPU-less speech synthesis.
- [sdfsfsk/matsuko_cover](https://github.com/sdfsfsk/matsuko_cover) and [dsh-cover-pipeline](https://github.com/InariNGT-Ofiicial/dsh-cover-pipeline): inspiration for the singing/cover pipeline.
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): plugin host, models, attachments, settings.

Each project keeps its own license; this project borrows design ideas only and does not copy restricted assets.

### Known limits

- QQ login and risk control are decided by QQ/NapCat; this plugin does not bypass them.
- Voice/singing need edge-tts network access and local audio tools.
- Vision depends on the selected model; text-only models fall back to text.
- Group messages are sent to the selected model provider; evaluate privacy accordingly.
- Follow QQ rules and group rules; do not use for harassment, spam or unauthorized automation.







































### v1.14.0 GPT-SoVITS backend

- Added GPT-SoVITS backend; adapter gateway on 50123, API on 9880.
- The gateway translates POST /tts into GPT-SoVITS GET /tts and returns WAV.
- v1 base model on CPU: short sentence about 2.4s; character model not trained yet.
- Reference audio is a locally generated female voice; replaceable with the trained character model later.

### v1.21.0 QQ Zone and seven-character voice

- New QQ Zone tab: manual / draft / auto modes.
- Visibility defaults to private; friends or public optional.
- Daily cap, minimum interval and auto chance; draft from today's diary.
- Strips links and QQ/group numbers before publishing; local history with delete.
- GPT-SoVITS adds Huohuo, Bailu, Hook, Qingque and Clara, for 7 v2ProPlus characters.
- Voice keeps only Edge TTS and GPT-SoVITS; RVC, CosyVoice2, Kokoro and IndexTTS removed.
- Diary loads all entries on scroll; Save All is pinned to the top of every tab.

### v1.11.0 Kokoro GPU TTS

- Added Kokoro-82M local TTS with ONNX Runtime DirectML for the 780M iGPU.
- Separate Kokoro HTTP gateway (default 50122); short sentences take about 6s.
- Added Kokoro to the voice backend list; selecting it fills 50122 automatically.
- Kokoro supports Chinese built-in voices (e.g. zf_005); CosyVoice2 remains better for free-form emotion descriptions.
- IndexTTS-2.5 option remains reserved; its service is still not deployed.

### v1.10.0 Local TTS backend list

- Voice tab now switches between Edge TTS / CosyVoice2 / IndexTTS-2.5.
- Added local TTS HTTP gateway protocol: POST /tts, JSON {text, style}, returns WAV.
- CosyVoice2 gateway verified; 8.7s speech takes about 60s on CPU.
- Local backends accept style/emotion text; failures are explicit, Edge remains the fast default.
- IndexTTS-2.5 option is reserved; its model service is not deployed yet.

### v1.9.3 Explicit voice/singing fixes

- Fixed "sing a song for me" extracting the bogus title "歌来听听" and falling back to text; no title now uses the default song.
- Fixed "sing Little Star" without the word "song" not being recognized.
- Fixed "say it in a voice message" not being recognized.
- Explicit voice/singing now defaults to 100% and remains configurable.
- Fixed the voice-send gate so an explicit request still sends even when the normal voice chance is 0.

### v1.9.2 RVC preview temp directory

- RVC worker output now goes to a temp directory under the model directory, avoiding unwritable user-cache paths in Windows/sandboxed child processes.
- Workers point TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR at their own writable directory, fixing ONNX no-usable-temp errors.
- Preview failures now report the concrete error.

### v1.9.1 Preview and explicit voice/singing

- The preview button now applies the current RVC settings, including unsaved model/device/pitch; on failure it plays the original voice and reports why.
- Explicit "send a voice message / say something / let me hear your voice" uses the configurable requested-voice chance (default 95%, 100% = always).
- Explicit "sing / request a song / sing a song" uses the configurable requested-singing chance (default 90%, 100% = always).
- Fixed singChance not being applied when the model chose to sing by itself.

### v1.9.0 RVC model library and 780M

- Voice tab scans the model directory and lists .pth/.onnx + index; no long paths.
- Model dropdown, open folder, refresh and dedupe; multiple models switchable.
- Device switch: auto / DirectML (780M) / CPU; ONNX automatically uses the DirectML worker.
- Pitch, timeout and max duration are sliders.
- Added ONNX worker + onnxruntime-directml; verified Chinese conversion on the 780M.

### v1.8.0 RVC external worker

- Optional RVC: edge-tts dry audio → external Python worker → converted WAV → QQ voice.
- Speech and singing share RvcConverter; failures fall back to the original audio.
- Configure Python, worker script, model/index, device auto/cpu/dml, pitch and timeout.
- 780M iGPU can use DirectML; real-time is not required.
- Disabled when no script/model is configured; existing edge-tts is unaffected.

### v1.7.1 quoted images and auto-start

- Quoted previous images are fetched via get_msg and passed to vision.
- Quoted image + “is this you / look / evaluate” goes through direct reply.
- autoStart now defaults to false: restarting DSH does not start QQ; use the Start button.

### v1.7.0 per-group mood v1

- Each group has its own mood 0–100 plus seven dimensions; baseline 70.
- A short model judgement after direct replies; actual change divided by 3; 12h half-life.
- Low confidence / insignificant / daily cap means no injection.
- Injection is background only, never a command; insults do not lower mood.
- Chat tab shows mood, dimensions, latest reason and reset.

### v1.6.0 proactive v2

- Probability hit line: peak/off-peak base × timing factor + miss bonus.
- Recent chat makes it harder; long silence makes it easier; quiet hours skip.
- Trial mode defaults on (log only); one group per tick.
- Legacy fixed-backoff mode remains selectable.
- Chat tab adds controls and shows misses/trial state.

### v1.5.0 memory v3

- New memory-v3 layer: freshness, importance, emotion, fact keys, source.
- Events decay; stable facts do not. The latest item wins per fact key.
- Evidence-based recall, max 6 items / 800 chars / 2 facts (configurable).
- Legacy qq-memory.json is kept and migrated into memory-v3.json.
- Every 12 turns (configurable) extracts 1–2 memories; compression also writes.
- Memory page supports add/edit/delete and recall stats.

### v1.4.0 selfie library and implicit visual intents

- Added a **whale-girl selfie** library inside Stickers, separate from the normal sticker repo; upload/delete/open-folder supported.
- "Show your tail / show yourself / send a selfie" without an attached image is treated as a selfie request and uses a per-group selfie chance.
- Selfie chance 0–100%; 100% always sends when an asset exists.
- With an empty library it replies as normal text and never says "I have no photo".
- When an image is attached, "look at you/tail" prefers image understanding and does not send a selfie.
- Extra selfie trigger words are configurable per group in the Stickers tab.

### v1.3.0 sticker request and singing probability

- Image probability moved to the top of the Stickers tab:
  - normal send probability when the model wants to send;
  - requested-send probability

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). `pnpm run dev:web` builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in one terminal, and `make help` lists the matching Make targets for Web and Desktop; the guide's application commands section owns the full table. For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseek-harness2026, title={DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, publisher={GitHub}, howpublished={\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness}}, } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
